members.doc: The outline's and the holes' points, as three.js Shape.extractPoints.

interfaces.name: Path2Class
interfaces.doc: og.Path2: `new og.Path2(points?)`.

members.name: new
members.doc: A path, through the points when given (setFromPoints).

interfaces.name: ShapeClass
interfaces.doc: og.Shape: `new og.Shape(points?)`.

members.name: new
members.doc: A shape, through the points when given (setFromPoints).

x-og-modules.name: load
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset loading from cooked output: `og cook` turns assets/ into cooked/ (.ogb blobs and the manifest cooked/.cook.ogt), and the runtime reads only cooked/.
Paths are asset ids: the path under assets/ (`models/ship.glb`, `scenes/main.ogt`); an `assets/` prefix is accepted. Every blob is checked against the manifest's type, schema version and cook stamp.
The game's bundle (`cooked`) is opened before the first tick and GameDesc.scene is spawned then. Loads from an open bundle complete at once on both hosts (the web host fetches the bundle's files before the engine starts); only og.load.bundle of another bundle can be pending, and it completes at a tick boundary.

functions.name: bundle
functions.doc: Open another cooked bundle (the game's own `cooked` is open before the first tick). Its loads read through it once it is ready.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The cooked directory, relative to the project (or the page), such as `dlc/cooked`.

functions.returnsDoc: The bundle's handle: pending until its manifest is read, then ready or failed.

functions.name: bundleInfo
functions.doc: What an open bundle holds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: asset
params.doc: A bundle handle; the game's own bundle is og.load.bundle's first answer, also given by `defaultBundle`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-bundle asset.

functions.name: defaultBundle
functions.doc: The game's own bundle, opened before the first tick from `cooked/`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when cooked/ was missing or unreadable (run og cook); the reason names the path.

functions.name: gltf
functions.doc:
Load a cooked glTF (.gltf or .glb), as three.js GLTFLoader.load: its meshes, materials and textures join the renderer once.
A MagicaVoxel `.vox` cooks to a glTF and loads here too: greedy-meshed, flat-shaded, its palette as vertex colours, z-up turned y-up, each model about its centre (MagicaVoxel's pivot, with a scene graph or without). Its import settings (`models/hut.vox.ogt`, `type import`) size and place it: `model { voxScale 0.1 voxOrigin bottom }` is 0.1 m a voxel (default 1) and the lowest voxel on y = 0 (default `center`, the editor's origin). A `.vox` with frames (MagicaVoxel's animation) cooks to clips that swap the frames' models, played by og.AnimationPlayer as any skinned clip: `voxFps 8` (default 10) and `voxClip walk 0 3` (frames 0 to 3; default one clip `frames` of the file's playback range, else of every frame); a node's `_loop` repeats its keys as the editor plays them.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle, or why it was refused (an uncooked path, a cook stamp mismatch, no open bundle).

functions.name: scene
functions.doc: Load a cooked scene (.ogt). world.instantiate spawns its entities: depth first, parents before children, each component table matched to a registered component by its reflected name (`Transform` is og.Transform) and migrated field by field; a field the scene lacks keeps its default, one the component lacks is dropped with a warning.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The scene's asset id, such as `scenes/main.ogt`.

functions.name: prefab
functions.doc: Load a cooked prefab (an .ogt of `type prefab`: one entity tree authored once and placed many times, docs/design.md §2.5). world.instantiate spawns it as it spawns a scene, its root under the desc's root entity, each entity unnamed (place a prefab many times without name clashes) and carrying an og.PrefabLink. A scene places one with a `prefab` line in an entity, and the cook flattens it there.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The prefab's asset id, such as `prefabs/crate.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: The prefab, or why not (not cooked, or not a prefab).

functions.name: font
functions.doc: Load a cooked MSDF font for og.render.text, or an icon set (an `.ogt` of `type icons`: SVG icons cooked into a distance-field atlas like a font) for UiDesc.icons.font.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

params.name: path
params.doc: The font's asset id, such as `fonts/NotoSansSC-Regular-subset.ttf`.

functions.name: fontInfo
functions.doc: A loaded font's metrics.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: sound
functions.doc:
Load a cooked sound for the audio module. Sounds are `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.ogg` (Vorbis) and `.flac` files under assets/ (and procedural `.ogt` presets): og cook decodes each to 16-bit PCM and encodes it to QOA, so every format plays, streams and loops the same. The asset id keeps the source's extension (`audio/theme.mp3`).
A long sound (music, ambience) can be cooked in chunks of whole QOA frames: `sound { stream true chunk 4 }` in its import settings, `<file>.ogt` (`theme.mp3.ogt`; chunk in seconds, 1 to 60, default 4), and every sound whose QOA file would pass 1 MiB unless `stream false`. Its first chunk loads with it and the others follow the playheads (SoundInfo.chunks), so music is never resident whole; it plays sample for sample as the whole file would, loops and crossfades included. A sound cooked in chunks cannot join a streaming group.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the sound.

params.name: path
params.doc: The sound's asset id, such as `audio/blip.wav`.

functions.name: lut
functions.doc: A colour lookup table for PostEffects.lut, from a cooked `.cube` file (Adobe/Resolve 3D LUT; other sizes are resampled to 32). Loaded once per path. One in a streaming group's pack loads once its group is resident (refused before, naming the group); while the group is unloaded PostEffects.lut grades nothing with it, and it comes back under the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook).

functions.name: environment
functions.doc: A prefiltered environment map for Environment.map, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type environment`: `source` an equirectangular Radiance `.hdr` or OpenEXR `.exr` (the centre column faces +X, as three.js maps it) or a KTX2 cube map (six square faces +X -X +Y -Y +Z -Z with rows from the top; RGBA16F, RGB9E5, BC6H and the other HDR formats, decoded at cook time), or `faces` with six `.hdr`/`.exr` images in that order; `size` level 0's face size (a power of two, 16 to 2048, default 128), `intensity`, `rotation` (degrees about +Y) and `samples`. The cook prefilters it into a cube of five GGX levels (roughness 0 to 1) in RGB9E5 and the diffuse irradiance as nine harmonics, so loading only uploads it; `prefiltered true` takes a KTX2 cube's own mip chain as those levels instead (one already GGX-prefiltered by cmgen, IBLBaker or the glTF IBL sampler: level k of L at roughness k / (L - 1)), at the file's own size, without filtering it again. On the web it is fetched with the bundle like any blob; one in a streaming group's pack loads when its group is resident, and the sky lights the scene until then. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook) or not an environment map.

functions.name: emitter
functions.doc: A particle emitter asset for ParticleSystem.emitter, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type particles`: shape, rate and bursts, lifetime, speed, size and colour over life, gravity, drag, noise, a texture and sprite sheet, blending, collision (`collision <bounce> <friction> [depth | colliders]`: off the drawn depth, or off the scene's colliders on the GPU), billboard, mesh (`render mesh box | sphere | tetrahedron | "<model id>"`: each particle a small lit shape that tumbles with its rotation) or 2D sprite rendering, `lit true` (billboards and meshes shaded by the sun, the sky and local lights), `distortion <0..1>` (billboards that bend the scene behind them: heat haze, shock rings), `subEmitter <birth | death | collision> "<emitter id>" <count> [<inherit velocity>]` (up to 4: another emitter's particles born where this one's are born, die or bounce; or `subEmitter life "<emitter id>" [<inherit velocity>]`: each particle runs the other emitter's own emission, its rate, bursts, duration and looping, from its birth while it lives, born where it is; one level deep) and `events <birth | death | collision>...` (og.ParticleEvent: its systems simulate in the tick). A sprite-mode emitter may draw from a texture array instead (`array "<id>" [<layers>] [off | life <cycles> | fps <n> | random]`: each particle shows a layer by its age, at a rate, or one at random for its life; one draw per array whatever the layers; `round true` fades each particle to the soft dot's round edge). `effect "<id>"` draws its billboards or mesh particles with an effect material (an `.ogt` of `type effect`: a main texture, gradient ramp, mask, noise erosion, flow map, fresnel and soft depth fade, each texture with its own tile, scroll, turn and polar coordinates; intensity, alpha, the uv offset, the erosion and eight custom numbers as a constant, a random range per particle or a curve over its life; an optional material shader whose surface_color hook runs last and reads effect_life(), effect_random(), effect_custom1() and effect_custom2()). Expressive lines: `speedOverLife`, `spinOverLife` and `rateOverTime` curves (<t> <value> pairs, against the velocity, the angular velocity and over each cycle against `rate`); `attractor <x> <y> <z> <strength> [<radius>]` (up to 4 points in the emitter's space that pull, or push when negative); `field curl <strength> [<frequency> <scroll>]` (divergence-free curl noise) or `field "<texture>" <strength> <size>` (a vector grid the cook bakes from an image N² wide and N high, N up to 16: pixel x + z·N, y from the bottom, rgb 0..1 as -1..1); `shape spline <x> <y> <z> ... [closed]` (2 to 8 Catmull-Rom points, emitted evenly along it and along its tangent); `inheritVelocity <fraction>` (of the emitter's own velocity, world space). Every one runs the same in compute and on the CPU path. The textures, array, mesh model, effect material and sub-emitters it names are loaded with it (a sub-emitter that fires its parent is refused); while the array's streaming group is not resident its systems draw nothing. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle, or a texture, texture array, model or sub-emitter it cannot load.

functions.name: shader
functions.doc: A material shader for og.render.shaderMaterial, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type shader` (its WGSL compiled by the cook for every back end). `mode hooks` (the default) defines hooks of the lit shader; `mode full lit` or `mode full unlit` defines `fn vertex(v: VertexInput, model: mat4x4<f32>, p: Params) -> VertexOutput` and `fn fragment(f: FragmentInput, p: Params) -> SurfaceOutput` over the binding contract (camera(), the model with its skin, Params, tex0 to tex7 for the material's eight texture slots), lit by the frame's lights or drawn as returned, the prepass and every shadow pass drawn through the same entries. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle or not a shader.

functions.name: post
functions.doc: A custom post pass for PostEffects.custom, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type post`: `code` or `source` (a `.wgsl` beside it) defining `fn post(f: PostInput, p: Params) -> vec4<f32>` and `param <name> float|vec2|vec3|vec4|color <default...>` lines (at most eight). The function reads previous(uv), scene_color(uv), depth(uv), normal(uv) and f.uv, f.pixel, f.size, f.time, and returns linear HDR colour. The cook compiles it for every back end. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle or not a post pass.

functions.name: vector
functions.doc: A cooked vector for og.ui's VectorFill, from an `.ogt` of `type vector`: `source` an SVG (or `svg` inline) of paths, basic shapes, groups and transforms, filled and stroked with colours or linear and radial gradients, and `tolerance` (curves flattened to within it, view-box units). The cook cuts it into triangles whose edges the UI pass antialiases at any size; anything outside the subset is refused by name. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle or not a vector.

functions.name: uiMaterial
functions.doc: A custom UI material for og.ui's LayerDesc, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type ui-material`: `code` or `source` (a `.wgsl`) defining `fn material(m: MaterialInput, p: Params) -> vec4<f32>`, which returns the composite's straight-alpha linear colour at m.uv (0 to 1 over the layer; m.pixel, m.size in CSS px, m.time the UI clock), reading the layer with layer(uv) and layer_texel(), and `param <name> float|vec2|vec3|vec4|color <default...>` lines (at most four). The cook compiles it for every back end. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle or not a UI material.

functions.name: texture
functions.doc: Load a cooked texture for og.render.sprite and a document's ``, as three.js TextureLoader.load. Sources are PNG, JPEG or KTX2 files under assets/ (`texture { kind color|normal|linear|pixel }` in `.ogt`). A KTX2's `KTXorientation` and `KTXswizzle` are honoured: one that is not `rd` and `rgba` is decoded, flipped to rows top to bottom and swizzled, and cooked again; one that is (Basis ETC1S or UASTC, or RGBA8, of a colour or linear kind) is taken as it is.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the texture.

params.name: path
params.doc: The texture's asset id, such as `textures/stone.png`.

functions.name: textureArray
functions.doc:
Load a cooked texture array (an `.ogt` of `type texture-array`: `kind color|normal|linear|pixel` and one `layer "<file>"` per layer, 1 to 256 images of one size, each path beside the file or under assets/) and upload it as one 2D-array texture, its layers in file order, each in the encoding the device takes for its kind. Each layer is also a texture of its own, `<path>#layer<n>`, for og.load.texture. Loading the same path again answers the same array.
SpriteDesc.array (world and screen sprites), og.Sprite.array and 2D particle emitters (an emitter's `array` line) draw from its layers, one draw per array whatever layer each shows, with glow and the additive blend; an `array true` flipbook sheet cooks its frames into one (materials and terrain layers do not sample arrays yet). TextureArrayInfo and the frame's texture bytes report it. One in a streaming group's pack loads once its group is resident (refused before, naming the group); when the group unloads the renderer lets it go, og.render.sprite of it is refused and og.Sprite and particles of it draw nothing until the group is resident again, when it comes back under the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the array.

params.name: path
params.doc: The array's asset id, such as `tiles/ground.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook), not a texture array, or layers that do not agree.

functions.name: style
functions.doc: Load a cooked UI style (an `.ogt` of `type style`: every palette role, the radii, type ramp, durations, and its art: the atlas and its nine-slice frames, ornaments, fonts, icons, motion and sounds; the grammar is og-ui's `parse_style`) for UiDesc.style. Version 3, the CSS dialect (docs/ui.md §3.2, what `og style upgrade`, `og style new` and `og ui migrate` write and every built-in style is), has the tokens (rarity, team, damage and chart colours each with its cue, the type scale per breakpoint, the space, size, radius and stroke scales, elevation, the shape language, motion springs and eases, sounds and haptics per UI event; colours and lengths as custom properties, `--panel-raised: #211a15`) and dresses parts with selector blocks (`Button::base.primary:active { -og-slice: … }`). Versions 1 and 2 still load. Its atlas, fonts, icons and sounds are loaded with it. Loaded once per path. A built-in style a look names is in the bundle as `@styles/<name>/style.ogt`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI uses it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The asset id, such as `styles/pixel/style.ogt` or `@styles/pixel/style.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle, a style that does not parse (the reason names the line) or an asset it names that cannot load.

functions.name: document
functions.doc: Load a cooked UI document (an `.ogt` of `type screen` or `type component`, validated by og cook against og-ui's reflected props; the grammar is og-ui's README §Documents: version 2, CSS declarations for an element's look and layout, docs/ui.md §3.2; `og ui migrate` writes a version 1 document as version 2) into the world's UI, where og.ui.push and og.ui.replace name a screen and a document's own markup names a component by its `name` line; its timelines are defined as `<name>/<timeline>`. Loading one of the same name again replaces it in place, the UI's state kept; `og dev` does this for an edited document.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI uses it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle or a document that does not parse (the reason names the line).

functions.name: look
functions.doc: Load a look: an `.ogt` of `type look` binding a frame's art direction as data. Its top-level `name`, `extends` (a built-in preset's slug, such as `anime-cel-3d`, or another look's asset id: the game's own `assets/looks/<slug>.ogt` wins over the built-in preset of that slug), `ui` (a UI style: a built-in style's slug, such as `cartoon`, or the game's own style file's asset id) and `antialias`, then one block per resource it sets (RenderSettings, PostEffects, Stylise, MaterialStyle, Fog, Sky, Environment, and the art contract's ArtPalette, ArtPixels, ArtTexels, ArtShape, ArtLine, ArtMotion, ArtCamera) with that resource's fields by name, an asset id where a field is a handle (`lut "luts/warm.cube"`, `palette "palettes/dusk.hex"`). The cook validates every field against the resources' reflected schema and flattens `extends`, so the blob is the whole look. The textures, LUTs, palettes, environment map and UI style it names are loaded with it. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook) or an asset it names that cannot load.

functions.name: lookInfo
functions.doc: What a loaded look holds and sets.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the look.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a look not loaded in this world.

functions.name: palette
functions.doc: A colour palette for Stylise.palette, from a cooked `.hex` (one RRGGBB per line, as palette sites publish them) or GIMP `.gpl` file: up to 256 sRGB colours, in file order. Loaded once per path. One in a streaming group's pack loads once its group is resident; while the group is unloaded Stylise.palette quantises to no palette, and the palette comes back under the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook).

functions.name: soundInfo
functions.doc: A loaded sound's format and length.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the sound.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead sound.

functions.name: status
functions.doc: Where a load is.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.name: error
functions.doc: Why a load failed.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: The reason, naming the fix; null unless the load failed.

functions.name: gltfInfo
functions.doc: What a ready glTF holds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-glTF asset.

functions.name: animation
functions.doc:
Load a cooked glTF's animation (its `<model>#anim` blob: the rig, the clips, the skin and morph streams) and register its skeleton and clips with og.anim. Loading the same model again answers the same handles.
Clips are cooked as f32 samples, or with `animation { compress true tolerance 0.0001 }` in the model's import settings as quantised keys (rotations as 48-bit smallest-three, translations, scales and weights as 16 bits over each channel's range) with every frame dropped that interpolation rebuilds within the tolerance; either way every frame is rebuilt here and the clip plays as f32. Morph targets are cooked sparse (the vertices each moves).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the assets.

params.name: path
params.doc: The model's asset id, such as `models/walker.glb` (a `#anim` suffix is accepted).

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an uncooked path, a model the cook wrote no `#anim` blob for (no skins, clips or morph targets), a cook stamp mismatch or an invalid rig.

functions.name: rig
functions.doc: Load a cooked humanoid map (an `.ogt` of `type rig`: a naming scheme and bones named outright) for og.anim.retarget and og.anim.humanoid. Loading the same path again answers the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation uses it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The rig's asset id, such as `rigs/strider.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a cook stamp mismatch.

functions.name: flipbook
functions.doc: Load a cooked flipbook sheet (an `.ogt` of `type flipbook`, with its Aseprite or TexturePacker atlas resolved by the cook) and its texture, and register it with og.flipbook. A sheet may name animated GIF, WebP or APNG files instead of a texture (`source "hero_run.gif"`, a clip per file, with `key auto` to key out a flat background, `align feet` to hold the figure still and `scale` to resample): the cook turns their delays into clip durations, crops every frame to one size with the pivot at the anchor, shares identical frames and packs them into the texture `<sheet>#sheet`; `og sprite inspect` measures a source's frames, drift, loop seam and edge fringe. A sheet with `array true` is cooked into a texture array instead (its frames, one size, cut out of the texture as layers): its sprites draw frame n as layer n, every sprite of the sheet one draw whichever frame each shows, and FlipbookInfo.array names the array. A sheet in a streaming group (its array and layers with it) loads once its group is resident (refused naming the group before), and its sprites draw nothing while the group is away. Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation and renderer own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The sheet's asset id, such as `sprites/hero.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a texture it cannot load.

functions.name: tilemap
functions.doc: Load a cooked map (a tilemap `.ogt`, a Tiled `.tmj` or an LDtk `.ldtk`), its tilesets and their textures. Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer and tilemaps own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The map's asset id, such as `maps/room.tmj`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle, a missing tileset or texture, or a terrain its tileset lacks.

functions.name: video
functions.doc: Load cooked footage (an `.ogt` of `type video`: `source` an .mp4, .webm or .mov beside it or under assets/, `fps`, `maxSeconds`, `size W H`, `kind color|pixel`, `audio`, and for a stream `stream true`, `keyframe`, `crf`), which og cook turns with ffmpeg into a clip (a texture array of its frames) or a stream (AV1, decoded as it plays) and its sound track. A clip's frames are uploaded as one 2D-array texture; a stream's units are fetched (on the web, from now: it is not part of the startup bundle) and decoded ahead of its players. Either way it makes the video's Texture (VideoInfo.texture), which shows the frame its og.VideoPlayer is at: a material map, an og.Sprite or a UI image draws it like any texture. Load it in GameDesc.start (every process of an og render --jobs run loads it the same way, so its handles agree). Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer and audio own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The video's asset id: the `.ogt`, such as `clips/intro.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook: a video needs ffmpeg there, og doctor) or not a video.

functions.name: videoInfo
functions.doc: A loaded video's size, frames, rate, length, texture and sound.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a handle og.load.video did not answer.

functions.name: timeline
functions.doc: Load a timeline: an `.ogt` of `type timeline` (the og.timeline module's file: duration, paths and tracks of keys), cooked with its caption files imported. Loaded once per path; play it with an og.Timeline whose asset is the handle, or `timeline:play:<name>` on the command channel.

params.name: path
params.doc: The timeline's asset id, such as `timelines/intro.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a file that is not a timeline.

functions.name: vfx
functions.doc: Load a composed effect: an `.ogt` of `type vfx` (the og.vfx module's file: a duration, events and a timeline of emitters, effect meshes, trails, beams, lights, decals, flashes, pixel-effect flipbooks, shakes and sounds), with every emitter, effect material, model, flipbook sheet and sound it names. An Effekseer effect in assets/ (`.efkproj`, `.efkefc`) is one too: the cook converts its nodes into the engine's own vfx, emitters, effect materials and meshes and warns of what it could not carry; `og vfx import` writes the same conversion as `.ogt` text to edit. Loaded once per path; play it with og.vfx.spawn or an og.Vfx whose asset is the handle.

params.name: path
params.doc: The effect's asset id, such as `fx/fireball-impact.ogt` or `fx/slash.efkproj`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook), a file that is not a vfx, or an asset it names that will not load.

functions.name: rig2d
functions.doc: Load a cooked 2D rig (an `.ogt` of `type rig2d`, written by hand or imported by the cook from DragonBones JSON) and its texture, and register it with og.skeleton2d. Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation and renderer own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The rig's asset id, such as `rigs/hero.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a texture it cannot load.

functions.name: imageData
functions.doc:
Load an image from bytes, uncooked, at run time: a PNG or JPEG a player drew, uploaded or a generator made. Its size, width and height are read from its header and checked against the budget before it is decoded. On the web the browser decodes it off the engine's thread (createImageBitmap in the engine's Worker), and no decoder is in the wasm; natively a worker thread decodes it. The handle is pending until the image is in place, then ready (og.load.imageInfo gives its texture) or failed (og.load.error says why).
Completion is host input, applied at a tick boundary and journaled like a key press: natively a load is in place before the tick after the call; on the web it lands at the first boundary after the browser has decoded it, and og.load.completions records that tick, so a replay (og replay --compare, og.load.replayCompletions) puts it in place at the same tick. In a lockstep or rollback room content made by one player is not on the others' machines, and the completion is local to each session (an asset's status is not world state and is in no snapshot or hash): send the bytes with og.platform.roomSend (at most 64 KiB a message), let each peer load them, and let the shared simulation use the content only from a tick the peers agree on through their inputs (og.net.submit), never from og.load.status.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: name
params.doc: A name for it in errors and dumps, such as `drawings/cat.png`.

params.name: desc
params.doc: How to read it and its budget.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle (pending), or why it was refused now: over the budget's bytes or textureSize, or not a PNG or JPEG.

functions.name: gltfData
functions.doc:
Load a glTF 2.0 model from bytes, uncooked, at run time: a .glb, or a .gltf whose buffers and images are data: URIs, that a player made or a generator wrote. At the call its JSON is read and its size, its triangles (every triangle primitive of every mesh) and each image's header are checked against the budget before anything is decoded. Then its images decode off the engine's thread, as og.load.imageData's do, while its primitives are converted at the tick boundaries, one at a time within LoadBudget.frameMs on the web. The handle is pending until the model is in place, then ready: world.instantiate spawns it (from a system, which cannot instantiate, insert og.Model { asset } on an entity it spawns) and og.load.gltfInfo describes it, as for a cooked glTF. Or it is failed, and og.load.error says why.
Read as the cook would, without what only the cook makes: the metallic-roughness materials (base colour, metallic-roughness, normal, occlusion and emissive maps, alpha mask, double-sided, KHR_materials_unlit, KHR_materials_emissive_strength), the node tree and scenes, vertex colours and tangents. A colour texture magnified nearest is drawn as pixel art. Skins and animations are skipped and counted, points and lines skipped; no levels of detail or raycast BVH are cooked (a raycast builds one when first needed), and the other KHR_materials extensions, KHR_texture_transform and KHR_lights_punctual are not read. Refused by name: Draco and meshopt compression, Basis, WebP and AVIF textures, sparse accessors, a buffer or image in another file (pack the model as one .glb) and any other required extension.
Completion is host input, applied at a tick boundary and journaled as og.load.imageData's is: natively the model is in place before the tick after the call; on the web the first boundary after its images are decoded and its primitives converted, recorded by og.load.completions, so a replay puts it in place at the same tick. In a lockstep or rollback room it is local to each session, as og.load.imageData's is: share the bytes with og.platform.roomSend and agree on the tick through the peers' inputs.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: name
params.doc: A name for it in errors and dumps, such as `creations/kite.glb`; its textures are `<name>#tex<n>`.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle (pending), or why it was refused now: over the budget's bytes, triangles or textureSize, not a glTF 2.0, an image that is not a PNG or JPEG, or something the reader refuses by name.

functions.name: environmentData
functions.doc:
Load an HDR environment from bytes, uncooked, at run time: an equirectangular Radiance .hdr (or OpenEXR .exr where RenderCapabilities.exrDecode is true) that a player uploaded or a generator wrote, for Environment.map as og.load.environment's cooked maps are. The game fetches the file itself (from a URL, an upload or a generator) and passes its bytes. Its size, width and height are read from its header and checked against the budget before it is decoded; the image is twice as wide as it is tall (the centre column faces +X, as three.js maps it). Natively a worker thread decodes it; on the web the .hdr decodes in rows at the tick boundaries, within LoadBudget.frameMs, never in one long stall. The diffuse irradiance (nine harmonics) is gathered as it decodes, and when the renderer first draws with it the image is resampled into a cube and GGX-prefiltered into the five levels a cooked map has (roughness 0 to 1), on the GPU by the passes the sky's own light runs (the cook's `bake` does the same on the CPU for cooked maps and for tools without a GPU). The handle is pending until the map is in place, then ready (og.load.environmentInfo gives the map) or failed (og.load.error says why); until then Environment lights the scene by the sky.
Completion is host input, applied at a tick boundary and journaled as og.load.imageData's is, so a replay puts it in place at the same tick; in a lockstep or rollback room it is local to each session (share the bytes with og.platform.roomSend).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: name
params.doc: A name for it in errors and dumps, such as `uploads/sunset.hdr`.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its face size, intensity and budget.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle (pending), or why it was refused now: over the budget's bytes or textureSize, not twice as wide as tall, a size that is not a power of two from 16 to 2048, not a Radiance .hdr or OpenEXR file, or an .exr where RenderCapabilities.exrDecode is false (the reason names it: convert the image to .hdr, or cook it).

functions.name: environmentInfo
functions.doc: A ready uncooked environment's map and sizes.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused while it is pending (say so), when it failed (with its reason) or for another kind of asset.

functions.name: release
functions.doc: Free an uncooked asset (og.load.imageData, og.load.gltfData, og.load.environmentData): a load still pending is dropped (it never completes, so it is never journaled), and a ready one's textures and meshes are emptied under their handles, so what still names them draws nothing and nothing breaks, while their memory on the GPU and their copies on the CPU go (the probe's memory report and `dump_memory` show both). An og.Model of a released model draws nothing; a sprite or material of a released texture draws one clear texel; an Environment that names a released map is lit by the sky. The handle then answers failed, naming the release. Physics shapes built from its geometries are world state and stay. Releasing again does nothing.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: asset
params.doc: A handle og.load.imageData, og.load.gltfData or og.load.environmentData answered.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a cooked asset, which stays with its bundle (a streamed one with its group).

functions.name: imageInfo
functions.doc: A ready uncooked image's texture and size.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused while it is pending (say so), when it failed (with its reason) or for another kind of asset.

functions.name: completions
functions.doc: The world's journal of uncooked loads put in place, oldest first: what a replay hands og.load.replayCompletions to put each in place at the same tick. og replay --record keeps it in the trace.

functions.name: replayCompletions
functions.doc: Put this world's uncooked loads in place at the ticks a recorded run did (its og.load.completions), not when this host finishes them: a load is held back until its tick, and at its tick the engine waits for it. Call it before the first tick; og replay --compare does. A load the journal names as failed fails at its tick whatever this host made of it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused once a tick has run.

x-og-modules.name: physics
x-og-modules.doc:
Rigid bodies over rapier (rapier3d in the 3D profile, rapier2d in 2D, both with enhanced determinism): game code owns the components, the engine's og.physics system steps them after the game's systems and writes the dynamic bodies back.
The profile is the project's (`profile "2d"` or `"3d"` in project.ogt). In 2D, bodies move in the xy plane and rotate about z; a transform keeps its z. A collider without a RigidBody is static at its transform.
The rapier world persists between ticks and is world state: snapshots, restore and the world hash cover the whole simulation. Events sent in tick N are read in tick N + 1.

consts.name: MAX_RAYCAST_HITS
consts.doc: The most hits og.physics.castRayAll returns.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along x.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along y.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along z.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about x.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about y.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about z (the 2D profile's only rotation).

consts.name: SHAPE_BOX
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a box of `size` (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_SPHERE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a sphere of `radius` (a circle in 2D).

consts.name: SHAPE_CAPSULE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a capsule along y of `radius`, with `height` between the cap centres (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_CYLINDER
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a cylinder along y of `radius` and `height` (3D only).

consts.name: SHAPE_CONVEX
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the convex hull of the vertices of `mesh` (3D), or of their xy (a convex polygon, 2D).

consts.name: SHAPE_TRIMESH
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the triangles of `mesh` (for static and kinematic bodies); in 2D the outline of their xy (the edges no two triangles share) as a hollow polyline, which stops what comes from outside.

consts.name: SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the height field registered as `mesh`, centred on the entity (3D only; a terrain: og.terrain.load's TerrainInfo.geometry).

consts.name: SHAPE_DIAMOND
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a rhombus whose diagonals are size.x (along x) and size.y (along y), an isometric tile's diamond; in 3D a prism size.z deep (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_HEXAGON
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a pointy-top hexagon in the box size.x by size.y, corners at the top and bottom middles and a quarter down each side, a hex tile's (turn it a quarter about z for a flat-top one); in 3D a prism size.z deep (both profiles).

consts.name: PROFILE_2D
consts.doc: Physics.profile: rapier2d, bodies in the xy plane rotating about z.

consts.name: PROFILE_3D
consts.doc: Physics.profile: rapier3d.

consts.name: JOINT_FIXED
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: the two bodies move as one.

consts.name: JOINT_REVOLUTE
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a hinge about `axis` (2D: about z), with optional limits and a motor.

consts.name: JOINT_PRISMATIC
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a slider along `axis`, with optional limits and a motor.

consts.name: JOINT_SPRING
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a damped spring pulling the anchors to `restLength` apart.

consts.name: JOINT_ROPE
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a rope: the anchors stay at most `length` apart, free inside it.

consts.name: JOINT_BALL
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a ball and socket (3D; the 2D profile treats it as a hinge).

consts.name: MOTOR_NONE
consts.doc: `Joint.motor`: no motor.

consts.name: MOTOR_VELOCITY
consts.doc: `Joint.motor`: drive towards `motorTarget` speed (rad/s or m/s).

consts.name: MOTOR_POSITION
consts.doc: `Joint.motor`: spring towards `motorTarget` angle or position (a servo).

consts.name: CHARACTER_JUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: a jump from the ground (or in coyote time).

consts.name: CHARACTER_LANDED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: touched the ground after being in the air.

consts.name: CHARACTER_WALL_JUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: a jump off a wall.

consts.name: CHARACTER_AIR_JUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: a jump in the air (PlatformerController.airJumps).

consts.name: CHARACTER_LEFT_GROUND
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: left the ground without jumping (ran off an edge).

consts.name: CHARACTER_BUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: hit a ceiling while rising.

consts.name: DRIVE_REAR
consts.doc: `Vehicle.drive`: the rear wheels drive.

consts.name: DRIVE_FRONT
consts.doc: `Vehicle.drive`: the front wheels drive.

consts.name: DRIVE_ALL
consts.doc: `Vehicle.drive`: every wheel drives.

consts.name: VEHICLE_ARCADE
consts.doc: `Vehicle.model`: the arcade car: engineForce, faded out towards maxSpeed.

consts.name: VEHICLE_DRIVETRAIN
consts.doc: `Vehicle.model`: an engine with a torque curve driving through a gearbox.

consts.name: SIMULATION_GAMEPLAY
consts.doc: `Cloth.simulation`, `SoftBody.simulation`, `Garment.simulation`: simulated in the physics step on the CPU, deterministic: its points are world state that snapshots, replays, lockstep and the hash carry, and that og.physics.clothPoints, softBodyPoints and garmentPoints read. The default.

consts.name: SIMULATION_VISUAL
consts.doc: `Cloth.simulation`, `SoftBody.simulation`, `Garment.simulation`: simulated by the renderer on the GPU (XPBD in small steps), for looks only, never read back. The tick leaves it unsolved: its points (og.physics.clothPoints, softBodyPoints, garmentPoints) are its rest shape carried rigidly by the entity (a garment's: the skinned pose), SoftBody.volume stays 1 and SoftBody.center is that shape's mean, so gameplay reads a stable proxy and a headless server pays nothing. The drawn motion runs on tick time: frames that skip ticks step those too, up to eight, and a world restored, rolled back or more than eight ticks ahead starts again from the rest shape. It meets the colliders drawn this frame (og.Collider boxes, spheres, capsules and height fields; convex, cylinder and triangle-mesh shapes are passed through) and, with thickness, itself. A visual cloth's or garment's wind is air moving along `wind` at its magnitude in metres a second, meeting each triangle with drag and lift against the triangle's own motion and scaled so a still face square to it feels `wind`; `gust` sends bands of stronger, veering air down it, so it ripples and flaps rather than leaning. Where RenderCapabilities.visualSimulation is false (no compute or no vertex storage) it draws that rest shape.

consts.name: PIN_TOP
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: the whole top row is pinned.

consts.name: PIN_TOP_CORNERS
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: the top-left and top-right corners are pinned.

consts.name: PIN_LEFT
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: the whole left column is pinned (a flag on a pole).

consts.name: PIN_TOP_RINGS
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: every fourth point of the top row (curtain rings).

consts.name: SOFT_SPHERE
consts.doc: `SoftBody.shape`: a sphere of `radius` (an icosphere; 2D a ring).

consts.name: SOFT_BOX
consts.doc: `SoftBody.shape`: a box of `size` (each face a grid of `detail` + 1 cells; 2D a rectangle).

consts.name: SOFT_MESH
consts.doc: `SoftBody.shape`: the closed surface of geometry `mesh` (3D only).

functions.name: castRay
functions.doc: The nearest collider along a ray. Inside a system it sees the colliders as they were at the start of the tick (og.physics.queries records them before the game's systems); between ticks, as the world holds them.
functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null when nothing is hit; refused for a zero direction.

functions.name: castRayAll
functions.doc: Every collider along a ray within its reach, one hit each at its first crossing, nearest first (ties in collider entity order, so every host and run list them alike), at most `maxHits`: what a piercing shot passes through, everything under a cursor. The same view of the colliders as og.physics.castRay; its first hit is castRay's.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The ray, the filter and the cap.

functions.returnsDoc: The hits, nearest first; empty when nothing is hit; refused for a zero direction.

functions.name: projectPoint
functions.doc: The nearest point on any collider to a point, within maxDistance: snapping to a surface, the closest cover, whether a point is inside a solid. The same view of the colliders as og.physics.castRay.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The point, its reach, solid or surface, and the filter.

functions.returnsDoc: The projection, or null when no collider is within reach; refused for a point that is not finite.

functions.name: castShape
functions.doc: The first collider a shape meets when swept along a direction; the same view of the colliders as castRay.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its sweep and the filter.

functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null; refused for a zero direction or an unknown mesh.

functions.name: overlap
functions.doc: Every collider overlapping a shape, sorted by entity id; the same view of the colliders as castRay.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its placement and the filter.

functions.name: applyForce
functions.doc: Push a dynamic body with a force (N, world axes) over the next physics step, at a world point or its centre of mass: call it every tick for a steady force (thrust, wind, a car's downforce or an anti-roll assist). Applied by the og.physics step after the systems, in the order given, then gone; a hit stop drops it. Kinematic and static bodies ignore it. Pushes not yet applied are world state (in snapshots and the hash).

params.name: force
params.doc: The force in newtons (2D uses x and y).

params.name: point
params.doc: Where it acts, in world space; omitted is the centre of mass (no spin).

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or a force or point that is not finite.

functions.name: applyImpulse
functions.doc: Give a dynamic body an impulse (N·s, world axes) at a world point or its centre of mass: a sudden change of momentum (a kick, a hit, a jump: its velocity changes by impulse / mass), applied by the next physics step (after a hit stop ends). As applyForce otherwise.

params.name: impulse
params.doc: The impulse in newton-seconds (2D uses x and y).

params.name: point
params.doc: Where it acts, in world space; omitted is the centre of mass.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or an impulse or point that is not finite.

functions.name: applyTorque
functions.doc: Turn a dynamic body with a torque (N·m about each world axis; 2D uses z) over the next physics step, as applyForce: call it every tick for a steady twist.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or a torque that is not finite.

functions.name: applyTorqueImpulse
functions.doc: Give a dynamic body an angular impulse (N·m·s about each world axis; 2D uses z): its spin changes at once, as applyImpulse.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or a value that is not finite.

functions.name: setMesh
functions.doc: Register (or replace) the geometry a convex or triangle-mesh Collider names by its mesh handle. Loaded glTF geometries are registered under their own handles already; meshes are assets, not world state: world.snapshot carries a mesh, convex-hull or height-field collider by its handle and scale, not its triangles, and world.restore rebuilds the collider from the geometry registered then (so load or register it before restoring; a save naming one that is not is refused).

params.name: mesh
params.doc: The handle colliders name in Collider.mesh.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty, non-finite or out-of-range mesh.

functions.name: ropePoints
functions.doc: An og.Rope's points after the last step, from its entity to its end (empty before its first step). The engine draws visible ropes itself; this is for game logic and custom drawing.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Rope.

functions.name: garmentPoints
functions.doc: An og.Garment's points after the last step, in the world: one per position of the garment's mesh (vertices at the same position, split along a seam, share one), in the order the mesh first uses them.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Garment, or one not simulated yet (it needs og.Model, og.Skeleton and a loaded og.load.animation of the model).

functions.name: clothPoints
functions.doc: An og.Cloth's points after the last step, row by row (`columns` per row, rows downwards from the top edge).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Cloth.

functions.name: softBodyPoints
functions.doc: An og.SoftBody's points and the triangles of its surface after the last step (none before its first step). The engine draws visible soft bodies itself; this is for game logic (where it touches, how squashed it is) and custom drawing.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.SoftBody.

functions.name: fluidParticles
functions.doc: An og.Fluid2D's particle positions after the last step, in world space.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Fluid2D.

functions.name: fluid3dParticles
functions.doc: An og.Fluid3D's particle positions after the last step, in world space (emitted particles last, in the order they appeared).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Fluid3D.

functions.name: waterHeight
functions.doc: The surface height of an og.WaterSurface (world y) or an og.WaterLine (world y at `x`; `z` ignored) at a point, as the last step left it, plus an og.Water's sea (og.Water.wind) at this tick, the surface it draws: for boats that bob and spray that starts on the surface.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without water; outside the water, its rest level.

functions.name: vehicleWheels
functions.doc: An og.Vehicle's wheels after the last step (front left, front right, rear left, rear right; or its og.VehicleWheel children in entity order), for drawing wheel models.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without a vehicle.

functions.name: ragdollRigFromSkeleton
functions.doc: A ragdoll rig from a loaded skeleton (og.load.animation's `skeleton`): a bone per joint of its first skin, parents first, each from its joint's rest pose to its first child joint, every bone naming its joint and the rig naming the skeleton. Pass it to og.physics.setRagdollRig, edited or not.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a skeleton that is not loaded or has no skin.

functions.name: setRagdollRig
functions.doc: Give an entity with an og.Ragdoll its bones (and, from og.physics.ragdollRigFromSkeleton, the skeleton they stand for: its og.Model is then drawn blended from the animation towards the bones by og.Ragdoll.blend). While weight is 0 the bones follow the rig's rest pose at the entity. Rigs are assets, not world state: kept by the engine and given again to a reloaded world.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty rig or a parent that does not come before its child.

functions.name: ragdollPose
functions.doc: An og.Ragdoll's bones after the last step, in rig order (empty before its first step).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without a ragdoll.

functions.name: stats
functions.doc: What the last physics step cost: each phase's time and whether it ran on the lanes pool. All zero before the first step.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an engine without physics.

x-og-modules.name: atmosphere
x-og-modules.doc:
Fog, a procedural sky, the day-night cycle, weather, the wind that sways vegetation and water, declared as resources and components (the E5 round). Everything is off by default: a world that sets none of them draws exactly as before.
The day-night clock is a function of the tick (DayNight.start plus the simulated time times speed), so it is the same on every run and after a restore; rendering reads the world and never writes it.

consts.name: WEATHER_NONE
consts.doc: Weather.kind: clear.

consts.name: WEATHER_RAIN
consts.doc: Weather.kind: rain streaks falling with the wind, the light dimmed and a grey distance fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_SNOW
consts.doc: Weather.kind: flakes drifting down on gusts, a pale fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_DUST
consts.doc: Weather.kind: dust blowing along the wind near the ground, a warm thick fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_MIST
consts.doc: Weather.kind: no particles, a dense low height fog.

functions.name: timeOfDay
functions.doc: The DayNight clock at the current tick, in hours from 0 to 24 (its start when the cycle is off): for lamps that light at dusk and shops that close at night. Inside a system, declare og.DayNight among its reads.

x-og-modules.name: anim
x-og-modules.doc:
Skeletal animation over og-anim: glTF skins and clips (cooked into the `<model>#anim` blob, loaded with og.load.animation), blend-tree graphs with layered state machines, root motion, two-bone and FABRIK IK and blendshapes, evaluated by the engine's og.anim system after the game's systems and before physics.
Game code owns the components and sets players, graph parameters and IK targets; og.anim writes the pose (kept as world state in the `og.anim` state block, so snapshots, restore and the world hash cover it), the joint palette, root motion into og.Transform and the fields marked written. Asset handles are what og.load.animation and og.anim.graph answer; 0 is none.
Clips bind to a skeleton's nodes by name, so a clip of one rig plays on another with the same node names; a rig with other names or proportions plays it retargeted (og.anim.retarget at run time, or a model's `animation { library }` import setting at cook time). Assets are not world state: a hot reload registers them again.

functions.name: graph
functions.doc: Register a blend-tree graph for AnimationGraph.asset. Its `clip` lines are resolved by name against `clips`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the graph.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The text and the clips it may name.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a parse error (the reason names the line), a clip name `clips` lacks, or an invalid graph.

functions.name: humanoid
functions.doc: The standard humanoid bones of a skeleton, as retargeting sees them: to check a rig before retargeting onto it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeleton.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered skeleton or rig, or a rig naming a node the skeleton lacks.

functions.name: retarget
functions.doc: A new clip for `target` from a clip of `source`: each animated humanoid bone turns as the source's does from its rest pose (after a rest correction, so a T-pose drives an A-pose and other bone frames agree; fingers turn from their hand, so a hand pose holds whatever the arm does), the target keeps its bone lengths, the hips travel the source's distance scaled by the leg ratio (root motion kept, hip height scaled), and with footIk the feet land where the source's do, scaled, on the ground each rig's `footHeight` names (else its rest pose's foot heights). The target's twist bones (unmapped nodes named `twist`, or Rigify's `DEF-….001`, on an upper or lower arm or leg) take a share of their segment's twist by how far along it they sit. Same name, duration and markers. The cook does the same for a model's `animation { library }` import setting; this is for clips chosen at run time.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeletons and the clip.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The clip, the two skeletons and their rigs.

functions.returnsDoc: The new clip (what AnimationPlayer.clip takes). Refused for an unregistered clip, skeleton or rig, a skeleton without recognisable hips (name them in a `type rig` file), or a rig naming a missing node.

functions.name: mirror
functions.doc: A new clip that plays `clip` on the other side: every frame reflected in the skeleton's x = 0 plane, each node taking its counterpart's motion (a left swing becomes the right's), rotations moved in model space so left and right bone frames need not mirror each other, root motion's sideways travel and turns flipped. Assumes a symmetric rest pose; a sided node without a counterpart keeps its rest pose. Same name, duration and markers (markers keep their names). Mirroring twice gives the clip back. A clip known ahead needs no call: a graph's `clip` line with `mirror true` plays it mirrored, and the cook's `animation { mirror "<clip>" }` writes the mirrored clip into the model.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeleton and the clip.

functions.returnsDoc: The new clip (what AnimationPlayer.clip takes). Refused for an unregistered clip or skeleton.

functions.name: clip
functions.doc: The index of a flipbook clip by name, for Flipbook.clip: `og.anim.clip(hero, "walk_down")`. -1 when the sheet has no such clip.

functions.name: clip
functions.doc: A loaded model's clip by name, for AnimationPlayer.clip: `og.anim.clip(og.load.animation(world, "models/slime.glb").value, "chase")`, the same lookup as a flipbook's (Animation.clips by ClipInfo.name). A skinned glTF's clips are its animations' names; an animated `.vox`'s are `frames` or its `voxClip` names. 0 (plays nothing) when the model has no such clip.

functions.name: clip
functions.doc: The index of a 2D rig's clip by name, for Skeleton2D.clip: `og.anim.clip(og.load.rig2d(world, "rigs/hero.ogt").value, "walk")`. -1 when the rig has no such clip.

functions.name: rig2dInfo
functions.doc: What a loaded 2D rig holds: its bones, slots, IK constraints and clips, by the handle Skeleton2D.rig keeps (og.load.rig2d answers the same on load).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the rig.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a handle og.load.rig2d did not answer.

functions.name: skeleton2dBoxes
functions.doc: The bounding boxes an og.Skeleton2D's pose showed when og.skeleton2d last ran (after the game's systems, so a system reads the previous tick's): hurt and hit boxes a clip switches on and off with its slots' attachments, to test against points or other shapes. Empty for a rig without boxes or when no slot shows one. They are part of the og.skeleton2d state block, so a restored snapshot answers what it saved.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation poses the skeleton.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity og.skeleton2d has not posed: no og.Skeleton2D with a loaded rig, or before its first tick.

x-og-modules.name: tween
x-og-modules.doc:
Tweens: animate any numeric field of a component (og.Transform.position, og.Sprite.color, og.Sprite.opacity, a game's own f32) from its value to a target over time with an easing curve, a delay, repeat and yoyo; chain them in sequences or run them in parallel. Advanced by the engine's og.tween system after the game's systems and before og.anim and physics, by scaled time (slow motion, hit stop) unless unscaled.
Running tweens are world state (the og.tween state block): snapshots, restore and the world hash cover them. og.TweenCompleted reports a tween or group that ends on its own; a cancelled one, or one whose entity or component went away, ends silently.
Feel presets are tweens too: og.tween.squash (squash and stretch that recovers) and og.tween.flash (a hit flash that fades).
Timelines are GSAP's: `const tl = og.tween.timeline(world, { defaults: { duration: 0.4, ease: "back.out" }, repeat: 1, yoyo: true })`, then `tl.to(enemies, { field: "position.y", to: 2, stagger: { each: 0.05, from: "center" } }).to(door, { field: "position.x", to: 3 }, "<0.1").call("door.open").addLabel("out", "+=0.5")`. Targets are entities and one numeric field per call (`field` and `to`, as og.tween.to), not JavaScript objects; vectors take one value per lane. Position is GSAP's: seconds, `"<"` (the start of what was added last), `">"` (its end), `"+=1"` and `"-=0.5"` (from the timeline's end), a label, `"label+=0.2"`, `"<50%"` (half way through what was added last) and `"-=25%"` (a quarter of what is inserted); none appends at the end. A label a position names that does not exist is added at the end.
A timeline renders from its playhead, never accumulated: play, pause, reverse, seek, progress and timeScale move it, and what they change is written in the next og.tween run (this tick, from a system before it). A child is written only when its own time changes, so a finished tween leaves its field to the game. from and fromTo write their start values on the timeline's first render, before their time (GSAP's immediateRender). A timeline stays when it completes (og.TweenCompleted is sent), so it can be reversed, restarted or extended, until kill() or `autoKill`. A refused call (a dead entity, a field that is not numeric, bad position text) adds nothing and its reason is the timeline's `error`; the call still answers the timeline, so chains read as GSAP's.
Callbacks are names, not closures: `onStart`, `onUpdate`, `onComplete` and `onRepeat` on a tween or the timeline, and `.call(name)`, send og.TweenEvent with that name, read by a system in the tick after. A seek or progress jump sends none. Timelines are world state: snapshots and restore cover the whole timeline, its playhead, labels and captured values, and a `random` stagger shuffles from the world's og.Rng seed (a fork: the main stream does not move; a system needs og.Rng among its reads).

functions.name: to
functions.doc: Start a tween. Systems may call it; it first moves in this tick's og.tween run.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The field, the values and the timing.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity, a component it lacks, a field that is not numeric, or values of the wrong length.

functions.name: from
functions.doc: Animate from desc.from to the field's value captured at this call, before the delay. The first og.tween tick writes from and holds it through the delay. Unlike GSAP immediateRender, the call itself never writes the field. A system must declare read access to the target component for capture. Snapshot/restore retains the captured endpoint; later writes during the delay cannot change it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unreadable target or invalid values.

functions.name: fromTo
functions.doc: Animate from explicit desc.from to desc.to; both are required. The first og.tween tick writes from, including during the delay. No endpoint is captured from the live field.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The explicit start, end and timing.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when from is missing or the target or values are invalid.

functions.name: sequence
functions.doc: Start tweens one after another (each with its own delay, duration and repeat); the time one leaves over goes to the next.

functions.name: parallel
functions.doc: Start tweens together; the group ends with the last one.

functions.name: timeline
functions.doc: A GSAP timeline: tweens, calls, labels and nested timelines placed on its own clock, played, paused, reversed and sought as one. It starts playing in this tick's og.tween run unless paused.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused settings are reported in its `error`; it still answers the timeline.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Stop a tween where it is (no event).
functions.returnsDoc: False when it was not running.

functions.name: cancelEntity
functions.doc: Stop every tween of an entity (no events), say before starting a new reaction. A timeline drops its tweens of the entity and plays on.
functions.returnsDoc: How many stopped.

functions.name: active
functions.doc: Whether a tween is still running.

functions.name: squash
functions.doc: Squash and stretch the entity's og.Transform.scale (cancels its earlier squash).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.Transform.

functions.name: flash
functions.doc: Flash the entity's og.Sprite, its og.Mesh, or its og.Model (a glTF instance: this instance only, the others sharing its materials stay as they are). Cancels its earlier flash.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity with none of og.Sprite, og.Mesh and og.Model.

interfaces.name: TweenTimeline
interfaces.doc: A GSAP timeline (og.tween.timeline): build it with to, from, fromTo, set, call, addLabel and add, each placed by a position and answering the timeline so calls chain; control it with play, pause, reverse, seek, progress, timeScale and kill.

members.name: tween
members.doc: Its handle: og.TweenCompleted and og.TweenEvent carry it, og.tween.cancel and active take it.

members.name: error
members.doc: Why the last refused call added nothing; null when none was refused.

members.name: to
members.doc: Tween a field of every target to `vars.to` (or through `vars.keyframes`), from its value when the tween starts.

params.name: targets
params.doc: An entity or several (staggered by vars.stagger).

params.name: vars
params.doc: The field, the values and the timing.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where: seconds or GSAP's position text; null appends.

members.name: from
members.doc: Tween from `vars.from` to each target's value at this call (read now: a system needs read access to the component). The start value is written on the timeline's first render.

params.name: vars
params.doc: The field, the start value and the timing.

members.name: fromTo
members.doc: Tween from `vars.from` to `vars.to`; both are required. The start value is written on the timeline's first render.

params.name: vars
params.doc: The field, both values and the timing.

members.name: set
members.doc: Set a field of every target to `vars.to` when the playhead reaches the position (a tween of no duration; going back before it restores the value it found).

members.name: call
members.doc: Send og.TweenEvent `name` when the playhead crosses the position, forwards or backwards (GSAP's call, named instead of a function).

members.name: addLabel
members.doc: Name a time, for positions (`"label"`, `"label+=0.5"`) and seek.

members.name: add
members.doc: Nest a running tween, sequence, parallel group or timeline (its `tween` handle) at the position: it stops running on its own and plays as part of this one. A string adds a label.

params.name: child
params.doc: The handle to nest, or a label.

members.name: play
members.doc: Play forwards, from a time or label when given.

members.name: pause
members.doc: Hold the playhead, at a time or label when given.

members.name: resume
members.doc: Play on in the direction it had.

members.name: reverse
members.doc: Play backwards towards the start, from a time or label when given.

members.name: restart
members.doc: Play forwards from the start (callbacks fire again).

members.name: seek
members.doc: Jump the playhead to a time or label without sending callbacks; it keeps playing or holding.

members.name: progress
members.doc: How far through its cycle the playhead is, 0 to 1; given a value, jumps there first (without callbacks).

members.name: time
members.doc: The playhead's time within its cycle, in seconds.

members.name: duration
members.doc: One cycle, in seconds: where its last child ends.

members.name: timeScale
members.doc: The playback rate; given a value, sets it first (2 twice as fast, 0 holds).

members.name: isActive
members.doc: Whether it is running and not paused.

members.name: kill
members.doc: Stop and remove it where it is (no events); its fields keep their values.

x-og-modules.name: tilemap
x-og-modules.doc:
Tilemaps: layers of tiles from a tileset atlas (an `.ogt` of `type tileset`: grid, solid tiles and collision rects, animated tiles, 47-blob and 16-bitmask auto-tiling terrains), loaded from a cooked map (a hand-written `.ogt` of `type tilemap`, a Tiled `.tmj` or an LDtk `.ldtk`) with og.load.tilemap and placed by an og.Tilemap component.
Layers draw through the sprite batch in 16x16-tile chunks culled to the view, each at the map's sprite layer plus its z, scrolled by its parallax; solid tiles become static og-physics colliders merged into rectangles. Runtime edits (og.tilemap.setTile, re-auto-tiling the neighbourhood) are world state (the og.tilemap state block), and the colliders follow them.
With og.Lighting2D enabled, a layer whose sprite layer (the map's layer plus its z) lies in minLayer to maxLayer is lit as the sprites there are: multiplied by the ambient plus every Light2D reaching it, with the shadows of Occluder2Ds and castShadow sprites, so a dark cave lit by torches is the map, its lights and its occluders. A layer that should stay as authored in the lit range (a sky, a far parallax backdrop) opts out: a bool custom property `lit` set to false on the Tiled layer, or a `lit false` line in a tilemap `.ogt`'s layer block (TileLayerInfo.lit reports it).
Cells count from the top-left corner, x right and y down (Tiled's); the map's top-left corner is at the entity's position.
Orientations: a map is orthogonal, isometric (diamonds on a turned grid), staggered (diamonds in rows) or hexagonal (pointy- or flat-top), from its `orientation` line or its Tiled map. cellAt, cellCenter and neighbours follow it; an isometric or staggered tile's image stands up from its cell's bottom (taller tiles overlap the ones behind, drawn back to front); solid tiles off the orthogonal grid collide as one collider per connected solid region, its outline (a hollow polyline in 2D, a prism in 3D; a layer's cellColliders makes it one diamond or hexagon per cell). Building them is one-time per map edit or resize; in 3D a non-orthogonal map's prisms build in about 75 ms per 400,000 triangles (a 256 × 256 hex map, half solid at random, release), so keep large 3D hex and iso collision layers in large solid regions, or edit them rarely. Stepping costs per region, not per cell. Terrain layers need a square grid (orthogonal or isometric).
Run-time maps: og.tilemap.create makes a map from a desc and og.tilemap.resize changes a map's size, both in game code. A map made or resized is world state: the og.tilemap state block saves it whole (its tilesets by asset id), so a save restores it in a session that never made it.

functions.name: setTile
functions.doc: Change a cell. It applies at once to getTile, and to drawing and colliders at the og.tilemap system (this tick when called before it). Deterministic: equal edits in equal order give equal maps.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The map, the layer, the cell and the tile.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity whose map is not adopted yet, an unknown layer, a cell outside the map or a tile the tileset lacks.

functions.name: fill
functions.doc: Write a block of cells, as setTile on each (row by row) but re-tiling a terrain layer and rebuilding the colliders once. Cells past the map's edge are skipped.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The map, the layer, where and the cells.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity whose map is not adopted yet, an unknown layer, a width of 0 or not dividing the cells, or a tile the tileset lacks (nothing is written then).

functions.name: create
functions.doc: Make an empty map in game code: draw it and edit it as a loaded one (an og.Tilemap with its `map`, then setTile and fill). Its handle comes from the world's own counter, so equal calls in equal order give equal handles, in a replay and after a restore. A world that makes none saves and hashes as before.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its size, tiles, orientation, tilesets and layers.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a size of 0 or past 16,777,216 cells, a tileset the bundle lacks, a layer naming a tileset index or terrain that does not exist, two layers of one name, or a terrain layer on a staggered or hex map.

functions.name: resize
functions.doc: Change a map's size (a loaded one too: from then on it is a run-time map, saved whole). Every og.Tilemap showing it keeps its edits, moved with the cells by (x, y); cells past the new edges are dropped, new ones are empty, terrain re-tiles, colliders rebuild at the og.tilemap system and its objects (TilemapInfo.objects) move with the cells.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The map, its new size and the shift.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown map, a size of 0 or past 16,777,216 cells, or an odd shift along a staggered or hex map's shifted axis (it would change which rows are shifted).

functions.name: neighbours
functions.doc: The cells next to a cell, clockwise from the top (or the top right): 4 on an orthogonal or isometric grid (the sides), 4 on a staggered one (the diagonal sides), 6 on a hex one; cells off the map are left out.

functions.name: getTile
functions.doc: A cell's tile id, -1 when empty: on a terrain layer the tile auto-tiling resolved from the neighbours (setTile writes 1 or 0 there; the id changes with them). -1 outside the map or before the map is adopted.

functions.name: cellAt
functions.doc: The cell under a world point (its xy), for a map at its entity's position.

functions.name: cellCenter
functions.doc: A cell's centre in world coordinates (z of the map).

x-og-modules.name: audio
x-og-modules.doc:
Sound: inside the tick, the engine's og.audio system (after the game's systems and physics) turns AudioSource changes into a deterministic, time-stamped command stream; outside the tick the host's mixer renders it (an AudioWorklet on the web, the output device, a capture or a null sink natively).
The stream, not the PCM, is world state: snapshots, restore and the world hash cover it, and nothing a sink does reaches the world. Load sounds with og.load.sound; inserting a source plays it, setting `playing` false stops it, and a one-shot sets `playing` back to false when it ends.
Spatial gain and pan are computed in the tick from the source's world transform relative to the first AudioListener's (three.js convention: the listener looks down -Z, +X is right; with none, the origin looking down -Z). A source, listener or zone on a child entity is placed at its og.Transform composed down og.Parent, as og.MatrixWorld is: a sound on a child is heard where its parent carries it, a listener under a camera rig hears from the rig.
Propagation, all in the tick and so in the stream: a spatial source or listener that moves shifts the pitch (Doppler, from their tick velocities: AudioSource.dopplerFactor, AudioListener.dopplerFactor, Audio.speedOfSound), a source with a cone is turned down away from its +Z (coneInnerAngle, coneOuterAngle, coneOuterGain, as three.js's setDirectionalCone), and a listener whose panningModel is hrtf places sources for headphones (interaural delay and head shadow) instead of the stereo panner.

consts.name: SOUND_FINISHED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: a one-shot played to its end.

consts.name: SOUND_STOPPED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: `playing` was set to false.

consts.name: SOUND_REMOVED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: the AudioSource was removed from a living entity.

consts.name: SOUND_REPLACED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: `sound` changed while it played.

consts.name: SOUND_CULLED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: more sources played than Audio.maxVoices and this one stood lowest (priority, then volume, then age).

consts.name: SOUND_RETRIGGERED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: AudioSource.retrigger started the sound again from the top; a new voice plays it.

functions.name: playFeedback
functions.doc: Play a presentation-only one-shot on the UI bus in this tick (the next tick when called between ticks). Creates no world entity or event, changes no simulation hash, and is not saved or replayed on restore. Silently unheard when no audio sink is attached. Use AudioSource for gameplay audio.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose presentation audio sink plays it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unloaded sound or invalid volume/playbackRate.

functions.name: createSound
functions.doc: Make a sound from PCM the game computed: it plays, loops and pitches as a loaded one (AudioSource.sound, AudioEvent.sounds), always resident, stored as 16-bit PCM, and og.load.soundInfo reports it. Between ticks or inside a system alike; the handle is the next one the bank gives, so a game that makes its sounds in the same order on every launch (in GameDesc.start) names the same handles in its saves.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the sound.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for no samples, a length that is not whole frames, a rate or channel count out of range, or a number that is not finite.

functions.name: outputLatency
functions.doc:
How long after its world time a sample leaves the speaker, as the host reports it: on the web the AudioContext's baseLatency and outputLatency and the worklet ring's buffer, natively the device's latency (cpal's playback less callback instant) and the mixer's buffer; 0 headless (the null and capture sinks are driven to the tick). Host input, written to og.Audio between ticks, so a replay carries it. A rhythm game hears a note at its time plus this: judge a press against the note's time plus the latency, then a calibrated rest (the display, the hand).
Inside a system og.Audio must be among its reads or writes.
functions.returnsDoc: Seconds; 0 headless.

x-og-modules.name: nav
x-og-modules.doc:
Navigation: grids (A* and jump point search with eight-way moves that never cut a blocked corner, line-of-sight smoothing), flow fields for crowds, and navmeshes (baked at cook time from a level's static colliders and models, or built at runtime for a flat procedural level) with funnel paths and box obstacles that rebuild only the tiles they touch.
Agents are entities with an og.NavAgent (and an og.Transform): the og.nav system, after the game's systems and before physics, plans their paths, follows them and adds the og.Steering behaviours; an entity with an og.Velocity (a physics body) gets its velocity written, any other its Transform moved. Everything is deterministic and in snapshots: paths, grid edits, obstacles and flow targets.
Agents move on the profile's plane: x and y in 2D (a grid's rows run up), x and z in 3D (y kept on grids, from the surface on a navmesh).

consts.name: NAV_IDLE
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: not seeking.

consts.name: NAV_MOVING
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: following a path or a flow field.

consts.name: NAV_ARRIVED
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: within stopDistance of the target.

consts.name: NAV_UNREACHABLE
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: no path reaches the target, or the agent is off its grid or navmesh.

consts.name: NAV_PARTIAL
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: the target is cut off; moving to the reachable point nearest it.

consts.name: NAV_ON_LINK
consts.doc: NavAgent.status: crossing an off-mesh link (a jump, a ladder, a door, a teleport).

functions.name: grid
functions.doc: A grid agents and path queries plan on. Runtime edits (og.nav.setCost) are world state.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its size, cell size, origin and costs.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for costs of the wrong length.

functions.name: gridFromTilemap
functions.doc: A grid over a placed map: its cells, its world position (the map's top-left corner at the entity), blocked where the collision layers have solid tiles. Edits to the map later do not follow; build another.

params.name: desc
