params.doc: The map's entity and the blocking layers.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Tilemap or a map not loaded.

functions.name: setCost
functions.doc: Change a grid cell's cost (0 blocks it): agents on the grid re-plan, flow fields over it rebuild.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown grid or a cell outside it.

functions.name: cellAt
functions.doc: The grid cell under a world point.

functions.name: findPath
functions.doc: A path between two points on a grid or a navmesh, now: corners, length and whether it reaches the end.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The grid or navmesh and the two points.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown grid or navmesh, or when no path starts (an end off the grid or mesh).

functions.name: flowField
functions.doc: A flow field towards targets over a grid: one Dijkstra pass gives every cell a direction, so any number of agents (NavAgent.nav = the field) steer by a lookup. It rebuilds when the grid changes.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown grid.

functions.name: setFlowTargets
functions.doc: Move a flow field's targets (rebuilds it).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown flow field.

functions.name: flowAt
functions.doc: The direction a flow field gives at a point (unit length, or zero at a target or where nothing is reachable).

functions.name: load
functions.doc: A cooked navmesh: an `.ogt` of `type navmesh` (the agent, the cell sizes, the bounds and the geometry: a scene's static colliders and models, glTF models, terrains, boxes) baked by og cook.

params.name: profile
params.doc: The agent profile, an `agent <name>` block's name: one mesh per body size (a rat under the table, an ogre round it). Omitted: the asset's first agent block (its unnamed one, if any).

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked navmesh, or a profile it has no agent block for (naming the ones it has).

functions.name: build
functions.doc: A navmesh over a flat floor with boxes carved out, built now: for procedural levels (a level with slopes and stairs is baked at cook time with og.nav.load).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The floor, the boxes and the agent.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty floor.

functions.name: setObstacle
functions.doc: Set, move or (with no box) remove an obstacle on a navmesh: the spans under the box (grown by the agent radius) are blocked and only the tiles it touches, and their neighbours, are rebuilt. Agents on the mesh re-plan. World state.

params.name: id
params.doc: The obstacle's id, the game's own (a door's number).

params.name: obstacle
params.doc: The box; omitted removes the obstacle.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown navmesh.

functions.name: carve
functions.doc: og.nav.setObstacle for any shape: a turned box (a door ajar, a fallen log), a cylinder (a pillar, a barrel) or a convex prism. The cells whose centres the shape covers, grown by the agent radius, are blocked and only the tiles it touches, and their neighbours, are rebuilt. Shares og.nav.setObstacle's ids. World state.

params.name: shape
params.doc: The shape; omitted removes the obstacle.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown navmesh or a convex shape of fewer than three points.

functions.name: setArea
functions.doc: Set, move or (with no desc) remove a run-time area on a navmesh (water, mud, a road): its tiles rebuild so no polygon mixes areas, and agents re-plan, weighing it by their og.NavFilter. World state.

params.name: id
params.doc: The area's id, the game's own.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape and the area; omitted removes it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown navmesh or an area past 63.

functions.name: setLink
functions.doc: Set, move or (with no desc) remove an off-mesh link on a navmesh. Paths cross it where it is cheaper than walking; an agent that reaches its start crosses it (NAV_ON_LINK, og.NavLinkReached) and lands at its end. Links baked in the navmesh asset (`link` lines) have the ids they were given. World state.

params.name: id
params.doc: The link's id, the game's own.

functions.returnsDoc: Whether both ends are on the mesh (a link with an end off it is kept but never crossed). Refused for an unknown navmesh.

functions.name: setLinkOpen
functions.doc: Open or close an off-mesh link (a door): a closed one is never planned across, and agents on the mesh re-plan. World state.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown navmesh or link.

functions.name: finishLink
functions.doc: End a crossing the game moves (NavLinkDesc.game): the agent lands at the link's end as og.nav next runs and goes on along its path.
functions.returnsDoc: False when it is not crossing such a link.

functions.name: nearest
functions.doc: The point on a navmesh nearest a world point, within `extent` (half sizes).

params.name: extent
params.doc: The search box's half sizes; zero: 2 2 2.

functions.returnsDoc: Null when no polygon is within the box.

functions.name: pathOf
functions.doc: The path an agent follows now (its corners from where it planned), for debugging and playtests; `dump_nav:<entity>` writes the same.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for an entity that has not planned.

x-og-modules.name: ai
x-og-modules.doc:
Enemy and NPC AI as data: behaviour trees and state machines in `.ogt` files of `type behaviour`, perception (sight cones checked against physics occlusion, hearing of spatial sounds and game noises) and a blackboard per agent.
BehaviourTree.CPP control names: ReactiveFallback rechecks priority from the first child each think; ReactiveSequence rechecks conditions from the first child; Sequence resumes its running child but restarts after failure or completion (not SequenceWithMemory). A higher-priority branch halts the lower running branch and resets its sequence cursor; game actions receive AI_INTERRUPTED. Inverter flips success/failure, ForceSuccess converts either to success; both preserve running. Command cooldowns remain explicit engine state.
A machine uses entry and exit action blocks. It is a tick machine, not an XState statechart: at most one transition per think, exit then entry (also on a self-transition), then the destination body. Initial entry runs once; snapshot restore preserves it. There are no queued events, parallel states or actors.
An entity with an og.AiAgent (and an og.Transform) thinks in the og.ai system before the game's systems: perception first, then its tree or machine, whose running action moves it through its og.NavAgent (og.nav plans and walks after the game's systems) or runs one of the game's commands (GameDesc.commands, with the agent's entity handle as its first argument) before the next tick.
Conditions read blackboard keys (declared, set by actions or og.ai.set, or built in: self, position, sees, heard, target, targetPosition, targetDistance, lastSeen, sinceSeen, heardAt, sinceHeard, elapsed), the agent's component fields (`Health.hp`) and resource fields (`Game.alarm`), and compare them with a literal or with another key or field read each time (`check Foe.hp below Tuning.fleeHp`), so thresholds live in a tuning resource. og.ai.restart starts a behaviour afresh. Deterministic; memories and blackboards are in snapshots. `dump_ai:<entity>` writes an agent's state, running node and blackboard.

consts.name: AI_RUNNING
consts.doc: AiAgent.status: the tree or state is still running.

consts.name: AI_SUCCESS
consts.doc: AiAgent.status: the tree succeeded on the last think.

consts.name: AI_FAILURE
consts.doc: AiAgent.status: the tree failed on the last think.

consts.name: AI_INTERRUPTED
consts.doc: AiActionStopped.result: the action stopped before the game finished it (another branch won, the state changed, the agent restarted).

functions.name: load
functions.doc: A cooked behaviour (an `.ogt` of `type behaviour`, validated by og cook); its `use` subtrees are read from their own cooked assets.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked behaviour.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: A behaviour from text, now (tests and generated behaviours; assets go through og cook). Its `use` subtrees are read from cooked assets.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused with the first error's line and the fix.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A blackboard value of an agent as of its last think.
functions.returnsDoc: A number, a boolean, a point `{x, y, z}`, an entity handle, or null for an unknown key or an agent that has not thought.

functions.name: set
functions.doc: Set a blackboard value of an agent: a number, a boolean, a point `{x, y, z}` or an entity handle `{entity}`.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key; built-in keys are refused.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an agent that has not thought yet, a built-in key or another kind of value.

functions.name: restart
functions.doc: Start an agent's behaviour afresh at its next think, as a new behaviour would: a machine in its initial state (its entry actions run again), a tree at its root, every timer and cooldown reset, the blackboard back to the declared keys, wander's centre where it then stands, and what it saw and heard forgotten. Actions without a speed keep the speed it first started with. For a new run or a respawn; an agent that has not thought yet starts afresh anyway.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world without og.ai.

functions.name: finish
functions.doc: End an agent's running game actions (og.AiActionStarted): each answers success or failure at the agent's next think and sends og.AiActionStopped. With `action`, only the running ones of that name. World state, in saves.

params.name: success
params.doc: Whether it worked: the node succeeds, or fails.

params.name: action
params.doc: The action's name; omitted: every game action it runs.

functions.returnsDoc: False when it runs no such action.

functions.name: noise
functions.doc: Make a noise agents may hear next tick (a gunshot, a door, a thrown stone).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world without og.ai.

functions.name: describe
functions.doc: What an agent is doing: its state, the node it runs and the path to it, its status, its blackboard and its target.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for an entity that has not thought.

x-og-modules.name: story
x-og-modules.doc:
Dialogue uses released Yarn Spinner 3.2.2 in `.yarn` files, compiled to engine-owned IR by og cook. Declare `#og-profile:yarn-spinner-3.2.2`; see the yarn guide for the language and engine extensions. Every line and option requires an explicit stable `#line:` id. Base text enters the string catalog under that id; og.story resolves through og.i18n on every read, so switching locale re-translates the current line and choices. Quests remain `type quest` data, with stages, reflected event objectives and rewards.
og.story.load a dialogue or quest in setup, og.story.start a conversation, read og.story.view each frame, and call og.story.advance or og.story.choose. Dialogue text retains its Speaker: prefix and carries typed TextSpan attributes in Unicode scalar offsets. Quests start with `<<quest start rescue>>` or og.story.startQuest, count with og.story.progress and advance stages themselves; og.story.quests lists them for a quest log.
Barks use Yarn nodes with `og-topic`, `og-when`, `og-priority`, `og-weight`, `og-cooldown`, `og-shared` and `og-once` headers. The engine scheduler still owns priority, cooldowns and once state. og.story.bark asks for one, og.story.ambient asks periodically, and og.story.barks lists those being said. A line's `#voice:` plays through og.audio. Quest objectives with `on Event` and `where` count reflected events without moving quest data into Yarn.
Saves checkpoint stable continuation, node, line and option ids, detour stacks, timers, variables and the story RNG fork. They never store bytecode offsets. Inserting or moving unrelated lines preserves the current line. A missing saved continuation is an error, never a restart that could repeat a command or reward. `=>` line groups prefer eligible conditional lines over unconditional fallbacks and draw ties by weight; line groups, barks and active checks use og.Rng's story fork on both hosts. Timers count ticks. Worlds without loaded stories keep their existing saves and hash.

functions.name: setSaliency
functions.doc: Select this world's Yarn content strategy after loading its story. The strategy and view counts are saved with the story.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused before a story is loaded or for an unknown strategy.

functions.name: load
functions.doc: A cooked `.yarn` dialogue or `type quest` asset. Loading again replaces it; stable ids preserve the conversation at its next step. The first load registers og.Story and its events, so call it in setup: inside a system it is refused until one load has run outside one.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked dialogue or quest.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: A dialogue or quest from text, now (tests and generated content; assets go through og cook). Registers og.Story as load does.

params.name: text
params.doc: Yarn text with its profile and name tags, or a `type quest` .ogt.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused with the first error's line and the fix.

functions.name: start
functions.doc: Start a conversation: it runs to its first line (or its choices) now, and og.DialogueShown is sent the next tick. Several may run at once.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The dialogue, and optionally the node, cast and starting variables.

functions.returnsDoc: The conversation, or why not: an unloaded dialogue, an unknown node, speaker or variable.

functions.name: view
functions.doc: The current dialogue line and choices, with text and markup spans resolved in the active locale.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for a conversation that does not exist (never started, or stopped).

functions.name: history
functions.doc: A conversation's lines so far, oldest first, with the choice made on each (a VN backlog).
functions.returnsDoc: Empty for an unknown conversation.

functions.name: conversations
functions.doc: The conversations that exist (started and not stopped), oldest first.

functions.name: advance
functions.doc: Move a conversation past its line: it runs to the next line, its choices or its end.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused while it waits on choices, after it ended, or for an unknown conversation.

functions.name: choose
functions.doc: Take a choice: an active check rolls (og.DialogueCheck), then its indented Yarn body runs, or #fail redirects a missed roll. A settled choice is not executed again on restore.

params.name: index
params.doc: ChoiceView.index, or 4294967295 for Yarn NoOptionSelected: continue past the option group without selecting an option.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a hidden or disabled choice, a conversation showing a line, or an unknown one.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: End a conversation now (og.DialogueEnded if it was running) and forget it. An ended conversation stays viewable until it is stopped.
functions.returnsDoc: False for an unknown conversation.

functions.name: bark
functions.doc: Ask an entity to bark a line of a topic: at the og.story system's next run, of that topic's barks whose `when` holds (it may read the world: `self.Health.hp`, `Game.alarm`) and whose cooldowns are over, the highest priority is said, ties drawn by weight on the story's stream; og.BarkSaid follows. Nothing is said when none qualifies, or the entity is saying a bark of equal or higher priority.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a topic no loaded dialogue has.

functions.name: ambient
functions.doc: Let an entity bark a topic on its own, every `every` ticks (and up to `jitter` more), as og.story.bark would; `every` 0 stops it. In saves; a despawned entity stops.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Who, which topic and how often.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a topic no loaded dialogue has.

functions.name: barks
functions.doc: The barks being said, by entity: draw each over its entity (a speech bubble) until it ends.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A story variable (a `global` of any loaded dialogue or quest): its value, else its declared default.
functions.returnsDoc: A number, a boolean, a string, or null for one nothing declares.

functions.name: set
functions.doc: Set a story variable; quests whose conditions now hold advance.

params.name: value
params.doc: A number, a boolean or a string.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for another kind of value or a world without a loaded story.

functions.name: reset
functions.doc: A new playthrough: the story's variables, seen nodes, conversations and quests are cleared. Lines read stay read (DialogueView.seen), so a second playthrough can skip them.

functions.name: startQuest
functions.doc: Start a loaded quest at its first stage.
functions.returnsDoc: False when it had started before. Refused for a quest not loaded.

functions.name: progress
functions.doc: Count toward an objective of an active quest's current stage (a wolf killed, a herb picked); the stage advances when its objectives are done.
functions.returnsDoc: False when the quest is not active or its stage has no such objective.

functions.name: setStage
functions.doc: Move an active quest to a stage, its counts cleared.
functions.returnsDoc: False when it is not active or already there. Refused for an unknown quest or stage.

functions.name: completeQuest
functions.doc: Complete an active quest now.
functions.returnsDoc: False when it is not active. Refused for a quest not loaded.

functions.name: failQuest
functions.doc: Fail an active quest now: its undone objectives are marked failed.
functions.returnsDoc: False when it is not active. Refused for a quest not loaded.

functions.name: quest
functions.doc: A started quest as the log shows it.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for a quest not started.

functions.name: quests
functions.doc: Every started quest, in the order they started (a quest log).

functions.name: track
functions.doc: Show a quest in the HUD tracker, or stop showing it.
functions.returnsDoc: False for a quest not started.

functions.name: markSeen
functions.doc: The player looked at a quest: clear QuestView.isNew and updated.
functions.returnsDoc: False for a quest not started.

functions.name: mark
functions.doc: Point a quest at an entity or a point (the map, compass and tracker read QuestView.marker), over its objectives' own markers.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The entity or point; both zero clears it.

functions.returnsDoc: False for a quest not started.

x-og-modules.name: platform
x-og-modules.doc:
Platform services as host capabilities (docs/design.md §2.8): cloud store, leaderboards, telemetry, Origin Point and AI marks. Game code names a method and its arguments, never a credential, a URL or a cookie: the host owns them. On the web the shell forwards each call to the Player through origin-checked postMessage (Player protocol 2, docs/web-export.md); natively the host answers from a local JSON store (`og run --platform-store`, default `<project>/.og/platform.json`).
Calls are asynchronous: each returns a request number at once, and the answer arrives at the start of a later tick, when og.platform sends PlatformAnswered; read it with og.platform.result. Answers are host input, like key presses: the probe's `dump_platform` lists every call, its arguments, its answer and the ticks.
Errors carry the Player's stable codes: offline, timeout, invalid, unauthorized, not_found, conflict, too_large, rate_limited, unavailable, failed, cancelled (the player backed out of a purchase, an ad or a share sheet) and no_fill (no ad to show now); retryable is true for offline, timeout, unavailable, rate_limited and no_fill.
Purchases, ads, achievements, the player, friends, invites and share (products, purchase, showAd, achievementUnlock, player, friends, inviteSend, share, ...) are the platform's: accounts and money never enter the engine. Each call is a method name and its arguments, the host attaches the player's game-scoped credential, and every id it hands back (the player, a friend, a purchase, an invite) is opaque and scoped to this game. A host that lacks one answers it `unavailable`: ask og.platform.supports first. Natively and in playtests a deterministic fake answers them (`og run --platform-fake`, PlaytestDesc.platform); a published page never fakes them. Entitlements are always the host's answer, never the engine's log or a save: ask og.platform.entitlements when the game starts, and grant a consumable once per purchase with og.platform.grant.
Unasked host input (a pending purchase settled, a refund, an entitlement changed on another device, an invite arrived) is a notice: og.PlatformNotice at the start of a tick, read with og.platform.notice, logged with the answers. In a running lockstep or rollback session (og.Lockstep) a platform answer or notice is this peer's alone: a system that reads og.PlatformAnswered or og.PlatformNotice, or calls og.platform.result or og.platform.notice, while it writes shared state (anything but the session's own records: input, audio, camera, og.Lockstep) hears nothing and reads null, and the engine logs it once; carry what every peer must see in og.PlayerInput (og.net.submit).
Rooms (roomCreate, roomJoin, roomSend, ...) put this engine with other players' engines: the host carries them (natively `og relay` with `og run --room`, on the web the platform's rooms through the shell, docs/platform-asks.md) and its answers and the other peers' messages arrive as events at the start of a tick (og.RoomJoined, og.RoomPeerJoined, og.RoomPeerLeft, og.RoomMessage), host input like key presses. Deterministic play over a room is og.net's lockstep.

functions.name: storeGet
functions.doc: Read one key of the player's store for this game.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed key. The answer's data is `{ key, value, revision }` (value null and revision 0 for a key never written).

functions.name: storeSet
functions.doc: Write one key of the player's store for this game; with a revision, only if nobody wrote it since (another device, another tab).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The key, the value and the revision it must be at.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed key or a value over 64 KiB. The answer's data is `{ key, revision }` (the new revision); `conflict` when the key moved past desc.revision.

functions.name: storeList
functions.doc: The keys of the player's store and their revisions.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ keys: [{ key, revision }] }`.

functions.name: leaderboardSubmit
functions.doc: Submit a score; the board keeps the player's best.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The board, the score and its order.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a score that is not finite. The answer's data is `{ board, rank, best }`, or `{ board, rank: null, queued: true }` while offline.

functions.name: leaderboardTop
functions.doc: The best entries of a board, and the player's own.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ board, order, entries: [{ rank, name, score, me }], me }`.

functions.name: leaderboardAround
functions.doc: The entries around the player's rank.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The board and how many around the player.

functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is the leaderboardTop shape with the entries around the player's rank.

functions.name: telemetry
functions.doc: Record a game event for the game's analytics.

params.name: name
params.doc: The event: `level.started`, `level.completed`, `boss.defeated` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`; the Player files it as `game.custom.<name>`).

params.name: attrs
params.doc: Its attributes: an object of at most 16 strings (up to 512 characters), numbers, booleans or null, keys a lowercase letter then letters, digits and `_`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed name or attributes. Fire and forget: nothing answers.

functions.name: point
functions.doc: Ask for Origin Point for something the player did.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a reason outside 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. The answer's data is `{ granted, balance }`; under a Player today always `{ granted: 0, balance: null }` (the platform grants nothing until a release carries an approved point policy), locally the amount asked.

functions.name: aiMark
functions.doc: Disclose AI-generated content the game shows.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty kind or label. The answer's data is `{ marked: true }`.

functions.name: loadSettings
functions.doc: Ask for the game's saved settings (volume, controls, language): store.get of the key `og.settings`. Where the Player has no store, or is offline, the shell answers from the browser's own storage; natively, from the local store.
functions.returnsDoc: The request; its answer's data is `{ key, value, revision }` (value null before the first save).

functions.name: saveSettings
functions.doc: Save the game's settings under `og.settings` (the last save wins), with the same local fallback as loadSettings.

params.name: value
params.doc: The settings: an object, at most 64 KiB encoded.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a value that is not an object or is too large.

functions.name: saveSlot
functions.doc: Save a long text under a slot, in as many store keys as it needs: a mid-size 3D world's snapshot is over a key's 64 KiB (93 entities with skinned characters, cloths and minds: about 78 KB). The parts go in the bank of keys the slot's last save did not use (`<slot>.a*` or `<slot>.b*`), then the manifest (`<slot>`: the bank, the part count, the length, a checksum and `meta`) is written last, at the revision read before: so a save cut short leaves the last one whole, and another device's save landing meanwhile is a conflict, never a mix. One request for all of it; a slot takes at most 17 of the player's 64 keys for this game (its two banks and the manifest: 1 MiB, the platform's budget for a player and game), and a world that would take more saves a selection of what it keeps (world.snapshot's SnapshotDesc).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The slot, the text and what a title shows of it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed slot name, a text over 512 KiB or a meta over 4 KiB. The answer arrives when the manifest is written: data `{ slot, parts, bytes, revision }`; an error is the first refused part's, or the manifest's (`conflict`: another save of the slot landed meanwhile; the slot holds that one).

functions.name: loadSlot
functions.doc: Read a slot saveSlot wrote: its manifest, then its parts, joined and checked against the manifest's length and checksum. One request for all of it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The slot, and whether to read its meta alone.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed slot name. The answer's data is `{ slot, text, meta, parts, bytes, revision }`: text and meta null for a slot never saved, text null with metaOnly; `invalid` for a key that holds no slot manifest or parts that do not match it.

functions.name: products
functions.doc: Describe the products the game sells: titles and prices as the player's store shows them. The catalogue and the prices are the platform's.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id or more than 100. The answer's data is `{ products: [{ id, kind, title, description, price: { amount, currency, display } }] }`: kind `consumable`, `durable` or `subscription`, amount in the currency's units, display as the player's store writes it.

functions.name: purchase
functions.doc: Ask the player to buy a product: the host shows its own purchase sheet and takes the money. The answer is the host's word on it; deliver a consumable with og.platform.grant and then og.platform.consume.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed product id. The answer's data is `{ purchase, product, quantity, state }`: state `completed`, or `pending` (waiting for a parent's approval or a payment; a `purchase` notice settles it). Errors: `cancelled` (the player backed out), `not_found` (no such product), `conflict` (a durable already owned), `unavailable`.

functions.name: entitlements
functions.doc: What the player owns in this game, as the host knows it: durables, active subscriptions and consumables not yet consumed. Ask when the game starts and after a restore, never trust a save for it.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ entitlements: [{ purchase, product, kind, quantity, expires }] }`, expires UTC milliseconds for a subscription, null otherwise.

functions.name: consume
functions.doc: Tell the host a consumable purchase was delivered: it leaves the entitlements. Grant it first (og.platform.grant).

params.name: purchase
params.doc: The purchase id an answer, an entitlement or a notice carried.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id (1 to 128 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and `:`). The answer's data is `{ purchase, product, consumed: true }`; `not_found` for a purchase not owned or already consumed.

functions.name: grant
functions.doc: Record that this world granted purchase `purchase` (in og.PlatformGrants): true the first time, false for one already granted, so a purchase's answer, notice or entitlement seen again (a replay, a relaunch, a save restored from before og.platform.consume) grants once. It records; it is not proof of payment (the host's answer is). Inside a system, declare og.PlatformGrants among its writes.
functions.returnsDoc: Whether it was new. Refused for a malformed id, or inside a system that did not declare og.PlatformGrants.

functions.name: granted
functions.doc: Whether this world granted purchase `purchase` (og.platform.grant). Inside a system, declare og.PlatformGrants among its reads.

functions.name: adReady
functions.doc: Ask whether an ad can be shown now, to offer a rewarded one only when there is one.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed placement. The answer's data is `{ kind, placement, ready }`.

functions.name: showAd
functions.doc: Show an ad. While it shows, the host pauses the game through its lifecycle (no ticks, no audio: on the web the Player's pause and resume) and the answer arrives after it resumed, at a tick's start. Grant a reward only on `completed`.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed placement. The answer's data is `{ kind, placement, outcome }`: outcome `completed` or `skipped` for a rewarded ad, `shown` for an interstitial. Errors: `no_fill` (no ad now; retryable), `rate_limited` (the platform's frequency cap), `unavailable`.

functions.name: achievementUnlock
functions.doc: Unlock an achievement. The achievements and their titles are the platform's, by id.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id. The answer's data is `{ id, percent: 100, unlocked: true, new }`, new false when it was unlocked before.

functions.name: achievementProgress
functions.doc: Report progress towards an achievement; 100 unlocks it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed id or a percent outside 0 to 100. The answer's data is `{ id, percent, unlocked, new }`.

functions.name: achievements
functions.doc: The player's achievements in this game.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ achievements: [{ id, percent, unlocked, time }] }`, time the unlock's UTC milliseconds or null.

functions.name: player
functions.doc: Who is playing: an id scoped to this game (the same player has another id in another game) and the name to show.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ player, name, guest }`, guest true for a player without an account.

functions.name: friends
functions.doc: The player's friends, those playing this game first.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ friends: [{ player, name, online, playing }] }`, ids scoped to this game; `unauthorized` for a guest.

functions.name: inviteSend
functions.doc: Invite a friend to this game, or offer an invite link through the share sheet. The invited player opens the game with the invite in og.platform.invites.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Whom, the words and what the game hands them.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a malformed friend id, a message over 120 characters or a payload over 1 KiB. The answer's data is `{ invite, to }` (to null for a link); `cancelled` when the player closed the share sheet.

functions.name: invites
functions.doc: The invites to this game the player has not acted on, the one the game was opened with marked `opened`.
functions.returnsDoc: The answer's data is `{ invites: [{ invite, from: { player, name }, payload, time, opened }] }`.

functions.name: share
functions.doc: Share through the device's share sheet: the text, the game's own Play link and, with image, the frame drawn last.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty text, one over 280 characters, a title over 80 or a malformed path. The answer's data is `{ shared: true, target }` (target the app the player picked, when the host knows it, else null); `cancelled` when the player closed the sheet.

functions.name: supports
functions.doc: Whether the host answers platform method `method` (`purchase.buy`, `ad.show`, `share`: og.platform.info's capabilities): what to offer the player before asking. A method it lacks is answered `unavailable`.

functions.name: notice
functions.doc: A notice og.PlatformNotice announced. The engine keeps the last 256.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for a number never given, one older than the last 256, or inside a system that writes shared state in a running lockstep session.

functions.name: result
functions.doc: The answer to a call, once it arrived.
functions.returnsDoc: Null while it is in flight, for an unknown request, or inside a system that writes shared state in a running lockstep session.

functions.name: info
functions.doc: What answers platform calls here, and what it answers.

functions.name: now
functions.doc: The host's wall-clock time, UTC milliseconds since 1970, as of this tick: what the host last told the engine (when it attached, and with every answer, applied at a tick's start like the answers) moved on by the ticks since. The one wall-clock read game code may make: it is host input, so a replay with the same answers gives the same values. Use it to know how long the game was closed (a save's time against a launch's), never to time play (that is og.Time).
functions.returnsDoc: UTC milliseconds; 0 until a host has told the time (`none`).

functions.name: roomCreate
functions.doc: Create a room and join it. The answer is og.RoomJoined, with the room's id to share (natively the relay names it `room-N`; on the web the platform does).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused with no room host (og.platform.roomInfo's host `none`), while in or joining a room (roomLeave first), or for a malformed name.

functions.name: roomJoin
functions.doc: Join a room by its id. The answer is og.RoomJoined (with ok false and `not_found` or `full` when it cannot); then og.RoomPeerJoined and og.RoomPeerLeft as others come and go.

params.name: room
params.doc: The room's id: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused with no room host, while in or joining a room, or for a malformed id.

functions.name: quickPlay
functions.doc: Quick play: wait to be matched with other players asking for the same mode and number of players, then play in a room of their own. The answer is og.RoomJoined once the room has filled (every matched peer hears it at once, numbered in the order they asked), or ok false with `timeout` after timeoutMs. roomLeave stops waiting (og.RoomJoined with `cancelled`). Natively `og relay` matches the engines connected to it (`og run --room ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/`); on the web the platform's matchmaking does (platform ask 21: until then the Player answers `unavailable`).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The mode, the players, how long to wait and this player's name.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused with no room host, while in or joining a room, or for a malformed mode or name.

functions.name: roomLeave
functions.doc: Leave the room: og.RoomPeerLeft with this engine's own peer number answers, and the other peers hear it leave after its last message. While joining (quick play waiting for its match) it stops waiting: og.RoomJoined answers with ok false and `cancelled`.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused when in no room and not joining one.

functions.name: roomSend
functions.doc: Send a message to every other peer in the room, or to one: a JSON value, or bytes (a Uint8Array). It arrives as og.RoomMessage, after every earlier message of this peer.

params.name: data
params.doc: What to send: a Uint8Array, or any JSON value; at most 64 KiB encoded.

params.name: to
params.doc: The one peer to send it to; omitted is every other peer.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when in no room, for a message over 64 KiB, or a peer not in the room.

functions.name: roomPeers
functions.doc: The peers in this engine's room, this one included, by number; empty in none.

functions.name: roomInfo
functions.doc: The room this engine is in, and what carries rooms here.

functions.name: roomMessage
functions.doc: A message og.RoomMessage announced: who sent it and what it carries. The engine keeps the last 256.
functions.returnsDoc: Null for a number never given, or a message older than the last 256.

x-og-modules.name: i18n
x-og-modules.doc:
Localization: one string table per locale (`.ogt` of `type strings`: `locale "ja"`, its font chain `fonts "..."`, `string "key" "message"`), messages in a subset of ICU MessageFormat (`{name}`, `{n, number}`, `{n, plural, =0 {..} one {..} other {..}}` with `#`, `{g, select, a {..} other {..}}`), CLDR plural rules, and the locale the host asks for (the browser's `navigator.language` on the web, `og run --locale` natively).
The active locale is the best loaded table for the request (ja-JP takes ja; zh-TW takes zh-Hant or zh-TW), else the base table (`base true`, else en, else the first). A key it lacks is read from its `fallback` table, then the base. It also sets the UI's font chain (its fonts first, then the locale's installed font pack, then packs a frame needed for characters only they cover, then the other tables' fonts) and direction: a right-to-left locale (ar, he, fa, ur) mirrors og.ui's layout, and og-ui shapes Arabic words with the font's own tables (a font cooked with the `arabic` charset carries them). `og cook` warns about every key a locale lacks, or takes other arguments for, than the base.
Formatting (formatCompact, formatCurrency, formatDate, formatTime, formatDuration, and the message styles `{n, number, compact}`, `{p, number, currency/EUR}`, `{d, date, short}`, `{d, time}`) writes from a CLDR subset built into the engine, for the languages the plural rules cover and zh-Hant; another language is written as en. It follows the active locale (else the requested one, else en). A date or time is seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC that the game passes in (a save's timestamp, a server's event time): nothing reads a clock, so the same value gives the same text on every host and in a replay. A message's dates are UTC; formatDate and formatTime take an offset.

functions.name: load
functions.doc: Load a cooked string table; the active locale is negotiated again.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked string table, or a font of its chain that is not cooked.

functions.name: setLocale
functions.doc: Ask for a locale (a player's choice in settings); the active one is the best table for it.

functions.name: locale
functions.doc: The requested and active locales, the direction and the font chain.

functions.name: t
functions.doc: A key's message in the active locale, formatted with its arguments; a key no table has answers the key itself and logs one warning.

params.name: args
params.doc: The arguments: an object of strings and numbers, `{ count: 3, name: "Kai" }`.

functions.name: has
functions.doc: Whether the active locale's own table has the key (not a fallback).

functions.name: formatNumber
functions.doc: A decimal number using the active locale's grouping, separators, native digits and sign. pseudo/en-XA expands and brackets output; ar-XB also isolates it right-to-left. Pseudo requests remain active for formatting even when translations fall back to a real table.

functions.name: formatCompact
functions.doc: A number written short in the active locale: `1.2K`, `12K`, `1.2M` (en), `1,2 Mio.` (de), `1.2万` (ja). Below the locale's first compact size (de compacts no thousands) the whole number, grouped.

params.name: decimals
params.doc: Optional fixed fraction digits, clamped to 20; omitted uses compact precision.

functions.name: formatCurrency
functions.doc: An amount of money in the active locale: `$1,234.50` (en), `1.234,50 €` (de), `￥1,235` (ja), with the currency's own fraction digits (none for JPY and KRW). A code the subset lacks is written as itself.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The amount, in the currency's whole units (dollars, not cents).

functions.name: formatDate
functions.doc: A date in the active locale, in the style asked for: `Nov 2, 2026` (en), `02.11.2026` (de).

params.name: seconds
params.doc: Seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC; fractions are dropped.

functions.name: formatTime
functions.doc: A time of day in the active locale: `3:05 PM` (en), `15:05` (de).

params.name: seconds
params.doc: Seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC; fractions are dropped.

functions.name: formatDuration
functions.doc: A length of time as a clock face, `1:02:03` from an hour and `2:05` below, in the locale's digits; whole seconds, rounded down. og.ui's `duration` and `clock` formats are the in-document equivalents.

params.name: seconds
params.doc: The length in seconds; negative is written with a minus.

params.name: style
params.doc: Clock face (default) or a narrow cooldown label.

x-og-modules.name: ui
x-og-modules.doc:
The engine's UI: an immediate-mode toolkit. Systems describe the tree every tick with these calls; the engine lays it out Clay-style, styles it with the game's UI style (the engine's default style until the game picks one), draws it over the frame and answers the probe (dump_ui, touch_move_to, move_to_text) from it.
The engine opens the frame before the game's systems (from og.Input and the play surface) and closes it after them, so calls belong inside systems; outside one they do nothing and log a warning. Interaction is decided against the previous tick's rectangles, which are also what the probe resolves, so a scripted touch_move_to and a click agree; response edges (clicked, changed, submitted) last one tick.
Lengths are CSS pixels of the play surface (origin top left, y down), the unit of og.Input and the probe. Ids: an element's id is unique among its siblings (`idi("Slot", 3)` is `Slot#3`); a path `Inventory/Slot#3` names it after its nearest ancestors. The UI state (hover, press, focus, caret, scroll) is world state: snapshots and the world hash carry it.

functions.name: configure
functions.doc: Set how the UI looks (the scheme, density, fonts, style, sounds, motion…), typically in GameDesc.start; it takes effect from the next tick. The desc is a partial: a field left out keeps the last UiDesc's value, the one an earlier call or a look's style (og.render.applyLook) gave it, so a settings screen that configures sounds or reducedMotion keeps the style and the fonts; null clears a field to its default (`style: null` goes back to the default style). A UI left with no font at all (no font, no style with fonts, no fallback or locale font) warns: it would draw no text.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI is configured.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The fields to change; the others keep their values.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font or style, or a desc that is not an object.

functions.name: viewport
functions.doc: This tick's play surface as the UI lays out on it: the render target's size, safe area and covered region in og-ui units (CSS pixels over UiTheme.unit, docs/ui.md §6.1: 1 on touch and up to 720p, so CSS pixels there) and device pixels per unit, from what the host reports.

functions.name: theme
functions.doc: The style values the UI draws with.

functions.name: framePointer
functions.doc: The primary pointer of the frame being built, without the world: for a component that hit-tests a shape it draws itself (a pie's wedges, a wheel's slices) by angle and radius rather than by rectangles. Keys and pads reach the same choices through focusable parts.

functions.name: frameCursor
functions.doc: The pointer's shape the last frame resolved (never auto): the cursor set on what the press holds or the pointer is over, or around it, else its kind's. The web shell sets the canvas's CSS cursor from each frame's answer (`cursor`); a native host that draws its own window (og dev, Origin Desktop's shared frames) reads the same answer.

functions.name: frameViewport
functions.doc: The play surface of the frame being built: og.ui.viewport without the world, for code that only builds UI.

functions.name: hasIcon
functions.doc: Whether the icon atlas has an icon of this name (components draw a fallback otherwise).

functions.name: seconds
functions.doc: The UI's clock in seconds: frames built over the tick rate (simulation time, never the wall clock).

functions.name: setFocus
functions.doc: Move the focus (the pointer's, the keys' and pad 0's) to the element at a full path when this frame ends, if a focusable control is there then: a component moving the focus with its choice (a radio group's arrow keys, a list opening at its chosen option, a keyboard's first key). The ring shows as navigation's does. The last call in a frame wins; a path with no focusable control leaves the focus where it is.

params.name: path
params.doc: The element's full path (og.ui.focus, the probe's dump).

functions.name: scrollIntoView
functions.doc: Scroll the scroll container around a control (an interactive or focusable element, by its full path) so the control is in its view, by where both were in the last frame: by the least that shows it whole, or centred in the view (a saga map opening on the current level, a list on its chosen row). The offset stays in the container's range and stops a fling. Nothing for a path the last frame had no control at or that is in no scroll container.

params.name: path
params.doc: The control's full path (og.ui.focus, the probe's dump).

params.name: center
params.doc: Centre it in the view, as far as the range allows; false scrolls by the least that shows it.

functions.name: frameDirection
functions.doc: The writing direction of the frame being built, `ltr` or `rtl` (og.i18n's locale sets it): code that draws its own arrows, chevrons or progress along a line mirrors them by it; layout mirrors rows and insets itself.

functions.name: frameTheme
functions.doc: The style values of the frame being built: og.ui.theme without the world, for code that only builds UI (the components and patterns).

functions.name: bounds
functions.doc: Where an element was in the last frame, by id or `Parent/Child` path (topmost first), as touch_move_to resolves it.

functions.name: scrollState
functions.doc: A scroll container's offset, view and whole content, by its full path (as the probe's dump names it): what a component virtualises its rows by, since og.ui.bounds is cut to the view and a row scrolled away has none. The offset is this tick's; the sizes are the last frame's. Null for a path that was no scroll container.

functions.name: toast
functions.doc: Queue a toast: it stacks at UiDesc.toastAnchor, enters, stays its time and leaves; at most three are up (older ones leave first); a press dismisses it. Callable anywhere (systems, commands, start); it is world state, so snapshots carry it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI shows it.

functions.returnsDoc: Its id, for dismissToast.

functions.name: dismissToast
functions.doc: Start a toast's exit.

functions.name: navigate
functions.doc: Queue a navigation intent for the next tick: a gamepad og.Input does not read yet, a custom binding, a command. A move queued while the focus is on nothing puts the focus on the first control, whatever its direction, and no further: moves asked again before the focus lands (each tick until og.ui.focus answers a path) land on that same first control.

functions.name: back
functions.doc: Escape or gamepad B this tick, not taken by a dialog or menu: true once, then taken. A pause screen closes on it. While a dialog or menu that Back closes is open (the topmost of the last frame) it answers false and leaves Back to it, even when asked before the dialog is built this tick: a HUD drawn under pause never takes the Back that closes pause. A locked dialog lets Back through.

functions.name: setPlayers
functions.doc: Local multiplayer: how many players this screen takes (1 to 4; 1 by default). Pads 1 to count - 1 each move a focus of their own among the same controls, shown as a ring in the player's colour (info, success, warn), and their A presses the control under it (Response.pad says which pad); pad 0 shares the one focus with the keyboard and the pointer, and Back and adjusting a slider stay pad 0's. Declare it every tick the screen shows; it takes effect from the next tick, and a dialog's focus scope holds every pad's focus inside it.

functions.name: setVirtualCursor
functions.doc: A pad's virtual cursor, for a screen built for the pointer (a map, a shop grid, a strategy HUD) played on a pad: pad 0's left stick moves it instead of the focus, slowing and sticking over controls; its A presses where it points as the mouse's button does (drags, sliders and long presses work); its right stick scrolls under it. The style draws it and the system cursor hides (og.ui.frameCursor answers none). The real pointer moving hides it and the stick shows it again. Declare it every tick the screen shows; it takes effect from the next tick. Null turns it off.

params.name: desc
params.doc: How it moves; null is none.

functions.name: virtualCursor
functions.doc: The virtual cursor as the last frame left it; null when none is declared.

functions.name: setHudEdit
functions.doc: Turns the HUD edit mode on or off (docs/ui.md §2.1; kept until changed). While it is on, elements with the `customize` attribute stop answering their own presses and show their outlines: a press selects one and a drag moves it, two touches or the wheel scale it, and with no virtual cursor pad 0's left stick moves the selected one. The hud-editor screen document (og ui eject hud-editor) gives the steps, Next, Reset and Done.

functions.name: setHudPlayer
functions.doc: Whose layout this screen shows and edits, 0 to 3 (0 by default; kept until changed): each player of a shared screen keeps a layout of their own.

functions.name: hudEdit
functions.doc: The HUD edit mode as the last frame left it.

functions.name: hudLayout
functions.doc: A player's HUD layout as JSON, for the game's settings: each moved, scaled or faded element's key with its x, y, scale and opacity. Save it when HudEdit.changed says so; give it back with og.ui.setHudLayout on the next run.

functions.name: setHudLayout
functions.doc: Gives a player's HUD layout back (og.ui.hudLayout's JSON; `{}` resets it). Answers false and leaves the layout as it was when it does not read (the reason is in the frame's warnings).

functions.name: hudSelect
functions.doc: Selects an element to edit by its key (empty: none).

functions.name: hudStep
functions.doc: Steps the selected element's size and opacity: each -1, 0 or +1 step (a tenth larger or smaller, a tenth more or less opaque), within its limits.

functions.name: hudReset
functions.doc: Puts an element back where it was laid out: its key, empty for the selected one, `*` for every one.

functions.name: focus
functions.doc: The path of the control pad pad's focus is on in the last frame (pad 0: the shared focus of the pointer, keyboard and pad 0), as touch_move_to resolves it; empty when it is on none.

params.name: pad
params.doc: The pad, 0 to 3; past 3 answers empty.

functions.name: a11y
functions.doc: The accessibility tree of the last frame: every element with a role, its name, value, states and bounds, and the focus order Tab walks. A shell mirrors it into the page for screen readers; a playtest reads the same fields on dump_ui's elements.

functions.name: feedback
functions.doc: Play a UI event's feedback from the style (docs/ui.md §3.1): one sound of its set, at random and never the one it played last, at a volume and pitch from the set's ranges, and its haptic pattern at the player's strength (setHaptics). Widgets play their own events (press, focus, select, confirm, back, open, close, tab, toggleOn, toggleOff, sliderTick); game code plays the rest: scrollTick, typewriter, counterTick, notification, warning, error, success, reward and the reveals revealCommon to revealMythic. The choices come from the UI state, so a replay plays the same. An unknown event or one the style leaves silent plays nothing.

params.name: rise
params.doc: A rising cascade's step, 0 to 1, walking the set's pitch range up (a counter's ticks); below 0 picks the pitch at random.

functions.name: setHaptics
functions.doc: The player's haptic strength (a settings screen's vibration slider or switch): 0 turns the UI's haptics off, 1 (the default) plays the style's patterns as set; between scales them. The web shell rumbles the gamepad and vibrates a phone; the native host rumbles its pad.

functions.name: setNavigation
functions.doc: Whether keyboard and gamepad navigation moves focus on this screen (on by default). A gameplay HUD whose keys move the player turns it off; an open dialog or menu turns it back on while it is open. Takes effect from the next tick.

functions.name: tick
functions.doc: Frames the UI has built: its clock, for animations by the tick.

functions.name: previewViewport
functions.doc: Lay the UI out for another play surface (a phone in portrait at 3x, a notch) until cleared with null: for headless previews and playtests of responsive layouts. Render at width x dpr by height x dpr (`og run --size`).

params.name: viewport
params.doc: The surface to lay out for; null returns to the host's.

functions.name: defineTimeline
functions.doc: Define a timeline by name: configuration, like the theme, defined once at start. Plays and state groups name it.

functions.name: play
functions.doc: Play a choreography on an element from the end of this tick: its timelines' keys drive the elements' props and its events fire as it passes them (og.ui.motionEvents). Returns the play's id (0: no element, or a choreo of no known kind).

params.name: path
params.doc: The element's full path; empty is the element built just before.

functions.name: playTimeline
functions.doc: Play one timeline (by name) on an element: og.ui.play with a single step.

params.name: path
params.doc: The element's full path; empty is the element built just before.

functions.name: seek
functions.doc: Move a play to a time; it fires no events on the way. Returns false for an unknown play.

functions.name: pause
functions.doc: Hold a play where it is.

functions.name: resume
functions.doc: Let a held play go on.

functions.name: reverse
functions.doc: Turn a play round where it is: an interrupted opening closes from where it got to.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Stop a play: its elements go back to their own values (on their motion, if they have one).

functions.name: playInfo
functions.doc: Where a play is; null once it is gone.

functions.name: forceState
functions.doc: Force a state group of an element (the probe and agents render and check each state this way); null lets it go.

functions.name: visualState
functions.doc: The state a group of an element is in (last tick); empty for none.

functions.name: animate
functions.doc: Any number on a spring or an ease (docs/ui.md §3.1: every value is animatable): call it every tick with the target and it answers this tick's value. A retarget keeps its value and velocity; under reduced motion it jumps.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id under the open element.

functions.name: gesture
functions.doc: What the drag or pinch on an element is doing.

functions.name: motionEvents
functions.doc: The UI's motion events of the last frame: sounds, haptics, bursts, state changes, callbacks, ends, dismissals, drops and snaps.

functions.name: overlaps
functions.doc: The last frame's overlaps between elements (docs/ui.md §2), with both paths: an absolute, anchored or floating element over another's drawing, and siblings in the flow over each other. What the engine places over another on purpose (a badge on its item's corner) is left out; whether any other overlap is meant is the reader's call.

functions.name: layoutStats
functions.doc: What the last frame built, rebuilt, laid out and kept.

functions.name: formatNumber
functions.doc: A number written in a notation: grouped, compact, idle letters, scientific or engineering, with a sign, prefix and suffix and the locale's separators, and past 1e308 through its exponent. Deterministic: the same text on every host.

functions.name: defineMass
functions.doc: Declare a mass element template by name and answer its handle; declaring the name again replaces it and keeps the handle. Invalid timing text returns an error naming the text and required syntax; it never falls back to linear.

params.name: desc
params.doc: What it draws and how it moves.

functions.name: spawnMass
functions.doc: Start instances of a template on this tick: each plays its template's timeline over its lifetime and leaves after it (damage numbers, pickups). They live in the UI's state, so a snapshot or a replay carries them.

functions.name: massCount
functions.doc: The live spawned instances of a template.

functions.name: scope
functions.doc: The entry to named svelte/store-compatible presentation data and retained document mounts. Rust owns values, the dependency graph and mounted elements. No Svelte compiler, runes, TS elements or asynchronous primitives. See docs/ui.md for a worked example and If you know Svelte.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the presentation checkpoint.

params.name: id
params.doc: An explicit, nonempty stable scope name.

functions.name: push
functions.doc: Push a screen onto the layer stack (docs/ui.md §2.1), over the layers of its kind and under those of a later kind (hud, menu, modal, popover, toast, tooltip, system); the active layer remembers its focus. Callable anywhere (systems, commands, start); the stack is world state, so snapshots carry it.

params.name: vm
params.doc: Its viewmodel (null: its document's first fixture, else an empty object).

functions.returnsDoc: The layer's serial. Refused for a name no screen document has.

functions.name: pop
functions.doc: Pop the active layer; the next active one takes its remembered focus. Answers the popped screen's name (empty: the stack was empty).

functions.name: replace
functions.doc: Replace the active layer with a screen.
functions.returnsDoc: The new layer's serial.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Empty the layer stack.

functions.name: layers
functions.doc: The layer stack, bottom first.

functions.name: screenVm
functions.doc: A layer's viewmodel as its two-way bindings left it (the top layer of that screen); null when it is not on the stack.

functions.name: docEvents
functions.doc: Take the events of the documents built this frame: pushed layers and store-driven mounts.

functions.name: gameInput
functions.doc: Gameplay takes input this tick: no layer whose input is `menu` is on the stack. Input goes to the top layer that takes it, once per tick.

functions.name: paused
functions.doc: A layer that pauses the game (`pause`) is on the stack: the engine holds the time scale at 0 while one is, and gives back the one it had.

functions.name: defineAction
functions.doc: Define (or redefine) a UI action. confirm (Enter, Space, A), back (Escape, B), tabNext (E, ], RB), tabPrev (Q, [, LB), details (X, Y) and rotate (R, X) are defined by default.

functions.name: action
functions.doc: The action fired this tick (a document's `on action` fires on the top layer that takes input).

functions.name: actionHeld
functions.doc: A hold action is held past its hold, or its toggle is on.

functions.name: glyph
functions.doc: An action's glyph on the device used last: its first binding there. Null for an unknown action or one with no binding on that device.

functions.name: frameGlyph
functions.doc: An action's glyph on the device used last, as og.ui.glyph answers it, without the world: for a component that shows a prompt (a tab row's bumpers, the action bar) and only builds UI. It follows the device live (keyboard, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, a generic pad, touch) and the player's rebinding. A name that is no UI action answers as og.input.glyph does for the world whose frame is being built (a gameplay action an ability slot names). Null for an unknown action, one with no binding on that device, or outside a frame being built.

functions.name: device
functions.doc: The device the player used last (glyphs follow it live): a key or the mouse, a pad of the family set with og.ui.setDevice (Xbox by default), or a touch on a coarse pointer.

functions.name: filePicker
functions.doc: Whether this host opens a file picker for a document's `<input type="file">` (a capability query, the same on every host that has one): false on the web and natively today, where such an input is refused at build with a warning. Where true, a press sends the host a `filepick` event (its `accept` and `multiple`) and the host writes the chosen names to the input's bound value.

functions.name: setDevice
functions.doc: Set the device (the host's when it knows: a pad's family from its id); a pad family also becomes what pad input shows from then on.

functions.name: actionBar
functions.doc: What an action bar component reads: the actions the top layer's document lists (`actions { confirm "Buy" }`), each with its hint and its glyph on the device used last.

functions.name: documentSchema
functions.doc: The reflected schema documents are validated against (docs/ui.md §2.1): every element kind and every prop, with its value type, the kinds it applies to and whether a control writes it back.

functions.name: setProp
functions.doc: Set a prop of a document element live (Tune, the probe's ui:set): presentation only, over the document's own line until og.ui.saveEdits writes it into the file. The value is written as the document's line would be (`token primary`, `grow`, `bind gold compact`).

params.name: value
params.doc: Its value as a document line writes it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown prop or a value it does not take.

functions.name: saveEdits
functions.doc: Write the live edits into their documents' `.ogt` files under the project's assets (each edited element's line of that prop replaced, or one added; every other line kept), as save_scene writes scenes; the documents take the new text at once. Answers the files written.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused on a host with no project directory, or a write that fails.

interfaces.name: UiSource
interfaces.doc: A store's stable checkpoint identity. Stores are created in a named scope.

members.name: scope
members.doc: The owning scope.

members.name: id
members.doc: The store ID within that scope.

interfaces.name: UiScope
interfaces.doc: Named presentation stores for one world, following the svelte/store contract. Svelte template documents own structure; this scope supplies data. Re-register the same IDs on reload to preserve source values.

members.name: id
members.doc: The stable scope ID.

members.name: writable
members.doc: Create a named writable store with subscribe, set and update. Re-registration preserves its checkpointed value. Failures are reported by takeErrors; setters also return Result.

params.name: id
params.doc: An explicit, nonempty stable store ID.

params.name: initial
params.doc: The initial serializable value, used only for a new store.

members.name: readable
members.doc: Create a named readable store. start runs when its first subscriber arrives and its cleanup runs when the last leaves. No promises, timers or wall-clock work in a tick.

members.name: derived
members.doc: Derive a store synchronously from one store or a tuple of stores. Inputs are explicit and settle before subscribers run; undeclared reads and reentrant writes report errors in every build. Failure preserves the last good value, or the optional initial fallback; without either it reports an error and yields undefined.

params.name: id
params.doc: The stable derived store ID, also its callback reload identity.

params.name: stores
params.doc: One named store or a readonly tuple of named stores from this world.

params.name: compute
params.doc: A pure synchronous function of the input values.

params.name: initial
params.doc: An optional fallback if the first computation fails.

members.name: get
members.doc: Read a store by subscribing and immediately unsubscribing, as svelte/store get does.

members.name: collection
members.doc: The engine-specific store: ordered rows with stable string keys, plus insert, remove, move and field patch. Duplicate keys and key-changing patches are refused. Re-registration keeps data and order.

params.name: items
params.doc: Initial rows, used only for a new collection.

members.name: mount
members.doc: Register a loaded document once with named store inputs. The native renderer updates it from store changes; no per-element TypeScript calls are made. Re-registering the same ID and inputs preserves its mounted identity. Inputs stay subscribed until unmount or scope disposal. A `type screen` document is a layer of the stack while it is mounted (docs/ui.md §2.1): its `<meta name="screen" data-layer …>` decides its kind, input, pause, Back and focus memory, Back or a `pop` trigger unmounts it, and its `@view-transition` animates it (a cross-fade by default) as it joins and leaves the stack.

params.name: id
params.doc: Stable mount ID within this scope.

params.name: inputs
params.doc: Document input names mapped to named stores from this world.

params.name: content
params.doc: Content passed by reference (Svelte snippets as props): a name the document renders with `{@render name()}`, mapped to a loaded document's name (its root) or `document#snippet` (one of its snippets), rendered with this mount's stores.

members.name: unmount
members.doc: Remove a registered document and release its input subscriptions. Removing an absent mount succeeds.

params.name: id
params.doc: The mount ID in this scope.

members.name: takeErrors
members.doc: Drain operation and scheduler errors naming scope and store. Errors are reported in publish too; the scheduler never throws into the engine.

members.name: dispose
members.doc: Remove the scope's stores and subscriptions and run start/stop cleanups.

x-og-modules.name: systems
x-og-modules.doc: Systems the engine ships as TypeScript: game-level code, listed explicitly in GameDesc.systems like the game's own, so the schedule (and dump_world) shows them and nothing runs that the game did not ask for.

values.name: cameras
values.doc: The camera controllers, in this order: og.orbitCamera (og.OrbitCamera), og.followCamera (og.FollowCamera) and og.follow2D (og.Follow2D). Each moves og.Camera only while an entity carries its component. List them before the game's systems that read og.Camera: `systems: [...og.systems.cameras, ...yours]`.

x-og-modules.name: commands
x-og-modules.doc:
The command channel: actions scheduled on simulation time, from `og run --commands "t:action[:args];..."` or the probe's commands().
Core actions ship with the engine; a module or a game registers more. Unknown actions warn and continue. Not in publish builds.
Outputs are relative to the output directory: an absolute path, a `..` component or a name starting with `.` (kept for the harness, such as a playtest's kept store) is refused. A file an earlier step of the script wrote is never overwritten: the later step's is written as `<stem>-2.<ext>` with a warning naming both steps.

functions.name: register
functions.doc: Register an action into the command channel. GameDesc.commands does this for a game's own actions.

params.name: name
params.doc: The action name, snake_case, such as `spawn_wave`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a name a core action or another registration already uses.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: Parse a script without scheduling it.
functions.returnsDoc: The steps, or the first malformed step.

functions.name: help
functions.doc: Every action the channel knows: core actions in CoreAction order, then registered ones by name.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose channel is asked.

functions.name: schedule
functions.doc: Schedule a script on simulation time, from the current tick.
functions.returnsDoc: The report, or the first malformed step.

callbacks.name: CommandHandler
callbacks.doc: A registered action. It runs at the start of the tick it was scheduled for.

params.name: args
params.doc: The `:`-separated arguments after the action name.

x-og-modules.name: probe
x-og-modules.doc:
The probe: RuntimeProbe protocol 5 (origin/packages/contracts/src/probe.ts) served natively, plus the engine's wire members.
In a page it is published on globalThis.__runtime_probe__; on native, `og` serves it as JSON-RPC 2.0 over a loopback WebSocket at /probe.
A refusal is false or null exactly as protocol 5; a JSON-RPC error is only for a malformed call or an unknown method.
Probe entity ids are entity names; an unnamed entity is `#<index>.<generation>`.

consts.name: PROBE_GLOBAL
consts.doc: The global the page publishes the probe on.

consts.name: PROBE_VERSION
consts.doc: The RuntimeProbe contract revision both sides speak.

consts.name: PROBE_WIRE_VERSION
consts.doc: The wire revision hello reports.

consts.name: REPLAY_SEED_PARAM
consts.doc: The page query parameter that starts a deterministic replay from a uint32 seed.

consts.name: PLAYTEST_MAX_TICKS
consts.doc: The longest playtest one request may advance, in fixed steps.

consts.name: PROBE_PROGRAM_MAX_OPERATIONS
consts.doc: The most operations one probe program may carry.

consts.name: CAPTURE_FIT
consts.doc: The long side capture, marks and key frames fit an image to unless asked otherwise: a whole frame a model reads in few tokens; a detail is cut at full resolution as its own image (capture's region).

interfaces.name: RuntimeProbe
interfaces.doc: RuntimeProbe protocol 5, member for member. Every member answers synchronously with JSON-serialisable values.

members.name: version
members.doc: PROBE_VERSION.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps the world has taken since load.

members.name: state
members.doc: A JSON snapshot: the fixed timings head, then the game's own facts.

members.name: advance
members.doc: Take whole fixed steps regardless of the wall clock.
members.returnsDoc: The tick after the steps.

members.name: pause
members.doc: Hold the wall-clock loop; advance still steps.

members.name: resume
members.doc: Release the wall-clock loop.

members.name: input
members.doc: One event through the input layer's own path.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

members.name: accepted
members.doc: Page events (keyboard, pointer, wheel) the input layer accepted since load.

members.name: pick
members.doc: The scene entity under a point of the play surface, and the UI element over it (pickUi's answer) outside a publish build.
members.returnsDoc: Null when nothing is under the point.

members.name: entity
members.doc: One entity's published parameters: its tunable fields as `Component.field` keys.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: bounds
members.doc: The ranges of one entity's tunable fields, from the schema.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: patch
members.doc: Move one tunable field for this run only; it applies within one frame. The probe never writes project files.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

members.name: run
members.doc: Run a program of the members above in order, stopping at the first refusal.

interfaces.name: EngineProbe
interfaces.doc: The engine's probe: protocol 5 plus the wire members of the loopback WebSocket and the in-page request ring.

members.name: hello
members.doc: Who is speaking: protocol, wire, engine version, tick rate, renderer tier, build.

members.name: capture
members.doc:
The frame of the current tick, rendered offscreen and read back as a PNG; null without a renderer (hello's tier `none`).
Size rule: width and height are both 0 (or absent), which is the render target's size, or both 1 to 4096, which renders that size with the same camera (the aspect follows the requested size); one zero and one not is a malformed call.
On the web the readback is asynchronous: through the request ring the answer arrives when the copy completes; a synchronous in-page call answers null on the first tick and the frame from then on (a capture is requested on tick N and answered on N + 1).
Fit rule: a PNG whose long side exceeds fit is downscaled to it with the aspect kept, each pixel the mean of the area it covers (CAPTURE_FIT, 1280, by default: the size a model reads a whole frame at); 0 keeps the rendered size, as a reference frame needs.
Region: a box of the play surface (CSS px) cut from the rendered frame before fitting, so a detail comes at full resolution as its own image; scale and region map its pixels back to the surface.

params.name: width
params.doc: Width in pixels; 0 is the render target's.

params.name: height
params.doc: Height in pixels; 0 is the render target's.

params.name: fit
params.doc: The longest side the PNG may have; 0 keeps the rendered size.

params.name: region
params.doc: A box of the play surface to cut out (CSS px); null is the whole frame.

members.returnsDoc: Null without a renderer, or for a region outside the surface.

members.name: marks
members.doc:
The frame of the current tick with a numbered box over each UI element and each scene entity it shows (Set-of-Mark), and what each number is: its path, kind, text, box, a point to pick or touch it at, and the document or scene line that made it, with the style part and rule of an element. A reviewer names a number; the map says where to change it.
The elements are those pickUi answers (they show something or take input) inside the surface, an element and an ancestor of the same box (within a CSS pixel) marked once, as the one that takes input or else the topmost; a backdrop that covers the whole surface and takes no input is not boxed. The entities are describe's, the main camera's, nearest first. The image follows capture's size and fit rules; the marks are drawn at the fitted size, so the numbers stay legible.
On the web it waits for its readback as capture does.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The size, the fit, what to mark and how many.

members.returnsDoc: Null without a renderer.

members.name: timeline
members.doc: What happened in the run since the last call, each with its tick: inputs, command steps, screen changes, assertion firings and expectations. A tool that records or steps a run reads it to pick the frames where something happened (og render --keyframes) and to sync them to ticks.

members.name: sweep
members.doc: A filmstrip over one tunable: per value, restore, patch, advance, capture.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameter, values, steps and size.

members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity or parameter, or without a renderer.

members.name: reload
members.doc: Hot reload: snapshot, swap the game bundle, re-register components by name, restore.
members.returnsDoc: Null when the new bundle fails to load; the old one keeps running.

members.name: snapshot
members.doc: Snapshot the whole world in the running process.

members.name: restore
members.doc: Restore a snapshot taken by this process.
members.returnsDoc: False for an unknown id.

members.name: dump
members.doc: A world, entity or UI dump, as the command channel's dump actions write.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: commands
members.doc: Schedule a command script on simulation time, as `og run --commands`.
members.returnsDoc: Null for a malformed script.

members.name: listen
members.doc: The last seconds of audio the host's mixer rendered (a null sink renders too, into a two-second ring), as a WAV with its peak and RMS: what a person would have heard.
members.returnsDoc: Null without audio, or before anything was rendered.

members.name: memory
members.doc: What the engine holds: the wasm linear memory on the web or the process's resident memory natively, the engine's counted heap, the world's entities, the streaming budget and the audio bank, in the same shape on both hosts.
members.returnsDoc: Null from a host that gives no figures.

members.name: describe
members.doc: The frame of the current tick as data: the visible entities with screen boxes, depth order and occlusion from the entity-id pass, their names, archetypes and labels; the UI elements with rects and text; the camera. Answers without a renderer too (the pass runs on the CPU).

members.name: expect
members.doc: Evaluate one expectation now (the forms of the command channel's `expect:`); the result is also kept for expectations().
members.returnsDoc: A malformed expectation is a malformed call.

members.name: expectations
members.doc: Every expectation evaluated since the last call (scripts' `expect:` steps, programs, expect()), and the counts.

members.name: assertions
members.doc: The run's assertions (og.assert, the default invariants, `invariant:` steps): every site with whether it fired, each violated one's first violation with its tick, entity, record, field and value, each's buckets, and what never fired. With take, the report is answered and a new one starts: the sites stay listed, unfired, so an independent run (another playtest, a sibling fork) inherits none of this one's violations or coverage.

params.name: take
params.doc: Start a new report after answering this one.

members.name: assertionEvents
members.doc: The assertions' stream since the last call: each site's first firing, each each-bucket's first holding and each site's first violation, with its tick, in the order they happened (at most 4,096 between calls; more are counted in dropped). A tool that steps a run reads it after each advance and stops at the first violation, instead of reading the whole report.

members.name: observe
members.doc: The game's reflected state as values: each of its resources' fields, and each of its components' fields on up to 256 entities by probe id (`{ tick, resources: { Score: { value } }, components: { Health: { hero: { hp } } } }`). Records names which (engine records too, `og.Transform`); empty is every record the game declared. What a search of the game's states abstracts its cells from (og explore).

params.name: records
params.doc: The records to read; null or empty: the game's own.

params.name: types
params.doc: Also answer `types`: each of those records' kind (component, resource or event) and fields with their type, min, max and variants, the events among them.

members.name: saveScene
members.doc: Write every scene the world was assembled from back from the world (the boot scene's and each og.world.instantiate made): its entities' and resources' changed field lines and the fields set and patch tuned, keeping every other line, comment and the order; with spawned, the entities the game spawned under the boot scene's marked section. The probe writes the files only with write; otherwise the texts are returned.

params.name: spawned
