params.doc: Write the entities the game spawned at run time under the boot scene's marked section.

members.returnsDoc: Null without a scene to write back (the reason is in the log).

members.name: pickUi
members.doc: The UI element under a point of the play surface: what pick names in the UI, with the document line that built it and the style rules that dress it. A tool asks it first, then pick for the scene.
members.returnsDoc: Null when no UI element that shows something or takes input is under the point.

x-og-modules.name: terrain
x-og-modules.doc:
Terrain (phase 2): a height field over a rectangle, cooked by `og cook` from a `type terrain` .ogt (a 16-bit grey PNG or an EXR heightmap, an optional control map, up to sixteen layered materials with slope and altitude rules (each pixel blends its four strongest), their maps separate textures (the first four layers) or layers of two texture arrays: `layers` and `layerNormals` with each layer's `albedoLayer` and `normalLayer`, two sampled textures instead of up to eight and the only way past four layers, the control map one image per four layers, and an optional `holes` map whose black or transparent cells are cut out of the surface: a cave mouth, a pit, a tunnel through a hill) into tiles; drawn as a geometry clipmap around the camera (nested levels by distance, no cracks) that casts and receives shadows under the fog; collided with as a height field; baked into navmeshes by a navmesh file's `terrain` entry.
Load it with og.terrain.load, then place it: an og.Terrain on an entity draws it placed by the entity's world transform (centred on its position, turned and scaled with it), and an og.Collider of shape SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD naming the TerrainInfo's geometry makes it solid. og.TerrainScatter grows grass, flowers or stones over a layer near the camera. og.terrain.sample answers the surface's height and normal anywhere (pass it the entity's position, quaternion and scale); og.terrain.edit raises, lowers, flattens, smooths or paints it at runtime, and og.terrain.setLayer retunes a layer. Terrain is 3D: the 2D profile's publish and lanes modules leave it out (RenderCapabilities.world3d is false), where every call here answers a refusal naming that field. Edits are world state: a snapshot keeps them, the world hash covers them, and a restore brings the ground back as it was (rebuilt from the cook with the restored edits replayed, for the renderer, physics and sample alike).
Its tiles stream (phase 3): the cook stores the field as a pyramid of tiles, each compressed on its own, and every frame the renderer keeps on the GPU only the tiles the camera's clipmap wants, within each terrain's tile budget (16 MiB by default), decoded off the frame (a worker thread natively, the browser's DecompressionStream on the Web) a few at a time, the most needed first; until a tile arrives its area draws from the coarser level that holds it, then fades in. Nothing a tick reads depends on which tiles are resident (collision and og.terrain.sample read the whole field), so a run's world hash is the same streamed or not. The probe's `terrain_stream:resident` decodes every wanted tile before each frame instead (`terrain_stream:stream[:<MiB>]` streams again, within that budget), and `dump_stream`'s `terrain` gives the tiles resident, waiting, decoding and cached.

functions.name: load
functions.doc: Load a cooked terrain (a `type terrain` .ogt under assets/) and its layers' textures (or texture arrays, kept resident while it is loaded), and register its height field with physics under TerrainInfo.geometry. Loading the same path again answers the same terrain.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path that is not a cooked terrain, or a layer texture that does not load.

functions.name: sample
functions.doc: The surface under a world point: its height, normal and slope. Each height-field cell splits along the diagonal whose corner heights differ less; ties keep the (-x, -z) to (+x, +z) diagonal. Sampling, rendering at the finest level and the native height-field collider use this same rule. Callable inside systems (it reads the terrain, not the world).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The terrain, where it stands and the point.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain.

functions.name: bounds
functions.doc: A terrain's box in world space when it stands at `origin`, turned by `quaternion` and scaled by `scale` (its entity's world transform): the box around its turned corners.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain.

functions.name: edit
functions.doc: Change a terrain under a round brush: raise, lower, flatten or smooth its heights (the renderer, physics and og.terrain.sample see the change from the next frame and tick), or paint a layer into its control map (making one when it has none).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain, a layer beyond its layers, or a brush that misses it.

functions.name: stamp
functions.doc: Carve a terrain under a mesh (its og.TerrainStamp's), or cut holes under it: the triangles are rasterised from above over the height samples, deterministically, and what changed is world state like og.terrain.edit's (a snapshot keeps it, the world hash covers it, a restore replays it, and the replay needs only the log, not the mesh). The renderer, physics and og.terrain.sample see the change from the next frame and tick. Answers the stamp's id in TerrainEdit.stamp.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The terrain, the mesh, where both stand, and what to do.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain, a geometry that is not loaded, or a mesh that covers none of the terrain.

functions.name: unstamp
functions.doc: Take a stamp back: the terrain is rebuilt from its cook with every other edit and stamp replayed in order, as if it had never been made.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain or a stamp it does not hold.

functions.name: layer
functions.doc: A terrain's layer as it is now (for a tuning tool: read it, change it, setLayer it).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain or layer.

functions.name: setLayer
functions.doc: Replace a terrain's layer look and rules (its textures stay). Drawn from the next frame.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unknown terrain or layer.

x-og-modules.name: stream
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset streaming groups (phase 3): a scene's `stream "<name>" { asset ...; distance x y z r [unload d] | volume "<entity>"; priority n }` blocks name glTF models (without skins or morph targets), textures, texture arrays, flipbooks (an `array true` sheet brings its array), sounds, environment maps, palettes, looks and colour LUTs (`.cube`) that load and unload together, and what loads them: the camera within `r` of the anchor (kept until it is past `unload`, 1.25 r by default), the camera inside the named entity's box (its position ± half its scale, turned with it), or neither (og.stream.request only). `og cook` packs each group's files into `cooked/stream/<name>.ogb`; `og build --publish` ships the packs beside the boot bundle, which the shell and the service worker fetch first, and fetches a pack only when its group loads.
At every tick boundary the engine decides which groups are wanted, admits them by priority (then name) within the memory budget (256 MiB by default; GPU textures and meshes and decoded audio, as the cook measured them), evicting lower-priority resident groups to make room for a higher one, and reads and puts in place at most one group's assets per boundary. A group that cannot fit waits, queued; one larger than the whole budget fails. Until its group is resident, a model draws its proxy (its coarsest LOD, untextured), a texture is a 1x1 grey placeholder and a sound plays as silence of its own length; then the real ones take over the same handles. Physics always collides with the proxy's meshes and a sound's length never changes, so nothing a tick reads depends on what is resident: a run's world hash is the same streamed or not.
Texture arrays, flipbooks, environment maps, palettes, looks and colour LUTs have no stand-in: they load once their group is resident, and when it unloads the renderer lets them go and their handles wait (the sky lights the scene, Stylise.palette quantises to none, PostEffects.lut grades nothing, og.render.sprite of the array and applying the look are refused, an og.Sprite, a flipbook's sprite or a particle emitter of the array draws nothing) until the group is resident again, when they come back under the same handles. One the frame still uses when its group unloads (the map Environment lights it with, the palette Stylise quantises to, an array a sprite, a screen sprite or a particle emitter draws from, the look last applied, the LUT PostEffects grades with) is never freed under the frame: it is kept, with a warning naming it in the engine's log, until the frame stops using it. What is kept still takes its memory: its bytes count in the budget's `used` (and `kept`, and its group's StreamStatus.kept) until it is let go, so a group that would not fit beside it waits.
Every change of a group's state sends StreamEvent at the start of the next tick; og.stream.status and og.stream.budget answer at once, and the probe's `dump_stream` lists the budget, the memory used and its peak, every group (trigger, state, why, since which tick, what it keeps for the frame after unloading with each asset's bytes), the recent changes, the terrain streamer's tiles and the fetch queue.
What streams is read through one queue: first the chunks of the sounds cooked in chunks that a playhead needs soonest (the one it is playing, then by the seconds until it gets there at its pitch, a loop's start by the time to its wrap), then the loading groups' packs by priority (then name). At most four reads are in flight at once (on the web, fetches; natively a read completes at once, so only the order shows); the rest wait in that order. `dump_stream`'s `fetch` lists what is in flight and what waits, each with its path and what it is for (a sound's chunk and its seconds, a group's pack and its priority).
World cells (G3-3) stream entities, not assets: an entity with an og.StreamCell and a sub-scene (a `scene "<id>"` line in its scene block, or StreamCell.scene from og.load.scene) is a cell. Its sub-scene's entities, and with them their colliders, bodies and everything else they carry, spawn when it loads, placed by the cell's transform (its top-level entities are roots, at the cell's transform after their own, so physics bodies among them are where they look) and each with an og.CellMember naming the cell; when it unloads, every member and its descendants are despawned. Whether a cell is loaded is decided as each tick starts, before any system runs, from world state alone: it loads while an og.StreamAnchor (a player, a vehicle) is within StreamCell.load of its box, unloads once every anchor is past StreamCell.unload, and stays loaded while StreamCell.pin is set. Without any anchor the og.Camera resource's position anchors, a convenience for a single-player game; a lockstep or rollback session (og.net) refuses that, since each peer's camera is its own. Cells load in entity id order and a sub-scene's entities spawn in its text order, so the same world spawns the same entity ids on both hosts, in a replay, a rollback and after a restore. A sub-scene's blob is in the boot bundle unless the sub-scene declares a cell group (`stream "<name>" { cell; asset ... }`): then the blob is in that group's pack with the assets it names, fetched ahead of the anchors (StreamAnchor.maxSpeed), and its models and textures draw their stand-ins until the group is resident. A tick that would load a cell whose blob has not landed is held, never skipped or reordered: frames go on drawing, the engine's log records each hold and how long it lasted, and `dump_stream`'s `hold` says what the tick waits for. Natively a read completes at once, so a native run or replay never holds.
A cell's state is world state: StreamCell.loaded, and its sub-scene's entities, are in snapshots, saves and the world hash, so restoring a save restores which cells are loaded and what is in them; an unloaded cell's entities are not in the world and come back from its sub-scene, as authored, when it loads again. Each change sends CellEvent in the tick it happens, and add hooks and `added` filters on the sub-scene's components see its entities arrive. The probe's `dump_stream` lists every cell (`cells`): its entity, sub-scene, state, entities and the ticks it last loaded and unloaded.

consts.name: STREAM_UNLOADED
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group is unloaded (StreamState unloaded).

consts.name: STREAM_QUEUED
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group waits for room in the budget (StreamState queued).

consts.name: STREAM_LOADING
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group's pack is being read (StreamState loading).

consts.name: STREAM_RESIDENT
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group's assets are in place (StreamState resident).

consts.name: STREAM_FAILED
consts.doc: `StreamEvent.state`: the group failed (StreamState failed; og.stream.status says why).

functions.name: status
functions.doc: One streaming group's state.

params.name: group
params.doc: The group's name, as its scene declares it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a group no scene declares.

functions.name: request
functions.doc: Ask for a group (any trigger) until og.stream.release: it loads from the next tick boundary, within the budget by its priority.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a group no scene declares.

functions.name: release
functions.doc: Stop asking for a group; it unloads at the next tick boundary unless its trigger still wants it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a group no scene declares.

functions.name: budget
functions.doc: The memory budget, what the groups take now, the peak and every group.
functions.returnsDoc: The budget and the groups; refused only for a world that does not exist.

functions.name: setBudget
functions.doc: Set the memory budget from the next tick boundary; a lower one evicts the lowest-priority groups until the rest fit.

params.name: bytes
params.doc: The bytes resident groups may take.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a negative or non-finite size.

x-og-modules.name: video
x-og-modules.doc:
Footage in a game (docs/design.md §2.9): a `type video` asset cooked by ffmpeg, loaded with og.load.video and played by og.VideoPlayer. A clip (the default, for short loops: at most 256 frames) is cooked into a texture array of its frames; a stream (`stream true`: any length) is cooked to AV1 and decoded as it plays, natively by rav1d on a thread of its own, on the web by WebCodecs, or by rav1d in a Worker of its own where the browser has no AV1 decoder (og.video.capabilities says which). Either way the frame shown is a Texture (VideoInfo.texture, also VideoPlayer.texture) any material map, og.Sprite or UI image draws, and the sound plays on the entity's og.AudioSource in step with it.
Playback is simulation, decoding is presentation: the og.video system (after the game's systems, before og.audio) advances VideoPlayer.time by the tick's dt times `speed` (not the time scale, so the picture stays with its sound; a paused game, whose ticks do not run, pauses both), so the frame a player is at on a tick is the same on both hosts, in every run and after a snapshot is restored. With a 30 Hz tick a player started at 0 is at the source's frame 3 s in at tick 90. A stream's texture shows that frame once it is decoded: an executor (og run, og render, og test) waits for it, so every capture shows exactly its tick's frame; a game on the web keeps the last frame decoded until it is, and nothing the decoder has or has not finished reaches the world.

functions.name: capabilities
functions.doc: How streams play on this host: the decoder, whether it is hardware and its largest real-time size.

x-og-modules.name: debug
x-og-modules.doc:
Debug draw: lines, boxes, spheres, arrows, axes and labels in the world, each for a number of ticks, drawn over the finished frame (after every post effect, before the UI) so they read in every capture and never hide behind geometry; and the debug views (physics, navigation, bounds, levels of detail, and the lit image's terms: shadow cascades, ambient occlusion, albedo, image-based and direct light) the command channel's `debug:` actions switch.
Development only: not in publish builds, where every member does nothing and answers its default, so a game may leave its debug draws in. Debug draw is rendering: it never feeds back into the simulation, and its draws are not world state (a snapshot or a replay does not carry them).

functions.name: line
functions.doc: A line from one point to another.

functions.name: box
functions.doc: A box's twelve edges, as three.js Box3Helper (turned by desc.rotation).

functions.name: sphere
functions.doc: A sphere as its three great circles.

functions.name: arrow
functions.doc: An arrow from one point to another, its head a fifth of its length (three.js ArrowHelper): a velocity, a force, a direction to a target.

functions.name: axes
functions.doc: A frame's three axes, as three.js AxesHelper: +x red, +y green, +z blue (desc.color is not read).

params.name: desc
params.doc: Width, duration and the frame's rotation.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: A label anchored at a world point, drawn in screen space at a constant size in the UI's body font (a world with no UI font draws none), centred above the point: an entity's state, a counter, a name.

params.name: position
params.doc: The point the label sits above.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Colour and duration (width is the text's size in CSS pixels, 14 where it is 2 or less).

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Remove every debug draw that is still showing.

functions.name: setView
functions.doc: Show a debug view besides og.debug's draws (the command channel's `debug:<view>`); none shows the draws alone.

functions.name: view
functions.doc: The debug view shown.

functions.name: setEnabled
functions.doc: Show or hide every debug draw and view (`debug:on`, `debug:off`); on by default outside publish builds.

functions.name: enabled
functions.doc: Whether debug draws and views show.

x-og-modules.name: assert
x-og-modules.doc:
Assertions: properties of the game checked as it runs, after the Antithesis SDK's. `og.assert.always(world.get(hero, Health).hp >= 0, "hp never negative", { hp })` holds on every call, `og.assert.sometimes(boss.phase === 2, "boss reaches phase 2")` must hold at least once in a run, `og.assert.reachable("door opened")` must run at least once, `og.assert.unreachable("fell through the floor")` must never run, and `og.assert.each(level, cleared, "each level cleared")` keeps one bucket per distinct key, each of which must hold once.
Each is identified by its name and the place it is called from (`src/player.ts:42`, which the build records for every `og.assert.<kind>(...)` call, so a site that never runs is still listed). A call that passes costs a lookup in the runtime, without a call into the engine; nothing an assertion does reaches the world, so a run with them hashes and replays as one without.
Violations and coverage go through the probe (`assertions`) into `og run --json`'s `assertions` and `og test`'s results: the tick, the name and place, and the values (`details`). At the end of a run, every `sometimes`, `reachable` and `each` bucket that never fired is listed as uncovered: a sometimes that never fires is a test that never got there. A playtest's `require` names the ones that must fire.
Beside them, every tick of a development or test build checks the default invariants from reflection: no NaN or infinity in a reflected float, a number inside its field's min..max where it declares one, no Entity field naming a despawned entity, and, where the world declares og.WorldBounds, every entity's place inside them. They read the components that changed (where the world tracks their changes) or every row, never write, and name the entity, component, field and value of their first failure.
Not in publish builds: every member does nothing there, so a game may leave its assertions in.

functions.name: always
functions.doc: The condition holds on every call: a false one is a violation, reported with its tick, its name, its place and `details`.

params.name: name
params.doc: What it means, in a few words: `hp never negative`.

params.name: details
params.doc: Values worth seeing when it fails, as `{ hp, damage }`.

functions.name: sometimes
functions.doc: The condition holds on at least one call in the run; one that never held is listed as uncovered when the run ends.

params.name: condition
params.doc: What must hold at least once.

params.name: details
params.doc: Values worth seeing at the first time it holds.

functions.name: reachable
functions.doc: This line runs at least once in the run; one that never ran is listed as uncovered.

params.name: details
params.doc: Values worth seeing the first time.

functions.name: unreachable
functions.doc: This line never runs: running it is a violation.

params.name: name
params.doc: What reaching it would mean: `fell through the floor`.

params.name: details
params.doc: Values worth seeing when it does.

functions.name: each
functions.doc: One bucket per distinct key (a level, a weapon, an enemy kind): each bucket the run saw must hold its condition once (Antithesis's SOMETIMES_EACH). Buckets seen that never held are listed as uncovered, and every bucket is in the probe's report, the hints a search of the game's states starts from.

params.name: key
params.doc: The bucket: a string, a number, or a small object of either (`{ level, weapon }`).

params.name: condition
params.doc: What must hold once in the bucket.

functions.name: record
functions.doc: The one call the members above make into the engine: a site's first call, a violation or a first firing. Game code calls those, not this. With null, it only answers the report's epoch.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world the assertion was called in.

functions.returnsDoc: The report's epoch: it moves on each time the probe's assertions member starts a new report.

x-og-modules.name: path
x-og-modules.doc:
Paths: a curve through or controlled by points, measured by arc length so a parameter t from 0 to 1 moves along it at an even speed however its points are spaced. catmullRom passes through every point (three.js CatmullRomCurve3, tension 0.5), bezier chains cubic segments `p0 c0 c1 p1 c2 c3 p2 ...` (three.js CubicBezierCurve3 in a CurvePath), linear joins the points with straight segments. A closed path joins its last point to its first and wraps t.
Make one with og.path.create, or declare it in a scene (`path "<name>" { kind catmullRom; closed false; point x y z ... }`) and find it by name with og.path.find; a timeline's camera rides one with `rail "<name>"`. og.PathFollower moves an entity along one, og.CameraRail.path moves the camera along one, og.render.tubeGeometry makes a tube along one (TubeGeometryDesc.path). Paths are assets: they are not world state, and a hot reload registers them again.

functions.name: create
functions.doc: Make a path from points.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The points, kind, closed and tension.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for too few points for the kind (bezier needs 3n + 1 open, 3n closed) or a point that is not finite.

functions.name: find
functions.doc: A path a loaded scene declares (`path "<name>" { ... }`), by name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The path's name in its scene.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a name no spawned scene declares; the reason lists the names.

functions.name: sample
functions.doc: The point at arc-length parameter t: 0 the start, 1 the end (a closed path wraps, an open one clamps). Equal steps of t are equal lengths along the curve.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead path.

functions.name: length
functions.doc: Its length along the curve.
functions.returnsDoc: Metres; refused for a dead path.

functions.name: nearest
functions.doc: The point of the path nearest a point, with its parameter: snapping to a track, projecting a pointer onto a rail.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead path.

x-og-modules.name: timeline
x-og-modules.doc:
Timelines: cutscenes and sequences as data, Unity's Timeline and Godot's AnimationPlayer as an `.ogt` the agent reads and diffs. A `type timeline` file has a `duration` in seconds, `path "<name>" { ... }` blocks (as og.path's) and `track <kind> ["<entity>"] { key <seconds> { ... } }` blocks; `og cook` cooks it (importing caption files) and og.load.timeline loads it. Tracks: `camera` (position and target keys, or `rail "<path>"` with `at` 0..1 along it, or `follow "<entity>"` with offsets; fov; eased), `transform "<entity>"` (position, rotation in degrees or quaternion, scale; eased), `animation "<entity>"` (clip, speed, blendIn, loop; `model` names the glTF whose clips they are, else the entity's og.Model), `audio` (sound, volume, playbackRate, bus), `music` (sound, volume, fadeIn, fadeOut, end, loop, bus), `caption` (text from `key` to `end` with a UI type step `style` and an `anchor`; `captions "narration.srt" [offset]` imports a SubRip file or word timestamps `.json`), `event` (`do "<command-channel action>"`: teleport, set, a game's registered command; `retroactive true` runs it when a seek passes it), `transition` (kind cut, fade, wipe, dissolve, iris or slide; mode through, in or out; duration, color, from, over og.ui's screen cover) `marker` (`name`, sending og.TimelineMarker when played past), `property ["<entity>"]` (`field "og.PointLight.distance"`, keys of `value`: any reflected field of a component on the entity, or of a resource without one), `light "<entity>"` (its og.DirectionalLight, og.PointLight, og.SpotLight, og.RectLight or og.Light2D: color, intensity, distance, angle, ...), `visibility "<entity>"` (`visible true|false` of whatever it draws, stepped), `post` (og.PostEffects' fields), `blendshape "<entity>"` (og.Blendshapes w0 to w7; its source becomes component), `material "<entity>"` (its og.Mesh's material, or its og.Model's material `index N`: StandardMaterialDesc fields by name, other names the material shader's parameters) and `timeline` (`play "<timeline>"`, speed, loop: from its key until the next, another timeline plays nested at (time − key) × speed, its markers sent as `<file>/<marker>`, at most four deep) and `shot` (`camera "<entity>"`, a virtual camera's name, or `none`; `blend` seconds and `ease`: from its key until the next, that og.VirtualCamera is og.CameraBrain.solo, blended to over the key's blend by its ease or by the camera's own; `none` and the timeline's end hand back the solo it found). Camera keys also take `roll` (degrees about the view direction), `focus` (a distance) or `focusOn "<entity>"` and `focusRange`, which set og.PostEffects' depth of field while the track owns the camera. The cook checks every field against the engine's records (a field the record lacks, one a timeline cannot drive, a value of the wrong shape) and refuses nesting in a cycle or deeper than four; a track kind this engine does not read is refused naming it and the engine's version.
Between two keys that set a value the later key's `ease` (og.tween's Ease names, linear when it gives none) mixes them; before the first and after the last the value is held. Every value is evaluated at the timeline's time, never accumulated over ticks, and that time is kept exactly (in steps of a thousandth of a tick), so seeking to a time and playing to it give the same world: a seek is how a video render starts at any frame.
An og.Timeline component plays one on its entity, run by the engine's og.timeline system after the game's systems (and tweens) and before og.anim and physics, so what it sets is what animation, physics and the frame see that tick. While one with a camera track plays (or is paused) it owns og.Camera, and hands back the camera it found when it stops or ends. Its event keys' actions run at the start of the next tick, as og.ai's commands do. Loading a timeline (og.load.timeline, outside a system) grants og.timeline the records its tracks write; values they wrote stay when it stops, while the camera, its depth of field and the materials go back. A material track is presentation, not world state: it is applied every frame from the timeline's time, so a restored save draws the right material on its next frame. The command channel plays them too: `timeline:play:<name>` (`timelines/<name>.ogt`, or an asset id), `timeline:seek:<seconds>[:<name>]`, `timeline:pause[:<name>]`, `timeline:resume[:<name>]`, `timeline:stop[:<name>]`.

functions.name: info
functions.doc: What a loaded timeline holds.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a timeline not loaded in this world.

functions.name: play
functions.doc: Play the entity's og.Timeline from its time (0 after a stop or an end); systems may call it, it takes effect at this tick's og.timeline.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.Timeline, or one whose asset is not loaded.

functions.name: pause
functions.doc: Hold the entity's og.Timeline where it is (it keeps the camera).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.Timeline.

functions.name: seek
functions.doc: Jump to a time: this tick evaluates every track there exactly as playing to it would, without sending the markers or running the events passed (except `retroactive` ones).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.Timeline or a time outside 0 to its duration.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Stop at 0: the camera is handed back, its sounds and music stop, its caption and cover go.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.Timeline.

x-og-modules.name: net
x-og-modules.doc:
Deterministic lockstep over a room (docs/design.md §2.10): every peer runs the whole world, and what crosses the room is each player's input, one per tick, and the world's hash. Turn it on with og.Lockstep (`enabled`, `players`); join a room (og.platform.roomJoin, or `og run --room ws://127.0.0.1:P/<room>` with `og relay` natively). Until the room holds `players` peers the world runs freely on each (a lobby, the local input driving the local player); then the authority (the lowest peer number) starts: every other peer takes its world's snapshot, the seats go to the peers in number order, and from then on tick t runs only when every seated player's input for t is in. Once the room is full, the other peers' worlds hold for that snapshot (for at most stallTimeout, 5 s when it is 0), so a slow authority's start does not find them far into a lobby it replaces. A peer that joins a running room takes a free seat (or watches) from a snapshot a running peer hands it.
Inputs are og.PlayerInput: one entity per player carries it with `player` set to its seat; the engine writes every other field at the start of each tick from that seat's input for the tick. A system reads the inputs from og.PlayerInput, never from og.Input, and gives this peer's own with og.net.submit (from a system that reads og.Input: what the local player holds now, sent for the tick inputDelay ticks on). Without a room, or with lockstep off, og.net.submit drives the local player's og.PlayerInput the next tick, so the same game plays alone.
Rollback (og.Lockstep.mode `rollback`, maxPrediction) keeps the same seats, inputs and hashes but does not wait for a late input: the tick runs on a prediction (the player's last input) and, when the real one differs, the world is rewound to the engine's own snapshot of that tick and runs forward again in the same frame, sounds played once and the view snapped. The peers agree on the confirmed world (og.net.finalHash); og.net.resimulating tells a game's own presentation that a tick runs again. Inputs cross the room unreliably and are repeated until acknowledged, so a lost message costs time, not the room.
A peer that goes silent (a frozen tab, a lost connection the room has not noticed yet) is reported as og.PeerStalled after a second, and dropped after og.Lockstep.stallTimeout: the authority (the lowest running peer that is not itself silent) agrees with every other running peer how far the seat's inputs reach, and every peer empties the seat from the tick after its last input, so og.SeatDropped arrives at one tick everywhere and the room plays on; a peer that leaves the room is dropped the same way at once. A dropped seat's input is empty (og.PlayerInput's zero value), so a held move or fire stops; a game that wants a bot there reads og.SeatDropped and drives that seat itself. With og.Lockstep.rejoin a dropped player that comes back (the same peer, or a newcomer of the same name) takes its seat again from the authority's world, og.SeatRejoined at one tick on every peer. Wall time decides only when a peer is reported and dropped, never what the confirmed world is.
Every tick each peer hashes its world without its own session (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad, og.PointerLock, og.Audio, og.Camera, og.Lockstep, the gameplay actions of og.input, the input, room, platform, asset and stream events, the UI's focus and hover) and every hashEvery ticks sends the hashes since its last batch; the first tick whose hashes differ is reported once as og.Desync, and the probe's `desync` dump (`dump_desync`) names it with the component-level diff of the two peers' snapshots of that tick: the answer to what is not deterministic (Math.random, Date.now, a wall clock, iteration over a Set of objects, a module variable, input read from og.Input or og.input's actions).

functions.name: submit
functions.doc: Give this peer's player's input: in lockstep, for the tick inputDelay ticks from the one running (sent to every peer when the tick ends); otherwise, for the next tick. It holds until the next call, so a game calls it once a tick from a system that reads og.Input (or og.Gamepad, or the UI's touch controls). Callable from a system.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an axis that is not finite.

functions.name: shape
functions.doc: Give the room a game's own input shape: a component of the game's in place of og.PlayerInput, and commands (an RTS's orders, a card played, a unit built) that act on one tick only, never repeated by a prediction. Call it in setup or start, outside a system and before the room starts, the same on every peer: a peer whose shape differs is refused the room's start. Without a call, og.PlayerInput and no commands.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The input component, the command component and the most commands per tick.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused inside a system, while lockstep runs, or for a component that is not a game's own with a u32 `player` field.

functions.name: submitInput
functions.doc: Give this peer's player's input when og.net.shape named an input component: its fields as og.net.submit's (`player` and `tick` are the engine's). It holds until the next call. Callable from a system.

params.name: value
params.doc: Its fields; omitted ones take their defaults.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for another component than the shape's, or a field that does not fit.

functions.name: command
functions.doc: Give a command for this peer's player: in lockstep, for the tick inputDelay ticks on (with this tick's input), sent once and read on every peer by og.net.commands at that tick; alone, or with lockstep off, at the next tick. Given while a rollback re-simulates a tick it is ignored (its first run gave it already). Callable from a system.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused with no command shape, for another component, or past maxCommands this tick.

functions.name: commands
functions.doc: The commands every seat gave for the tick now running, the same list on every peer: by seat, then in the order given, each with `player` set to its seat. Empty without a command shape. Callable from a system.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for another component than the shape's.

functions.name: status
functions.doc: Lockstep on this peer: running, the seats and who it waits for.

functions.name: resimulating
functions.doc: Whether the tick running is a rollback's re-simulation: the world was rewound and this tick runs again, so its presentation already happened once. The engine already plays each sound once and snaps the view; a game that triggers its own presentation from a system (a screen shake, a haptic) checks this first. False in lockstep and alone. Callable from a system.

functions.name: finalHash
functions.doc: The shared hash (og.net.hash) of the final world of `tick`, hex: the world every peer agrees on once each input for the ticks before it arrived, kept for the last 1024 final ticks while hashing (hashEvery above 0). In lockstep every tick run is final; in rollback a tick is final some ticks after it first ran. Null before the tick is final, after it is no longer kept, or outside lockstep.

params.name: tick
params.doc: The tick, in ticks: the world after tick - 1 ran, as og.Time.tick reads.

functions.name: hash
functions.doc: The world's shared hash now, hex: the hash lockstep compares, which leaves this peer's session out (og.Input, og.Lockstep, input and room events, the UI's focus; module docs). Two peers at the same tick agree on it exactly when their simulations agree; the world dump's `hash` covers everything and differs between peers.

x-og-modules.name: art
x-og-modules.doc:
A game's art contract: what every asset of its style holds, as seven resources a look sets beside the render ones (docs/art.md §2.1): the palette its texels sit on (ArtPalette), one pixel size for 2D art (ArtPixels), one texel density for 3D surfaces (ArtTexels), the shape language of its models (ArtShape), its line (ArtLine), the step of its motion (ArtMotion) and its camera (ArtCamera). A style is the assets, not a filter on the frame: the look's render resources treat the frame, these say what the assets themselves must be.
Every field is no constraint at its zero value (0, false, the first variant, an empty list), so a look without these blocks, and every game made before them, cooks and draws exactly as before. The built-in presets (templates/looks/<slug>.ogt) carry each catalogue style's values and a game's look overrides them field by field. They are resources, so game code reads the contract too (a sprite snapping to ArtPixels.unit, a spawner picking colours from ArtPalette); project.ogt's `look` names the look whose contract the cook reads. Writing them changes neither the frame nor the simulation: the cook's conformance of assets, the runtime defaults from them and og style check are docs/art.md §2.3 to §2.5.

x-og-modules.name: motion
x-og-modules.doc:
Generated motion for humanoids: the engine's motion model (a 17.6M-parameter student distilled from NVIDIA MotionBricks, og-motion) moves a character between the goals the game gives it, on the GPU. Give an entity with an og.Skeleton (a humanoid rig og.anim.humanoid recognises, or one an og.MotionAgent.rig names) an og.MotionAgent, then queue goals: og.motion.pose (a pose of the model's library where the character stands), og.motion.place (a pose at a place, facing a heading), og.motion.face (turn to a heading), og.motion.walkTo (walk or run to a point) and og.motion.jump (a jump whose arc the simulation owns). og.motion.poses lists the library: idle, walk, run, jump, crouch, wave, cheer.
**Presentation only.** The generated pose is drawn, never simulated (docs/design.md §2.4): it replaces og.anim's joint palette when the frame is drawn, and nothing a tick reads (og.anim's pose, its joint queries, root motion, physics, the world hash) depends on it, so a run is deterministic on every GPU. Game logic never reads og.motion's poses or presentation: the model's results are applied when they come back, so what a frame draws may vary run to run (a capture, an og test screenshot, a reference frame or a fork check waits for every result due by its tick, and reproduces). A simulation that needs a pose reads og.anim's, which og.motion never changes; og.motion.setBackend cpu runs the model on the CPU instead. A development build logs a warning when a system reads og.motion.presentation on the gpu backend. The model never moves the character: og.Transform is its root, always. With og.MotionAgent.drive the og.motion system moves the Transform to the goals itself with fixed math inside the tick (walkTo at its speed along a straight line, place over its duration, face at turnSpeed), and the generated pose is re-rooted onto the Transform, its planted feet absorbing the difference; without drive the game moves the Transform (its own physics, path or controller) and the character's motion follows it (walking, running or standing by how fast it moves). No model root motion ever reaches the simulation.
**Goals are the game's.** A goal is current from the tick it starts until it ends by fixed rules (walkTo when the mover arrives, pose, place and face after their duration), then the next queued one starts; og.motion.status answers the queue and the current goal, never the model's progress, so game code may branch on it. og.motion.presentation reports visual readiness for a host cover; game logic must not branch on it. The probe's `dump_motion` also reports readiness, generated frames, batches and timings.
**The model.** Its weights (35 MB in f16) ship inside @origingame/engine; `og cook` writes them as an optional file, cooked/motion/model.ogb, only for a project that uses og.motion (the manifest names it), and the engine reads and uploads it in the background as soon as the bundle is open, before any agent needs it (natively on a thread of its own; on the web a fetch after the boot bundle, never in it). The model runs on the GPU beside the renderer (in the engine Worker on the web): one batch for every agent at once, submitted in slices of about 3 ms of GPU time a frame, so a batch never costs a frame its vsync, and decoded a few characters a frame. Until the weights are resident, or when they fail to load, og.motion.capabilities answers backend none and each agent is drawn as og.anim poses it: its og.AnimationPlayer or og.AnimationGraph is the fallback, so give it an idle or walk clip.

functions.name: pose
functions.doc: Queue a library pose where the character stands, after its other goals.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The pose and how long it is current.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent or a pose the library lacks (og.motion.poses).

functions.name: place
functions.doc: Queue a library pose at a place and heading; needs og.MotionAgent.drive (the mover takes the Transform there).

params.name: desc
params.doc: The pose, place, heading and duration.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent or without drive, a pose the library lacks, or a position that is not finite.

functions.name: face
functions.doc: Queue a turn to a heading where the character stands; needs og.MotionAgent.drive.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The heading and the least time the goal is current.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent or without drive.

functions.name: walkTo
functions.doc: Queue a walk (or a run, above 2.5 m/s) to a point; needs og.MotionAgent.drive. The mover travels in a straight line, gains speed at acceleration up to speed, brakes at deceleration to stop at the target (or to the speed the next queued walk or jump starts at), and turns at turnSpeed. With a CharacterController it writes the controller's move input before physics; collision and ground height remain the controller's. The goal ends on actual arrival and completion of arrivalHeading, when supplied.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Where, how fast, and the pose on arrival.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent or without drive, or a position that is not finite.

functions.name: jump
functions.doc: Queue a jump after the agent's other goals; needs og.MotionAgent.drive. Takeoff, height, flight and landing are the simulation's (the controller's with an og.CharacterController, a fixed ballistic arc without one), deterministic and in snapshots; the motion model only draws it. A jump cleared in the air without a controller holds where it is.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent or without drive, a pose the library lacks, or a height, distance, heading or time that is out of range or not finite.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Drop the agent's goals, the current one included: the character holds where it is.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent.

functions.name: lookAt
functions.doc: Replace the timed look overlay without interrupting locomotion. Empty desc releases it. State is snapshotted and advances only on ticks; the turn is applied after generated motion or the animation fallback, on both hosts.

params.name: entity
params.doc: An entity with an og.MotionAgent and humanoid og.Skeleton.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a missing agent, skeleton or mapped head/spine, or invalid inputs.

functions.name: react
functions.doc: Replace the authored reaction overlay without discarding locomotion goals. Empty desc releases it. A motion-action asset names a humanoid clip and rig, hold interval and optional head-local hand contact. The hand is solved after the look so it stays on the hood.

params.name: entity
params.doc: An entity with an og.MotionAgent and humanoid og.Skeleton.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a missing agent, skeleton, action or required bones, an invalid hold interval, or invalid inputs.

functions.name: status
functions.doc: The agent's current goal and queue.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent.

functions.name: capabilities
functions.doc: Where the model runs: gpu (or cpu with the opt-in) once its weights are resident, none before (loading) or when they failed to load. Asking starts the load when no agent has yet.
functions.returnsDoc: Never refused.

functions.name: setBackend
functions.doc: Where the motion model runs: a presentation setting of this engine, outside the world (a snapshot does not keep it). gpu, the default, runs it beside the renderer, cheapest per character. No tick waits for it: a result is applied when it comes back, as of the tick it was due, and until then a frame draws the poses it has, so live frames may vary run to run (what checks a frame waits for it, as the module's overview says). cpu runs it on the CPU across the lanes instead, each generation spread over the ticks before it is due (about 21 ms of CPU a generation natively, 23 ms in wasm), for a few characters. Set it before the first agent; a change later loads the model again on the other backend and every agent's generated motion starts again.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for none.

functions.name: presentation
functions.doc: Presentation-only readiness on both hosts. Game logic must not branch on this value: it depends on GPU timing and is outside snapshots and hashes; a development build logs a warning when a system reads it on the gpu backend. A host may keep its page or shell cover up while the agent remains in the world and warms, then lift the cover on ready or failed (showing reason). Never write a component, gate a goal or advance a tick from this answer. ready requires generated frames and their palette for the current rendered frame; authored fallback does not count. Available in the probe's dump_motion too.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.MotionAgent.

functions.name: poses
functions.doc: The model's pose library, by name: idle, walk, run, jump, crouch, wave, cheer. Fixed by the engine's version, known before the weights are resident, so a goal's pose is checked the same everywhere.
functions.returnsDoc: The names.

x-og-modules.name: destruction
x-og-modules.doc:
Props that break: walls, crates, pillars, glass. A model cooked with a `fracture { }` block (at the top of a `type model`, or in a glTF's import settings) is cut by the cook into Voronoi chunks bonded where they touch, and the chunks resting on its floor are anchored to the world. Give the entity that draws it (its og.Model) an og.Destructible: hits, og.destruction.damage and og.destruction.explode wear the bonds down, a broken bond splits the prop into islands, an island anchored to the world stays put and every other island falls as one rigid body, and a stress solver (NVIDIA Blast's) breaks what can no longer carry its own weight, so a wall shot out at its foot comes down.
**Deterministic.** Damage, bonds, islands and the stress solver are fixed f32 arithmetic in the tick (og.destruction runs after the game's systems and before og.physics), the chunks are world entities and the bonds' health is in a state block: snapshots, restores, replays and the world hash cover the whole fracture, on both hosts.
**What a game sees.** og.Fractured, the tick after, for every island that breaks loose (play a sound by its volume, shake the camera); each loose chunk is an entity with og.Chunk (its body is a dynamic og.RigidBody: query it, push it, despawn it). Its look: the og.Destructible's `breakFx` emitter bursts where each island breaks loose and `hitFx` at each damaging hit, each the material's own (dust for stone, splinters for wood, shards and glints for glass, a few sparks only for metal). Budgets (og.Destruction): a loose island (a body and the chunks it carries) smaller than `debrisVolume` despawns after `debrisLifetime`, and past `maxChunks` loose chunks the oldest islands go first.
**2D: pixel terrain.** An og.PixelTerrain is ground made of cells, Worms and Noita style: og.destruction.carve2d digs a round hole, fill2d builds ground back (or bedrock, which nothing carves), explode2d blows a hole and throws the ground round it as pieces, fracture2d breaks a piece (or a terrain with no bedrock) into Voronoi pieces. Each chunk of it collides as its smoothed outline (a static og.Collider per chunk, rebuilt only where a change touched it), ground cut loose from the bedrock and the bottom row falls as an og.PixelPiece (a dynamic body), and og.PixelDetached reports each. The cells, the pieces and the queued changes are world state, carried by snapshots, restores, replays and the world hash on both hosts; the drawn image is made from them each frame they change.
Props (og.Destructible) are the 3D profile's. The chunks of a dynamic prop (a crate with an og.RigidBody) fly with its velocity; a prop without a body, or with a static one, stands on its anchors.

consts.name: CAUSE_IMPACT
consts.doc: Fractured.cause: a collision's impulse (og.CollisionStarted) past the prop's impactThreshold.

consts.name: CAUSE_DAMAGE
consts.doc: Fractured.cause: og.destruction.damage.

consts.name: CAUSE_EXPLOSION
consts.doc: Fractured.cause: og.destruction.explode; PixelDetached.cause: og.destruction.explode2d.

consts.name: CAUSE_STRESS
consts.doc: Fractured.cause: the stress solver: a part that could no longer hold its own weight.

consts.name: CAUSE_SHATTER
consts.doc: Fractured.cause: a chunk with children (the fracture block's `children`) took three times the damage that breaks a bond of its cross-section, and broke into them: they fly free, each its own body, leaving a hole.

consts.name: MATERIAL_BRICK
consts.doc: og.destruction.material: brickwork in mortar (no-tension masonry: stands by its weight, steps back over its piers).

consts.name: MATERIAL_CONCRETE
consts.doc: og.destruction.material: plain concrete (strong, breaks in chunky lumps, holds what is left).

consts.name: MATERIAL_WOOD
consts.doc: og.destruction.material: timber boards (light and weak across the grain: splinters where it lands or is struck).

consts.name: MATERIAL_GLASS
consts.doc: og.destruction.material: a glass pane (shatters at a touch, no stress solver).

consts.name: MATERIAL_STONE
consts.doc: og.destruction.material: dry-laid stone (masonry with no mortar: no tension, heavier and tougher than brick).

consts.name: CAUSE_FRACTURE
consts.doc: Fractured.cause: og.destruction.fracture; PixelDetached.cause: og.destruction.fracture2d.

consts.name: CAUSE_CARVE
consts.doc: PixelDetached.cause: og.destruction.carve2d cut it loose.

functions.name: damage
functions.doc: Damage a destructible at a point: every bond, anchor and chunk within reach takes the amount, all of it within innerRadius and falling to nothing at radius. Applied by og.destruction after the game's systems this tick (in the order called), so a bond broken now splits the prop before this tick's physics step.

params.name: entity
params.doc: An entity with og.Destructible, or one of its chunks.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Where, how far and how much.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity that is neither, or a point that is not finite.

functions.name: explode
functions.doc: An explosion: damage to every destructible in reach (as og.destruction.damage), then a push outwards to their loose chunks. Applied by og.destruction this tick, as damage. Push other bodies with og.physics.applyImpulse.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its centre, reach, damage and push.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a point that is not finite.

functions.name: fracture
functions.doc: Break every bond of a destructible at once (this tick, as damage): its anchored chunks stay, the rest fall.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without one.

functions.name: info
functions.doc: How much of a destructible stands.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without one, or one whose model is not loaded or has no fracture.

functions.name: material
functions.doc: A material's og.Destructible tuning (MATERIAL_*): toughness, strength, friction, tension, density and how hard a hit must be to hurt it, measured against the props of the destruction-yard test fixture (a brick wall, a concrete pillar, a crate, a pane). Pair it with a model whose fracture block has the same `style` (brick, concrete, wood, glass).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a kind that is none of MATERIAL_*.

functions.name: capabilities
functions.doc: What destruction does on this device.

functions.name: carve2d
functions.doc: Empty a round hole in an og.PixelTerrain, this tick (applied by og.destruction2d after the game's systems, in the order called): the chunks it touches collide as their new outline before this tick's physics step, and what it cuts loose falls.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.PixelTerrain, or a point or radius that is not finite.

functions.name: fill2d
functions.doc: Make a round patch of an og.PixelTerrain solid (ground, or bedrock), this tick, as carve2d. Bedrock stays bedrock.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Where, how big and what with.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.PixelTerrain, or a point or radius that is not finite.

functions.name: explode2d
functions.doc: A blast on every og.PixelTerrain in reach, this tick, as carve2d: a hole of `radius`, the ring of ground `debris` wide round it cut into Voronoi pieces and thrown outwards, the islands it cuts loose and the pieces already in reach pushed outwards. Push other bodies with og.physics.applyImpulse.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a point or a size that is not finite.

functions.name: fracture2d
functions.doc: Break an og.PixelPiece (or every cell of an og.PixelTerrain but its bedrock) into Voronoi pieces, this tick, as carve2d: each piece is an og.PixelPiece moving as what it broke from moved; the piece broken is despawned.

params.name: entity
params.doc: An entity with og.PixelPiece or og.PixelTerrain.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity with neither.

functions.name: cell2d
functions.doc: The cell of an og.PixelTerrain under a world point, as the last tick left it: 0 empty, 255 bedrock, any other ground (fill2d writes 1). Outside the terrain, 0.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.PixelTerrain, or one og.destruction2d has not yet filled (the tick after it is added).

x-og-modules.name: vfx
x-og-modules.doc:
Composed effects: one effect (a fireball's impact, a heal, a level-up) as a timeline of elements in an `.ogt` of `type vfx`, Effekseer's and Niagara's systems as text the agent reads and diffs. A file has `duration <seconds>`, `loop true|false`, `event <seconds> "<name>"` and `impact <seconds>` (`event <seconds> "impact"`, at most one; the same four lines mean the same in a `type vfx2d` pixel effect), and element blocks, each with `at <seconds>` from the effect's start, `offset <x> <y> <z>` and `rotate <x> <y> <z>` (degrees) in the effect's space, `move <x> <y> <z>` (metres per second) and `accelerate <x> <y> <z>` (per second squared) carrying it from its offset from its start (an emitter spawns along the path), and `life <seconds>` or `until <seconds>` for those that last: `emitter "<id>"` (an og.load.emitter asset; `until` stops its emission and its particles live out; `seed`), `mesh sphere | quad | ring | box | cylinder | "<model id>"` (drawn with `effect "<id>"`, an effect material: `scale`, a value over its life, `spin` degrees per second, `color`, `blend additive | alpha`; a `ring` takes its own shape with any of `inner <radius>` (outer 1), `band <0..1>` (its middle row), `height <outer> <inner>` (its edges raised along its axis: a cone, a tube), `arc <start> <length>` (degrees from +x), `segments <n>` and `colors <outer rgba> <band rgba> <inner rgba>`, its u then along the arc and v from the outer edge to the inner, built at load), `trail` (`effect`, `width <head> <tail>`, `lifetime`, `color`, `orbit <radius> <turns per second>` and `rise <metres per second>` about and up the element's y), `beam` (`to <x> <y> <z>` from the element, `width`, `effect`, `segments`, `jitter`, `color`), `light` (a point light: `color`, `intensity` a value over its life, `distance`), `decal` (projected down the element's -y: `uv <u0> <v0> <u1> <v1>`, its region of og.RenderSettings.decalAtlas, `size <x> <y> <z>` with y the depth it reaches, `fade <seconds>` at its end, `color`), `flash` (a soft glow facing the eye: `size` a value over its life, `color`), `shake` (`trauma`, og.camera.shake), `flipbook "<id>"` (a pixel effect, an `.ogt` of `type vfx2d`, or any og.load.flipbook sheet: a camera-facing og.Sprite with og.Flipbook playing its first clip, `size` its height with the width by the frame's shape, `color`, `blend additive | alpha`, for `life` or its clip's length; its og.FlipbookEvent events, the impact frame among them, reach the game as this effect's og.VfxEvent of the same name) and `sound "<id>"` (`volume`, `playbackRate <min> <max>` picked by the seed; a child entity with og.AudioSource at the element, cut when the effect despawns). A value is a number, `random <min> <max>` (fixed per instance) or `curve <t> <v> ...` over the element's life. `og cook` checks the file and that what it names is in the project.
An og.Vfx plays one from its startTick at its entity's MatrixWorld, so an effect follows the entity it is spawned on (og.vfx.spawn with a parent) or stays where it was spawned. Its visuals are drawn from (asset, seed, startTick, the tick) alone: the renderer expands its elements every frame and nothing of them is world state, so a replay, a restore or a seek draws the same effect. Its gameplay side runs in the tick, in the engine's og.vfx system (scheduled when a game first names og.Vfx or og.VfxEvent, after the systems defined so far): each `event` line sends an og.VfxEvent on the tick its time lands on (startTick plus its time rounded to ticks; an effect started after og.vfx ran that tick catches up on the next), each `shake` adds its trauma and each `sound` plays, then an effect that has ended and does not loop despawns its entity and its sounds (unless `despawn` is false). Element times run on the tick.

functions.name: spawn
functions.doc: Play a composed effect now: a new entity with og.Transform (at the desc's position and rotation, a child of its parent when it has one) and og.Vfx started at this tick (world.tick). A system calling it writes og.Transform, og.Vfx and, with a parent, og.Parent. The entity despawns when the effect ends (og.Vfx.despawn).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an asset not loaded in this world or a dead parent.

functions.name: info
functions.doc: What a loaded composed effect holds.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an effect not loaded in this world.

Vector3.description: A 3D vector, as three.js Vector3. The engine is right-handed with +Y up, as three.js.

Quaternion.description: A unit quaternion rotation, as three.js Quaternion. The zero value is the identity.

Matrix4.description: A 4x4 matrix, as three.js Matrix4: sixteen elements in column-major order. The zero value is the identity.

elements.description: The elements, column-major, as three.js Matrix4.elements.

Color.description: A linear RGB colour, as three.js Color with colour management on. Components are usually between 0 and 1; above 1 is HDR.

direction.description: The unit direction the ray points in.

Box3.description: An axis-aligned box, as three.js Box3. A box whose min exceeds its max on an axis is empty (box3.empty() makes one: min +Infinity, max -Infinity).

Sphere.description: A sphere, as three.js Sphere. A negative radius is empty.

radius.description: The radius.

Plane.description: A plane, as three.js Plane: the points p with dot(normal, p) + constant = 0; normal is unit length, and the positive side is where it points.

constant.description: The signed distance from the origin to the plane, negated along the normal (three.js Plane.constant).

Frustum.description: A view volume, as three.js Frustum: six planes whose normals point inwards (right, left, bottom, top, far, near, three.js's order). frustum.fromCamera and frustum.fromProjectionMatrix make one.

FieldOptions.description: Metadata of one field. Ranges and units are what Tune and the probe's bounds show. Nothing clamps writes: world.insert and writes from outside the game (the probe's `set`, `patch` and sweeps, Tune, a look's fields at cook) are refused outside min..max with the range named. Game code's other writes (world.set, a resource field, a column) are stored as given.

unit.description: A unit name from the API's unit table, or empty.

label.description: The person-facing name; empty uses the field name.

doc.description: One sentence on what the field means.

tunable.description: Publish the field to Tune and to the probe's bounds and patch.

worldspace.description: Where a Vector2, Vector3, f32 or f64 field's numbers lie when og.WorldOrigin shifts the world: `world` (a point in the world, moved by every shift), `root` (in its entity's Transform frame: moved on an entity without a parent), `none` (an offset, a size, a direction), then optionally its axes (`world y` for an absolute height); empty for a field that is not a coordinate.

Entity.description:
An entity: an index and a generation. The value is index + generation * 2^32, with the generation below 2^21, so it stays an exact JavaScript number.
Generations start at 1, so 0 is never a live entity.

SpawnDesc.description: How to spawn an entity. `{}` spawns an unnamed entity at the origin with a Transform.

name.description: A unique name; the probe and the command channel address the entity by it. Empty leaves it unnamed.

parent.description: The parent entity; the new entity's Transform is then relative to it. It gives the new entity an og.Parent, so inside a system og.Parent must be among the system's writes (as og.Transform must, unless `bare`).

scale.description: The initial Transform.scale.

bare.description: Spawn without a Transform: a pure data entity.

source.description: Where a person would change it (`src/enemies.ts:42`), which the probe answers as the entity's source (pick, marks). Outside a publish build the runtime fills it with the game's own TypeScript line that called spawn (the first frame of the call's stack outside the engine and node_modules); a value given here wins, so a helper may name its caller. A publish build keeps none.

migrate.description: Map a type whose layout changed since the save field by field, by name, as a hot reload does: a field added since takes its default, a removed one is dropped, an enum value is mapped by its variant's name, a field of another type starts at its default, and a type this build no longer registers is dropped. Off, such a save is refused naming the type and its fields, except for the host's input the restore keeps (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad, og.PointerLock, og.Audio), which is mapped either way: a save from before og.Gamepad's eight pads restores without it.

session.description: Take the save's input too (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad, og.PointerLock: the keys, buttons and pointers held and this tick's edges) instead of keeping the host's. Off, a loaded game reads the keys the player holds now; on, the world is the one saved, hash and all, which a tool returning to a state needs (og explore, a replay from a snapshot). A selection keeps the host's input either way.

SnapshotDesc.description: What world.snapshot saves. `{}` (or no desc) saves the whole world; naming tags or resources saves a selection: the entities that carry every component of `with` (with all their components and names) and the resources `resources` names, nothing else. world.restore of a selection replaces the live entities that carry those tags by the saved ones (spawned anew, in saved order, a saved entity's Entity fields pointed at its new id) and sets those resources, and leaves the rest of the world (other entities, og.Time, the modules' state, the session) as it is: a game keeps its progress and settings this way and rebuilds the level from its scene. A selection is small (only the types it uses are in its table) and so takes fewer store keys.

with.description: The tags: an entity carrying all of them is saved. Empty with `resources` empty: the whole world.

resources.description: The resources a selection keeps (settings, progress).

SaveType.description: A type a save holds, as it was saved.

version.description: Its schema version when it was saved.

SaveRecord.description: One saved value of a type: a component of an entity, or (entity null) the type's resource.

entity.description: The saved entity, or null for the resource.

value.description: The value's fields by name, as saved.

into.description: The type to write them as, one this build declares; empty: the type itself (as this build declares it).

records.description: The new values; a field a record leaves out takes its default, a key the type lacks is refused.

TransformDesc.description: How SaveEdit.transform writes what it returns.

into.description: The type to write the results as, one this build declares; empty: the type itself.

SaveSpawnDesc.description: An entity a migration adds to a save.

name.description: A unique name; empty leaves it unnamed.

components.description: Its components by type name, each a value of the type as this build declares it (`{ "og.Transform": {}, Chest: { gold: 5 } }`).

SaveMigration.description: A game's save migration step (GameDesc.migrations): run on a save of version `from` on its way to GameDesc.saveVersion, after the engine's own migrations.

from.description: The save version it migrates from, to from + 1; from 1 to GameDesc.saveVersion - 1, each at most once.

WorldRestored.description: A world.restore applied: the tick after it (the first whole tick after a save taken mid-tick, whose next step completes the saved tick) delivers this, read through world.events like any event. Everything in the world came back as saved, request numbers and resources the session filled included; the session did not, so a system that reads this resets what belongs to the session: it forgets requests answered long ago, asks the store again for the settings and progress, and closes a menu the player had open. Sent as that tick starts, not when the restore applies, so the world between the two hashes as the save did.

from.description: The tick the world was at when the restore applied.

tick.description: The saved tick: og.Time's tick right after the restore.

QueryDesc.description: Which entities a query matches. The change filters (changed, added, removed) narrow an archetype's rows to those that pass every filter (ArchetypeView.rows) and read what happened since the last tick began; a component is tracked once a system filters on it (SystemDesc.changed, added, removed), and filtering on one no system tracks is refused.

without.description: Components an entity must not have.

changed.description: Components (required, as `with`) whose value changed: a write that leaves a value as it was is not a change.

added.description: Components (required, as `with`) added: spawned with, or inserted into an entity without them.

removed.description: Components the entity lost (removed; a despawned entity is in no archetype, so it is in world.removed only).

SpatialDesc.description: Which entities world.spatial places: every live entity with an og.Transform (and every component of `with`, none of `without`), at its og.Transform.position (relative to its parent, for a child).

with.description: Components an entity must have to be placed.

without.description: Components an entity must not have.

cell.description: The hash's cell size; 0 picks one from the entities' spread. Answers never depend on it, only speed.

Neighbour.description: One entity a spatial query found.

distance.description: Its distance from the query's centre.

StateWhen.description: When a system bound to a state machine's value runs.

x-og-variants.during: Every tick while the state machine holds the value.
x-og-variants.enter: Once, as the tick begins, when the machine enters the value (the first tick, for its initial value).
x-og-variants.exit: Once, as the tick begins, when the machine leaves the value.

StateDesc.description: A state machine (GameDesc.states): a name and the values it moves between; it holds one at a time, and world.setState moves it as the next tick begins. Its value is world state: saves, the hash and replays carry it.

values.description: Its values, at least one, each unique.

initial.description: The value it starts in; empty or omitted: the first.

SystemDesc.description: A system's declared access and order.

reads.description: Components, resources and events the system reads (world.events). Every component here is also required by its query: a matched entity has all of the reads' and writes' components.

writes.description: Components, resources and events the system writes (world.emit). Every component here is also required by its query, with the reads'.

without.description: Components a matched entity must not have.

after.description: Names of systems that must run before this one.

before.description: Names of systems that must run after this one.

changed.description: Change filters on the query: components (required, as reads) whose value changed since this system last ran. A change is a value that differs from the one last compared, compared after each system and hook for what it writes and as each tick begins for what was written between ticks: counted in system runs, never by a clock, so saves and replays carry it. The archetypes the query hands carry the rows that pass every filter (ArchetypeView.rows).

added.description: Components (required, as reads) added since this system last ran: spawned with, or inserted into an entity without them.

removed.description: Components the entity lost since this system last ran (a despawned entity: world.removed).

state.description: A state machine (GameDesc.states) the system is bound to; empty: none.

value.description: The value of `state` it is bound to.

when.description: When it runs: during the value, or once on entering or leaving it.

runIf.description: A run condition: the system runs only on ticks it answers true. A skipped tick is not a run: the change filters keep reading from the last one.

x-og-variants.add: The component was added (spawned with, or inserted into an entity without it): the hook runs after it is in place.
x-og-variants.remove: The component is being removed (removed, or its entity despawned): the hook runs before it goes, and reads it.

HookDesc.description: A hook's event and declared access.

reads.description: What it reads, as a system declares it.

writes.description: What it writes, as a system declares it.

GameDesc.description: A game: its tick, scenes, systems and commands.

tick.description: The fixed tick rate. Left unset, project.ogt's `tick` applies (else 60); tick, seed, scenes and scene set both here and in project.ogt to different values refuse the engine, naming both.

seed.description: The project seed every Rng stream derives from; left unset, project.ogt's `seed` (else 0). A replay overrides it.

scenes.description: Scene names to `.ogt` paths, as `{ main: "scenes/main.ogt" }`; left unset, project.ogt's `scenes` block.

scene.description: The scene loaded first; left unset, project.ogt's `scene` (else main).

systems.description: The systems, in declaration order before `after`/`before` constraints apply. -1 is skipped: the TypeScript runtime sends it for a token defineSystem did not make.

hooks.description: The hooks (og.defineHook), in the order they run. -1 is skipped: the TypeScript runtime sends it for a token og.defineHook did not make.

states.description: The state machines systems bind to (SystemDesc.state).

resources.description: The game's own resources, created at their defaults.

commands.description: Game actions registered into the command channel, by action name.

commandHelp.description: Each game action's argument form and one sentence, by its name in commands, for `help`: `{ place: { usage: "<x>:<y>", doc: "Move the hero there." } }`. An action without an entry is listed by name alone.

maxCatchUp.description: The most ticks one frame may run to catch up with the clock; the accumulator drops the rest.

facts.description: The game's own facts for the probe's state().

start.description: Called once before the first tick, after the first scene spawned. A throw fails the run: no tick runs on the half-built world, `og run`, `og test` and `og dev` exit non-zero naming the error with its stack, and the web shell shows it.

ui.description: Register retained UI after start and after a hot-reload restore. The engine checks world_hash before and after. Duplicate IDs, incompatible store types and gameplay writes fail registration as errors; ui never reruns start. Fresh-process restore runs start, then ui, then restores named presentation values.

render.description: How the renderer is created: antialiasing and shadow map size. Read once, when the host attaches the renderer.

saveVersion.description: The game's save version, written into every save: raise it when a release changes a saved type, and add the step from the old version to GameDesc.migrations. Left unset, project.ogt's `saveVersion` (else 1); the two set to different values refuse the engine.

migrations.description: The game's save migrations: world.restore runs each one whose `from` lies between the save's version and saveVersion, in order (rename a field, transform values with the old record in hand, drop or split a type, add an entity). A number is a step's `from` alone, as the TypeScript runtime sends it (the steps run in TypeScript). The save envelope must be og-save:3; earlier envelope formats are refused with both versions in the error, never converted.

explore.description: How `og explore` searches this game's states: what a cell reads and which inputs it presses. Left out, cells come from every field of the game's resources and components and the inputs from every button action and none of the intents. Read by the tool only; the engine and the world never see it.

look.description: A look (`looks/<name>.ogt`, og.load.look) applied after the first scene spawned and before start runs, so start may still change any of it; its antialias is the renderer's when render leaves antialias out. Left out or empty, project.ogt's `look "looks/<name>.ogt"` (the look whose art contract the cook reads) is applied when it has one, else none; the two naming different looks is refused (one value in two places).

ExploreDesc.description: `og explore`'s view of a game (GameDesc.explore): the state its archive of cells abstracts and the inputs it perturbs from them. Every field is optional.

cells.description: The fields a cell reads, as `Record.field` or a whole `Record` (a resource or a component): what tells two states apart. Empty: every field of the game's own resources and components. A named entity's fields count by its name, unnamed entities as their number and each field's set of values. Numbers are bucketed (an integer up to 16 by value, a number within -1..1 in eighths, others by power of two, NaN and the infinities apart), bools, strings and enums by value. The time is a cell's too, in 64 slices of the search's horizon, unless `ignore` names `@tick`.

ignore.description: Fields left out of cells (`Record.field` or `Record`): timers, counters and caches that make every state look new; `@tick` for a game whose state does not depend on when things happen.

actions.description: The actions it presses, by name. Empty: every button action the game defines (og.input.actions), each by its first key or pad binding.

intents.description: The intents it sends (og.input.intent's events): the recorded input a UI's controls stand for. None by default.

values.description: The payloads to send, as objects of its fields. Empty: drawn from its reflection (each enum variant, a ranged integer's values, both bools, a ranged float's min, middle and max; other fields at their defaults).

Transform.description: Where an entity is, relative to its parent (or the world).

scale.description: The scale, as three.js Object3D.scale.

Parent.description: The entity this one's Transform is relative to. Set by SpawnDesc.parent.

MatrixWorld.description: The world matrix the engine composes after the systems run, as three.js Object3D.matrixWorld.

WorldOriginPlane.description: The axes og.WorldOrigin moves the world's zero along.

x-og-variants.xz: x and z: the ground plane of a 3D world (heights stay absolute).
x-og-variants.xyz: x, y and z: a world that is also deep or high (space, flight).
x-og-variants.xy: x and y: a 2D world (its z, the drawing order, stays).

WorldOrigin.description:
Large worlds (R12): naming it keeps every place in the world near its zero. As each tick starts, before any system runs, when the focus is farther from the zero than `step` along one of the plane's axes, the whole world shifts by the multiple of `step` nearest the focus, so the focus is within half a step of the zero again: every Transform of an entity without a parent, and every field the API marks `worldspace`, moves by the same amount (a body, its contacts and warm starts, a path, a particle, a tween to a place, the camera), and nothing in the world sees a change but the numbers. Precision then holds however far the world goes, while the zero's own place is kept here, in f64.
The shift is world state, decided from world state alone (the focus's Transform, else the first og.StreamAnchor, else og.Camera.position), so a replay, a rollback, a restore and every peer of an og.net session shift on the same tick by the same amount; a session refuses the og.Camera fallback (each peer's camera is its own) and holds the zero until a focus or an anchor exists. A world that never names it keeps its hash and frames.
