Values a game keeps outside the marked fields (a world position in its own component, a key it set in an og.ai blackboard) are its own: OriginShifted says when to add its `delta` to them. 2D worlds shift too, on `xy`.

step.description: How far the focus may stray from the zero along an axis before the world shifts, and the grid the zero moves on (whole metres).

plane.description: The axes the zero moves along: xz (the default), xyz, or xy for a 2D world.

focus.description: The entity the zero follows (a player, a vehicle; a root). 0: the first og.StreamAnchor by entity id, else og.Camera.position.

off.description: Hold the zero where it is.

x.description: Written: where the zero is in the world, along x (a place's absolute position is its own plus this).

y.description: Written: where the zero is, along y.

z.description: Written: where the zero is, along z.

shifts.description: Written: how many times the world has shifted.

OriginShifted.description: og.WorldOrigin shifted the world as this tick started, before any system ran: every marked place moved by `delta`. Add it to the world positions a game keeps of its own.

delta.description: How far every place moved (a whole multiple of og.WorldOrigin.step along each axis of its plane).

x.description: Where the zero is now in the world, along x (og.WorldOrigin.x).

Time.description: The fixed tick's clock. Every value is a function of the tick count, so a replay sees the same numbers. The world keeps the time scale in a second resource, og.TimeScale (`scale`, `hitStop`, and `elapsed`, which is scaledElapsed), set through og.time.setScale and og.time.hitStop; read og.Time, which carries all of it. The probe's `get:og.Time` answers every field here, as a system's `time` does; `set:og.TimeScale.scale=0.5` slows time from a script.

tick.description: Fixed steps taken since load.

dt.description: The length of one tick: 1 / rate.

elapsed.description: Simulation time since load: tick * dt.

scale.description: Global slow motion, set with og.time.setScale: 1 is normal, 0.5 half speed, 0 stopped. Physics, animation, flipbooks and tweens advance by scaledDt; the tick itself, the UI, input and the probe keep their pace.

hitStop.description: Ticks of hit stop left (og.time.hitStop): while above 0, scaledDt is 0.

scaledDt.description: This tick's scaled length: 0 during a hit stop, else dt * scale. Move gameplay by it so slow motion and hit stop reach game code too.

scaledElapsed.description: Scaled seconds since load: the sum of every finished tick's scaledDt.

TimeGroup.description: Which time group the entity is in (0 to 15): its animation (og.anim, flipbooks, 2D skeletons), its scaled tweens and its og.nav agent advance by scaledDt times og.time.setGroupScale's scale for the group, and its og.ParticleSystem's particles at the group's scale. Physics stays on the global scale: a body in a slowed group falls at the world's pace. An entity without one is at the global pace.

TimeGroups.description: Each time group's scale on top of the global one, set with og.time.setGroupScale (every group starts at 1). Registered when a game first names og.TimeGroup or og.TimeGroups. Physics stays on the global scale.

scales.description: Per group, its scale (0 to 10); past the list's length 1.

Rng.description: The world's main random stream, seeded from GameDesc.seed (or the replay seed). Its state is part of every snapshot.

seed.description: The seed the stream started from.

state.description: The generator state; snapshot and restore carry it.

x-og-variants.perlin: Ken Perlin's improved noise (2002): 0 on every whole-number point, smooth between.
x-og-variants.simplex: Simplex noise (Perlin 2001, Gustavson's construction): fewer directional artefacts, cheaper in 3D.

FbmDesc.description: Fractal noise (FBM): `octaves` layers, each `lacunarity` times the frequency and `gain` times the amplitude of the last, divided by the amplitudes' sum, so the value stays about -1 to 1. One octave is plain noise.

seed.description: The stream's seed: `world.resource(og.Rng)`'s value `.fork("terrain").seed`. Each octave reads its own table derived from it.

frequency.description: The first octave's frequency: features about 1 / frequency apart.

lacunarity.description: Each octave's frequency over the last's.

gain.description: Each octave's amplitude over the last's (persistence).

threeD.description: Sample 3D noise at z (a slice that changes smoothly with z: animate it by moving z); 2D ignores z.

NoiseGridDesc.description: A grid of noise samples, row-major from (x, y), `step` apart: a height field, a biome map, a cave mask.

PoissonDesc.description: Points no closer than `radius` to each other, filling an area evenly with no grid look (Bridson 2007): trees in a forest, loot in a field.

radius.description: The least distance between two points.

attempts.description: Candidates tried around a point before it is done (more fills tighter).

CellRect.description: A rectangle of grid cells: column x, row y (from the top), width and height in cells.

BspDesc.description: A dungeon by binary space partition: the area is split in two along its longer side, again and again, each leaf gets a room and every split's halves are joined by an L-shaped corridor.

minRoom.description: A room's least side, in cells.

maxRoom.description: A room's greatest side; an area larger than it with its padding is always split.

depth.description: The most splits, down any branch (up to 2^depth rooms).

padding.description: Wall cells kept between a room and its leaf's edge.

rooms.description: One room per leaf, left before right down the tree.

cells.description: width × height, row-major from the top: 0 wall, 1 room, 2 corridor. og.tilemap.fill writes it into a layer (map the values to tiles first).

WfcTile.description: A tile for og.procgen.wfc: its weight and the socket on each edge. Two tiles may sit side by side when the sockets on their shared edge are equal (a road edge meets a road edge).

weight.description: How often it is drawn against the others that fit.

up.description: The socket on its top edge.

right.description: The socket on its right edge.

down.description: The socket on its bottom edge.

left.description: The socket on its left edge.

rotations.description: It also comes turned 90°, 180° and 270° clockwise (its sockets with it; turns that look the same count once).

WfcCell.description: A cell fixed before generation starts (an entrance, a river's source).

WfcDesc.description: Wave function collapse, the simple tiled model: a grid filled with tiles whose edges all fit. The cell with the fewest tiles left (ties: the first) is decided by a weighted draw and the choice spreads to its neighbours; a dead end restarts on a fork of the seed.

tiles.description: The tiles (with rotations, at most 1,024 variants).

fixed.description: Cells decided before the first draw.

wrap.description: The edges wrap round (a tiling texture).

WfcResult.description: What og.procgen.wfc made, row-major from the top.

RecordedIntent.description: One deterministic input, independent of presentation checkpoints. Replay it between ticks, when world.time.tick equals tick.

tick.description: The simulation boundary at which the input was sent.

layoutHash.description: The schema layout hash as an exact decimal u64.

payload.description: The reflected packed field bytes, each 0 to 255.

PauseIntent.description: An engine gameplay intent: apply scale at the next tick boundary. UI pause layers send this through the same recorded intent path as game controls.

scale.description: Simulation time scale; zero pauses.

InputDevice.description: A kind of input device: the set a glyph is drawn from, the device used last, and what a pad is. og.ui's UiDevice has the same values.

x-og-variants.xbox: An Xbox pad (and the family a pad whose kind the host could not tell is drawn as).
x-og-variants.switch: A Nintendo Switch pad (its south button is B).
x-og-variants.gamepad: A generic pad: glyphs name positions (South, East).

x-og-variants.button: On or off: down, pressed, released, held. An analog control (a trigger, a half axis) presses it at ActionDesc.threshold and lets go under three quarters of it.
x-og-variants.axis: One value, -1 to 1: A and D, a stick's x, a trigger (0 to 1), the wheel, the mouse's x movement (CSS px).
x-og-variants.axis2: Two values, x right and y up: WASD, a stick, the d-pad, a touch stick, the mouse's movement.

TouchZone.description: Where on the play surface a touch binding's touches must start, in fractions of it from the top left; a zone of no size is all of it.

InputBinding.description:
One binding of an action: a control, or a composite of parts (A and D as one axis, WASD as two). Controls are named by strings: a key code (`KeyW`, `Space`), `mouse.left`, `mouse.middle`, `mouse.right`, `mouse.x`, `mouse.y`, `mouse.xy` (the mouse's movement this tick, CSS px), `wheel.x`, `wheel.y` (notches of 100 CSS px), `pad.a` to `pad.home` (GamepadButton's names, any pad), `pad.leftX`, `pad.leftY`, `pad.rightX`, `pad.rightY`, `pad.leftTrigger`, `pad.rightTrigger`, `pad.leftXY`, `pad.rightXY` (a stick), `pad.dpad`, `touch` (a touch held) and `touch.xy` (a touch stick). A one-axis control takes `+` or `-` for its half (`pad.leftX+`: 0 to 1, a direction as a button).
Every y is up-positive in actions (W, the stick pushed up, the mouse moved up, the wheel scrolled up, a touch dragged up: +1), whatever the raw og.Gamepad says. A binding with neither a control nor parts is an unbound slot.

control.description: The control; empty for a composite or an unbound slot.

up.description: A two-axis composite's control for y = 1 (`KeyW`).

down.description: A two-axis composite's control for y = -1.

left.description: A two-axis composite's control for x = -1.

right.description: A two-axis composite's control for x = 1.

scale.description: Multiplies the value: the binding's sensitivity (a mouse look's 0.1, a stick's 2); negative inverts it.

invertY.description: A two-axis value's y is turned over (inverted look).

deadzone.description: A pad axis's dead zone for this binding, over the pad's (og.input.setDeadzones) when above 0: values inside it read 0 and the rest is rescaled to reach 1.

zone.description: `touch`, `touch.xy`: where a touch must start to count (empty: anywhere).

radius.description: `touch.xy`: how far a touch drags for a full deflection (0: 64).

ActionDesc.description: A gameplay action: a name the game reads instead of keys (`jump`, `move`, `look`), its kind and default bindings over keys, the mouse, pads and touch. Actions are read once per tick, before the game's systems, from og.Input, og.Pointers and og.Gamepad, so they replay with them; the player rebinds them (og.input.rebind, og.input.startCapture) and a settings screen lists them (og.input.actions).

actionMap.description: Its action map (og.input.setActionMaps): `gameplay`, `menu`, `vehicle`, or the game's own.

label.description: What a settings screen and prompts call it (empty: its name).

bindings.description: The default bindings, in slot order: the player's rebinding replaces a slot, reset brings these back.

threshold.description: Where an analog value presses it (a button; and an axis's down).

deadzone.description: A dead zone on its combined value (radial for two axes), after each binding's own.

holdMs.description: How long it is down before `held` (0: never), counted in ticks.

locked.description: The player cannot rebind it (pause, a debug key).

toggle.description: A button whose press turns it on and the next press off (a hold's alternative, XAG 107); the player may change it (og.input.setToggle).

down.description: Its binding is past the threshold (or its toggle is on).

pressed.description: It went down this tick (a press and a release between two ticks set both edges).

value.description: A button's strength (0 to 1: a trigger's travel), an axis's value, a two-axis value's length.

vector.description: A two-axis action's value (x right, y up); value and 0 for the others.

device.description: The device whose binding drove it last.

ActionInfo.description: An action as a controls screen lists it.

label.description: Its label (its name when it has none).

bindings.description: Its bindings now: the player's, else the defaults.

toggle.description: It toggles (the player's choice, else its desc's).

BindingConflict.description: Another binding a rebinding would share a control with: an action of the same action map (or another slot of the same action).

control.description: The shared control, as the new binding names it.

ConflictPolicy.description: What a rebinding does with a control another action holds.

x-og-variants.refuse: Change nothing and answer the conflicts (a controls screen asks the player).
x-og-variants.swap: The other action takes what this slot had.
x-og-variants.replace: The other action loses the control (its slot is left unbound).
x-og-variants.allow: Bind it anyway: both actions read it.

RebindDesc.description: A player's rebinding of one slot of an action.

slot.description: Which binding: 0 the first; one past the last adds one.

part.description: A composite's part to change (`up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `negative`, `positive`); empty sets the whole binding.

binding.description: The new binding; for a part, its control is the part's.

policy.description: What to do with a control another action holds.

applied.description: The binding changed (false: refused over conflicts).

conflicts.description: The bindings it shared a control with.

CaptureDesc.description: A capture of the player's next input for a slot of an action: a controls screen's "press a key". From the next tick every action reads nothing until it ends; what was pressed for it moves no action until it is let go.

slot.description: Which binding: 0 the first; one past the last adds one.

part.description: A composite's part (`up` of WASD); empty: the whole binding (a two-axis action then takes a stick or the d-pad).

timeoutMs.description: It cancels itself after this long (0: never), counted in ticks.

CaptureState.description: Where a capture is: waiting, done with the control it took, or cancelled.

done.description: It took a control: apply it with og.input.applyCapture (or show the conflicts first).

cancelled.description: The player cancelled it, or it timed out.

binding.description: The slot's binding with that control in it.

conflicts.description: What applying it would share a control with.

InputGlyph.description: A control's glyph, for prompts and a controls screen.

icon.description: The icon a style's set draws: `key.space`, `mouse.left`, `xbox.a`, `ps.cross`, `switch.b`, `pad.south`, `xbox.stickL`, `key.wasd`, `touch.stick`.

text.description: The text that names it: `Space`, `LMB`, `A`, `×`, `L Stick`, `W A S D`.

device.description: The device it is drawn for.

control.description: The control it names (a composite's: its parts', space-separated).

SensitivityDesc.description: The player's sensitivity and inversion of an axis action on one device class: a look action's mouse and its stick each have their own (a settings screen's Mouse sensitivity and Stick sensitivity sliders, Invert Y). Kept by og.input.saveBindings, forgotten by og.input.resetBindings; a world whose player set none saves and hashes as before.

device.description: The device class it is for: keyboardMouse (the mouse's movement and the wheel; inversion turns the keys over too), any pad family (every pad), or touch (a touch stick).

scale.description: Multiplies the value of the action's analog bindings on that class (the mouse's movement, the wheel, a stick, a trigger, a touch stick), after each binding's own scale: 2 turns twice as far for the same mouse movement. Keys, buttons, the d-pad and composites read whole.

invertX.description: The value's x (an axis action's only value) is turned over.

invertY.description: A two-axis value's y is turned over: inverted look (an action's y is up-positive, so the mouse moved up then reads down).

KeyLabel.description: A key and what the player's keyboard layout prints on it: `KeyQ` and `a` on AZERTY.

label.description: The character it types without modifiers, as the layout map gives it (`a`, `,`, `ö`).

MouseDesc.description: How the host reads the mouse while the pointer is locked (og.PointerLock): the player's setting, kept by the game with its settings (og.platform.saveSettings). Host only: none of it is world state.

raw.description: Raw input: ask the browser for the mouse's movement without the OS's pointer acceleration (requestPointerLock with unadjustedMovement), where it supports that (Chrome and Edge on Windows, macOS and ChromeOS); elsewhere the lock is the plain one and the movement keeps the OS's acceleration (MouseInfo.rawUnsupported). Takes effect at the next lock.

MouseInfo.description: The mouse as the host reads it (og.input.mouse).

rawActive.description: The lock now delivers raw movement: the browser granted unadjustedMovement. False while unlocked.

rawUnsupported.description: The browser refused unadjustedMovement (Firefox, Safari, Linux): its lock moves with the OS's acceleration. A settings screen shows the Raw input switch as unavailable then.

DeadzoneDesc.description: A pad's dead zones: what its sticks and triggers read as rest. The player's to set (a settings slider); og.input.saveBindings keeps them.

stick.description: The sticks' (radial for a stick's two axes).

RumbleDesc.description: A rumble of a pad's motors: output for the host, never world state (a replay does not repeat it).

pad.description: The pad, 0 to 7; -1 every connected pad.

ms.description: How long; 0 stops the pad's rumble.

GamepadButton.description: A gamepad button in the W3C standard mapping, in its index order (a is button 0).

x-og-variants.leftTrigger: The left trigger, as a button (its analog value is the leftTrigger axis).
x-og-variants.rightTrigger: The right trigger, as a button.

GamepadAxis.description: An analog input of a gamepad.

x-og-variants.leftY: The left stick's y, -1 (up) to 1 (down), as the Gamepad API reports it.
x-og-variants.rightY: The right stick's y, down positive.

KeyAction.description: What an injected key event does.

x-og-variants.press: Down, then up on the next tick.

PointerAction.description: What an injected pointer event does.

x-og-variants.click: Down, then up on the next tick, at the point.

PointerButton.description: A physical pointer button; `none` is a hover move.

x-og-variants.left: The primary button, or a touch.

Modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during a key event.

platform.description: Command on macOS, the Windows key on Windows.

KeyInput.description: A key event. `key` names the physical key as KeyboardEvent.code does: ArrowRight, Space, KeyA.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

PointerInput.description: A pointer event at a point in CSS pixels of the play surface.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one (the mouse, the first touch; what protocol 5 means), 1 to 4 further touches held at the same time (an engine extension). Omitted is 0.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

movementX.description: The mouse's relative movement since its last event (the browser's movementX), which keeps coming while the pointer is locked and x, y stand still: og.Pointers.movement sums pointer 0's over the tick for mouse-look. Omitted is 0. An engine extension of protocol 5.

movementY.description: The relative vertical movement (movementY, down positive). Omitted is 0.

PointerLockReport.description: The host reports whether the pointer is locked to the play surface now (an engine extension of protocol 5): the web shell sends one from the page's pointerlockchange, and a playtest can send its own; og.PointerLock.locked follows it.

GamepadInput.description: A gamepad's whole state (an engine extension of protocol 5): the shell sends one whenever a pad changes, and a playtest can send its own.

connected.description: Whether the pad is connected (omitted is true); a disconnected pad holds nothing.

axes.description: Left stick x, y, right stick x, y; each -1 to 1, y down. Missing values are 0.

triggers.description: The left and right analog triggers, 0 to 1. Missing values are 0.

device.description: The pad's family as the host tells it from the pad's id (xbox, playstation, switch, or gamepad for a pad it cannot place); omitted keeps what was said. Glyphs follow it.

WheelInput.description: A wheel or trackpad scroll at a point.

TextEntry.description: Typed or composed text (an engine extension of protocol 5): what the page's `beforeinput` inserted (a key's character, a paste, an input method's commit), or with `composing` an input method's composition so far. Raises TextInput events; the UI's focused text field takes them.

text.description: The text.

composing.description: An input method's composition, not yet committed: it replaces the composition before it, and empty ends it. Omitted is false: committed text.

A11yActionKind.description: What an assistive technology asks of a UI control.

x-og-variants.focus: Move the UI's focus to it (with the focus ring).
x-og-variants.activate: Press it, as Enter on it would (a text control takes the focus).
x-og-variants.increment: Step an adjustable control (a slider, a stepper) up.

A11yRequest.description: A screen reader's request on a UI control (an engine extension of protocol 5): the web shell's mirror of og.ui.a11y() sends it when a reader focuses, activates or adjusts a mirrored node. Raises an A11yAction event; the UI acts on it at the start of the next frame, against the last frame's controls (a path naming no focusable control of the topmost dialog is ignored; increment and decrement also take a stepper's spinbutton, whose buttons are the focusable controls).

path.description: The control's path, as og.ui.a11y() names it.

InjectedInput.description: One input event in the game's own vocabulary, as the probe's input() and playtest scripts carry it.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one (the mouse, the first touch; what protocol 5 means), 1 to 4 further touches held at the same time (an engine extension). Omitted is 0.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

movementX.description: The mouse's relative movement since its last event (the browser's movementX), which keeps coming while the pointer is locked and x, y stand still: og.Pointers.movement sums pointer 0's over the tick for mouse-look. Omitted is 0. An engine extension of protocol 5.

movementY.description: The relative vertical movement (movementY, down positive). Omitted is 0.

connected.description: Whether the pad is connected (omitted is true); a disconnected pad holds nothing.

axes.description: Left stick x, y, right stick x, y; each -1 to 1, y down. Missing values are 0.

triggers.description: The left and right analog triggers, 0 to 1. Missing values are 0.

device.description: The pad's family as the host tells it from the pad's id (xbox, playstation, switch, or gamepad for a pad it cannot place); omitted keeps what was said. Glyphs follow it.

text.description: The text.

composing.description: An input method's composition, not yet committed: it replaces the composition before it, and empty ends it. Omitted is false: committed text.

oneOf.description: A screen reader's request on a UI control.

path.description: The control's path, as og.ui.a11y() names it.

oneOf.description: The host's word on the pointer lock (og.PointerLock.locked).

Input.description:
The input state at the start of this tick (og-input's og.Input, version 2). Edges (pressed, released) last exactly one tick; read the state through the methods.
Key sets are 128 bits over og-input's KEY_CODES (KeyboardEvent.code names): code i is bit i % 32 of word i / 32. Button masks: left 1, middle 2, right 4.

pointerInside.description: Whether a pointer event has placed the pointer over the play surface.

buttons.description: Held pointer buttons, as a mask.

buttonsPressed.description: Buttons that went down this tick.

buttonsReleased.description: Buttons that went up this tick.

buttonsReleaseNext.description: Buttons a click releases at the end of the next tick.

keys0.description: Held keys, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

keys1.description: Held keys, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

keys2.description: Held keys, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

keys3.description: Held keys, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

pressed0.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

pressed1.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

pressed2.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

pressed3.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

released0.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

released1.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

released2.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

released3.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext0.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext1.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext2.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext3.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

Pointers.description:
Every pointer on the play surface at once, at the start of this tick (og-input's og.Pointers): a touch stick and a touch button can be held together. Pointer 0 is og.Input's pointer; ids 1 to 4 are further touches, in the order they landed (the lowest free id).
Edges last exactly one tick, as og.Input's do. Masks are bit `id`; read them through the methods.

heldMask.description: Pointers held down, as a mask.

pressedMask.description: Pointers that went down this tick.

releasedMask.description: Pointers that went up this tick.

releaseNextMask.description: Pointers a click releases at the end of the next tick.

movement.description: The mouse's relative movement this tick: the sum of the movementX, movementY of pointer 0's events since the last tick (y down), zero again when the tick ends. Mouse-look reads it: it keeps coming while the pointer is locked (og.PointerLock), when the position stands still. The web shell fills it from the browser's movementX/Y; headless, only injected pointer events with movementX/Y move it.

PointerLock.description:
Pointer lock for mouse-look (a first- or third-person camera turned by the mouse), as browser games ask for it with requestPointerLock: the game sets `wanted` (a system that writes og.PointerLock), the host hides the cursor and locks the pointer to the play surface, and og.Pointers.movement carries the mouse's movement each tick. Off by default.
On the web the shell reads `wanted` from each frame and asks for the lock on the next press on the canvas (browsers grant it only to a gesture, so the click that starts play takes it), releases it when `wanted` goes false, and reports `locked` from pointerlockchange: the player's Escape releases it, and `locked` goes false while `wanted` stays true, so show a "click to look" prompt then. While locked, og.Input.pointer and og.Pointers' positions stand still (the UI's hover stays where it was) and the mouse's buttons still press. Native runs (og run, og dev) are headless: `locked` stays false unless a script injects `{ kind: "pointerLock", locked: true }`. `locked` is the host's (session state, as og.Input is: a restore keeps it, lockstep peers do not compare it).

wanted.description: The game wants the pointer locked and the cursor hidden.

locked.description: The pointer is locked now, as the host last reported it.

Gamepad.description:
Up to eight gamepads at the start of this tick (og-input's og.Gamepad, version 2), in the W3C standard layout: on the web the shell polls the pads each display frame, maps a pad the browser does not map (Firefox, Linux, many third-party pads) through its table, and sends their state through the input ring, so a pad is world state and replays; it also maps pads to keys for games that only read keys.
Button masks are bit `GamepadButton` index per pad; edges last exactly one tick, and a press and a release between two ticks leave both edges set. Read them through the methods. Sticks and triggers are raw: dead zones are the actions' (og.input.setDeadzones). `devices` holds each pad's family as the host told it (og.input.padDevice).

devices.description: Each pad's family, four bits per pad (pad p at bit 4p): an InputDevice index (1 xbox, 2 playstation, 3 switch, 4 gamepad), 0 when the host did not say.

pressed0.description: Buttons of pad 0 that went down this tick.

pressed1.description: Buttons of pad 1 that went down this tick.

pressed2.description: Buttons of pad 2 that went down this tick.

pressed3.description: Buttons of pad 3 that went down this tick.

pressed4.description: Buttons of pad 4 that went down this tick.

pressed5.description: Buttons of pad 5 that went down this tick.

pressed6.description: Buttons of pad 6 that went down this tick.

pressed7.description: Buttons of pad 7 that went down this tick.

released0.description: Buttons of pad 0 that went up this tick.

released1.description: Buttons of pad 1 that went up this tick.

released2.description: Buttons of pad 2 that went up this tick.

released3.description: Buttons of pad 3 that went up this tick.

triggers1.description: The left (x) and right (y) triggers of pad 1, 0 to 1.

triggers2.description: The left (x) and right (y) triggers of pad 2, 0 to 1.

KeyDown.description: A key went down (a down for a held key is a repeat and sets no edge). Input events are sent between ticks and read by the next tick's systems.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

TextInput.description: Text typed or composed (an engine extension): the shell sends it from the page's `beforeinput` and composition events, the probe's `type:`, `compose:` and `commit:` from scripts. A text longer than 255 bytes arrives as several events in order. Key events still arrive for the keys; a text field types from these once a world has had one.

text.description: The text (whole characters).

composing.description: An input method's composition so far, not committed: it replaces the composition before it (empty ends it). False: committed text to insert.

more.description: Continues the composition of the event before it (a composition longer than one event).

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

PointerDown.description: A pointer button went down (or a touch landed).

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one, 1 to 4 further touches (og.Pointers).

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

PointerUp.description: A pointer button went up (or a touch lifted).

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one, 1 to 4 further touches.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one, 1 to 4 further touches.

movementX.description: The relative movement this event carried (movementX), CSS pixels; 0 when the host gave none. While the pointer is locked x and y stand still and only this moves.

movementY.description: The relative vertical movement (movementY, down positive), CSS pixels.

A11yAction.description: A screen reader's request on a UI control (an engine extension): the web shell sends it from its mirror of og.ui.a11y(); the UI takes it at the start of the next frame. A path longer than 255 bytes is refused.

path.description: The control's path, as og.ui.a11y() names it.

Camera.description: The camera the frame is rendered from. Rendering reads it after the tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

quaternion.description: Its rotation; the camera looks down its local -Z.

fov.description: The vertical field of view of the perspective projection.

zoom.description: The zoom factor, as three.js Camera.zoom.

orthographic.description: Use an orthographic projection (the 2D profile) instead of a perspective one.

height.description: The visible world height of the orthographic projection.

background.description: The clear colour, as three.js Scene.background. The default is the brand ink #14161b in linear RGB.

exposure.description: Exposure before tone mapping, as three.js toneMappingExposure.

trauma.description: Screen shake, 0 to 1, added by og.camera.shake and decayed by traumaDecay every tick (unscaled, so a hit stop still shakes). The offset and roll grow with trauma squared and follow smooth noise of the tick: visual only, a replay shakes the same.

traumaDecay.description: How much trauma drains per second.

shakeOffset.description: The largest offset at trauma 1, as a fraction of the view height.

punch.description: A zoom punch in progress (og.camera.punch): the view is narrowed by this fraction, decaying by punchDecay. Visual only.

punchDecay.description: How fast a punch springs back (exponential, per second).

kick.description: A kick in progress (og.camera.kick): the view is offset by this, decaying by kickDecay. Visual only.

kickDecay.description: How fast a kick returns (exponential, per second).

zoneActive.description: The followed entity is in an og.CameraZone: the view keeps inside zoneMin to zoneMax. Written by the og.camera system.

zoneMin.description: The zone the view keeps inside: its bottom-left corner.

zoneFromActive.description: A room transition is in progress from the zone zoneFromMin to zoneFromMax: the view scrolls from where that zone kept it to where the new one does.

zoneFromMin.description: The zone being left: its bottom-left corner.

zoneScroll.description: How far the transition has come, 0 to 1 (eased; 1 is settled).

zoneScrollTime.description: How long the transition takes: the entered zone's scrollTime.

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Camera.layers.mask: the frame draws the meshes, models, world sprites, particle systems, lines and points whose layers share a bit with it. 1 (layer 0) by default, as every object's.

OrbitCamera.description:
Orbits og.Camera around the entity carrying it, as three.js OrbitControls: a left-button drag on the play surface turns it, the wheel zooms, autoRotate turns it on its own.
Camera controllers are game-level systems the engine ships in TypeScript (og.systems.cameras); list them in GameDesc.systems: `systems: [...og.systems.cameras, ...yours]`. The first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.
The camera sits `distance` from the orbited point (the entity's position plus `target`) in the direction given by `azimuth` about +Y and `polar` from +Y, and looks at the point. Every angle is computed with deterministic arithmetic, so a replay moves the camera identically on every host.

target.description: The orbited point, relative to the entity's position.

distance.description: How far the camera is from the orbited point, as three.js OrbitControls' distance.

minDistance.description: The closest the wheel zooms in, as three.js OrbitControls.minDistance.

maxDistance.description: The farthest the wheel zooms out, as three.js OrbitControls.maxDistance.

azimuth.description: The horizontal angle about +Y; 0 puts the camera on the +Z side of the point.

polar.description: The angle from +Y: near 0 looks straight down, half pi is level with the point.

minPolarAngle.description: The smallest polar angle a drag reaches, as three.js OrbitControls.minPolarAngle.

maxPolarAngle.description: The largest polar angle a drag reaches, as three.js OrbitControls.maxPolarAngle.

rotateSpeed.description: Drag sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.rotateSpeed: at 1, dragging the play surface's height turns a full circle.

zoomSpeed.description: Wheel sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.zoomSpeed: at 1, 100 CSS pixels of wheel change the distance by a tenth.

autoRotate.description: Turn about the point on its own while not dragged, as three.js OrbitControls.autoRotate.

enabled.description: Read the pointer and the wheel; false keeps only autoRotate and the fields' own values.

dragging.description: Controller state: a left-button drag that started on the play surface is in progress.

pointer.description: Controller state: where the pointer was on the previous tick of a drag.

FollowCamera.description: Chases the entity carrying it with og.Camera: a third-person 3D view that eases towards a point offset from the entity and looks at it. Driven by og.systems.cameras; the first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.

offset.description: Where the camera sits relative to the entity: in the entity's own axes with followRotation, else in world axes.

lookOffset.description: The point the camera looks at, relative to the entity's position.

followRotation.description: Turn the offset with the entity's rotation, so the camera stays behind it.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up with a moved entity; 0 snaps it there every tick.

Follow2D.description: Keeps og.Camera on the entity carrying it in the xy plane, for 2D games: the camera moves only when the entity leaves the dead zone, eases by smoothTime (smoothTimeY for y when set) and, with clamp, stays inside the bounds; lookAhead leads it in the direction the entity moves. The camera keeps its z, rotation and projection. Driven by og.systems.cameras; og.CameraZone entities then keep the view inside the zone the entity is in.

offset.description: Where the camera centre sits relative to the entity.

deadZone.description: Half the width and height of the box around the camera centre inside which the entity moves without moving the camera.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up; 0 snaps it every tick.

smoothTimeY.description: The same for y alone (a platformer follows jumps more lazily than runs); below 0 uses smoothTime.

lookAhead.description: Lead the entity by its velocity times this many seconds (0: no look-ahead).

lookAheadMax.description: The largest lead along x and y.

lookAheadSmoothing.description: Roughly how long the lead takes to turn when the entity does.

last.description: Controller state: the entity's position on the previous tick.

clamp.description: Keep the camera centre between boundsMin and boundsMax.

boundsMin.description: The smallest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

boundsMax.description: The largest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

CameraZone.description: A rectangle of the xy plane (min to max, world units, not moved by the entity's Transform) that keeps a 2D view inside it while the entity followed by og.Follow2D is in it: rooms, arenas, a level's bounds. Of overlapping zones the highest priority wins, then the first in query order. The engine's og.camera system picks the zone after the game's systems (into og.Camera's zone fields); entering another zone scrolls the view across over the new zone's scrollTime, or jumps when it is 0. A zone smaller than the view centres it.

scrollTime.description: Seconds the view takes to scroll from the zone the entity left into this one (a room transition, eased in and out); 0 jumps at once. Visual only: the camera resource records the transition, so replays scroll the same.

CameraRail.description: Moves og.Camera along a spline through p0 to p(points - 1) (Catmull-Rom, through every point) to the point nearest the entity carrying it, easing by smoothTime: a corridor, a side-scroller's track, a 3D chase on rails. A perspective camera looks at the entity; an orthographic one keeps its z and rotation. Applied by the engine's og.camera system after the game's systems.

points.description: How many of p0...p7 the rail uses (2 to 8).

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up along the rail; 0 snaps.

path.description: A path (og.path.create, or a scene's `path` by og.path.find) the rail follows instead of p0 to p(points - 1): any number of points, catmullRom, bezier or linear, closed or not. 0 uses the points.

VirtualCamera.description:
A shot og.Camera can take, as Cinemachine's virtual cameras: a position (its own entity's, or following another entity), what it looks at, a field of view, roll and focus. The engine's og.camera system (og.CameraBrain) makes the enabled one with the highest priority live and writes its pose into og.Camera, blending from the previous shot over the incoming one's blendTime by its blendEase. This is the way to drive the camera in a new 3D game: a vcam with `follow` and `collide` replaces og.FollowCamera, and a cutscene or a dialogue switches shots by priority or og.CameraBrain.solo.
Registered when a game first names it, with og.CameraBrain and og.CameraCut: a world without virtual cameras keeps its hash. Its pose is tick state on every host, drawing on no randomness; it changes only og.Camera (and og.PostEffects' depth of field for a vcam with focus), which the simulation reads only if the game does. While a timeline's camera track plays, the timeline drives og.Camera and the brain waits. A vcam drives og.Camera after the game's systems, so do not also give the game an og.OrbitCamera or og.FollowCamera.

priority.description: Of the enabled virtual cameras the highest priority is live; of equal ones, the one enabled last (`activated`), then the first in query order.

enabled.description: Takes part in the brain's pick. Disabling the live camera blends to the next one.

follow.description: The entity it follows: it sits at followOffset from it, easing by smoothTime. 0: it sits at its own entity's og.Transform position.

followOffset.description: Where it sits relative to the followed entity: in that entity's own axes with followRotation, else in world axes.

followRotation.description: Turn followOffset with the followed entity's rotation, so it stays behind it.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long it takes to catch up with the followed entity; 0 snaps every tick. It snaps when it is enabled.

lookAt.description: The entity it looks at, at lookOffset from its position. 0: it keeps its own entity's og.Transform rotation.

lookOffset.description: The point it looks at, relative to the lookAt entity's position (and the point collision keeps clear from).

fov.description: The vertical field of view it gives og.Camera.

roll.description: A turn about the view direction, applied after the look (a Dutch angle).

focus.description: Depth of field: the focus distance it gives og.PostEffects (depthOfField on), handed back when no live camera has one. 0 leaves og.PostEffects alone.

focusRange.description: Depth of field: the range around the focus distance that stays sharp.

blendTime.description: Seconds the brain takes to blend to it when it goes live (0 cuts); below 0 uses og.CameraBrain's blendTime and blendEase.

blendEase.description: The curve of the blend to it: position lerped, rotation slerped, fov, roll and focus lerped by the curve's value at the blend's time.

collide.description: Keep a sphere of `radius` clear of colliders between the look point and where it sits: it pulls in towards the look point at once and eases back out over damping. Against the colliders as the tick started (og.physics' query view): it never moves a body.

radius.description: The sphere collision keeps clear.

damping.description: Roughly how long it takes to ease back out once the way is clear; 0 snaps.

collisionLayers.description: The physics layers collision considers (a collider counts when its layers meet these); 0 every layer.

eased.description: Controller state: the followed point after smoothing, before collision, in world space (a floating-origin rebase shifts it).

pull.description: Controller state: how far collision has pulled it in towards the look point.

activated.description: Controller state: og.CameraBrain.activations when it was last enabled (the later wins a priority tie).

primed.description: Controller state: it was evaluated last tick (enabled, live or blended from); one that was not snaps to its goal and, if enabled, takes the next activation.

CameraBrain.description:
Picks the live og.VirtualCamera every tick and blends og.Camera to it, as Cinemachine's brain: the solo shot if one is set, else the enabled one with the highest priority. A change of live camera blends from the previous camera (still moving) over the incoming one's blendTime by its blendEase; a change during a blend starts from the blended pose, so the view never jumps. The first live camera of a world cuts. With no live camera og.Camera is left where it is.
Registered with og.VirtualCamera. Its state fields are world state, saved and restored with the world, so a replay or a restore mid-blend continues the same blend.
Read and write it as any resource: `const brain = world.resource(og.CameraBrain)`; when `brain.ok`, `brain.value.live` is the live shot and `brain.value.solo = shot` makes one solo (0 releases it). A system that reads it lists og.CameraBrain among its reads, one that sets solo among its writes.

enabled.description: Drive og.Camera; false leaves it to the game (the vcams' state still updates).

blendTime.description: Seconds of a blend to a camera whose blendTime is below 0.

solo.description: A shot that outranks every priority while it is set (a cutscene or a dialogue close-up): an entity with an og.VirtualCamera, live even when it is not enabled; 0 releases it and the brain blends back to the highest priority. Anything else is ignored. og.story sets it for a dialogue line's `shot` and a timeline's shot track for its keys.

soloBlend.description: Seconds of the blend to the solo shot when it goes live (0 cuts); below 0 the solo camera's own blendTime and blendEase (then the brain's). A timeline's shot key sets it with solo; og.story sets it to -1.

soloEase.description: The curve of that blend when soloBlend is 0 or more.

from.description: The camera being blended from; 0 when the blend starts from a held pose (an interrupted blend).

blend.description: How far the blend has come, 0 to 1 (1: settled on the live camera); the weight is the curve at this time.

fromPosition.description: A held pose to blend from: its position, in world space (a floating-origin rebase shifts it).

activations.description: How many times a virtual camera has been enabled (og.VirtualCamera.activated).

focusHeld.description: The brain is driving og.PostEffects' depth of field and holds what it found: heldDepthOfField, heldFocusDistance and heldFocusRange, handed back when no live camera has focus.

heldDepthOfField.description: og.PostEffects.depthOfField as the brain found it.

heldFocusDistance.description: og.PostEffects.dofFocusDistance as the brain found it.

heldFocusRange.description: og.PostEffects.dofFocusRange as the brain found it.

CameraCut.description: The live virtual camera changed (sent by the og.camera system; read the tick after).

from.description: The camera that was live (0: none).

blend.description: The blend's length in seconds (0: a cut).

Geometry.description: Vertex and index data, as three.js BufferGeometry. Comes from a loaded glTF.

Side.description: Which faces are drawn, as three.js FrontSide, BackSide and DoubleSide.

RenderTier.description: The backend the renderer runs on; the probe's hello reports it.

x-og-variants.webgpu: WebGPU in a browser: the full feature set.
x-og-variants.vulkan-cpu: Native Vulkan on a CPU rasterizer (Mesa lavapipe or llvmpipe, SwiftShader): the executors' sandboxes. Frame times there say nothing about a player's GPU.
x-og-variants.none: No renderer (a sandbox without a GPU; natively also OG_RENDERER=none): the simulation, the dumps and the world hash are the same as with one, a screenshot step writes no PNG and reports its frame unchecked, and capture answers null.

Antialias.description: Antialiasing, as og-render's Antialias. RenderCapabilities.antialias reports what the device resolved.

x-og-variants.tier: The engine's default method, on every backend (WebGPU, Metal, Vulkan, DX12): 4x MSAA in a 2D project (project.ogt's profile 2d), where TAA's jitter and history blend would soften nearest-sampled pixel art; TAA in a 3D one.
x-og-variants.msaa4: 4x MSAA (what tier resolves to in a 2D project): sharp sprites and text, no temporal blur; FXAA where the HDR format cannot be multisampled.
x-og-variants.taa: Temporal antialiasing (what tier resolves to in a 3D project): a sub-pixel jitter per frame and a reprojected history; converges over about eight frames. RenderOptions.taaHistory and taaSharpen refine it.
x-og-variants.fxaa: FXAA: one full-screen pass over the tonemapped image (the overlay stays sharp), no extra samples and nothing to converge; softer than MSAA on fine texture.
x-og-variants.smaa: SMAA 1x high preset: perceptual luma edges, area/search weights and neighbourhood blending over the tonemapped image; the overlay stays sharp. No jitter or history; an alternative to TAA, not combined with TAAU.
x-og-variants.smaaT2x: SMAA temporal 2x: two quarter-pixel-jittered SMAA frames, reprojected with the engine's camera and object velocity and neighbourhood rejection. Resolves in linear display colour before stylisation and the overlay; first frame and camera cuts use only the current frame. Exclusive of TAA, TAAU and MSAA; render scale uses spatial upscaling. taaHistory and taaSharpen apply only to TAA.

PointShadows.description: How a point light's shadow map is stored, as og-render's PointShadows. RenderCapabilities.pointShadows reports what the device resolved.

x-og-variants.cube: Six 90 degree faces: six shadow passes per light.
x-og-variants.paraboloid: Two paraboloid hemispheres (below and above the light): two passes per light instead of six, coarser, and large casters' silhouettes approximate (their edges stay straight in the curved projection).

TaaHistory.description: How TAA resamples its history each frame, as og-render's TaaHistory.

x-og-variants.bilinear: One bilinear tap: cheap, slightly soft while the camera moves.
x-og-variants.catmullRom: A Catmull-Rom filter over 4x4 texels (9 taps): the history stays sharp under camera motion.

Upscaler.description: The temporal resolve under TAA (RenderSettings.upscaler), as og-render's Upscaler: what turns the jittered frame, drawn at the render scale, into the output. RenderCapabilities.upscalers names the ones this device draws. Without TAA neither runs: the frame is scaled bilinearly.

x-og-variants.taau: The engine's TAA resolve with temporal upscaling: one pass, a neighbourhood clamp of the history and the RenderOptions.taaHistory filter, then RenderOptions.taaSharpen. The cheapest; softer on thin geometry and ghosts a little more on disocclusion.
x-og-variants.fsr3: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 3.1's upscaler (MIT), in fp32 without subgroups so it runs alike on every host: depth-based disocclusion, locks that keep thin geometry and edges through motion, luma instability, Lanczos upsampling and RCAS sharpening (taaSharpen's strength). Transparent surfaces (the order-independent transparency's coverage) feed its reactive mask, so particles and glass do not smear. More GPU time than taau (docs/design.md §11 has the measurements).

DebugView.description: What the debug overlay shows besides og.debug's draws (og.debug.setView, RenderOptions.debugView, `debug:<view>`), drawn over the finished frame; the lit image's views (cascades, ao, albedo, iblDiffuse, iblSpecular, direct, aoDepth, aoRaw) draw in place of the lit image instead, for looking at one term of the lighting. Streams add views as they add what to show.

x-og-variants.physics: The colliders' shapes, joints and contacts as the last physics step left them.
x-og-variants.nav: The navigation grids (blocked cells) and navmeshes (polygon edges), and every og.NavAgent's path.
x-og-variants.bounds: Every drawn mesh's bounds (its geometry's box at its transform).
x-og-variants.lod: Every og.Model tinted by the level of detail it draws (green the full mesh, yellow level 1, orange level 2, red level 3 and beyond), so the levels' distances read in one frame.
x-og-variants.cascades: In place of the lit image: each lit pixel coloured by the directional light's shadow cascade that covers it (red, green, blue, yellow for cascades 0 to 3; black beyond the last).
x-og-variants.ao: In place of the lit image: the screen-space ambient occlusion term (white unoccluded), with PostEffects.ao set.
x-og-variants.albedo: In place of the lit image: the lit materials' base colour after their maps and hooks, unlit.
x-og-variants.iblDiffuse: In place of the lit image: the diffuse image-based light (Environment's map or sky) each lit material receives.
x-og-variants.iblSpecular: In place of the lit image: the specular image-based light each lit material reflects.
x-og-variants.direct: In place of the lit image: the direct light (directional, point and spot lights, shadows applied) each lit material receives.
x-og-variants.aoDepth: The ao view with the depth the ambient occlusion pass reads in place of its term, as its fraction of a metre (one ramp per metre), to check the depth the AO sees.
x-og-variants.aoRaw: The ao view before the term's depth-aware blur, to tell the search's noise from the blur's.
x-og-variants.terrain: Terrain projection weights: XYZ as RGB (green is planar XZ). Dark lines show clipmap cells and white marks the outer morph band. dump_entity reports the clipmap regions and their triangle spacing.
x-og-variants.terrainLayers: Terrain's strongest raw layer (control times slope and altitude), coloured by index; magenta means the first-layer fallback. Brightness shows its share before height blending.
x-og-variants.terrainMip: Terrain normal-map mip footprint: one colour per estimated isotropic mip, darkening between levels. This is a derivative-based estimate, not the hardware anisotropic mip selection.
x-og-variants.terrainProjection: Dominant raw terrain layer's actual projection weights, XYZ as RGB, without cell or morph overlays. Planar layers are green (top-down Y projection).
x-og-variants.terrainDensity: Dominant raw terrain layer's vertical albedo texel footprints for X/Y/Z projections as RGB. Each linear channel is d/(1+d), where d is base-level texels per vertical screen pixel; 0.5 means one texel per pixel. Density is measured before projection weighting; a missing albedo shows the unsupported checker.

Transparency.description: How the main camera's blended surfaces (transparent materials, alpha billboards, alpha particles and trails) are composited, as og-render's Transparency: in any order, never sorted. Additive effects stay additive and drawn after them; 2D sprites, text and the UI keep their layer order; secondary cameras, reflections and probe faces still sort back to front. RenderCapabilities.transparency reports what the device resolved.

x-og-variants.weighted: Weighted blended order-independent transparency (McGuire and Bavoil 2013) with each pixel's nearest layer kept exact (hybrid transparency, Maule et al. 2013): a billboard or pane in front keeps its own colour over what lies behind it, and only the layers behind the nearest read as their weighted mean rather than strictly front over back. The nearest layer is the nearest fragment at least 1/8 opaque, marked by a depth pass of its own (where the device cannot write storage from fragment shaders, every layer is weighted). Two submission orders agree within the half-float rounding of the sums (at most one 8-bit step per channel for a few layers).
x-og-variants.linkedList: Per-pixel fragment lists: each pixel keeps up to RenderOptions.transparencyLayers fragments, sorted by depth (equal depths by a stable key of the draw and its primitive) and composited exactly, the same in any submission order. A pixel with more fragments is resolved whole as weighted, and counted (the render dump's transparency.fallbackPixels). Weighted where the device cannot write storage from fragment shaders, or where the scene is too large for one node a pixel in its largest storage buffer.

LitFeature.description: An optional feature of the lit shaders that RenderOptions.without can leave out. Every lit shader (meshes, material shaders, clustered meshes, terrain, grass, water, scattered copies, lit particles) carries each one's code behind a runtime test, and its pipelines compile it whether or not a scene uses it. RenderCapabilities.without lists those the renderer was made without.

x-og-variants.surfaceWeather: The weather on lit surfaces: og.WeatherState's wet ground, rain streaks, puddles, snow and dust, and the shore a sea's surf wets (og.Water). Left out, surfaces stay dry; og.Weather's particles, fog and light still draw.
x-og-variants.gi: The probes of GlobalIllumination (method probes or both): left out, they are not traced and lit surfaces do not gather them, so those methods bounce no light from probes (both keeps its screen-space rays). The screen-space method and LightVolume are not this feature.
x-og-variants.areaLights: Rect lights (og.RectLight): left out, a rect light is not drawn, lights nothing and casts no shadow.
x-og-variants.decals: Decals (og.Decal): left out, none is drawn.
x-og-variants.caustics: The caustics a water surface casts on what lies below it (og.Water.caustics): left out, none is drawn.

RenderOptions.description: How the renderer is created for a game (GameDesc.render). The host reads it once, when it attaches the renderer.

antialias.description: The antialiasing method; left out, tier (4x MSAA in a 2D project, TAA in a 3D one).

hdr.description: Request extended-range HDR surface output. Opt-in; not yet accepted on a real HDR display (acceptance belongs to the compatibility phase). False keeps SDR and its tone operator. Unsupported surfaces fall back to SDR; capabilities.hdrSupported reports the float extended-sRGB surface path, capabilities.hdr reports the resolved mode. Headless renderers remain SDR. HDR uses the LPM display mapper and linear UI composition, with the surface transfer applied last.

paperWhiteNits.description: HDR reference white; 0 means 203 nits. Clamped to 80..1000. On Apple EDR and web, absolute display nits are unavailable: white follows OS SDR white and peakNits/paperWhiteNits sets relative headroom. On DXGI/Vulkan scRGB this sets absolute paper white. Read once at renderer creation.

peakNits.description: HDR target peak; 0 means 1000 nits. Clamped to 80..10000 and at least paperWhiteNits. A display can limit actual output below this target. Read once at renderer creation.

shadowMapSize.description: The side of each of the directional light's cascade maps (RenderSettings.shadowCascades of them), in texels; smaller saves memory on phones (three 2048 maps are 48 MB, with their depth buffer 64 MB).

pointShadows.description: How point lights' shadows are stored: cube faces, or two paraboloid hemispheres (fewer passes, coarser).

taaHistory.description: With TAA: how the history is resampled.

taaSharpen.description: With TAA: a sharpening pass after it, 0 (none) to 1; it never pushes a pixel past its neighbours' range.

planarReflections.description: How many planar reflection surfaces draw at once: water surfaces (og.Water.planarReflection) that mirror the scene in a pass of their own in the same frame. 1: the first surface that asks (a grid surface before one over a mesh); a second surface reflects as if it did not ask (screen-space and sky reflections), never in the first's mirror, and the log says so once. 2: a second surface in view mirrors the scene too, and material shaders can read the first's mirror (`planar_reflection`), at the cost of one more texture in every lit pipeline and a second reflection pass while both are in view. RenderCapabilities.planarReflections reports the count the renderer was made with.

transparency.description: How blended surfaces are composited: weighted (the default) or the exact per-pixel lists where the device allows them.

transparencyLayers.description: With transparency linkedList: the fragments a pixel keeps and sorts exactly (0: 4), as far as the device's largest storage buffer holds them for every pixel at the render size; RenderCapabilities.transparency says whether the lists run at all.

without.description: Optional lit features to build no lit shader with, for a game that never uses them: empty (the default) builds every one into every lit shader, as before. Each one left out is in no lit pipeline the renderer makes, on any host, so those pipelines compile faster and draw a little faster; it is not drawn: a scene that uses it draws as if it did not, and the log says so once. Each name once, in any order. Read once, when the renderer is created; RenderCapabilities.without reports it.

debugView.description: A debug overlay from the first frame (og.debug.setView, the command channel's `debug:<view>`): none in a game, a view while building one. Not in publish builds.

FoliageDesc.description: Leaf lighting. Zero keeps ordinary opaque-surface lighting; this does not enable glass transmission or change alpha coverage.

translucency.description: Thin-leaf backlighting tinted by the base colour and attenuated by the light's shadow.

domeNormals.description: Blend leaf normals towards the canopy dome, before normal mapping. Requires cooked foliage anchors.

StandardMaterialDesc.description:
A physically based metallic-roughness material with three.js MeshStandardMaterial parameter names.
It is og-render's reflected StandardMaterial field for field: metalnessMap and roughnessMap read a glTF metallic-roughness texture (blue metal, green rough), so give both the same texture; alphaTest above 0 discards below that alpha; transparent blends, sorted back to front.
The stylised fields: unlit (three.js MeshBasicMaterial), toon with its gradientMap ramp, a rim (fresnel) light, a hit flash, dissolve with a glowing edge, and a per-material outline. All are off at their defaults. og.MaterialStyle fills the ones a material leaves at their defaults unless the material sets styled false.
The MeshPhysicalMaterial fields, under three.js's names and glTF's KHR_materials_* meanings, all off at their defaults: clearcoat with clearcoatMap, clearcoatRoughnessMap and clearcoatNormalMap; sheen (velvet, cloth) with sheenColor, sheenRoughness and their maps; transmission (glass, water) refracting the opaque scene behind through thickness, attenuationColor and ior; iridescence (soap film, oil) with its film's iridescenceIOR and iridescenceThicknessRange; anisotropy (brushed metal) along anisotropyRotation or anisotropyMap. They draw on every backend; unlit and toon materials ignore them.
A transmissive material is drawn after the opaque scene, back to front with the transparent ones, and refracts what was drawn before it (not other transmissive or transparent objects); thickness is in the mesh's own units, scaled with it.
normalMap is read in glTF's tangent frame: red tilts towards +u, green up the image. The tangents come from the model (the cook generates MikkTSpace ones where a glTF has none) or are generated when the geometry is made; normals follow a non-uniform scale correctly.

foliage.description: Leaf shading; omitted parameters keep their values on updateMaterial. The reflected foliage vector stores translucency in x and domeNormals in y.

metalnessMap.description: Metalness from the texture's blue channel.

roughnessMap.description: Roughness from the texture's green channel.

aoMap.description: Ambient occlusion from the texture's red channel.

emissiveIntensity.description: A multiplier on the emitted colour.

opacity.description: The opacity; below 1 only with transparent.

transparent.description: Blend instead of writing opaque pixels.

alphaTest.description: Discard pixels whose alpha is below this.

alphaToCoverage.description: With MSAA (antialias msaa4), an alpha-tested material turns its alpha into sample coverage instead of a hard cut at alphaTest, as three.js alphaToCoverage: minified foliage cards cover part of a pixel and the scene shows between them instead of drawing as solid sheets. Without MSAA it is a hard cut too, half a pixel's change of alpha below alphaTest (where the coverage reaches 0), so an edge keeps a few more pixels than alphaTest's own cut.

normalScale.description: How strongly the normal map bends the normal, per tangent axis.

aoMapIntensity.description: How strongly aoMap darkens the ambient light.

unlit.description: No lighting at all, as three.js MeshBasicMaterial: the colour (times map) plus emissive.

toon.description: Cel shading, as three.js MeshToonMaterial: light is quantized by gradientMap (three built-in bands without one), highlights are hard.

gradientMap.description: The toon ramp: a texture whose first row maps the light's angle (left dark, right lit) to the light received, read without filtering.

rimColor.description: Rim (fresnel) light added at grazing angles, unshadowed (linear).

rimIntensity.description: The rim light's strength; 0 is none.

rimPower.description: How tight the rim is (higher: thinner).

flashColor.description: The colour a hit flash mixes towards (linear, may exceed 1).

flash.description: How far the final colour is mixed towards flashColor (0 none, 1 flat): animate it per tick for a hit flash.

dissolve.description: The dissolved fraction: 0 whole, 1 gone. Pixels whose noise is below it are discarded (shadows too); the band just above glows with dissolveEdgeColor.

dissolveMap.description: The dissolve noise from the texture's red channel; without one, value noise over the object-space position.

dissolveEdgeColor.description: The glowing edge (linear, usually above 1 so it blooms).

dissolveEdgeWidth.description: The width of the glowing band in noise units.

dissolveScale.description: The frequency of the built-in noise (cells per object-space unit).

outlineWidth.description: This material's outline width in pixels; 0 is none (PostEffects.outline outlines everything). A hull outline, as toon shading draws one: the object's silhouette, where one part of it passes in front of another, and its creases against other objects (where it meets the ground or a wall), never the edges between its own faces, so a .vox model or any flat-shaded, hard-edged mesh keeps clean faces inside its silhouette; a face seen at a grazing angle (a box's side nearly edge-on, a large ground plane) is not lined across, only where it ends. Creases inside an object are Stylise.inkDepth's.

styled.description: Whether og.MaterialStyle (a look's scene-wide toon, rim, outline, flat facets, shadow tint and outline distance) reaches this material. false keeps it exactly as declared under any look: a lantern's lacquer, a UI-like prop, a hero kept photographic in a toon scene. A material with a MeshPhysicalMaterial lobe (clearcoat, sheen, transmission, iridescence, anisotropy, an ior other than 1.5) keeps its physical shading under the style's toon even when styled (toon would drop those lobes) and takes the rest of the style; its own toon true still makes it toon.

clearcoat.description: A clear lacquer over the surface, as three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoat: a second, 4 % reflective specular layer on the surface's normal before normalMap (car paint, varnished wood, wet plastic); 0 is none.

clearcoatRoughness.description: How rough the clear coat is, as three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatRoughness.

clearcoatMap.description: The coat's strength from the texture's red channel, times clearcoat (MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatMap).

clearcoatRoughnessMap.description: The coat's roughness from the texture's green channel, times clearcoatRoughness.

clearcoatNormalMap.description: A tangent-space normal map of the coat alone; the base keeps normalMap (MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatNormalMap).

clearcoatNormalScale.description: How strongly clearcoatNormalMap bends the coat's normal, per tangent axis.

sheen.description: A velvet-like layer that brightens grazing angles (cloth, fuzz, peach skin), as MeshPhysicalMaterial.sheen and glTF KHR_materials_sheen: Estevez and Kulla's Charlie fibres with their shadowing and soft terminator, lit by the environment through its directional albedo, and what it reflects taken from the surface under it, so cloth never glows (velvet: a very dark base, a bright desaturated sheenColor, sheenRoughness about 0.5; cotton and wool: a dim sheenColor at sheenRoughness 0.8 to 1; roughness 1 on both). Its strength, times sheenColor; 0 is none.

sheenColor.description: The sheen's colour (linear), times sheenColorMap; black is none.

sheenRoughness.description: How rough the sheen is: low keeps it to a thin rim, high spreads it over the surface.

sheenColorMap.description: The sheen's colour from the texture's RGB (sRGB).

sheenRoughnessMap.description: The sheen's roughness from the texture's alpha channel.

transmission.description: How much light passes through, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.transmission (glass, water, thin plastic): the opaque scene behind is refracted and blurred by roughness; 0 is none. Unlike opacity, the surface keeps its reflections.

transmissionMap.description: Transmission from the texture's red channel.

thickness.description: The volume's thickness under the surface in the mesh's own units (glTF KHR_materials_volume): how far refraction bends the view and how much attenuationColor absorbs; 0 is a thin wall.

thicknessMap.description: Thickness from the texture's green channel.

attenuationDistance.description: The distance light travels in the volume before it is tinted to attenuationColor (world units); 0 is no absorption, three.js's Infinity.

attenuationColor.description: The colour white light becomes after attenuationDistance in the volume (linear).

ior.description: The index of refraction (glTF KHR_materials_ior): the reflectance of a dielectric, ((ior - 1) / (ior + 1))^2 (4 % at 1.5), and how far transmission refracts.

iridescence.description: A thin-film interference layer, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.iridescence (soap bubbles, oil, beetle shells); 0 is none.

iridescenceThicknessRange.description: The film's thickness in nanometres: x where iridescenceThicknessMap is black, y where it is white and everywhere without the map (three.js's [100, 400]).

iridescenceMap.description: Iridescence from the texture's red channel.

iridescenceThicknessMap.description: The film's thickness between iridescenceThicknessRange's ends from the texture's green channel.

anisotropy.description: Stretches the specular highlight along a direction of the surface, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.anisotropy (brushed metal, hair, satin); 0 is none, 1 fully stretched. Needs the geometry's tangents (generated when it has none).

anisotropyRotation.description: The stretch's direction in radians from the tangent (+u) towards the bitangent.

anisotropyMap.description: The stretch's direction in red and green (-1 to 1 in the tangent frame, turned by anisotropyRotation) and its strength in blue, times anisotropy.

mapArray.description: The base colour from layer mapLayer of a texture array (og.load.textureArray) instead of map: variants of one look (tiles, skins, damage states) are one material, each Mesh picking its layer with Mesh.materialLayer, and every mesh of the material is one draw whichever layer it shows. A material with mapArray or normalMapArray reads its base colour and normal map from arrays only (map and normalMap are not read). Physical materials (the MeshPhysicalMaterial fields) and shader materials do not take arrays.

mapLayer.description: The layer of mapArray drawn where the Mesh does not pick one (past the array's last layer: the last).

normalMapArray.description: A tangent-space normal map from layer normalMapLayer of a texture array (linear: cook it with `kind normal`), the counterpart of mapArray.

normalMapLayer.description: The layer of normalMapArray read where the Mesh does not pick one.

mapOffset.description: The uv offset map is sampled at, as three.js Texture.offset and glTF KHR_texture_transform: uv' = offset + rotation(rotation) * (repeat * uv), glTF's order. A loaded glTF's transform is here unless the cook baked it into the model's uvs. A transform's own texCoord (a second uv set) is not read: the cook notes it and every map samples TEXCOORD_0.

mapRepeat.description: How many times map repeats across the uvs, as three.js Texture.repeat (glTF's scale): tiling and atlas cells.

mapRotation.description: The uv rotation of map, counter-clockwise in uv space about the uv origin, as glTF KHR_texture_transform's rotation.

metalnessMapOffset.description: The uv offset metalnessMap and roughnessMap (one glTF texture; a physical material's other maps and aoMap are packed with them and sampled here too) is sampled at, as three.js Texture.offset and glTF KHR_texture_transform: uv' = offset + rotation(rotation) * (repeat * uv), glTF's order. A loaded glTF's transform is here unless the cook baked it into the model's uvs.

metalnessMapRepeat.description: How many times metalnessMap and roughnessMap (one glTF texture; a physical material's other maps and aoMap are packed with them and sampled here too) repeats across the uvs, as three.js Texture.repeat (glTF's scale): tiling and atlas cells.

metalnessMapRotation.description: The uv rotation of metalnessMap and roughnessMap (one glTF texture; a physical material's other maps and aoMap are packed with them and sampled here too), counter-clockwise in uv space about the uv origin, as glTF KHR_texture_transform's rotation.

normalMapOffset.description: The uv offset normalMap is sampled at, as three.js Texture.offset and glTF KHR_texture_transform: uv' = offset + rotation(rotation) * (repeat * uv), glTF's order. A loaded glTF's transform is here unless the cook baked it into the model's uvs.

normalMapRepeat.description: How many times normalMap repeats across the uvs, as three.js Texture.repeat (glTF's scale): tiling and atlas cells.

normalMapRotation.description: The uv rotation of normalMap, counter-clockwise in uv space about the uv origin, as glTF KHR_texture_transform's rotation.

emissiveMapOffset.description: The uv offset emissiveMap is sampled at, as three.js Texture.offset and glTF KHR_texture_transform: uv' = offset + rotation(rotation) * (repeat * uv), glTF's order. A loaded glTF's transform is here unless the cook baked it into the model's uvs.

emissiveMapRepeat.description: How many times emissiveMap repeats across the uvs, as three.js Texture.repeat (glTF's scale): tiling and atlas cells.

emissiveMapRotation.description: The uv rotation of emissiveMap, counter-clockwise in uv space about the uv origin, as glTF KHR_texture_transform's rotation.

aoMapOffset.description: The uv offset aoMap is sampled at, as three.js Texture.offset and glTF KHR_texture_transform: uv' = offset + rotation(rotation) * (repeat * uv), glTF's order. A loaded glTF's transform is here unless the cook baked it into the model's uvs.

aoMapRepeat.description: How many times aoMap repeats across the uvs, as three.js Texture.repeat (glTF's scale): tiling and atlas cells.

aoMapRotation.description: The uv rotation of aoMap, counter-clockwise in uv space about the uv origin, as glTF KHR_texture_transform's rotation.

wireframe.description: Draw the edges of the mesh's triangles instead of its faces, as three.js Material.wireframe: one CSS pixel wide, in the colour the surface shows along each edge (color times map and the vertex colours, plus emissive times emissiveMap) or wireframeColor, unlit, depth tested; drawn as lines, not a polygon mode (WebGPU has none). Its meshes cast no shadow.

wireframeAngle.description: With wireframe: only the mesh's feature edges, its open borders and the edges whose two faces meet at more than this angle (welded by position, so uv seams and split hard edges do not show): a box's 12 edges, nothing across a smooth sphere but where it ends. 0 is every triangle edge.

wireframeColor.description: With wireframe: one colour for every edge (linear, above 1 blooms) instead of the colour the surface shows along it; black (the zero value) is the surface's.

paintDetail.description: How much of its detail the painterly filter (Stylise.paintRadius) keeps on this material, times Stylise.paintDetail: 0 painted at the full radius, 1 kept as drawn (a face, a hand, a sign's lettering).

weathering.description: How much og.WeatherState reaches this material: its wetness, rain streaks, puddles, snow and dust (1 all of it, 0 none). 0 for what the weather never touches: an indoor floor seen through a door, a screen, a hero kept clean, a surface a game wets itself; between for a coat that sheds some.

Mesh.description:
Draws a geometry with a material at the entity's MatrixWorld, as a three.js Mesh.
The material is a handle from og.render.standardMaterial or from a loaded glTF (GltfInfo.materials); its StandardMaterialDesc maps to the renderer as that struct's docs say.

castShadow.description: Cast shadows, as three.js Object3D.castShadow: drawn into the sun's cascades and the shadowed lights' maps. Off by default: a lamp's own glass around its light, a glow card or a decal-like slab casts none.

receiveShadow.description: Receive shadows, as three.js Object3D.receiveShadow: darkened where the sun's cascades and the shadowed lights' maps say something stands between it and the light. On by default (three.js's is off): every mesh received shadows before the flag was applied. false lights it as if unshadowed by every light, while it still casts as castShadow says: a glowing sign, a hero kept readable in a dark alley.
