flash.description: A hit flash on this mesh only: the lit colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (og.tween.flash fades it out). Carried with its transform to the lit shaders, as og.Model's, so a flashing mesh is one draw with the other meshes of its geometry and material, and the amount is continuous.

flashColor.description: The flash's linear colour, 0 to 1 a channel (8 bits a channel).

materialLayer.description: The texture-array layer this mesh's material reads (StandardMaterialDesc.mapArray and normalMapArray), in place of the material's mapLayer and normalMapLayer: one material, one draw, a layer per mesh (a tile set, a crowd's skins). -1 keeps the material's layers; a material without arrays ignores it.

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Object3D.layers.mask: bit n set puts it on layer n. A camera (og.Camera, og.CameraView, og.Mirror) draws it when their masks share a bit, and og.render.raycast tests it when its own `layers` does. Shadow maps take every caster whatever its layers, so a body hidden from a first-person camera still casts.

DirectionalLight.description:
The sun, as three.js DirectionalLight: parallel light along the entity's local -Z (aim it with transform.lookAt, as a camera). The first one found is drawn, with RenderSettings.shadowCascades shadow cascades (3 by default).
Without one, the renderer's default sun (from above and to the side, intensity 3) lights the scene.

intensity.description: The radiance multiplier, as three.js DirectionalLight.intensity.

castShadow.description: Cast shadows through the cascades (RenderSettings.shadowCascades), as three.js Light.castShadow.

shadowDistance.description: How far from the camera shadows reach; they fade over the last tenth. Smaller is sharper.

shadowSoftness.description: Soft shadows (PCSS): the penumbra's width per metre between caster and receiver, the tangent of the sun's apparent radius (the real sun's is 0.005). 0 keeps the hard one-texel edge; 0.01 to 0.05 is a soft sun, sharp at contact and blurring with distance. Costs a blocker search and a 16-tap filter per shadowed pixel.

shadowBox.description: One shadow map over a fixed box instead of the cascades: its half size across the light. 0 keeps the cascades. Everything outside the box is lit; the casters are drawn once, not once per cascade (three.js games that fit the light's orthographic shadow camera around the player draw this way).

shadowFocus.description: With shadowBox: how far ahead of the camera (along its level forward) the box is centred.

shadowFocusDrop.description: With shadowBox: how far below the camera the box's centre sits (the ground under a first-person eye).

shadowBias.description: With shadowBox: the depth bias toward the light (three.js shadow.bias times its camera's depth range). 0 is one texel. Leaf cards need a few centimetres or they shadow each other dark.

shadowNormalBias.description: With shadowBox: how far a receiver is pushed along its normal before it reads the map (three.js shadow.normalBias). 0 is one texel.

cascadeBlend.description: The fraction of each shadow cascade's depth over which it fades into the next, hiding the seam where the shadow's resolution changes. 0 is none; 0.1 to 0.2 is typical (those pixels read two cascades).

PointLight.description:
A light shining in every direction from the entity's position, as three.js PointLight. Its radiance at distance d is color * intensity / d^2, faded smoothly to zero at distance.
Lights are clustered (Forward+): each pixel shades only the lights whose distance reaches it, so hundreds are cheap. Lights out of view are skipped; up to MAX_LIGHTS in view are drawn, and past that (or past what one screen cluster holds, MAX_CLUSTER_LIGHTS) the ones brightest at the camera are kept. Of those in view with castShadow, RenderCapabilities.maxShadowedLights (16) caps how many get shadows and RenderSettings.shadowedLights (8 by default) chooses it, the brightest at the camera first.

distance.description: Where the light reaches zero, as three.js PointLight.distance (never infinite here).

castShadow.description: Cast shadows: six cube faces or two paraboloid hemispheres (RenderOptions.pointShadows).

cookie.description: A light cookie projected all around the light: a cube of six square faces in one texture, stacked top to bottom as +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z (a KTX2 cube's face order and a cube map's orientation, world axes; the texture is six times as tall as it is wide). The light's colour is multiplied by the texel its direction meets, so a lamp behind a pierced shade throws its pattern on the walls. 0 is none.

SpotLight.description: A cone of light along the entity's local -Z, as three.js SpotLight.

intensity.description: The radiance at one metre on the axis.

angle.description: The half-angle of the outer cone, as three.js SpotLight.angle.

penumbra.description: The fraction of the cone over which the light fades out, as three.js SpotLight.penumbra.

cookie.description: A light cookie, as three.js SpotLight.map: the texture projected along the cone (its centre on the axis, its edges at the outer angle, its top towards world up), multiplying the light's colour, so a spot throws a window's bars or a stained-glass pattern. 0 is none. A shadowed spot keeps its shadow over the pattern.

ToneMapping.description: The curve from the lit HDR image to the display, as three.js toneMapping. RenderSettings.toneMapped false clamps instead, whichever is chosen.

x-og-variants.aces: ACES (the fitted filmic curve), as three.js ACESFilmicToneMapping: the default.
x-og-variants.agx: AgX (Blender 4's and three.js AgXToneMapping's fit, base look): bright saturated lights go to white instead of skewing hue, and keep their hue further up than under ACES.
x-og-variants.none: No curve: the exposed linear colour is clamped to 0..1, so 2D colours come out exactly as authored at exposure 1 (the same as toneMapped false).
x-og-variants.neutral: Khronos PBR Neutral, as three.js NeutralToneMapping: colours up to about 0.8 come out as authored (a white-lit base colour shows as the colour picked), only brighter ones roll off to white. For product shots and saturated stylised colour that ACES would darken and shift.

GraphicsQuality.description: A graphics preset: a row of RenderSettings' quality fields that og.render.applyQuality writes (its doc has the table). A settings page offers the three.

x-og-variants.medium: The full frame: every quality field at its default.
x-og-variants.low: The cheapest frame: no rect-light shadows, two shadowed lights, half-size shadow maps, plain fog, hard particles, no screen-space reflections, ambient occlusion or global illumination, FXAA for MSAA; and, for a game that turns one of those back on, ambient occlusion at half resolution and half the reflection and fog steps.
x-og-variants.high: The full frame refined, at the GPU time of the effects the scene draws: FSR 3.1 as the temporal upscaler (sharper and steadier in motion than TAAU, about 1 ms to 2 ms more at 1080p and 1440p on an M4 Pro), the shadow maps at twice their side, ambient occlusion at full resolution whatever PostEffects.aoResolution asks, twice PostEffects.ssrSteps and twice the volumetric fog's slices (or raymarch steps). A scene without those effects differs from medium only by its shadow maps.

AoResolutionSetting.description: The resolution RenderSettings.aoResolution draws ambient occlusion at.

x-og-variants.full: Full resolution whatever PostEffects.aoResolution says (the high preset).
x-og-variants.half: Half resolution whatever PostEffects.aoResolution says (the low preset).

QualityPreset.description: The preset RenderSettings' quality fields were last written with (RenderSettings.quality).

x-og-variants.none: No preset applied: the fields are their defaults or the game's own.

RenderSettings.description: The frame's look after lighting: environment light, sky, bloom, exposure metering and tone mapping, and what the frame may cost: the quality fields (rectShadows to upscaler) that og.render.applyQuality sets from a graphics preset. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation. Camera.exposure is the manual exposure.

environmentIntensity.description: The strength of the image-based ambient light from the sky; og.Environment.intensity takes its place while an environment map is set.

sky.description: Draw the procedural sky behind the scene instead of Camera.background (with an og.Environment map set, the map).

bloom.description: Light above the threshold bleeds into its surroundings.

bloomThreshold.description: Brightness after exposure where bloom starts; 1 is display white.

bloomKnee.description: Softens the threshold over threshold plus or minus knee; 0 is a hard cut.

bloomIntensity.description: How much of the blurred light is added back.

bloomRadius.description: Below 0 (the default) keeps Origin's bloom. 0 to 1 switches to three.js UnrealBloomPass with this radius: a luminance high pass (smoothstep from bloomThreshold to bloomThreshold + bloomKnee, the colour kept whole above it) at half resolution, five Gaussian mips (kernels 3, 5, 7, 9, 11), mixed with weights mix(f, 1.2 - f, radius) for f = 1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2; bloomIntensity is its strength, and the mix is added as EffectComposer's additive copy does, weighted again by its alpha (strength times the weights' sum).

bloomContrast.description: With bloomRadius 0 or more: the high pass (and the blur) sees each channel as 0.18 x (colour / 0.18) to this power before exposure, as a contrast grade run ahead of UnrealBloomPass (the way a three.js grade pass before the bloom does) would leave it. 1, the default, leaves the colour as lit.

autoExposure.description: Meter every frame to middle grey, then apply Camera.exposure as compensation. With both adapt speeds 0 the exposure is the current frame's alone; otherwise it adapts over time like an eye, starting at the metered exposure of the first frame drawn after the first tick (a frame drawn before it, such as the web shell's first frame behind the play gate, meters at once and is never adapted from), so every host draws the same exposures for the same ticks.

adaptSpeedUp.description: How fast auto exposure rises when the view gets darker, in EV per second of game time: each drawn frame moves it by at most the speed times the ticks since the last drawn frame (never the wall clock, so a replay and every host adapt the same, however many frames each drew); 0 is instant. Snapshots and probe sweeps carry the adapted exposure.

adaptSpeedDown.description: How fast auto exposure falls when the view gets brighter, in EV per second of game time; 0 is instant. Eyes adapt to brightness faster than to the dark: 3 down and 1 up is a natural pair.

toneMapped.description: Tone mapping by toneMapping; false clamps, so 2D colours come out exactly as authored at exposure 1.

toneMapping.description: Which curve tone maps the frame while toneMapped is true: aces (the default), agx, neutral or none.

exposure.description: A multiplier on every camera's Camera.exposure, as three.js renderer.toneMappingExposure is one for the whole frame: a look's brightness without touching the cameras; 1 leaves them as they are.

decalAtlas.description: The texture Decal components take their uvMin to uvMax region from; 0 draws decals as solid colour.

lodBias.description: A multiplier on every model's projected level-of-detail error when its level is picked (og.Model.lodBias multiplies it again): a level is drawn while its error, measured by the cook against the full mesh, covers less than a pixel on the screen. 1 is the engine's choice, 2 keeps full meshes twice as far, 0.5 simplifies sooner; 0 draws every model at its full mesh.

bakedLighting.description: Draw the baked lighting of the scenes that have it (og bake lightmaps): static models with their lightmaps, everything else inside a LightVolume with its probes. False draws every scene as if unbaked, its ambient light from the sky or the environment map: to compare, or to see the realtime lights alone.

quality.description: The graphics preset og.render.applyQuality last wrote into the quality fields below (rectShadows to upscaler), or none. A record for the settings screen and the probe: the renderer reads the fields, never this, so a field the game sets after the preset is drawn as set.

rectShadows.description: Rect lights whose castShadow is on cast their soft shadows; false draws every rect light unshadowed, each keeping its castShadow for when this is on again. The low preset turns it off: a rect light's shadow is the costliest light in the frame.

shadowedLights.description: At most this many point, spot and rect lights cast shadows in a frame, the brightest at the camera kept (RenderCapabilities.shadowedLights caps it, 16); 0 casts none. The high preset keeps 16, medium 8, low 2. The directional light's cascades are not counted.

shadowCascades.description: The directional light's shadow cascades, 1 to 4: more cover the same shadowDistance with finer shadows near the camera, at one more shadow pass and one more map each. The high preset draws 4, medium 3, low 2. Changing it makes the cascade maps again at the next frame.

shadowMapScale.description: The shadow maps at this fraction of their full side: the directional light's cascades (2048 texels by default) and the local lights' layers (512), each kept within 64 texels and the device's limit (4096 for the cascades). Changing it makes the maps again at the next frame; RenderCapabilities.shadowMapSize is the cascades' side drawn.

volumetricFog.description: An og.VolumetricFog is drawn lit, with its light shafts; false draws the same medium as plain distance and height fog.

softParticles.description: Particles with a softDistance fade against the scene behind them; false draws them hard-edged and asks no depth prepass for them.

screenSpaceReflections.description: PostEffects.ssr draws; false leaves smooth surfaces the reflection probes' and the environment's reflection. PostEffects keeps its settings either way.

ambientOcclusion.description: PostEffects.ao darkens creases; false draws none. PostEffects keeps its settings either way.

aoResolution.description: The resolution ambient occlusion is searched at: postEffects (the default) draws PostEffects.aoResolution; full or half is drawn in its place, and PostEffects keeps its own for when this is postEffects again. The renderer reads this first, so the probe's RenderSettings and PostEffects together say what is drawn.

ssrStepScale.description: PostEffects.ssrSteps times this (within the 4 to 128 steps the pass takes): 2 is 128 steps for the default 64, finer contact with thin and distant reflected surfaces at a higher GPU time. PostEffects keeps its steps.

volumetricStepScale.description: An og.VolumetricFog's samples along each view ray times this: the froxel grid's 64 slices deep (8 to 256), each thinner, so a shaft's edge in depth and the fog just in front of a surface resolve more finely, or the raymarch's 24 steps per pixel (4 to 96) where the renderer draws one (RenderCapabilities.volumetricFog). The froxel grid's GPU time and memory grow with its slices; changing it makes the grid again at the next frame.

msaaSamples.description: Samples per pixel where the antialiasing multisamples (msaa4): 4, or 1, which draws FXAA instead. RenderCapabilities.maxMsaaSamples caps it, as maxShadowedLights caps shadowedLights: where the device resolved no MSAA (TAA, FXAA, off, or FXAA for want of a multisampled HDR format) it is 1, and one sample is drawn whatever this says; RenderCapabilities.antialias is what is drawn now. Changing it makes the multisampled targets and pipelines again at the next frame.

upscaler.description: Under TAA, the temporal resolve that takes the frame from the render scale (DisplaySettings.renderScale, automatic quality's) to the output: taau (the default, the low and medium presets) or fsr3 (the high preset). Automatic quality keeps it while it lowers the render scale and draws taau once its preset steps cap the quality at medium or low. A device that draws only some (RenderCapabilities.upscalers) draws taau for one it lacks. Switching starts the history again at the next frame.

interpolate.description: Draw what moves between the last two ticks. A display frame that falls between ticks (a 60 Hz tick on a 120 or 144 Hz screen) draws every entity's world transform and og.Camera's position and rotation blended from the tick before the last to the last, by the time past the last tick over the tick's length (positions and scales lerped, rotations slerped), so camera pans, cars and bullets glide instead of judder; skinned models blend their joints too (each joint's translation and scale lerped, rotation slerped, blendshape weights lerped; root motion and every pose the simulation reads stay at the tick), UI anchored to an entity (a document's `<anchor entity>`) stays on its drawn place, and object motion blur moves from the frame drawn before, never across a snap or a camera cut. Immediate-mode draws (og.render.sprite, og.render.text, og.debug.line and og.debug.text, placed by a system on its tick) and shader time stay at the tick. The frame then shows the world up to one tick late. A frame on a tick boundary (a host that steps whole ticks: og run without --realtime, og render, og test) draws the last tick exactly, as do the probe's screenshots and captures, so reference frames are the ticks'. Presentation only: the simulation, world_hash, snapshots, replays, lockstep, the probe and dump_* read the ticks, never the blend. og.Interpolation opts an entity out; og.render.snap, the probe's teleport and snapDistance keep a teleport from gliding.

snapDistance.description: An entity or og.Camera that moved further than this between the last two ticks is drawn at the last tick, not blended: a teleport or a respawn this far needs no og.render.snap. 0 never snaps by distance.

Interpolation.description: How the renderer draws this entity between ticks while RenderSettings.interpolate is on; an entity without it is blended. Presentation only: the renderer reads it, the simulation never does.

off.description: Draw this entity, and everything under it through og.Parent, at the last tick's transform on every frame, never blended: a marker the game already moves every frame, or an object that jumps on purpose (a clock hand that ticks).

Lut.description: A colour lookup table for PostEffects.lut, from og.load.lut (a `.cube` file).

EnvironmentMap.description: A prefiltered HDR environment map for Environment.map, from og.load.environment (an `.ogt` of `type environment` naming an equirectangular `.hdr` or `.exr`, a KTX2 cube map, or six face images).

ParticleEmitter.description: A particle emitter asset for ParticleSystem.emitter, from og.load.emitter (an `.ogt` of `type particles`).

Environment.description: Image-based light from a cooked HDR environment map instead of the sky, as three.js scene.environment, and the map behind the scene, as scene.background = the environment. Load the map with og.load.environment: the cook has already prefiltered it (GGX levels for reflections from mirror to rough, harmonics for the diffuse light), so setting it costs a few copy passes. Without a map the sky lights the scene as before (og.Sky, a DayNight, or the built-in one). Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

map.description: The map from og.load.environment; 0 lights by the sky.

intensity.description: The strength of the map's light on every surface, as three.js scene.environmentIntensity; while a map is set it replaces RenderSettings.environmentIntensity.

rotation.description: Turns the map about +Y, as three.js scene.environmentRotation.y: positive turns what was at +X towards -Z. The light and the background turn together.

background.description: Draw the map behind the scene, as three.js scene.background = the environment (Camera.background, og.Sky and RenderSettings.sky give way); false leaves the background as they set it.

backgroundIntensity.description: Multiplies the map where it is drawn behind the scene, as three.js scene.backgroundIntensity; the light is not changed.

backgroundBlurriness.description: Blurs the sky where it is drawn behind the scene, as three.js scene.backgroundBlurriness: 0 sharp to 1 the roughest of the prefiltered (GGX) levels the light already reads, so it costs nothing extra; the light is not changed. Applies to the sky background with or without a map.

groundHeight.description: Draws the sky on a dome with a flat ground under it, as three.js GroundedSkybox: how far above the ground the map was photographed (metres). Objects then stand on the map's ground instead of floating over its horizon, and reflections of the environment (mirrors, water, clear coats) show the same projected ground. 0 (the default) draws the sky at infinity.

groundRadius.description: The grounded dome's radius (metres, larger than groundHeight), as GroundedSkybox's radius: the ground looks flat out to about this distance.

groundCenter.description: The ground point under where the map was photographed: the dome's centre is groundHeight above it.

blendTo.description: A second map from og.load.environment that the light and the background blend towards (indoor to outdoor); 0 is none. Both maps turn by rotation and the background is scaled by backgroundIntensity.

blendWeight.description: How far the blend has gone: 0 the map, 1 blendTo, in between a mix of both maps' light (every GGX level and the harmonics) and background. Drive it from the tick (a tween or a system), never from a clock, so a replay blends alike; it is drawn in 128 steps, each regenerating the light once.

hemiSky.description: A hemisphere light's sky colour (linear), as three.js HemisphereLight.color: diffuse-only ambient light mix(hemiGround, hemiSky, 0.5 n.y + 0.5) * hemiIntensity, darkened by ambient occlusion like the map's light. Unlike light baked into the map it adds no reflection.

hemiGround.description: The hemisphere light's ground colour (linear), as three.js HemisphereLight.groundColor.

hemiIntensity.description: The hemisphere light's intensity, as three.js HemisphereLight.intensity; 0 (the default) is off.

x-og-variants.gtao: Ground-truth ambient occlusion (3 slices): the better looking one.
x-og-variants.ssao: Hemisphere SSAO with 8 samples: the cheaper one.
x-og-variants.screen: Depth-only disc AO in screen units (14 taps, radius clamp(1.6 / depth, 0.004, 0.06) of the screen width, fading out from 120 to 300 m, squared): the post-process SSAO of three.js-era games. It ignores normals, so ground seen at a low angle darkens a little too, as those games look. aoRadius and aoRadiusScale do not apply; aoIntensity scales the occlusion.

AoResolution.description: The resolution ambient occlusion is searched at.

x-og-variants.full: Every pixel searched, then a 4x4 depth-aware blur.
x-og-variants.half: Every second pixel in x and y searched (a quarter of the work) and blurred at that resolution, then brought to full resolution by a depth-aware upsample: softer contacts and thin creases, a fraction of the GPU time.

DofQuality.description: How many taps depth of field gathers per pixel.

x-og-variants.high: 48 taps at half resolution: rounder, smoother bokeh.

ScreenBlur.description: Which way PostEffects.screenBlur smears the whole frame.

x-og-variants.zoom: Along the line to screenBlurCenter, each way by screenBlurStrength's fraction of the distance to it (0.1 a light dash, 0.3 a hard impact): a dash forwards, a hit, a warp.
x-og-variants.spin: Round screenBlurCenter, each way by screenBlurStrength radians (0.05 is about 3 degrees), on circles in pixels whatever the frame's aspect: a spin, a vortex, a dizzy spell.
x-og-variants.directional: Along screenBlurAngle across the whole frame, each way by screenBlurStrength pixels at 720 lines (scaled with the frame's height): a fast pan, a sideways dash.

SpriteBlend.description: How a sprite is blended over what is below it.

x-og-variants.additive: Added (light, fire, magic): order-independent within a layer.

SpriteFacing.description: How a world sprite turns towards the camera that draws it: a billboard (three.js Sprite). Decided as a mode of og.Sprite and SpriteDesc rather than a component of its own: a billboard is the same quad, texture, region, flash, glow, blend, layer, drop shadow and texture array layer as any sprite, drawn by the same sprite batch and shader, which only stands its corners differently. The turn is computed on the GPU from each camera's own axes (the main camera, every og.CameraView and og.Mirror, every face of a reflection probe), so it never feeds back into the simulation and a snapshot holds only the mode. The sprite turns about its anchor (a nine-slice turns as one panel), `rotation` still turns it within its own plane, and its drop shadow is cast by the quad stood upright facing the sun, so it shows the whole shape from every camera. A faced sprite without sortY (and tone mapped) draws among the transparent meshes, back to front with them by the view depth of its anchor from the camera that draws it (each face of a reflection probe from the probe), its drop shadow before them, so a billboard behind a glass pane shows through it and one in front draws over it; its layer no longer orders it against other sprites. With sortY, or toneMapped false, it keeps the sprite order (layer, then key) after the transparent meshes and particles. A faced sprite is culled by its bounds (a sphere round the anchor through the farthest corner) against the camera's view. Sprites are depth tested and do not write depth. World text takes the same modes (TextDesc.facing, FloatingTextDesc.facing): it turns as one panel about its position and sorts as a billboard.

x-og-variants.none: In the world's xy plane facing +z, as every sprite before billboards.
x-og-variants.camera: In the camera's view plane: its x along the camera's right, its y along its up, as particle billboards (smoke, glints, impostors seen from any side).
x-og-variants.cameraY: Upright, turned about the world's y axis towards the camera: its y stays +y, its x the camera's right laid level. Trees, characters and props that must stand while the camera looks down on them.

StripBlend.description: How a trail, ribbon or beam is blended.

x-og-variants.alpha: Alpha blended: smoke trails, tyre marks.

PostEffects.description:
The post stack beyond RenderSettings' bloom, exposure and tone mapping, and camera shake. Every effect is off by default (its switch false or its amount 0) and then costs nothing: no pass is recorded. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.
Screen-space ambient occlusion, outlines, depth of field, motion blur and god rays run a depth-normal prepass, turned on with them. Grading, the colour adjustments (temperature to threshold), vignette, aberration, grain and the flash apply to the display colour after tone mapping, and lens distortion bends the result; the UI and screen-space sprites (the overlay) come after all of it.

ao.description: Screen-space ambient occlusion: darkens the ambient light in creases and contact areas.

aoRadius.description: The world-space radius searched for occluders.

aoResolution.description: Full resolution, or half for a fraction of the GPU time at softer detail.

aoDirect.description: How much the occlusion also darkens direct and local light (0 only the ambient light, 1 a fully occluded pixel keeps 35 % of it). Above 0 the AO sees and darkens water surfaces too; at 0 water is outside it.

aoRadiusScale.description: Above 0 the radius grows with the distance, min(aoRadius, aoRadiusScale × distance): a fixed share of the screen up close, as three.js SSAO passes size theirs, instead of a fixed world size; 0 keeps aoRadius everywhere. The benefit holds with ssao, whose open flat ground stays unshaded at any radius; gtao's slices darken open ground a little as the radius shrinks.

outline.description: Outlines every opaque surface from depth and normal edges, creases between the faces of one object included (materials with outlineWidth get their own hull outline instead).

outlineWidth.description: Line width in pixels, drawn inside the silhouette.

outlineDepthThreshold.description: The relative depth step that counts as a silhouette (0.04 is 4 %).

outlineNormalThreshold.description: The normal change that counts as a crease (1 - cos of the angle; 0.4 is about 53 degrees).

depthOfField.description: Bokeh depth of field: pixels away from the focus distance blur into discs.

dofFocusDistance.description: The distance from the camera that is sharp.

dofFocusRange.description: The half-width of the sharp band around it.

dofMaxBlur.description: The largest blur radius, as a fraction of the image height (0.012 is about 9 px at 720p).

dofFalloff.description: How quickly blur grows outside the band: full blur focusRange times (1 + falloff) away.

motionBlur.description: Per-object and camera motion blur along the screen-space velocity.

motionBlurShutter.description: The shutter as a fraction of the frame (0.5 is a 180 degree shutter).

screenBlur.description: A zoom, spin or directional blur of the whole frame (RedGPU's zoom, radial and directional blurs), weighted to the middle of its reach: one pass after motion blur and before bloom and the tone curve, so highlights streak and glow; the UI is not blurred. Off at none or at screenBlurStrength 0.

screenBlurStrength.description: How far it reaches each way: for zoom the fraction of the way to the centre, for spin radians, for directional pixels at 720 lines; 0 is off.

screenBlurCenter.description: Zoom's and spin's centre, in fractions of the frame from the top left.

screenBlurAngle.description: Directional's direction, counter-clockwise from the right (90 is vertical).

screenBlurSamples.description: Taps per pixel: more is smoother on long blurs, each one a texture read.

godRays.description: Screen-space light shafts from the DirectionalLight (the sun must be in front of the camera).

godRaysDecay.description: How fast the rays fade along their length.

godRaysDensity.description: How far towards the sun each ray samples (a fraction of the distance).

godRaysTint.description: A linear tint on the light the rays carry.

godRaysThreshold.description: Sky brightness (linear, before exposure) below which the sky carries no rays.

glow.description: Order-independent 2D glow: sprites with SpriteDesc.glow (and 2D particles with a glow) are blurred and added back, with or without bloom.

glowIntensity.description: How much of the blurred glow is added back.

lut.description: Colour grading by a lookup table from og.load.lut; 0 is none (and so is a LUT whose streaming group is not resident).

lutIntensity.description: 0 leaves the image as tone mapped, 1 applies the table fully.

temperature.description: White balance: towards warm orange (positive) or cool blue (negative), Unity's Temperature divided by 100 (a von Kries scaling in LMS from a white point moved along the daylight locus); 0 is off. The colour adjustments, temperature to threshold, apply in this order to the display colour after the tone curve and the LUT, each clamping it to 0..1 (the white balance in linear light, the rest on the sRGB-encoded colour). They cost no pass: the renderer bakes them with the LUT into one 32³ table whenever one changes, so adjustments held still cost nothing per frame, and a frame that changes one pays that bake on the CPU (about half a millisecond with one adjustment on, a few with all of them).

tint.description: White balance: towards magenta (positive) or green (negative), as Lightroom's and Unity's Tint divided by 100; 0 is off.

brightness.description: Added to every channel of the display colour; 0 is off.

contrast.description: Contrast around mid grey: positive spreads the tones by 1 / (1 - contrast), negative pulls them in by 1 + contrast (-1 is flat grey); 0 is off.

balanceShadows.description: The colour balance of the shadows (luminance below 0.5, fading out towards it): x shifts from cyan to red, y from magenta to green, z from yellow to blue, each -1 to 1 added to its channel; zero is off.

balanceMidtones.description: The colour balance of the mid-tones (what the shadows and highlights leave), as balanceShadows.

balanceHighlights.description: The colour balance of the highlights (luminance above 0.5, fading in from it), as balanceShadows.

preserveLuminosity.description: The colour balance keeps each pixel's luminance, so it moves only the hue (Photoshop's Preserve Luminosity).

hue.description: Turns every hue about the grey axis (red towards green at 120); 0 is off.

saturation.description: -1 grey, 0 unchanged, 1 twice the colour (the chroma around the luminance scaled by 1 + saturation).

vibrance.description: Saturation that spares colours already saturated and skin tones: positive livens dull colours, negative mutes them; 0 is off.

grayscale.description: How far each colour goes towards its luminance (grey); 0 is off.

invert.description: How far each colour goes towards its complement; 0 is off.

threshold.description: Above 0, each pixel white where its luminance reaches this level and black below it (the table's 32 steps soften the edge over about 1/31 of the range); 0 is off.

vignette.description: Darkened (or tinted) edges of the frame.

vignetteRadius.description: Where darkening starts, as a fraction of the half-diagonal.

vignetteColor.description: The linear colour the edges move towards.

chromaticAberration.description: Red and blue split towards the edges, in pixels at the corners at 720p; 0 is off.

lensDistortion.description: Barrel (positive: the centre bulges and straight lines bow outwards, a wide-angle or fisheye lens) or pincushion (negative: lines bow inwards) distortion of the frame; 0 is off. The radius is measured in pixels whatever the frame's aspect, and a barrel is fitted so its farthest corner stays on the image (no black edges wherever the centre is). One pass while on, after the Stylise passes that read the depth (paint, hatching, halftone and ink, whose lines bend with the image) and before its palette quantisation; the UI is not bent. Visual only: raycasts from the pointer see the undistorted frame.

lensDistortionCenter.description: The lens's centre, in fractions of the frame from the top left.

filmGrain.description: Luminance-weighted noise amplitude in display units, a new pattern every tick (0.04 is subtle); 0 is off.

sharpen.description: Contrast-adaptive sharpening (CAS) of the final image, as a three.js CAS pass after the output pass: each pixel pushed away from its four neighbours by a weight that falls where the neighbourhood is already near black or white. 0 is the mildest, 1 the strongest; below 0 is off.

flash.description: A full-screen flash: the display colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (animate it per tick); 0 is off.

shakeTrauma.description: Camera shake held at a fixed level (decay it yourself): 0 none, 1 the most (the amplitude is trauma squared). Prefer og.camera.shake, which decays by itself; the frame shakes by the larger of the two. Smooth value noise by the tick, so a replay shakes the same. Visual only.

shakeMaxOffset.description: The largest offset at trauma 1, as a fraction of the view height.

ssr.description: Screen-space reflections, stochastic and denoised (after AMD FidelityFX SSSR and Frostbite's SSR): each pixel up to ssrMaxRoughness casts one ray drawn from its GGX lobe, marched through a hierarchical depth pyramid of the depth-normal prepass; neighbours' rays are reused and the result accumulated over frames, so mirrors stay sharp and rough metal blurs as its lobe does. A hit reflects the previous frame's lit image (a frame after a cut has none yet). Lit surfaces blend it over the reflection probes', the probe GI's and the environment's reflection by how much of the lobe the screen resolved: where a ray leaves the screen, hits the sky or misses, those show. Opaque surfaces of a perspective 3D camera only; it turns on the depth-normal prepass.

ssrMaxDistance.description: How far a reflected ray marches, in world units; the last fifth fades into the probes'. The hierarchical march's cost is set by ssrSteps, not by the distance, so a long reach is cheap: the default lets a wet street mirror lights 40 m down it.

ssrThickness.description: How far behind the depth buffer a surface is taken to extend: a ray passing behind a surface by less than this hits it.

ssrSteps.description: The hierarchical march's iterations along each ray: each crosses a cell of the min-max depth pyramid's current level, and a ray behind everything in a cell crosses it on that level too. 64 lets a ray that passes behind thin and distant things (lamp posts down a street) reach what it reflects; a ray out of steps keeps the probes' reflection. Only the rays that need the steps pay for them.

ssrFade.description: The fraction of the screen's edge over which a reflection fades into the probes' (the last fifth of ssrMaxDistance fades too).

ssrIntensity.description: How much of the reflection replaces the probes' and the environment's where it resolved; 1 is physical (weighted by the surface's Fresnel and lobe as the probes' are).

ssrMaxRoughness.description: The roughest surface traced: rougher ones keep the probes' reflection, and the last quarter below it fades into them. Rays on rough surfaces cost the same as on mirrors, and the denoiser accumulates them over more frames.

ssrResolution.description: Half (the default): one ray per 2x2 block, a different pixel of the block each frame, denoised on the blocks and upsampled to the pixels by their depth, normal and roughness, so edges stay sharp: under half of Full's cost (about 1.6 ms at 1080p on an M4 Pro), with slightly softer near-mirror detail. Full: one ray per pixel, denoised at full resolution: the sharpest mirrors.

custom.description: The custom post passes, in order (og.load.post, `type post` assets): at most RenderCapabilities.maxCustomPosts (8, og-render's MAX_CUSTOM_POSTS). Each runs over the one before it (the lit image for the first), after depth of field and motion blur and before exposure, bloom and the tone curve, and reads the lit image, depth and normals too (any pass turns the prepass on). Write the whole list: `post.custom = [grade, crt]`, `post.custom = []`; a look gives it on one line (`custom "post/tint.ogt" "post/crt.ogt"`). A 0 in it is skipped. Its parameters are set with og.render.setPostParam. A pass the device fails to compile is reported (og.render.postErrors) and skipped.

LensFlare.description:
Lens flare, as Filament's screen-space flare (after John Chapman): ghosts and a halo mirror the bright parts of the bloom chain's first level through the centre of the frame with chromatic aberration, are blurred, and are added before the tone curve, the halo under a starburst. The sun and up to seven point and spot lights (the ones with the most light at the camera) also cast ghosts of their own, smooth aperture-shaped discs (the sun's 8 % of the frame's height in radius, a light's three times its size on screen up to that; magnified up to 1.5 times along the line through the centre, and fainter as they are), as bright as 0.56 % (the sun) or 0.28 % (a light) of the source's exposed radiance spread over the sun's disc, in proportion to its light as its bloom is (so a dim lamp's are faint, and a small lamp's small), each weighted by how much of it the depth shows, so a sun behind a roof or a lamp behind a pillar fades out; a ghost that would lie on its own source's glare is left out. Runs after bloom, after TAA, at a quarter of the frame, in exposed light, so the exposure and an HDR display apply to it as they do to bloom. With RenderSettings.bloom on, the flare's thresholds apply above bloomThreshold; with bloom off, the bloom chain's first level runs for the flare alone with no threshold of its own, and only the flare is added. In 3D it turns on the depth-normal prepass. Clouds dim the sun's flare through the light they leave the sun, and fog through what it leaves of the sky towards the sun; a single cloud crossing the sun's disc does not.
Off by default. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation, and a world that never names this resource keeps the type table, saves and hash it had without it.

intensity.description: How much of the flare is added (Filament adds its flare at its bloom strength, 0.1).

ghosts.description: Ghosts per bright spot, along the line through the centre of the frame; 0 is none.

ghostSpacing.description: How far apart the ghosts are, as a fraction of the way to the centre.

ghostThreshold.description: The exposed brightness above which a spot casts ghosts (each screen-space tap clamps at 1, display white; a source's own ghosts stay in proportion to its light).

haloRadius.description: The halo ring's radius, as a fraction of the frame's height.

haloThickness.description: The halo ring's thickness, as a fraction of the frame's height; 0 is no halo.

haloThreshold.description: The exposed brightness above which a spot feeds the halo.

chromaticAberration.description: How far the screen-space ghosts' red and blue split along the line to the centre, as a fraction of the frame (Filament's default is 0.005). Each ghost also takes one coating tint, amber, teal and violet in turn.

starburst.description: Filament's starburst: the halo streaked by an angular pattern round the centre of the frame that turns as the camera turns (Filament streaks the whole flare; here the ghosts stay smooth discs).

sun.description: The sun's own flare: a disc of the sun's size in the sky (0.27 degrees without a drawn disc), weighted by the share of it the depth shows as sky; the sky round it is kept out of the screen-space ghosts, so the sun flares once. 0 is none (no ghosts of the sun at all); 1 lets its ghosts reach full strength.

lights.description: The point and spot lights' own flares: each a 0.2 m disc of the light's radiance at its position (a spot only seen from inside its cone), hidden where the depth lies more than 0.2 m in front of it; its own bulb is kept out of the screen-space ghosts, so it flares once. 0 is none (no ghosts of those lights at all).

x-og-variants.screen: In screen space: rays through the depth-normal prepass take the light the previous frame showed where they hit. Fine detail and contact, but nothing from off screen or behind what the screen shows.
x-og-variants.probes: With probes: a grid of probes around the camera, each casting rays through a simplified copy of the scene (its meshes and terrains) every few frames, gathers the light arriving from every side, sky included; every lit surface takes its ambient light from the probes around it, tested for which of them see it. Light from off screen and behind walls bounces, a red wall lights the floor beside it however the camera looks, and the sky's light is occluded under roofs, in rooms and between buildings. Coarse (a probe every probeSpacing metres): pair it with PostEffects.ao for contact.
x-og-variants.both: Probes for the light from the whole scene and the sky, the screen-space rays for the detail they see.

GlobalIllumination.description: Global illumination: light bounces between surfaces, so shade is lit by what stands around it. By method: in screen space (`screen`), each pixel casts rays over the hemisphere of its normal through the depth-normal prepass, and where a ray meets a surface it takes the light that surface sent on the previous frame (so a few frames give many bounces): a red wall tints the floor beside it, a sunlit patch lights the room's ceiling, an emissive panel lights what faces it; light from off screen, or behind what the screen shows, is not bounced. With probes (`probes`), cascades of probes around the camera trace the scene in software and every lit surface (meshes, terrain, grass, scattered copies) takes its ambient light from them: the bounce from the whole scene, and the sky occluded by it. The bounce adds to the diffuse ambient light, and the rays that hit something take their share of the ambient light (the environment, the sky, baked lightmaps and LightVolumes) away, as ambient occlusion does; with PostEffects.ao on, its term does that, and with probes its bent normals (GTAO) pick the probes' light from the direction a crease opens to. Under TAA the screen rays change every frame and TAA averages them; without it a still frame keeps one pattern, blurred. Off by default. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation, and a world that never names this resource keeps the type table, saves and hash it had without it.

method.description: In screen space, with probes, or both.

intensity.description: Scales the bounced light; 1 is physical. With probes the sky's light and emission are not scaled, only what surfaces bounce.

maxDistance.description: How far each ray travels at most: the reach of a bounce. A ray also stops where it leaves the screen, its steps spread over what it crosses on screen. With probes (`both`) the rays reach one probe spacing at most: farther, the probes give the light.

thickness.description: How far behind the depth buffer a surface is taken to extend: a ray passing behind a surface by less than this hits it.

rays.description: Rays per pixel each frame: more is smoother and costlier (TAA adds the frames' rays together).

occlusion.description: How much of the ambient light the rays that hit something take away (1 physical, 0 the bounce is only added); not read while PostEffects.ao is on, whose term occludes.

resolution.description: Full resolution, or half for a quarter of the rays and a depth-aware upsample. With PostEffects.ao on, the AO is drawn at this resolution too. RenderSettings.aoResolution replaces it as it replaces the AO's.

probeSpacing.description: With probes: the distance between neighbouring probes of the finest cascade (16 × 8 × 16 probes around the camera); each next cascade's probes are twice as far apart, reaching twice as far. About a third of a room's size indoors, a few metres outdoors.

probeCascades.description: With probes: how many cascades, each doubling the reach of the one before (the first is updated every frame, the next every second frame, then every fourth).

probeRays.description: With probes: rays each probe casts when it is updated; more is smoother and costlier.

allowed.description: The graphics quality's switch: false draws none and enabled keeps the game's choice. og.render.applyQuality writes it (false in the low preset, true in medium and high) on a world that has this resource; a game that names the resource after applying a preset applies the preset again.

Palette.description: A colour palette for Stylise.palette, from og.load.palette (a `.hex` or GIMP `.gpl` file of up to 256 colours).

Look.description: A look from og.load.look (an `.ogt` of `type look`): the frame's whole art direction as data, applied with og.render.applyLook.

DitherPattern.description: The threshold pattern Stylise.dither spreads the steps of posterize and palette with.

x-og-variants.none: No dither: every pixel rounds to its nearest step or colour, in flat bands.
x-og-variants.bayer2: Ordered dither by a 2 by 2 Bayer matrix: the coarsest checker, as on early handhelds.
x-og-variants.bayer4: Ordered dither by a 4 by 4 Bayer matrix: the cross-hatched ramps of 8- and 16-bit art.
x-og-variants.bayer8: Ordered dither by an 8 by 8 Bayer matrix: finer ramps with 64 levels between two colours.
x-og-variants.blueNoise: Blue noise: an even grain without a visible grid (a 64 by 64 void-and-cluster tile the engine ships, repeated), fixed per pixel so a still frame does not crawl.
x-og-variants.interleavedGradient: Interleaved gradient noise: computed per pixel without a texture; a finer diagonal structure than blueNoise up close.

MaterialSurface.description: A made surface MaterialStyle.surface lays on every lit material: the hand-made materials of the shape styles, drawn by the material's shading itself (its normal, its colour and how it takes the light) in each mesh's own space, so a moving object carries it.

x-og-variants.none: No surface: each material as declared.
x-og-variants.clay: Modelling clay: soft lumps and thumb-pressed dimples bend the normal, the light wraps past the terminator as through a soft body and warms there, and the surface stays matte (roughness at least 0.75).
x-og-variants.paper: Paper and card: a fibre grain darkens and lifts the colour in fine streaks and bends the normal so lit faces catch it, the light wraps a little as through a sheet, and the surface is fully rough.
x-og-variants.plastic: Toy plastic or painted wood: a satin sheen (roughness held between 0.3 and 0.45, no metal), a soft wrap of the light and a faint moulding ripple, so pieces read as small and handled.

OutlinePlace.description: Where MaterialStyle's outlines lie against an object's silhouette (MaterialStyle.outlinePlace).

x-og-variants.inside: On the object's own edge pixels, inside its silhouette: its size is unchanged.
x-og-variants.outside: On the pixels round the object (a jump flood finds each pixel's nearest outlined silhouette), so the shape keeps its own pixels whole and a far character is not blacked out by its own line; round at the corners and anti-aliased at any width.
x-og-variants.both: Centred on the silhouette: half the width inside, half outside.

StyliseSpace.description: Where Stylise lays a pattern (the paint canvas, the hatching, the halftone).

x-og-variants.screen: Over the frame in logical pixels, as a print or a sheet of paper over the screen: the pattern stays put while the camera moves and the scene slides under it.
x-og-variants.surface: On the surfaces, through the depth-normal prepass's position and normal (three world planes blended by the normal): the pattern sticks to the scene as the camera moves and wraps round forms, a tonal art map's strokes on the objects. Hatching and halftone keep about their pixel spacing by fading between whole octaves of world spacing; the sky keeps the screen pattern. The frame runs the prepass PostEffects.outline uses.
x-og-variants.object: On the surfaces as surface, but in each mesh instance's own space (three planes of the instance blended by its normal, in metres along its axes): a moving, turning or skinned object carries its strokes, dots and grain instead of sliding through them, and keeps them however it is scaled. Terrain, scattered copies and the vertices a material shader moves keep the world pattern, the sky the screen pattern. The frame runs the prepass and an object pass that draws the opaque instances again.

x-og-variants.channel: Each display channel rounded to its own step, the classic posterize: a colour off the grey axis can change hue as light moves it across one channel's step before the others.
x-og-variants.tone: The colour's value (its largest channel) and its tint (the channels over that value) stepped apart, each to posterize's steps: a change of light, exposure or mood moves a colour's value and never its hue, so a near-grey stays grey and a gradient of one hue stays that hue.

x-og-variants.ink: One ink (halftoneColor) on paper: dots larger where the image is darker.
x-og-variants.cmyk: Four-colour process print: the colour split into cyan, magenta, yellow and black (grey component replacement), each a dot screen at its classic angle (black at halftoneAngle, cyan 30 degrees before it, magenta 30 after, yellow 45 before: 15, 75, 0 and 45 at the default angle), the inks multiplied on white paper, as comics were printed.

x-og-variants.shade: The shade only: Ben-Day dots in the shadows while lit tones keep their colour (Hi-Fi Rush, Spider-Verse).

Stylise.description:
Stylisation primitives that move the frame away from the photographic: a low-resolution pixel grid scaled up by whole numbers, fewer tones or a fixed palette through an ordered or blue-noise dither, halftone dots, cross-hatching, painterly smoothing over a canvas, ink lines on tonal edges, flat colour bands by depth, and the vertex snapping, affine textures and coarse depth of early 3D hardware. They compose: a look (og.load.look) sets this with PostEffects and RenderSettings, and the game's art direction is in that data, not in the engine. Every primitive is off at its zero value (0, false, none) and then costs nothing: no pass is recorded and no pipeline is built. RenderCapabilities.stylise names the primitives this renderer draws; a field it does not name is carried and read back but not drawn. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.
Order in the frame: depth bands colour the lit scene with the fog, before tone mapping; after tone mapping and PostEffects' grading come paint, hatching, halftone and ink, then posterize and palette quantise through the dither, all at the logical resolution, and the pixel grid is scaled up last. The UI and screen-space sprites are drawn over the scaled frame at the output's resolution, unstylised.

pixelHeight.description: The logical resolution: the scene is rendered this many pixels tall and scaled up to the output by a whole number with nearest filtering, as a low-resolution three.js render target drawn with NearestFilter; 0 renders at the output's resolution. The height sets the scale (pixelUpscale); the width is the output's aspect times the height, rounded, but at most the output's width over the scale, so the last column gives way rather than the scale: 240 rows at 1280x720 are 426.67 columns, rounded to 427, and 427 x 3 = 1281 does not fit, so the grid is 426 x 240 at 3x (1278 x 720, a 1-pixel border each side). Heights that divide the output's evenly fill it: 180 (4x), 240 (3x) and 360 (2x) at 720p, 270 (4x) and 360 (3x) at 1080p.

pixelUpscale.description: The whole-number scale from the logical to the output resolution, a hard request: honoured whenever pixelHeight times it fits the output's height (a smaller scale than the largest leaves the border it implies: 240 lines at 2x in 1280x720 draw 854 x 480 in a 213 x 120 border), else the largest that fits; 0 takes the largest that fits (720 / 240 = 3, 1080 / 240 = 4, rounded down). A frame that does not fill the output is centred with Camera.background round it.

pixelSnap.description: Snap the camera and world sprites to the logical pixel grid, so a moving orthographic camera scrolls by whole pixels and sprites in a 3D world keep their edges (pixel sprites in 3D sets).

posterize.description: Tones per colour channel after tone mapping (2 to 64): smooth gradients become flat steps; 0 is off.

posterizeMode.description: How posterize steps a colour: each channel apart (channel), or its value and its tint apart so light never changes its hue (tone).

palette.description: Quantise every pixel to the nearest colour of this palette (og.load.palette), measured in a perceptual space after posterize; 0 is none.

dither.description: How the steps of posterize and palette are mixed: none rounds every pixel, an ordered or blue-noise pattern alternates the two nearest steps in proportion.

ditherStrength.description: The dither's amplitude in steps: 1 spreads exactly one step, less keeps flatter bands.

ditherScale.description: The size of one dither cell in logical pixels.

halftone.description: Halftone print: tones become dots on a rotated grid, larger where the image is darker; 0 is off, 1 dots only.

halftoneSize.description: The dot grid's pitch in logical pixels.

halftoneSpace.description: Where the dots lie: screen, a grid over the frame; surface, grids on the surfaces that stay on them as the camera moves and wrap round forms (halftoneSize is then about the pitch in pixels where they lie); object, the same grids in each instance's own space, so a moving object carries its dots.

hatching.description: Pencil or ink cross-hatching from a tonal art map: darker tones add strokes in more directions over a paper-light ground, each set thinning and fading in from clean paper at its tone; 0 is off, 1 strokes only.

hatchingScale.description: The spacing of hatch lines in logical pixels.

hatchingLevels.description: How many tones the hatching distinguishes, each adding one stroke direction or density (1 to 6).

hatchingAngle.description: The direction of the first stroke set.

hatchingColor.description: The stroke colour (linear): graphite, sepia or ink.

hatchingPaper.description: The paper the strokes lie on (linear): one-ink hatching lifts the ground's light tones towards it, and under hatchingKeepColor the wash lies on the paper's colour at the wash's own lightness (a cream sketchbook, a grey card, a blue print); white keeps the frame's own.

hatchingSpace.description: Where the strokes lie: screen, stripes over the frame that follow the tone alone; surface, strokes laid on the surfaces that follow the tone and the form, wrapping round curved objects and staying on them as the camera moves (hatchingScale is then about the spacing in pixels where they lie); object, the same strokes in each instance's own space, so a moving or turning object carries its strokes.

hatchingDepth.description: Hatching from luminance and depth: the depth-normal prepass's silhouettes and creases darken the tone the strokes follow, at this strength, so strokes gather along contours and folds as inkDepth inks them (the edges are inkDepthThreshold's and inkNormalThreshold's, found within one stroke spacing). 0 is the tone alone; above 0 the frame runs the prepass PostEffects.outline uses.

paintRadius.description: Painterly smoothing (an anisotropic Kuwahara filter with eight sectors over a smoothed structure tensor, Kyprianidis 2009 and 2010): flat regions and incoherent texture (grass, noise) become strokes of one colour this many logical pixels across, while edges and thin lines keep their shape; with the prepass no stroke crosses an object's edge and detail (paintDetail) keeps its shape; 0 is off. In a profile 2d project under the art contract the paint and watercolor fields are the cook's, applied in each texture's own texels, and the frame draws neither pass, so a sprite is painted once.

paintAnisotropy.description: How far the strokes follow the image's structure: 0 round brush cells, 0.5 the filter's classic ellipses, 1 thin strokes along every coherent contour, which keep lines a pixel wide.

paintEdgeDarkening.description: Pigment pooling at the edges of colour regions, as wet watercolour dries darker at its rim; 0 is none.

paintBleed.description: Colour bleeding across edges into its neighbours, wet in wet; 0 is none.

paintCanvas.description: A tileable paper or canvas texture (og.load.texture) laid over the frame by paintCanvasStrength; 0 is none.

paintCanvasStrength.description: How much the canvas texture modulates the frame: 0 none, 1 its full grain.

paintCanvasScale.description: Canvas texels per logical pixel, with paintCanvasSpace screen (and on the sky).

paintCanvasSpace.description: Where the canvas lies: screen, over the frame (the scene slides under the paper as the camera moves); surface, on the surfaces, so the grain sticks to the scene, foreshortened with the floor and walls; object, in each instance's own space, so a moving object carries its grain.

paintCanvasWorldScale.description: Canvas texels per metre with paintCanvasSpace surface: 128 repeats a 256-texel canvas every two metres.

ink.description: Ink lines where the tone changes sharply (luminance edges), over every surface, sprite and texture alike: comic and storybook contours without PostEffects.outline's depth prepass. inkDepth adds the prepass's silhouettes and creases.

inkThreshold.description: The luminance step that counts as an edge (0 to 1 in display units): lower draws more lines.

inkWidth.description: The line width in logical pixels.

inkDepth.description: With ink: lines also where the depth-normal prepass breaks (silhouettes against what is behind, creases between faces), at this strength: comic contours round flat colours that luminance alone misses. 0 is luminance only; above 0 the frame runs the prepass PostEffects.outline uses.

inkDepthThreshold.description: With inkDepth: the relative depth step to a farther neighbour that counts as a silhouette (0.04 is 4 %), as PostEffects.outlineDepthThreshold: lower inks smaller steps.

inkNormalThreshold.description: With inkDepth: the normal change between neighbours of about the same depth that counts as a crease (1 - cos of the angle; 0.4 is about 53 degrees), as PostEffects.outlineNormalThreshold: lower inks gentler folds.

depthBands.description: Colour bands by depth (2 to 8): the scene from depthBandsNear to depthBandsFar is cut into this many equal layers, the first in depthBandsNearColor, the last in depthBandsFarColor, those between stepping evenly from one to the other in lightness, chroma and hue (never through grey), for layered-silhouette and stage looks; 0 is off. For side and three-quarter views, where the depth runs across the frame: seen from above the play area lies at one depth and falls in one band.

depthBandsFar.description: Where the last band ends; the last band (the far colour) starts one band's depth before it, and everything beyond it is the far colour too.

depthBandsNearColor.description: The nearest band's colour (linear, before exposure).

depthBandsFarColor.description: The farthest band's colour (linear, before exposure).

depthBandsFlatten.description: How far a band replaces the surfaces' own shading: 1 flat silhouettes in the band's colour; 0 a tint over the lit scene, its colours times the band's at unit luminance (a coloured filter: the shading, the value and the surfaces' own hues show through); between, a mix of the two.

vertexSnap.description: Snap every vertex of the 3D scene to a screen grid this many logical pixels wide, as fixed-point hardware did: geometry jitters by whole steps as it moves; 0 is off.

affineTexturing.description: How far texture coordinates are interpolated without perspective correction: 1 fully affine, so textures warp and swim across large polygons as on early consoles; 0 is off.

depthBits.description: Quantise depth to this many bits, for the coarse depth buffers of early 3D (12 to 16 are period-like: distant surfaces fight); 0 keeps full precision.

paintDetail.description: How far detail keeps its shape under paintRadius: a pixel's radius shrinks by its detail (its material's StandardMaterialDesc.paintDetail, or paintCharacterDetail on a skinned mesh) times this, so faces, hands and lettering stay drawn while grass and broad areas paint; with it no stroke crosses an object's edge. Above 0 the frame runs the depth-normal prepass where it draws meshes; 0 paints every pixel alike.

paintCharacterDetail.description: The detail of a skinned mesh's pixels (a character's face and hands) where its material sets less: 0 painted as the rest, 1 kept as drawn.

watercolorEdgeDarkening.description: The watercolour wash (Bousseau et al. 2006, Montesdeoca et al. 2018), drawn over the painted frame after paintRadius's strokes: pigment pooled in a rim two to three pixels wide at a wash's outer boundary, the colour there raised to one plus the strength, as a wash dries darker at its border. A boundary is a step between two colour regions wider than a line (the colour averaged over six pixels either side differs) or a silhouette against something farther behind; a seam, a crease or another object of the same colour is none, since one wash covers them, so a texture's seams and a tiled floor get no rim, where paintEdgeDarkening pools broadly over the source's structure; 0 is none.

watercolorGranulation.description: Pigment settling into the paper's grain: a pigment density about one from the paper's relief (paintCanvas's height about its mean, in units of its spread, so any canvas reads as paper; a noise a few pixels across without one), heavier in the pits and thinner on the peaks and broken by a grain two to three pixels across, each colour thinned towards the paper (watercolorPaper) where the density is under one and thickened where it is over (Bousseau's C(1 - (1 - C)(d - 1))). The density is weighed by the pigment load, so bare paper and the palest washes stay clean and the dark and saturated ones granulate, and the wash keeps its mean value where paintCanvasStrength's grain only darkens it; 0 is none.

watercolorTurbulence.description: Pigment drifting as the wash dries: the same density from a slow noise about a hundred canvas texels across (and half that), laid where the canvas lies (paintCanvasSpace) and seeded by the object under the pixel so no blotch runs across two washes, weighed by the pigment load so the paper and the palest washes stay even; a wash is patchy, lighter here and darker there; 0 is none.

watercolorDryBrush.description: A dry brush skipping over the paper's tooth: its peaks (the relief past half its spread, in the paper's own clusters) left bare as the paper (watercolorPaper) in the rim at a wash's outer boundary (watercolorEdgeDarkening's) and on the light-catching tones, the brightest washes first; 0 is none.

watercolorWobble.description: The painted frame displaced by the paper's relief, up to this many logical pixels, so every edge wavers with the tooth as a wash's does (MNPR's substrate distortion); 0 is none.

watercolorPaper.description: The paper's colour (linear): what the wash thins towards and the dry brush leaves bare.

ditherSpace.description: Where the dither's cells lie: screen, a grid over the frame (a moving camera slides the scene under it, so the pattern crawls); surface, cells on the surfaces at least ditherScale pixels on the screen each way (each surface axis by whole octaves, so a receding floor's cells are long along its depth), so the pattern stays on what it shades as the camera moves (Lucas Pope's Obra Dinn), and the sky's on a cube round the camera so turning carries them; object, in each mesh instance's own space, so a moving object carries its pattern. Off screen the frame runs the prepass.

halftoneMode.description: How the halftone inks: one ink (halftoneColor) or four-colour process print (cmyk).

halftoneMisregistration.description: With halftoneMode cmyk: how far the cyan, magenta and yellow plates sit off the black one, in logical pixels, as a cheap print's colour slips past its line art; 0 is in register.

halftoneRegion.description: Which tones the halftone prints on: all (the dots reproduce the tone on white paper, merging in the darks as print does), the shade only or the highlights only (the darkest or lightest third of the tones). Under a region the dots are Ben-Day dots: a tint printed over the region's own colour, at most 0.4 of their cell wide so they never touch, and a flat shade stays one colour with separate dots on it. They fade to flat ink on surfaces turned away from the camera (a floor seen from a game camera's height), where dots squeezed into a few rows read as a checker.

hatchingKeepColor.description: Colour hatching: the ground is a light wash of its colour (as light as one-ink hatching's paper, keeping its hue, and more of a strong colour's chroma than a weak tint's, so props keep their colour while a greyish floor goes to paper; conformed art keeps its authored colour, with half the chroma the lift would take) and each stroke is that colour darkened towards hatchingColor, so hue and chroma stay under the strokes; false lays strokes of hatchingColor over a paper-light ground.

MaterialStyle.description: Stylised defaults for every lit material, so a whole scene takes one treatment without editing each material: toon shading and its ramp, a coloured shadow side, rim light, outlines whose width falls off with distance, and flat facets. Each applies to a material (og.render.standardMaterial or a loaded glTF's) that leaves that field at its own default; a terrain (og.Terrain) takes toon (the built-in three bands, matte) and shadowTint; unlit and shader materials, materials with StandardMaterialDesc.styled false, sprites and the UI are untouched, and toon passes by a material with a MeshPhysicalMaterial lobe (clearcoat, sheen, transmission, iridescence, anisotropy, ior), which keeps its physical shading. All off (false, 0) is no change. A look sets it; RenderCapabilities.stylise names what this renderer draws. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

toon.description: Cel shading for every lit material, as StandardMaterialDesc.toon: light quantised by the ramp, hard highlights. A material with a physical lobe (clearcoat, transmission and the rest) keeps its physical shading; set its own toon to make it toon anyway.

gradientMap.description: The toon ramp for materials without their own (StandardMaterialDesc.gradientMap, og.load.texture): its first row maps the light's angle to the light received, read without filtering; 0 is three built-in bands.

shadowTint.description: The colour the shadowed side of a toon or lit surface moves towards instead of black (linear): the cool or warm shadow of illustration.

shadowTintAmount.description: How far shadowed light moves towards shadowTint; 0 is off.

shadowDarkness.description: How far shadowed surfaces fall towards black: where the sun does not reach (the toon ramp's dark band, the side turned away, a cast shadow) a surface loses this share of the sun's ramp and of the ambient light (the Environment's map and its hemisphere light) as well, so 1 draws every shadow as a solid black mass (the ink shadows of noir comics) and the toon ramp's middle band keeps half its light; point, spot and rect lights and the emissive still show inside it, and shadowTint's light is added after it. 0 is off.

rimColor.description: Rim (fresnel) light for materials without their own (linear).

rimIntensity.description: The rim light's strength; 0 is none.

rimPower.description: How tight the rim is (higher: thinner).

outlineColor.description: The outline colour for materials without their own (linear).

outlineWidth.description: The outline width in pixels at outlineDistance for materials without their own; 0 is none. A hull outline (StandardMaterialDesc.outlineWidth): silhouettes and creases against other objects, never the faces of one, so voxel and flat-shaded models stay clean. A surface seen at a grazing angle is lined only where it ends: a 1,600 m ground under a chase camera keeps its far edge and nothing else (no band along the horizon).

outlineDistance.description: The distance at which outlines are outlineWidth wide: nearer they grow, up to four times outlineWidth, farther they thin in proportion (an inked look keeps line weight by depth); 0 keeps every outline outlineWidth wide.

flatShading.description: Shade every lit material with face normals, as StandardMaterialDesc.flatShading: visible facets for low-poly, paper-craft and voxel looks.

surface.description: A made surface on every lit material (clay, paper, plastic): its normal detail, colour grain and light response, in each mesh's own space; none is no change. Unlit materials, materials with StandardMaterialDesc.styled false and those with a MeshPhysicalMaterial lobe keep their own shading.

surfaceStrength.description: How strongly the surface shows: its bumps, grain and wrapped light; 0 is none.

surfaceScale.description: The size of the surface's pattern in metres of the mesh's own space (a clay lump, the paper's fibre); 0 takes the surface's own (clay 0.12, paper 0.15, plastic 0.3).

toonAmbient.description: How smooth a toon material's ambient light (the Environment and its hemisphere light) stays: 0 one flat colour, the light from above and below averaged (MToon's equalised ambient), with the environment's reflection as one flat colour, so the bands sit on flat colour; 1 the smooth PBR ambient and reflections, which wash the bands out.

toonSoftness.description: The toon bands' and highlight's edges, anti-aliased over this many pixels (lilToon's screen-space smoothing); 0 hard steps that only TAA softens.

outlinePlace.description: Where outlines lie against an object's silhouette: inside (the zero value, its own edge pixels), outside (round it, at any width, anti-aliased) or both. Creases between objects stay inside.

wireframe.description: Draw every lit material's feature edges over its faces (StandardMaterialDesc.wireframe's edges, with wireframeAngle and wireframeColor from this style where the material sets none), in the colour the surface shows along each edge (its colour times its maps, plus its emissive light, so emissive colours glow through bloom) or wireframeColor; the faces stay drawn as usual and hide the edges behind them, as vector displays drew with hidden lines removed: vector and neon looks, whose dark materials make the fill. A material's own wireframe draws its edges alone.

wireframeAngle.description: The crease angle wireframe draws past (StandardMaterialDesc.wireframeAngle); 0 every triangle edge.

wireframeColor.description: The look's line colour for wireframe (StandardMaterialDesc.wireframeColor), linear, above 1 blooms; black (the zero value) draws each edge in the colour its surface shows there.

LookInfo.description: A loaded look: where it came from and what applying it sets.

name.description: Its name (the file's `name`, else its file name without `.ogt`).

extends.description: The looks it builds on, nearest first: asset ids under assets/ and built-in preset slugs.

mood.description: The mood it is drawn in (bright, dark, warm, cold, soft or high-contrast): a preset's own, or the one the game's look asked for, whose layer the cook laid over the preset (docs/art.md §2.10); unset for a look that names none.

resources.description: The resources it sets, by IDL name (RenderSettings, PostEffects, Stylise, MaterialStyle, Fog, Sky, Environment, and the art contract: ArtPalette, ArtPixels, ArtTexels, ArtShape, ArtLine, ArtMotion, ArtCamera). Applying it replaces each of them whole: the fields the look names take its values, the rest their defaults.

style.description: The UI style its `ui` line names (a game's own or a built-in by slug), loaded with it; applying the look configures the UI with it.

antialias.description: The antialiasing it asks for. GameDesc.look's is the renderer's when GameDesc.render leaves antialias out; a running renderer keeps its method.

Lighting2D.description: 2D lighting of the sprite layers minLayer to maxLayer (sprites, 2D particles and og.Tilemap layers there, a map layer unless its `lit` property is false): their colour is multiplied by ambient plus every Light2D reaching the pixel, shadowed by Occluder2Ds and sprites with castShadow. A texture with a normal map (`normal auto` or `normal "file.png"` in its import settings' texture block) is shaded by where its surface faces each light, which stands Light2D.height above the plane; a flat area keeps exactly the light it had. Other layers (and the overlay) are drawn as authored. Off by default.

ambient.description: Light everywhere (0 is darkness outside the lights).

maxLayer.description: The highest lit sprite layer (above it: UI and HUD layers stay unlit).

resolution.description: The light map's resolution as a fraction of the target.

shadowAngles.description: The angular resolution of each shadow-casting light's shadow: how many directions around it are traced against the occluders (more keeps a small occluder far from a large light sharp, at more cost).

Light2DKind.description: What shape of light a Light2D is.

x-og-variants.point: Light all around its position, to radius.
x-og-variants.spot: A cone along the entity's local +x (turned with its Transform about z), innerAngle to outerAngle either side of the axis, to radius.
x-og-variants.global: Light on every lit pixel of its layers at full intensity, from the direction of the entity's local +x at height (for normal maps); no radius and no shadows.

Light2D.description: A light in the 2D plane at the entity's position (z ignored): color times intensity at its centre, falling to zero at radius with (1 - d/r)^falloff (faded over its last tenth, so even a falloff below 1 ends without a rim), shadowed by occluders when castShadows. Lighting2D.enabled turns 2D lighting on; at most 64 are drawn.

radius.description: Where the light reaches zero, in world units.

sourceRadius.description: The light's own size: larger gives softer shadows.

castShadows.description: Occluders between the light and a pixel shade it (point and spot lights).

innerAngle.description: A spot's half-angle at full intensity, in radians.

outerAngle.description: A spot's half-angle where it reaches zero, in radians (at least innerAngle).

height.description: How far above the 2D plane the light is, in world units: the slant normal-mapped sprites see it at (0 grazes the surface).

layers.description: The light layers it lights: a bit per layer, matched against each sprite's, rig's or tilemap's og.LightMask2D (layer 0, bit 1, without one).

Occluder2D.description: A shape that blocks 2D light (walls, crates, characters), centred on the entity's position and turned and scaled with it about z: a width by height rectangle, or the polygon `points` gives. Pixels inside it are not shadowed by it. At most 128 are drawn.

width.description: Its width in world units (without points).

height.description: Its height in world units (without points).

points.description: A polygon instead of the rectangle: up to 16 vertices as x, y pairs in the entity's frame, in order around it; concave is fine. Fewer than three vertices keeps the rectangle.

layers.description: The light layers whose lights it blocks (a bit per layer, as Light2D.layers).

LightMask2D.description: The light layers that light the entity's sprite, flipbook, 2D rig or tilemap: a Light2D lights it when their `layers` share a bit. Without one an entity is on layer 0 (bit 1). At most four different masks are lit in one frame; any further mask is lit as layer 0.

layers.description: A bit per light layer.

Decal.description: A projected decal (scorch marks, blood, posters, bullet holes): the entity's unit box (-0.5 to 0.5 on each axis, scaled by its Transform) projected along its local -Z onto every lit opaque surface inside it, shaded with the surface. Its image is the uvMin to uvMax region of RenderSettings.decalAtlas (a solid colour without one); with a normalMin to normalMax region, that region of the same atlas is a tangent-space normal map that bends the surface's normal (cracks, a bullet hole's rim, embossed lettering). Later decals blend over earlier ones. Tens of thousands can be placed: each pixel walks only the decals whose box can reach it, and at most 255 overlap at one place (the newest are kept).

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the atlas.

uvMin.description: The atlas region's top-left corner, v down.

uvMax.description: The atlas region's bottom-right corner, v down.

emissive.description: Linear light added where the decal covers (glowing runes, lava).

roughness.description: The surface roughness under the decal; -1 keeps the surface's.

angleFade.description: Surfaces turned further than this from the projection direction are not covered (the last 15 degrees fade).

normalMin.description: The top-left corner of the decal's normal map in RenderSettings.decalAtlas, v down (glTF's convention: +X along u, +Y up the image). Equal to normalMax (the default), the decal has no normal map.

normalMax.description: The bottom-right corner of the decal's normal map in the atlas, v down.

normalScale.description: How strongly the normal map bends the surface, as three.js normalScale.
