targets.description: Where agents go: each point's cell is a target.

NavMeshDesc.description: A navmesh built at runtime over a flat floor (a procedural level): the floor box, the boxes it carves out, and the agent it is for.

min.description: The floor's lowest corner (its y is the floor's height).

blocked.description: Boxes standing on the floor (walls, crates).

agentRadius.description: Walls are kept this far away.

tileSize.description: Cells per tile side: an obstacle rebuilds the tiles it touches.

mesh.description: What NavAgent.nav and the queries take.

min.description: The lowest corner of the box around its polygons.

max.description: The highest corner of the box around its polygons (its highest walkable floor's y).

profile.description: The agent profile it was baked for (og.nav.load's profile); empty for a navmesh of one unnamed agent and for og.nav.build.

Behaviour.description: A loaded behaviour tree or state machine.

AiAgent.description: An entity that thinks with a behaviour. Give it an og.NavAgent to move and an og.Perception to see and hear.

behaviour.description: The behaviour it runs (og.ai.load); 0 runs nothing.

thinkEvery.description: Thinks every this many ticks (1: every tick); agents are staggered by their order.

status.description: AI_RUNNING, AI_SUCCESS or AI_FAILURE after the last think (0 before the first; written by og.ai).

state.description: The state machine's state, an index into BehaviourInfo.states (written by og.ai).

node.description: The node it ran last, an index into BehaviourInfo.nodes (written by og.ai).

changes.description: Times the state or the running node changed (written by og.ai).

Perception.description: What an agent sees and hears. It sees the nearest og.Perceivable of another team within `sight`, inside the `fov` cone around `forward` (or the way it last moved), unless a collider is in the way; it hears a spatial sound that starts (og.SoundStarted) or a game noise (og.ai.noise) within `hearing` times its loudness, except its own: a sound of its entity or of an entity under it (og.Parent), or a noise whose NoiseDesc.source is one of them.

fov.description: The width of its view cone (360: all round).

eyeHeight.description: Its eyes are this far above its position (+y).

occlude.description: Colliders hide what is behind them.

occluders.description: Collision layers that block sight (0: every layer).

hearing.description: How far it hears a sound of loudness 1 (a source's volume).

memory.description: How long a lost target stays its target.

team.description: Its team: it perceives og.Perceivable entities of other teams.

forward.description: Where it looks; zero: the way it last moved (before it moves, the way its Transform faces: +Z in 3D, +X in 2D).

target.description: What it sees or remembers seeing (written by og.ai).

sees.description: It sees the target now (written by og.ai).

lastSeen.description: Where it last saw the target (written by og.ai).

sinceSeen.description: Seconds since it last saw a target (written by og.ai; 1e6 before the first time).

heard.description: It heard something this tick (written by og.ai).

heardAt.description: Where it last heard something (written by og.ai).

sinceHeard.description: Seconds since it last heard something (written by og.ai; 1e6 before the first time).

Perceivable.description: Something agents of other teams can see.

team.description: Its team (agents of the same team ignore it).

eyeHeight.description: Agents look at a point this far above its position (+y).

AiChanged.description: An agent's state or running node changed (systems read it the tick after).

AiActionStarted.description: A game action (`action <name> args` in a behaviour) started: play its animation (such as a reload), open its door or speak its dialogue, then call og.ai.finish when it ends; until then the node runs. Read the tick after. Joins the world's types only once a behaviour with a game action is loaded.

node.description: The action's node, an index into BehaviourInfo.nodes.

args.description: Its arguments as written, separated by spaces (at most 255 bytes; longer ones are refused when the behaviour is parsed).

AiActionStopped.description: A game action stopped: the game finished it (og.ai.finish), or the behaviour moved on first (stop playing it). Read the tick after.

result.description: AI_SUCCESS or AI_FAILURE, as og.ai.finish said, or AI_INTERRUPTED.

keys.description: Its declared blackboard keys (its subtrees' too).

subtrees.description: The behaviours its `use` nodes inline, every one reached, in the order first met.

NoiseDesc.description: A noise agents may hear next tick.

loudness.description: How loud: heard within Perception.hearing times this.

source.description: Who makes it (0: nobody): that entity, and the agents it is under (og.Parent), do not hear it.

state.description: A machine's state (empty for a tree).

node.description: The node it ran last, such as `chase`.

path.description: The path to it from the root, such as `ReactiveFallback > ReactiveSequence chase > chase`.

blackboard.description: Its blackboard, keys to numbers, booleans, points and entity handles.

target.description: Its target (0: none).

StorySaliency.description: How Yarn node and line groups choose eligible content. All random draws use the checkpointed story RNG fork.

x-og-variants.first: First eligible content in source order.
x-og-variants.best: Most specific eligible condition, with source order breaking ties.
x-og-variants.bestLeastRecentlyViewed: Least viewed eligible content, then most specific, with source order breaking ties.
x-og-variants.randomBestLeastRecentlyViewed: Least viewed, then most specific, with random ties.
x-og-variants.conditionalFirstWeighted: Prefer conditional content over fallback content; draw ties by #weight (the engine default).

Story.description: The story's counters (written by og.story; the story itself is a state block). Registered at the first og.story.load.

lines.description: Lines shown so far (DialogueView.seq of the latest).

activeQuests.description: Quests started and not yet completed or failed.

DialogueShown.description: A conversation shows a new line (start the voice, reset the reveal). Sent before the game's systems, the tick after the call that moved it.

DialogueEnded.description: A conversation ended: its top-level Yarn node returned, reached `<<stop>>`, or og.story.stop stopped it. Sent the tick after.

DialogueCheck.description: An active check was rolled (d20 plus the stat against the target): reveal the roll. Sent the tick after.

stat.description: The variable read as the stat.

target.description: What the roll plus the stat had to reach.

passed.description: Whether roll + stat reached the target.

QuestUpdated.description: A quest started, counted, changed stage, completed or failed. Sent the tick after.

BarkSaid.description: An entity barked (og.story.bark or og.story.ambient): show its line over it with og.story.barks. Sent the tick after it was asked for.

bark.description: The bark's id in its dialogue.

StoryEvent.description: A Yarn command such as `<<give_sword {$amount}>>`: open the shop, give the sword, play the cutscene. Sent the tick after.

arg.description: Its argument, evaluated and written as text (empty without one).

name.description: A dialogue's name or a quest's id: what og.story.start and og.story.startQuest take.

nodes.description: A dialogue's nodes, in order (a quest: its stages).

variables.description: Declared variables: Yarn declarations are global unless listed in a #og-local file tag.

node.description: The node to start at (empty: the first non-bark Yarn node).

cast.description: Speaker ids to the entities playing them, `{ smith: entity }`: SpeakerView.entity (for a speech bubble or a camera).

id.description: The speaker's id (`narrator` for the narrator).

name.description: Its name, resolved in the active locale (empty for the narrator).

portrait.description: A portrait image's asset path (empty: none).

expression.description: The portrait's variant: the line's `expression`, else the speaker's.

stat.description: The variable read as the stat.

target.description: What the stat (passive) or a d20 plus the stat (active) must reach.

chance.description: The chance it passes, 0 to 1: an active check's share of the d20's faces that pass; a passive one's 1 or 0.

kind.description: passive (a threshold that enables the choice) or active (rolled when chosen).

ChoiceView.description: A choice the node offers (hidden ones are left out).

index.description: What og.story.choose takes: its place among the node's choices, hidden ones counted.

text.description: Its text, resolved in the active locale.

spans.description: Yarn attributes on the plain text, in Unicode scalar offsets; unknown attributes are preserved.

args.description: The arguments its text was resolved with.

enabled.description: Whether it can be chosen now (its `if` holds and a passive check passes).

reason.description: Why it is disabled, resolved in the active locale (empty without a `reason`).

reasonArgs.description: The arguments the reason was resolved with.

visited.description: Chosen before in this conversation (drawn muted).

kind.description: The game's word for its icon: leave, trade, attack, lie...

check.description: Its check, if it has one.

defaultChoice.description: The ChoiceView.index taken when it runs out.

stat.description: The variable read as the stat.

target.description: What the roll plus the stat had to reach.

DialogueView.description: What a conversation shows now: the line in full (the dialogue box paces its own reveal), its speaker and the choices, if it waits on them.

seq.description: Counts lines shown across the story: a new number is a new line, even when a node repeats.

seen.description: The line had been read before it was shown (skip-read, a dimmed backlog); og.story.reset keeps what was read.

args.description: The arguments it was resolved with (evaluated when it was shown).

text.description: The line, resolved in the active locale.

spans.description: Localized Yarn attributes in Unicode scalar offsets. The character span covers the full Speaker: prefix, including its whitespace.

voice.description: Its voice clip's asset path (empty: none). og.story plays it on its own entity (an og.AudioSource on the sfx bus) from the tick after the line is shown, and stops it when the line moves on.

voiceTicks.description: The voice's length in ticks (0: no voice, or one that did not load).

voiceLeft.description: Ticks of the voice still to play: voiceTicks until it starts, 0 once it has ended (advance then, for auto-advance).

shot.description: The camera shot it is shown in: its `shot`, else its node's (a virtual camera's entity name or a cast role); empty: none. While it shows, og.story makes that og.VirtualCamera og.CameraBrain.solo: a name is the entity of that name, a role the cast entity's own og.VirtualCamera, else the first one whose lookAt is that entity. When no running conversation's line has a shot the game's own solo is handed back.

choices.description: The choices, when it waits on them; empty while a line waits for og.story.advance.

timer.description: The choice timer, while it runs.

lastCheck.description: The last active check this conversation rolled.

ended.description: The conversation has ended (the view keeps its last line).

ChosenView.description: The choice made while a line was shown.

text.description: Its text, resolved in the active locale.

spans.description: Localized Yarn attributes in Unicode scalar offsets.

StoryLine.description: A line of a conversation's backlog.

text.description: The line, resolved in the active locale.

spans.description: Localized Yarn attributes in Unicode scalar offsets.

seen.description: It had been read before it was shown.

chosen.description: The choice made on it, if any.

entity.description: Who barks: its og.story.barks entry, `self.` in the bark's conditions and arguments.

topic.description: The topic: one of the bark's `topic`s, such as idle or alarm.

dialogue.description: Only this dialogue's barks (empty: every loaded dialogue's).

AmbientDesc.description: An entity that barks on its own.

jitter.description: Up to this many ticks more each time, drawn on the story's stream.

seq.description: The line's number: a new number is a new bark.

args.description: The arguments it was resolved with (evaluated when it was said, world reads included).

text.description: The line, resolved in the active locale.

spans.description: Localized Yarn attributes in Unicode scalar offsets.

speaker.description: The bark's speaker (entity: who says it).

voice.description: Its voice clip (empty: none), played as a conversation's.

voiceLeft.description: Ticks of its voice still to play.

priority.description: Its priority: only a higher one interrupts it.

MarkerDesc.description: Where a quest's objective is, for the map, compass and tracker.

entity.description: An entity to point at (0: none).

position.description: A point to point at, when there is no entity.

MarkerView.description: Where a quest points: the marker og.story.mark set, else the current stage's first undone objective's `marker`.

name.description: Its name, resolved in the active locale.

ObjectiveView.description: An objective of a quest's current stage.

text.description: Its text, resolved in the active locale with `count` and `target` among its arguments.

target.description: Counts needed.

failed.description: Left undone when the quest failed.

optional.description: Not needed to finish the stage.

hidden.description: Not revealed yet: declared hidden and not yet counted (the log leaves it out or shows ???).

QuestView.description: A quest as a quest log shows it.

title.description: Its title, resolved in the active locale.

summary.description: The current stage's summary, else the quest's, resolved.

tracked.description: Shown in the HUD tracker (og.story.track; the first quest started is tracked).

isNew.description: Not looked at since it started (og.story.markSeen clears it).

updated.description: Changed since it was last looked at (og.story.markSeen clears it).

updatedTick.description: The tick it last changed (sort the log by recent).

PlatformOrder.description: How a leaderboard sorts; the first submission to a board fixes it.

PlatformAnswered.description: An answer arrived: sent by og.platform at the start of the tick it was applied, read by systems the tick after (og.platform.result has it at once).

ok.description: Whether it succeeded; og.platform.result has the data or the error.

key.description: The key: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

value.description: Any JSON value, at most 64 KiB encoded.

revision.description: Write only if the key is at this revision (a conflict otherwise, whose error carries the revision the key is at now); 0 writes whatever is there (the last write wins).

create.description: Write only if the key has never been written (a conflict otherwise); revision is then ignored.

score.description: The score, or a time in seconds for an ascending board. Required: a desc without one is refused, never submitted as 0.

order.description: How the board sorts, fixed by its first submission.

count.description: How many entries: the top `count`, or `count` around the player.

PointDesc.description: Origin Point for something the player did.

reason.description: Why, as the game names it: `level.completed`, `daily.streak` (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`).

amount.description: How many points the game asks for; the platform decides what it grants.

AiMarkDesc.description: Marks content the game shows as generated by AI, for the platform's disclosure.

kind.description: What: `text`, `image`, `audio`, `level`, `character` (1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, `_` and `-`, a letter first).

label.description: What the player sees it as, at most 120 characters.

model.description: The model or service, when known (at most 80 characters).

SaveSlotDesc.description: A save slot: a long text (a world.snapshot()) kept across as many store keys as it needs.

slot.description: The slot's name: 1 to 60 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` (`slot1`). Its keys are the name itself (the manifest) and `<slot>.a0`, `<slot>.a1`, ... or `<slot>.b0`, ... (the parts).

text.description: The text: at most 512 KiB of UTF-8 (eight parts of 64 KiB).

meta.description: What a title screen shows of the slot (`{ place, hour }`), kept in the manifest so loadSlot with metaOnly reads it without the parts: any JSON, at most 4 KiB encoded.

LoadSlotDesc.description: Which slot to read, and how much of it.

slot.description: The slot's name, as saveSlot wrote it.

metaOnly.description: Read the manifest alone: the answer's text stays null (a title's Continue label, before the player asks for the world).

code.description: offline, timeout, invalid, unauthorized, not_found, conflict, too_large, rate_limited, unavailable, failed, cancelled or no_fill.

retryable.description: Whether the same call may succeed later.

revision.description: For a conflict of a conditional write: the revision the key is at now (read it again, merge, write at it); 0 otherwise.

data.description: The answer (see each function); null on failure.

tick.description: The tick it was answered at.

time.description: The host's clock when it answered, UTC milliseconds since 1970 (PlatformInfo.clock says whose); 0 when the host gave none. A slot call (saveSlot, loadSlot) answers the time of the store answer that ended it.

host.description: `player` (a Player frames the game), `local` (the native host's JSON store or the browser's own storage) or `none`.

capabilities.description: The methods it answers: store.get, store.set, store.list, leaderboard.submit, leaderboard.top, leaderboard.around, telemetry, point, ai.mark, purchase.products, purchase.buy, purchase.entitlements, purchase.consume, ad.ready, ad.show, achievement.unlock, achievement.progress, achievement.list, player.get, friends.list, invite.send, invite.list, share (og.platform.supports asks for one).

clock.description: Whose clock og.platform.now and the answers' `time` read: `player` (the Player's answers carry its time), `browser` (the web host's own clock: the Player gives no time yet, docs/platform-asks.md), `system` (the native host's system clock), `fixed` (`og run --clock` and playtests: a clock that starts where it is told and moves with the ticks) or `none`.

x-og-variants.rewarded: The player chose to watch it for a reward: the answer says whether they watched it to the end.
x-og-variants.interstitial: Shown at a break the game picks (between levels): the player may close it.

x-og-variants.purchase: A purchase settled: a pending one completed or failed, or one was refunded. Data `{ purchase, product, quantity, state }`, state `completed`, `failed` or `refunded`.
x-og-variants.entitlements: The player's entitlements changed without a call (bought on another device, a subscription expired): data `{ entitlements }`, the entitlements answer's shape.
x-og-variants.invite: An invite to this game arrived: data `{ invite, from: { player, name }, payload, time }`.
x-og-variants.host: A message from the page that frames the game, outside any platform service (a site steering a showcase, a launcher handing over a choice): data `{ name, ... }`, its meaning agreed between the game and that page. The engine gives it no meaning of its own; a game reading it handles an unknown name by ignoring it.

PlatformNotice.description: Unasked host input arrived: sent by og.platform at the start of the tick it was applied, read by systems the tick after; read it with og.platform.notice. Registered when a game first names it (a system's reads); without it notices are still logged and readable.

notice.description: The notice's number, for og.platform.notice: 1 for the first, counting up.

PlatformGrants.description: The purchases this world granted (og.platform.grant), so a consumable is granted once however its answer or notice comes back: a replay, a relaunch, a restored save. World state: saved, restored and hashed. Registered when a game first names it or calls og.platform.grant. Write it only through og.platform.grant.

ids.description: The 64-bit hashes of the granted purchase ids, each as two u32 (low, high), oldest first: the last 256 grants.

tick.description: The tick it was applied at.

time.description: The host's clock when it sent it, UTC milliseconds; 0 when it gave none.

ids.description: Product ids as the game's store lists them (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`), at most 100; empty: every product the game sells.

PurchaseDesc.description: A purchase to ask the player for.

placement.description: Where in the game, as the game names it (`level.end`, `continue`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` (default `default`).

id.description: The achievement's id (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`).

percent.description: How far, 0 to 100: 100 unlocks it. Progress never goes back (a lower value keeps the higher one).

count.description: At most this many, those playing this game first.

to.description: The friend's player id (og.platform.friends); empty: the host offers an invite link through the share sheet.

message.description: What the invite says, at most 120 characters; empty: the host's own words.

payload.description: What the game hands the invited player (a room id, a level): any JSON, at most 1 KiB encoded; their og.platform.invites carries it back.

ShareDesc.description: What to share through the device's share sheet.

text.description: The text, 1 to 280 characters.

title.description: A title, at most 80 characters; empty: the game's name.

path.description: A short query the game's own Play link carries back (`?share=<path>`), at most 256 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, `/` and `=`; empty: the plain Play link. The host builds the link: a game names no URL.

image.description: Attach the frame drawn last (a score screen).

name.description: What the room is called (at most 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`); empty for none. The host gives the room its id.

QuickPlayDesc.description: Quick play: what this engine waits to be matched for (og.platform.quickPlay).

mode.description: The mode to play (at most 32 of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`): only engines asking for the same mode and players are matched. Empty is `default`.

players.description: How many play together: the room is made once this many wait (set og.Lockstep.players to the same).

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the others, in milliseconds; then og.RoomJoined says `timeout`. 0 waits until roomLeave.

name.description: This player's name, as the other peers see it (og.platform.roomPeers); empty for none.

peer.description: Its number: the room numbers peers in join order from 0 and never gives one twice.

name.description: Its name, as its host gave it; empty for none.

RoomInfo.description: The room this engine is in.

state.description: `none` (in no room), `joining` (roomCreate, roomJoin or quickPlay asked, not answered yet: quick play waiting for its match) or `in`.

room.description: The room's id; empty in none.

host.description: What carries rooms here: `relay` (natively, `og run --room` through `og relay`), `player` (the platform's rooms through the Player, on the web) or `none` (roomCreate and roomJoin are refused).

peer.description: This engine's peer number; 0 in none.

peers.description: Every peer present, this one included, by number.

link.description: The room a Play link to a room (`?room=<id>` on the play page) named: the engine joined it at load (og.RoomJoined answers, as for roomJoin); empty without one.

RoomMessageData.description: A message another peer sent: what og.RoomMessage announced.

message.description: Its number (og.RoomMessage.message): 1 for the first message this engine received, counting up.

tick.description: The tick it was delivered at.

data.description: What it carries, when it was sent as a JSON value; null when it was sent as bytes.

bytes.description: What it carries, when it was sent as bytes.

RoomJoined.description: roomCreate, roomJoin or quickPlay finished, or the host put this engine in a room (`og run --room`, a Play link to a room): sent at the start of the tick after the host answered. With ok false the engine is in no room and `reason` says why.

ok.description: Whether this engine is in the room now.

room.description: The room's id (at most 63 bytes); empty when not ok.

peers.description: How many peers are in the room, this one included.

reason.description: Why it failed: `unavailable` (no rooms here), `not_found`, `full`, `invalid`, `offline`, `timeout` (quick play matched nobody in time) or `cancelled` (roomLeave while joining), then a colon and the host's words; empty when ok.

RoomPeerJoined.description: Another peer joined this engine's room.

peers.description: How many peers are in the room now.

RoomPeerLeft.description: A peer left this engine's room (it left, closed, or lost its connection), after every message it sent; or, with peer equal to this engine's own number, this engine is in no room any more (roomLeave, or the host lost the room).

peers.description: How many peers are in the room now (0 once this engine left).

RoomMessage.description: Another peer's message arrived; read it with og.platform.roomMessage. Messages from one peer arrive in the order it sent them. While lockstep runs (og.Lockstep) a message is this peer's host input alone: a system that changes the world from one makes it differ from the other peers' (og.Desync); carry what all must see in og.PlayerInput.

binary.description: Whether it was sent as bytes (else as a JSON value).

DateStyle.description: How much of a date to write (CLDR's styles; en shown).

TimeStyle.description: How much of a time of day to write (en shown).

offsetMinutes.description: Minutes ahead of UTC to show it in (a player's time zone, which the game passes in; 540 for Tokyo).
Minutes ahead of UTC to show it in.

requested.description: The locale the host or the game asked for (empty: none).

active.description: The table in use (empty: none loaded).

fonts.description: The UI's font chain, first first.

DecimalFormat.description: Decimal formatting from the engine's shared CLDR data; no host Intl dependency.

decimals.description: Exactly this many fractional digits (clamped to 20); null keeps up to three without trailing zeros.

grouping.description: Use the locale's digit grouping; null defaults to true.

x-og-variants.clock: Clock face: `1:02:03`, whole seconds rounded down.
x-og-variants.short: Narrow largest-unit label: `2h`, `3m`, rounded up; under a minute, whole seconds.

TextAlign.description: How the lines of a label align.

Scheme.description: The palette: games run on a stage, so dark is the default.

DensityMode.description: Control sizes by the input the player holds: auto picks touch sizes on a coarse pointer or a play surface under 768 px, mouse sizes otherwise.

x-og-variants.auto: Touch sizes on a coarse pointer or a narrow surface, mouse sizes otherwise.
x-og-variants.mouse: A mouse and keyboard: the tightest controls.
x-og-variants.pad: A gamepad across a room: larger controls, rows and gutters that read from a couch.
x-og-variants.touch: A finger: every control at least 44 CSS px.

ThemeColor.description: A colour role of the UI style in effect (the game's style, or the default style before it picks one).

x-og-variants.backdrop: The screen behind the UI where nothing else is.
x-og-variants.well: A recessed ground inside a panel: wells, map frames, empty slots.
x-og-variants.lineStrong: Stronger frames: high contrast, map borders, scrollbars.
x-og-variants.inkMuted: Secondary ink: captions, keys, inactive tabs.
x-og-variants.inkFaint: The faintest ink that still reads: placeholders, hints.
x-og-variants.inkInverse: Ink on a ground of ink (a selected chip).
x-og-variants.control: Neutral control fills: secondary buttons, tracks, fields.
x-og-variants.controlStrong: A neutral control hovered or pressed; selection.
x-og-variants.primary: The one directed action: primary buttons, a slider's fill, a switch that is on, the caret.
x-og-variants.highlight: Emphasised ink: a speaker's name, a price, a link, the player's map dot.
x-og-variants.selection: The selected row, tab or card, independent of primary actions.
x-og-variants.accent: Decorative emphasis, independent of primary and selection.
x-og-variants.sceneInk: Scheme-aware text drawn over the scene.
x-og-variants.sceneShadow: Separation shadow under text over the scene.
x-og-variants.focus: The focus ring of key and pad navigation.
x-og-variants.hud: HUD capsules over the game (scores, timers, toasts).
x-og-variants.gold: Currency: coins, gold, prices that can be paid.

TypeStepName.description: A step of the style's type ramp.

x-og-variants.caption: A step of the ramp.
x-og-variants.hero: The largest typography role, above display; displayXl2 is its legacy alias.

Insets.description: Padding or margins on four sides.

Paint.description: A colour: a theme token, or an sRGB colour as authored (components 0 to 1), with an alpha. Neither is white.

token.description: A semantic colour of the theme.

role.description: A colour role the style declares of its own (its `roles` block, docs/ui.md §3.1: a game's corruption or faction colour) by name, when no token is given; a name the style lacks draws magenta.

color.description: An sRGB colour as authored, when no token or role is given.

Viewport.description: The play surface the UI lays out in, in og-ui units (CSS px over UiTheme.unit) and device pixels per unit.

dpr.description: Device pixels per CSS pixel; rectangles snap to device pixels.

safeArea.description: The device's unsafe margins (notch, home indicator); the root pads by them, and CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) reads them with the covered region folded in (covered).

smallWidth.description: The surface's width with the browser's own controls (address bar, toolbars) shown, as CSS's small viewport: what svw, svi and svmin read; vw and dvw read width. Omitted or 0 is width (native hosts have no such controls).

smallHeight.description: Its height with the browser's controls shown (CSS svh); omitted or 0 is height.

largeWidth.description: Its width with the browser's controls hidden (CSS lvw); omitted or 0 is width.

largeHeight.description: Its height with the browser's controls hidden (CSS lvh); omitted or 0 is height.

coarsePointer.description: A touch screen or another coarse pointer.

reducedMotion.description: The page prefers reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, from the web shell): the UI's theme only fades, whatever UiDesc.reducedMotion says. Omitted is false.

highContrast.description: The page prefers more contrast (prefers-contrast: more, from the web shell): the UI's theme is the high-contrast one, whatever UiDesc.contrast says. Omitted is false.

reducedTransparency.description: The page prefers less transparency (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce, from the web shell): glass parts are opaque surfaces and the scrim and translucent fills flat, whatever UiDesc.reducedTransparency says (UiTheme.reducedTransparency). Omitted is false.

macKeys.description: Text controls take macOS's editing keys: Command with A, C, X and Z, Command+←/→ to the line's ends (↑/↓ the text's), Option+←/→ and Option+Backspace by words, Control+A and E to the line's ends. Off: Control takes the shortcuts and moves by words (Alt too), Home and End go to the line's ends. The web shell sets it from the browser's platform (Apple's); a native host sets it on macOS, so a script that holds Ctrl or Meta edits as a person on that OS would (og.ui.previewViewport pins either). Omitted is false.

covered.description: Where the host's own control covers the surface: on a published page the web shell's round Back to the Portal, top left (about 12, 12 to 52, 52 CSS px; its name shows beside it for the first seconds of play). A document's CSS `env(safe-area-inset-*)` clears it: it is folded into the one edge's inset that costs the least surface (the left one on a landscape surface, the top one on a portrait one), so a HUD placed at the insets (`position: fixed; left: calc(env(safe-area-inset-left) + 16px)`) never draws under it. A game drawing its own corner reads it from og.ui.frameViewport. Empty (omitted) is none: native hosts and pages without Back.

breakpoint.description: Its size class: phone portrait or landscape, tablet, desktop.

hud.description: The HUD band (read only): the safe area at most UiDesc.hudMaxAspect times its height wide, centred, where toasts lay out and a HUD document's CSS env(-og-hud-inset-*) places it; a game drawing its own HUD reads it so it sits with them on an ultrawide. Ignored where a host passes a viewport in.

UiDesc.description: How the UI looks: the scheme, the density, its fonts, the contrast, the game's primary colour, motion, transparency, the icon atlas, the style and the sounds. og.ui.configure takes it in part: a field left out keeps the value the last call (or a look's style) gave it, null clears it.

font.description: The body font, from og.load.font; null measures text at half an em per character and draws none.

displayFont.description: The display font; null uses the body font.

monoFont.description: The monospaced font; null uses the body font.

roundedFont.description: The rounded font (levels and scores); null uses the display font, then the body font.

fallbackFonts.description: Fonts for other scripts (Hebrew, Devanagari, a CJK face with `font { runtime true }`), tried in order after the locale's (og.i18n) for a text the role's font cannot draw whole. A text mixing scripts takes each run from the first font that has it (the role's for its Latin, a fallback for its CJK or Arabic), one label in several fonts.

contrast.description: Standard or high contrast. The page's prefers-contrast: more takes high contrast too (Viewport.highContrast).

primaryColor.description: An sRGB colour as the game's primary (its hover, pressed and soft tones derived from it, the ink on it whichever of ink and inkInverse reads better); null keeps the style's.

reducedMotion.description: Transitions only fade; sheens stop. The page's prefers-reduced-motion turns it on too (Viewport.reducedMotion).

textScale.description: The player's text size (a settings screen's slider, kept with the other settings): every text size and leading is multiplied by it and the layout grows around the text (control, row and header heights by the leading body text gains), never clipping it. 1 is the style's sizes, 1.5 the largest (a larger one lays out at 1.5): docs/ui.md §6.1 holds every screen to 1.5, 200 % deferred.

unitScale.description: The og-ui unit in CSS px (docs/ui.md §6.1): the UI lays out in units (og.ui.viewport and og.ui.frameViewport are the surface over it) and draws them at it, so every length grows with the surface (the style's text, space, radii and controls, and a game's own px, alike) and the player's textScale multiplies over it. 0 is auto: on a mouse or pad surface its 1080p-equivalent height (the shorter of the height and the width's 16:9 height) over 720, 1 to 2, so a 1280x720 layout fills a 1080p window with body text at 21 CSS px and the smallest step at 18; a touch surface keeps CSS px (1). A value of 1 to 2 pins it (a game that lays out for one size).

reducedTransparency.description: Nothing is see-through: glass parts (a style's glass line) are opaque surfaces (no blur of the frame under them, their frame whole), the scrim is the opaque colour it makes over backdrop and the translucent fills (control, controlStrong, primarySoft, hud) the opaque colours they make over panel. The page's prefers-reduced-transparency turns it on too (Viewport.reducedTransparency); UiTheme.reducedTransparency says it is on.

colorVision.description: The player's colour vision (a settings screen's colour-blind mode): the whole frame, the scene and the UI alike, is recoloured for it after every other effect (colorVisionFilter), and a document's CSS reads it as @media (-og-color-vision: protanopia) to add the cues it needs. none (the default) draws the frame as it is. Simulation uses Viénot 1999 for protanopia and deuteranopia and Brettel 1997 for tritanopia; correction is Fidaner 2005's daltonisation over them (docs/ui.md §3.2).

colorVisionFilter.description: What colorVision does to the frame: correct (the default; the player's setting) or simulate (how a viewer with it sees the frame, for checking a screen).

colorVisionStrength.description: The deficiency's severity, 0 to 1: 1 (the default) a dichromat's; less blends towards the frame as it is, for the commoner anomalous trichromacy.

icons.description: The icon atlas a document's `<og-icon>` draws from; null takes the style's.

fallbackIcons.description: The icon set that draws the names the atlas lacks (icons, or the style's when icons is null): a game's whole set, such as the UI kit's iconoir set, under a style pack's few painted icons, which keep the names they paint. A document's `<og-icon>`, rich text's [icon=], an action's glyph and an art slot's placeholder all look in it; a name in neither warns. null is none.

images.description: Pictures rich text draws inline by name ([img=<name>]): a portrait in a line of dialogue, an item's art in a tooltip. Any texture, not only the icon atlas's cells; each one em tall at its aspect, in its own colours.

toastAnchor.description: Where toasts stack; null is the bottom centre.

hudMaxAspect.description: The widest the HUD band is, over its height: on a wider surface (a 21:9 or 32:9 ultrawide monitor) the toasts and a HUD document placed at its CSS env(-og-hud-inset-*) (`right: calc(env(-og-hud-inset-right) + 24px)`) lay out in a band this wide, centred in the safe area, so the player's eyes stay near the play; og.ui.viewport's hud is that band. 16/9 keeps a 16:9 game's HUD where it was designed; 0 is the whole safe area (a HUD at the screen's edges). Full-screen layers (dialogs, menus, scrims, world-space markers and their edge clamping) keep the whole surface. The UI itself never stretches: it lays out in CSS pixels at every aspect.

style.description: A UI style from og.load.style: its palette, radii, type ramp, fonts, icons, frames, ornaments, motion and sounds replace the default style (fonts, icons and a primary colour given here still win); null is the default style, the design language the engine shares with origin-agent.

sounds.description: Sounds for UI events (they win over the style's).

UiSounds.description: Sounds the UI plays through og-audio (the ui bus) on its events; null is silent.

hover.description: The pointer reaches a control, or keyboard or gamepad focus moves to one.

press.description: A control is pressed: by the pointer, Enter, Space or the gamepad's A.

error.description: A refused press or a danger toast.

TypeStep.description: One step of the type ramp.

size.description: The font size.

cjkLineHeight.description: The leading text with Chinese, Japanese or Korean characters takes.

cjkTrackingEm.description: Tracking of text containing CJK characters, in em.

weight.description: The face weight (100 to 900); zero takes the font role's own face.

uppercase.description: Style-driven locale-sensitive uppercase, applied before measurement without rewriting source text or editable values.

features.description: The OpenType features the step turns on, as tags: smcp (small caps), c2sc (capitals to small caps), tnum (tabular figures), lnum (lining figures), case (case-sensitive forms). A style sets them after a type role's font (`display 42 48 0.02 700 display smcp`); they apply where the role's font is imported with the same `features` line, and a font without one draws its defaults.

ControlSizes.description: The control, row and header heights and the gutter of the density in effect.

UiTheme.description: The style values the UI draws with, read-only.

palette.description: Each ThemeColor, then each colour role the style declares of its own (docs/ui.md §3.1), as `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa` (sRGB as authored).

space.description: The spacing scale by name (xxs, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl, xl3), in CSS pixels.

radius.description: The corner radii by name (small, control, bar, panel), in CSS pixels.

sizes.description: The control sizes of the density in effect.

durationsMs.description: The motion durations by name (instant, fast, base, slow, spring, bounce), in milliseconds.

style.description: The configured style's name; empty for the default style.

styleVersion.description: The configured style file's version: 1 for a version-1 style, whose game keeps the controls and dialogs it shipped with (docs/ui.md §3); 2 for a version-2 style and the default style.

contrast.description: The variant in effect: high when the game asked for it or the page prefers more contrast.

reducedMotion.description: Transitions only fade and sheens stop: the game asked for it or the page prefers reduced motion. A game's own animations read it to keep their state changes and drop their movement.

textScale.description: The player's text scale in effect (UiDesc.textScale, 1 to 1.5): typeRamp and sizes already carry it; tokens' typography is the style's as authored, so a game's own text drawn from it multiplies by this.

unit.description: The og-ui unit in effect, in CSS px (UiDesc.unitScale; auto: 1 to 2 by the surface): what every length the UI reads and gives is in, og.ui.bounds and og.ui.viewport too. Only what leaves the UI for the page is CSS px: the probe's dump_ui and og.render's screen sprites; a game drawing its own screen sprites beside the UI multiplies by it.

colorVision.description: The player's colour vision in effect (UiDesc.colorVision).

colorVisionFilter.description: Whether the frame is corrected or simulated for it.

reducedTransparency.description: Nothing is see-through: the scrim and the translucent fills of `palette` are already the opaque colours they make over panel (the scrim over backdrop) and glass is an opaque surface; the game asked for it or the page prefers reduced transparency. A game's own translucent overlays read it to draw opaque too.

tokens.description: The style's tokens (docs/ui.md §3.1), what a game's own drawing reads to match its UI: `typography` (each role, display title heading body label caption numeric button, at each breakpoint: size, lineHeight, trackingEm, weight, font, features), the `space`, `size`, `radius` and `stroke` scales by step, `elevation` (each level's shadows: dx, dy, blur, spread, color), `shape` (each element class's corner and radius: the shape language), `springs` (ui, enter, exit, emphasis, playful: durationMs, bounce), `staggerMs`, `overshoot`, the `rarity`, `team` and `series` colours, `cues` (each colour token's cue besides its hue, by name: `{ icon: <index in the style's icons> }`, `{ pattern: <name> }` or `{ pips: <n> }`; docs/ui.md §3.2), and `feedback` (each UI event's set: how many sounds, the volume and pitch ranges, the haptic's [startMs, ms, low, high] pulses).

TextSpan.description: A named attribute range in plain text for a store and the Svelte text spans binding. Offsets count Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes, JavaScript UTF-16 code units or grapheme clusters. Unknown names and properties remain game data. A character span may cover the complete Speaker: prefix, including its separator. Names select text::part(name) styles; text is never reinterpreted as markup.

name.description: The style part name, for example emphasis or character.

position.description: Start in Unicode scalar values; an astral character counts once.

length.description: Number of Unicode scalars. Zero is a metadata marker.

properties.description: Typed attribute properties: only string, finite number or boolean, never nested data or null.

Anchor.description: A point of the safe area an anchored group sits at.

x-og-variants.top: The middle of the top edge.
x-og-variants.left: The middle of the left edge.
x-og-variants.right: The middle of the right edge.
x-og-variants.bottom: The middle of the bottom edge.

Tone.description: A status tone of badges, toasts and map markers.

x-og-variants.neutral: Neutral: control fill and muted ink.
x-og-variants.primary: The game's identity: the primary's soft wash and highlight ink.
x-og-variants.inverse: Neutral emphasis: ink fill, inverse ink.

x-og-variants.desktop: 1024 CSS px wide or more, the shorter side 600 or more.
x-og-variants.tablet: The shorter side 600 or more, under 1024 wide.
x-og-variants.phoneLandscape: The shorter side under 600, wider than tall.
x-og-variants.phonePortrait: The shorter side under 600, taller than wide.

x-og-variants.protanopia: No red-sensitive cones: reds dark, red and green confused.
x-og-variants.deuteranopia: No green-sensitive cones: red and green confused.
x-og-variants.tritanopia: No blue-sensitive cones: blue and green, yellow and violet confused.

ColorVisionFilter.description: What UiDesc.colorVision does to the frame.

x-og-variants.correct: Recolours the frame so what the deficiency confuses is told apart (daltonisation).
x-og-variants.simulate: Shows the frame as a viewer with the deficiency sees it.

Contrast.description: The theme variant: high contrast remaps muted inks, fills and lines to the style's stronger ones and outlines every control (no new colour).

x-og-variants.standard: The style's palette as it is.

NavIntent.description: A focus-navigation intent, as the arrow keys, Tab, Enter, Space, Escape and a gamepad's d-pad, stick, A and B give.

x-og-variants.next: The next control in reading order (Tab).
x-og-variants.activate: Press the focused control (Enter, Space, A).
x-og-variants.back: Leave: the topmost dialog or menu closes, else og.ui.back() answers true (Escape, B).

UiRect.description: A rectangle of the play surface.

IconAtlasDesc.description: The icon atlas: a texture of equal cells in a grid, named in reading order, or an icon set cooked like a font (font).

font.description: An icon set from og.load.font (an `.ogt` of `type icons` naming SVGs, such as the UI kit's iconoir set): its icons are distance-field glyphs, crisp at any size and tinted by their ink, named by the set; texture, columns, rows and names are then not used.

names.description: Each cell's name, in reading order: a document's `<og-icon>` draws a cell by its name.

UiInlineImage.description: A picture rich text draws inline by name ([img=<name>]).

texture.description: The texture, from og.load.texture; null leaves the name unregistered.

uv.description: The region drawn, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture.

aspect.description: Width over height of the region as drawn; 0 is square.

tone.description: Its tone: a dot of the tone's colour before the text.

durationMs.description: How long it stays; 0 is 3200 ms (6000 for danger).

UiPointer.description: The primary pointer as the UI reads it this tick.

x.description: Its x from the surface's left.

y.description: Its y from the surface's top.

inside.description: It is over the surface: false for a mouse that left it, or a touch screen with no finger down.

down.description: Its button or finger is down.

pressed.description: Its button or finger went down this tick: where a drag a component runs itself (an inventory's item, a card) starts.

released.description: Its button or finger came up this tick: where such a drag ends.

shift.description: A Shift key is held (a split stack, a quick transfer, a range of a list).

ScrollState.description: A scroll container as the last frame laid it out (og.ui.scrollState).

offsetX.description: How far its content is scrolled right.

offsetY.description: How far its content is scrolled down.

viewWidth.description: Its view's width, inside its padding.

viewHeight.description: Its view's height, inside its padding.

contentWidth.description: Its whole content's width, unclipped (the view's on an axis it does not scroll).

VirtualCursorDesc.description: A pad's virtual cursor (docs/ui.md §2.1). The zero value moves at 900 units a second, takes a quarter second from a fine start to full speed, has a half-strength magnet and scrolls 1200 units a second.

speed.description: Units a second at full tilt; 0 is 900.

accel.description: Milliseconds a held stick takes from a third of its speed to all of it, for fine aim first; 0 is 250, negative is none.

magnet.description: 0 to 1: how much it slows over a control and, once the stick rests, pulls to the control's centre; 0 takes the style's motion magnet (the design language's timing table: 0.5), negative is none.

scroll.description: Units a second the right stick scrolls under it at full tilt; 0 is 1200, negative leaves the right stick to the game.

VirtualCursor.description: Where a pad's virtual cursor is.

x.description: Its x, from the surface's left.

y.description: Its y, from the surface's top.

shown.description: It is shown: the stick moved it since the real pointer last moved.

HudPlacement.description: Where the player put a customisable element: moved from its laid-out place, scaled about its centre and faded.

scale.description: Its scale (1: as laid out).

HudEdit.description: The HUD edit mode as the last frame left it.

player.description: The player whose layout the screen shows and edits.

selected.description: The key of the element being edited; empty for none.

keys.description: The customisable elements on screen, in drawing order.

changed.description: The player changed the layout this tick (a move ended, a step, a reset): the time to save og.ui.hudLayout in the game's settings.

A11yNode.description: One node of the accessibility tree: an element with a role (layout containers and spacers have none and are left out).

path.description: Its path, as touch_move_to and og.ui.focus name it.

parent.description: The path of the nearest node above it in the tree; empty at the top.

role.description: Its role (probe.UiElement.role): button, link, text, heading, image, checkbox, radio, switch, slider, spinbutton, textbox, combobox, listbox, option, tab, tablist, radiogroup, progressbar, meter, timer, status, alert, log, dialog, tooltip, separator, group, list, listitem, and the landmarks navigation, main, banner, contentinfo, complementary, article, region.

name.description: Its accessible name: what a screen reader says it is. A text field or area is named by the label before it in its row, else by its placeholder, else by its id; never by the text in it (that is its value).

description.description: Read after the name (aria-description): a text field's placeholder when a label names it; empty for none.

value.description: Its value as text (a slider's number, a progress's percent, a field's text); empty for none.

states.description: Its states: disabled, focused, focusable, checked, selected, expanded, collapsed (expandable and closed), pressed, busy, offscreen (a scroll container cuts it out of view).

valueMin.description: A range's smallest value (aria-valuemin): a slider's min, a bounded stepper's, 0 for a progress (in percent) and a meter; null for a stepper without bounds and a control that is no range.

valueMax.description: A range's largest value (aria-valuemax): a slider's max, a bounded stepper's, 100 for a progress, a meter's max; null as valueMin is.

valueNow.description: A range's value as a number (aria-valuenow; value says it as people read it): a slider's, a stepper's, a meter's, a progress's percent; null for a control that is no range.

level.description: A heading's level, 1 to 6 (aria-level; <h1> to <h6>); null for anything else.

live.description: A live region's setting (aria-live, or its role's: status and log are polite, alert assertive): polite or assertive, empty for none. A screen reader announces what changes in it; the web mirror and the native tree speak it.

atomic.description: A live region that announces its whole text when any of it changes (aria-atomic, or its role's: status and alert); false for none.

notify.description: A live region that announces as it appears (an alert, a toast); another region announces only what changes in it after it entered.

x.description: Left edge of the whole element.

y.description: Top edge of the whole element.

A11yTree.description: The last frame's accessibility tree, built from the same nodes the UI draws and takes input on.

nodes.description: The nodes, in tree order: the page, then each layer over it (a dialog after the page).

focusOrder.description: The paths keyboard Tab and the pads visit, in order: the nodes marked focusable, within the topmost dialog while one is open.

focused.description: The path keyboard and pad 0's focus is on; empty for none.

UiProp.description: An animatable value of an element (docs/ui.md §3.1): a state, a timeline key, a presence or og.ui.animate moves it. Colours are sRGB components 0 to 1; rotation and skew are radians.

x-og-variants.x: Its horizontal offset, CSS px (the transform's x).
x-og-variants.rotate: Its turn, radians, clockwise on screen.
x-og-variants.opacity: Its opacity, 0 to 1, multiplied down the tree.
x-og-variants.z: Its z among its siblings (stepped, never tweened).
x-og-variants.inert: 1: it and its subtree take no input (stepped): a results screen's buttons wait for the sequence.
x-og-variants.blur: Its subtree blurred by this many CSS px (CSS blur()'s standard deviation): Svelte's blur transition.
x-og-variants.draw: How much of its stroke is hidden from the end (0 drawn whole, 1 none), over the outline's length: Svelte's draw transition on an SVG shape.

x-og-variants.absolute: Out of the flow, placed by its insets inside its parent's padding box.
x-og-variants.screen: Out of the flow, placed by its insets in the whole surface rather than its parent's box: under the notch, the status bar and the home bar. A screen document's full-bleed art or backdrop, whose layer keeps its content in the safe area.
x-og-variants.anchored: Out of the flow, its anchorSelf point on the anchorAt point of the element at anchorTo, moved by its start and top insets.

MotionToken.description: A named motion of the style (docs/ui.md §3.1): components use these, so a style's personality changes every motion at once.

x-og-variants.ui: The control spring: hover, press, toggles.

x-og-variants.pingPong: Forward then back, over and over.

SpringSpec.description: A spring by how it feels: about how long it takes to settle and how much it overshoots. Retargeting it keeps its value and velocity, so an interrupted motion never jumps.

durationMs.description: About how long it takes to arrive, ms.

bounce.description: 0 arrives without overshoot; 0.3 overshoots a little; up to 1 rings (below 0 is sluggish). The style's overshoot caps it.

TweenSpec.description: A duration on an ease: a retarget starts a new ease from where it is.

ease.description: A GSAP-named curve shared with tweens. Omitted: the UI arrival cubic Bézier, not a GSAP approximation.

bezier.description: A cubic Bézier (x1, y1, x2, y2) in place of the named ease (empty: the named one).

TokenRef.description: One of the style's motion tokens.

Transition.description: How a value moves to a new target.

oneOf.description: On a spring that keeps its velocity.

durationMs.description: About how long it takes to arrive, ms.

bounce.description: 0 arrives without overshoot; 0.3 overshoots a little; up to 1 rings (below 0 is sluggish). The style's overshoot caps it.

oneOf.description: Over a duration on an ease.

ease.description: A GSAP-named curve shared with tweens. Omitted: the UI arrival cubic Bézier, not a GSAP approximation.

bezier.description: A cubic Bézier (x1, y1, x2, y2) in place of the named ease (empty: the named one).

Cursor.description: The pointer's shape over an element (CSS cursor's keywords, CSS UI 4 §5.1, docs/ui.md §2), inherited by its subtree.

x-og-variants.auto: Its parent's; with none set above it, a text control's I-beam, a draggable element's open hand (closed while dragged), a link's hand, else the arrow.
x-og-variants.cell: A cell or cells can be selected.
x-og-variants.alias: An alias or shortcut is made.
x-og-variants.resizeCol: A column resizes left and right.
x-og-variants.resizeRow: A row resizes up and down.

EaseKey.description: A named ease into a key.

ease.description: The GSAP-named curve shared with tweens.

HoldKey.description: Holds the previous value, then jumps at the key.

BezierKey.description: A cubic Bézier into the key.

KeyEase.description: How the segment into a key moves.

ease.description: The GSAP-named curve shared with tweens.

oneOf.description: On a spring from the previous key's value (released at it).

durationMs.description: About how long it takes to arrive, ms.

bounce.description: 0 arrives without overshoot; 0.3 overshoots a little; up to 1 rings (below 0 is sluggish). The style's overshoot caps it.

TimelineKey.description: A keyframe: a value at a time.

ease.description: How the segment into it moves; null is the out ease.

TimelineTrack.description: Keys over one prop of the element the timeline plays on, or of a descendant by its path below it (`Stars/Star#2`). Before its first key it holds that key's value, after its last the last.

target.description: A path below the play's element (empty: the element itself).

SoundEvent.description: A UI sound of the style.

name.description: hover, press, open, close, success or error.

playbackRate.description: Its pitch (1: as recorded); a cascade step raises it 6 %.

HapticEvent.description: A haptic pattern for the host.

name.description: light, medium, heavy, success, warning or error.

BurstEvent.description: Rays and sparks from the target.

radius.description: How far they reach (0: the style's).

color.description: Their colour; null is the style's highlight.

StateEvent.description: Sets a state group of the target.

CallbackEvent.description: A callback to game code: it arrives in og.ui.motionEvents.

TimelineAction.description: What an event does when a play reaches it.

name.description: hover, press, open, close, success or error.

playbackRate.description: Its pitch (1: as recorded); a cascade step raises it 6 %.

name.description: light, medium, heavy, success, warning or error.

radius.description: How far they reach (0: the style's).

color.description: Their colour; null is the style's highlight.

TimelineEvent.description: An event at a time, on the play's element or a descendant.

target.description: A path below the play's element (empty: the element itself).

durationMs.description: Its length (0: its last key or event).

ChoreoPlay.description: A timeline on the play's element or a descendant.

target.description: A path below the play's element (empty: the element itself).

ChoreoStagger.description: One timeline on each target, each stepMs after the one before as ordered by from, the whole spread within capMs.

targets.description: Paths below the play's element (empty: its children in order).

stepMs.description: Between one target's start and the next's (0: the style's stagger).

capMs.description: The most the whole stagger spreads over (0: the style's cap).

from.description: Where delays grow from: start, end, center (nearest the centre of their bounds first), or `x,y` (nearest that point first).

ChoreoCascade.description: Steps where each starts at the first `on` callback event of the one before (or its end): a score that counts chips, then multiplies, each step pitched higher.

on.description: The callback that starts the next step.

target.description: A path below the play's element (empty: the element itself).

targets.description: Paths below the play's element (empty: its children in order).

stepMs.description: Between one target's start and the next's (0: the style's stagger).

capMs.description: The most the whole stagger spreads over (0: the style's cap).

from.description: Where delays grow from: start, end, center (nearest the centre of their bounds first), or `x,y` (nearest that point first).

on.description: The callback that starts the next step.

fromLabel.description: Start at a label of its first timeline (wins over fromMs).

hold.description: Keep the last values once it ends, until stopped.

decorative.description: Under reduced motion it does not play at all.

ended.description: Finished (a held play keeps its values).

GestureInfo.description: What a drag or pinch on an element is doing (last tick's answer, as responses are).

held.description: A press is held on it.

dragging.description: It moves with the pointer (the press travelled past the threshold).

offsetX.description: Its offset from where it was laid out.

scale.description: A pinch's scale (1: none).

snapped.description: The snap point the last release chose (-1: none).

over.description: The drop target under the drag (empty: none).

droppedOn.description: The drop target it was dropped on this tick (empty: none).

hovering.description: For a drop target: a drag is over it.

received.description: For a drop target: the element dropped on it this tick (empty: none).

tapped.description: Its tap this tick (its `tap` attribute), as Response.tapped.

longPress.description: How far into its long press the held press is, 0 to 1.

UiMotionEvent.description: What happened in the UI's motion this tick.

kind.description: sound, haptic, burst, state, callback, end (a play finished), dismiss (a swipe threw an element off), drop (a drag was dropped on a target), snap (a released drag chose a snap point), or tap, doubleTap and longPress (an element's `tap`, `doubleTap` or `longPress` attribute recognised one).

name.description: The sound, haptic, callback or state's name; for drop the target's path; for snap the point's index.

target.description: The element's path.

index.description: The clip's step in a cascade or stagger.

playbackRate.description: A sound's pitch: its own times 1.06 per cascade step.

UiOverlap.description: Two elements overlapping where neither declared it (docs/ui.md §2).

path.description: The element placed over the other (absolute, anchored or floating), or the later of two siblings in the flow.

inFlow.description: Both are in their parent's flow: a layout bug, not a placement.

UiLayoutStats.description: What the last frame rebuilt and laid out (docs/ui.md §2).

rebuilt.description: Elements whose inputs changed since the tick before (or are new).

laidOut.description: Elements laid out; the rest kept their last layout.

keptCommands.description: Elements whose draw commands were kept from the tick before.

x-og-variants.compact: CLDR compact notation in the active locale (12K, 1.2万), then scientific beyond 10^15. Explicit separators retain custom K/M/B/T notation.
x-og-variants.letters: Shortened as idle games do: K, M, B, T, then aa, ab, … az, ba … (1.25ab), never running out.
x-og-variants.engineering: As scientific with the exponent a multiple of three (12.8e6).

NumberFormatDesc.description: How og.ui.formatNumber and the counters write a number.

decimals.description: Fixed digits after the point; null uses whole grouped numbers, CLDR compact precision, or three significant digits for extended notations.

exponent.description: The value is value × 10^exponent: numbers past 1e308 (an idle game's 1.5e420 is value 1.5, exponent 420).

group.description: Explicit custom thousands separator; null follows the active locale.

point.description: Explicit custom decimal point; null follows the active locale.

VectorArt.description: A cooked vector (an `.ogt` of `type vector`: an SVG subset) from og.load.vector, drawn by a VectorFill.

UiMaterial.description: A custom UI material (an `.ogt` of `type ui-material`) from og.load.uiMaterial, which a LayerDesc composites through.

GradientType.description: How a gradient (Gradient.type) runs over the element's box (fractions: 0,0 top left, 1,1 bottom right).

x-og-variants.radial: Centred on `from`, `to` its x and y radii.
x-og-variants.conic: Around `from`, starting at the angle to.x (radians clockwise from 3 o'clock).
x-og-variants.diamond: Centred on `from`, `to` its x and y radii, by |x|/rx + |y|/ry.

GradientSpread.description: What a gradient does past its ends.

GradientStop.description: A gradient's colour at an offset.

color.description: Its colour: a theme token, resolved when the frame is drawn, or a literal.

Gradient.description: A gradient of up to 8 stops, mixed in OKLab (no grey middle between complementary colours) and dithered so a long shallow one shows no bands.

from.description: Its start or centre, a fraction of the box.

to.description: Its end, or its radii, a fraction of the box.

WorldOcclusion.description: What the scene in front of an anchored element does to it: a depth test of its point against the frame's depth, on the GPU.

x-og-variants.fade: Drawn at occludedAlpha where the scene is in front.
x-og-variants.hide: Not drawn where the scene is in front.

MassKind.description: What a mass element template draws.

x-og-variants.number: The instance's value as a number (a damage number, a score).
x-og-variants.text: One of strings, by the instance's value (a nameplate, a loot label).
x-og-variants.bar: A bar filled to the instance's value 0–1 with a ghost at its ghost (an overhead health bar).
x-og-variants.icon: Frame value of frames on texture (a status icon).

MassSpace.description: Where a mass element's position is.

x-og-variants.world: A world point, projected by the GPU each frame.

x-og-variants.square: A rectangle of size (a long thin one is a streak).

MassKey.description: A key of a mass element's timeline, evaluated in the shader.

scale.description: Its scale.

ease.description: Shared GSAP names or cubic-bezier()/steps() strings. Non-opcode curves use a deduplicated 4097-sample presentation LUT; step progress is quantized before lookup.

MassTemplateDesc.description: A mass element template (docs/ui.md §1): declared once, then instanced thousands of times a frame with a few values each. No instance is laid out; its motion is the timeline, evaluated on the GPU.

font.description: Numbers and text: the font (one page); null is the UI's body font.

texture.description: Icons: the texture its frames are in.

strings.description: Text: the strings an instance's value picks.

frames.description: Icons: uv rectangles, four numbers each (u0, v0, u1, v1).

barBack.description: Bars: the track's ink; null is near black at 85 %.

barGhost.description: Bars: the ghost's ink; null is pale.

size.description: Text and numbers: x is the em size; bars, icons and particles: width and height. 0: the kind's default, per component (text and numbers 24 × 24, bars 80 × 8, icons 32 × 32, particles 8 × 8).

pivot.description: The element's point on its position, fractions (0.5, 1: its bottom centre).

lifetime.description: Ticks an instance lives; 0 shows pushed instances for their tick only.

keys.description: The timeline over its life (up to 8).

drift.description: Each instance drifts sideways up to this far over its life, by its seed.

gravity.description: Added downward over its life, this much at its end.

drag.description: Instances' velocity slows to rest over the life.

reference.description: World space: the distance at which it is its size, nearer larger and farther smaller; 0 keeps its screen size.

minScale.description: World space: the smallest distance scale.

maxScale.description: World space: the largest distance scale.

occlusion.description: World space: what the scene in front of an instance does.

occludedAlpha.description: Its opacity behind the scene, for occlusion fade.

outline.description: Text and numbers: an outline's ink; null draws none.

MassInstance.description: One mass element: a few values; its template does the rest.

position.description: A world point, or CSS pixels (x, y) in screen space.

value.description: The number, the string or frame index, or the bar's fill 0–1.

color.description: Its ink (text, icon tint, bar fill, particle); null is white.

scale.description: Multiplies its timeline's scale (a critical hit).

UiCollectionDesc.description: A keyed collection's identity rule. The key is data, never the row index.

key.description: The row field containing a nonempty string key; empty means id.

UiDocEvent.description: Something a document did (docs/ui.md §2.1): a click, a changed control, a list row selected, a named event (`emit`, a timeline's callback), an action, a two-way write, or Back on a layer whose Back is `emit`.

mount.description: The document's mount: the screen's name, or a component instance's path.

rowKey.description: Stable collection key of the innermost each row; empty outside a row. Never an index.

kind.description: click, changed, select, emit, action, set, back, or activate and deactivate (a layer became or stopped being the active one).

name.description: The element's id (click), the prop (changed), the list (select), the event or action's name, or the viewmodel path a `set` wrote.

value.description: The new value (changed, set), the row's index (select); null otherwise.

UiLayer.description: A layer of the stack (docs/ui.md §2.1), as its screen declares it.

serial.description: Its number, unique for the UI's life: what push answered.

screen.description: The screen's name; also its layer's id, the first segment of its elements' paths.

mount.description: The store-driven mount that shows it, `scope:id` (a `type screen` document mounted with scope.mount is a layer while it is mounted); empty for a pushed screen.

kind.description: hud, menu, modal, popover, toast, tooltip or system.

input.description: game (input reaches gameplay), menu (input stays in the UI) or all.

capture.description: It takes the pointer on its gaps too.

pause.description: The game pauses while it is on the stack.

under.description: What happens to the layers under it: none, dim, blur or hide.

back.description: What Back does: pop, none or `emit <event>`.

focus.description: Where focus starts, a path below its root (empty: its first control).

remember.description: Focus returns where it was when it is the active layer again.

active.description: It is the active layer: the top one whose input is menu or all (the topmost with none). It takes Back, pop and focus.

hidden.description: A layer above hides it: it is not built.

inert.description: A menu layer above takes its input.

x-og-variants.hold: When it has been held holdMs.

UiActionDesc.description: A named UI action (docs/ui.md §2.1) bound to og-input's controls: a component asks for an action, not a key.

name.description: Its name: confirm, back, tabNext, tabPrev, details, or the game's own.

toggle.description: A hold's toggle alternative (XAG 107): a tap turns it on, the next tap off; og.ui.actionHeld answers true between.

label.description: What it says when no document gives it a hint.

action.description: A gameplay action (og.input.defineAction) it follows instead of keys and buttons: it is down when that action is, and its glyph is that action's binding on the device used last, so the player's rebinding moves the prompt too. Empty: keys and buttons.

UiDevice.description: The device a glyph set is for: the one the player used last.

x-og-variants.switch: A Nintendo Switch pad (south is B).

UiGlyph.description: An action's control on the device used last.

icon.description: The icon a style's set draws: `key.enter`, `xbox.a`, `ps.cross`, `switch.b`, `pad.south`, `touch.<action>`.

text.description: The text that names it: `Enter`, `A`, `×`.

UiActionHint.description: One entry of the action bar: an action the top layer accepts, its hint and glyph.

hint.description: What it does here (the document's `actions` line, else its label).

text.description: Its glyph's text.

CoreAction.description: The actions the engine ships. Arguments follow the action, separated by `:`.

x-og-variants.screenshot: `screenshot[:path][:full|:N]`: capture the next frame. Without a renderer it writes nothing and logs, not as a warning, that the frame is unchecked.
x-og-variants.listen: `listen[:path][:seconds]`: write the last seconds of rendered audio as a WAV.
x-og-variants.touch_move_to: `touch_move_to:<ui id>`: move the pointer to a UI element.
x-og-variants.touch_move: `touch_move:x,y`: move the pointer to CSS pixel coordinates.
x-og-variants.touch_start: `touch_start`: press the pointer where it is.
x-og-variants.touch: `touch:<id>:<down|move|up>:<x,y | ui id>`: a further touch (pointer 1 to 4) held while the pointer is busy elsewhere.
x-og-variants.gamepad: `gamepad:<a+b+...|->[@pad][:lx,ly[,rx,ry]][:lt,rt]`: set a pad's whole state (pad 0 unless `@1` to `@3` follows the buttons); `gamepad:off` disconnects it.
x-og-variants.intent: `intent:<Event>[:<fields as JSON>]`: send a gameplay intent through og.input.intent's recorded input path for the next tick, its fields from the JSON object and the rest at their defaults (`intent:Buy:{"item":3}`).
x-og-variants.key_down: `key_down:[Mod+]<Key>`: hold a key by its code, with the modifiers named before it (`Shift+ArrowLeft`, `Meta+ArrowLeft` for Command, apart from Ctrl).
x-og-variants.key_up: `key_up:[Mod+]<Key>`: release a key, then the modifiers named before it.
x-og-variants.type: `type:<text>`: type text, two ticks per character: its key press and the character as typed text (input.TextInput); a character no key types is typed text alone. The text runs to the `;` exactly, a trailing space included; after it a text field takes typed text only, so a bare key_down types nothing.
x-og-variants.compose: `compose:<text>`: an input method's composition so far (input.TextInput composing); a focused text field shows it underlined at the caret, `compose:` with nothing ends it.
x-og-variants.commit: `commit:<text>`: an input method commits text; a focused text field inserts it and the composition ends.
x-og-variants.move_to_text: `move_to_text:[=]text[@N]`: move the pointer to the UI element showing the text (exactly with `=`, the Nth with `@N`).
x-og-variants.frame_entity: `frame_entity:<entity>`: point the camera at an entity.
x-og-variants.dump_world: `dump_world[:path]`: tables, systems and their matched counts.
x-og-variants.dump_ui: `dump_ui[:path]`: the UI tree with bounds, and `style`, the configured UI style's name (empty for the engine's default style).
x-og-variants.set: `set:<entity>.<component>.<field>=<value>` or `set:<Resource>.<field>=<value>`: a Tune write through the schema: a number, `true` or `false` for a bool, `x,y,z` for a vector, an enum's variant name or its index; refused outside the field's FieldOptions min/max, never clamped.
x-og-variants.get: `get:<Resource>[.<field>]` or `get:<entity>[.<component>[.<field>]][:path]`: read through the schema as game code sees it (an enum as its variant's name, `"music"`; og.Time whole, with rate and the time scale; the DirectionalLight og.DayNight drives with the colour, intensity and direction it is drawn with), logged and written as JSON to `get-<tick>.json` (more unnamed ones on one tick: `get-<tick>-2.json`, ...).
x-og-variants.pause: `pause`: hold the clock; advance still steps.
x-og-variants.advance: `advance:<ticks>`: take fixed steps; the steps the script schedules for the same time after it run once it has stepped (a time is seconds: `0:advance:300;0:screenshot` shoots tick 300).
x-og-variants.describe: `describe[:path]`: write the frame as data (probe.Description): the visible entities with screen boxes, depth order and occlusion from the entity-id pass, what each secondary camera (og.CameraView, og.Mirror) shows from its own pass, the UI elements with rects and text, the camera.
x-og-variants.expect: `expect:<what>`: assert at this tick (probe.ExpectResult): `entity:<id>:within:x,y,w,h` (its visible box, CSS pixels) or `:within:x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` (its position, world units), `event:<Name>[:count]`, `ui:text:[=]<text>`, `region:x,y,w,h:color:#rrggbb[:tolerance]`, `frame:<ref.png>:rmse:<=v`, `state:<path>==<value>` (also != < <= > >=), `entity:<id>:<path>==<value>` (a field of its dump_entity: `render.lod==2`, `og.Transform.position.y>0`), `timings:<path>==<value>` (state().timings: `triangles<=1500000`). A value written `$<path>` is another path of the same source, read when the expectation is evaluated: `state:coins<=$total`, `entity:hero:Health.hp<=$Health.max`. A failure is a warning with the tick and the observed value; `og run --json` lists every result and exits 1 on a failure. Frame expectations without a renderer are unchecked, as are an entity's `render.*` fields and the renderer's timings (`triangles`, `render`, `passes`).
x-og-variants.invariant: `invariant:<what>`: from now on, check an expectation (any `expect:` form but `region` and `frame`) after every tick: the first tick it fails is an assertion violation (og.assert's report, the probe's `assertions`) with the tick and the observed value, which fails `og run --json` (exit 1) and the playtest. A playtest's `invariants` are these steps.
x-og-variants.save_scene: `save_scene[:path][:spawned]`: write every scene the world was assembled from back from the world (the boot scene's, then each og.world.instantiate made, each to its own `.ogt`): only the lines whose values changed (comments and order kept), the fields set or patch tuned, and resources as `resource <Name> { }` blocks; with `spawned`, the entities the game spawned at run time under the boot scene's marked section. To each scene's source, or with a path the boot scene's to that file under the output directory and the others beside it.
x-og-variants.help: `help`: list every action the channel knows, core and registered.
x-og-variants.mouse_move: `mouse_move:dx,dy`: move the mouse by relative CSS pixels (movementX/Y, summed in og.Pointers.movement: mouse-look) with the pointer's position held, as a locked pointer moves.
x-og-variants.pointer_lock: `pointer_lock:<on|off>`: report the pointer locked or released (og.PointerLock.locked), as the web shell does from pointerlockchange; headless hosts never lock on their own.
x-og-variants.apply_prefab: `apply_prefab:<entity>[:<Component>[.<field>]][:base]`: move an entity's prefab overrides (all, a component's or one field; a field set at run time too) into its prefab's `.ogt` at the entity's node, and out of its scene's instance block, so the scene cooks to the same world and every other instance takes the values; with `base`, into a variant's base (docs/design.md §2.5, prefabs).
x-og-variants.revert_prefab: `revert_prefab:<entity>[:<Component>[.<field>]]`: drop an entity's prefab overrides (all, a component's or one field) from its scene's instance block, and set the live values back to the prefab's.

CommandDesc.description: How a registered action describes itself in `og run --help` and the wiki.

doc.description: One sentence on what it does.

CommandStep.description: One parsed step of a command script.

at.description: When it runs, in simulation seconds from the start of the script.

CommandInfo.description: One action as help lists it.

doc.description: One sentence on what it does.

core.description: Shipped with the engine (true) or registered by a module or a game.

untilTick.description: The tick of the last step.

warnings.description: Unknown actions and other skipped steps, each naming the fix.

PickResult.description: What a screen point resolved to in the scene.

entity.description: The probe id of the entity under the point.

world.description: Where the pick landed in world space: two components in the 2D profile, three in 3D; nothing pads a plane with an unmeasured zero.
