The generated pose is drawn in place of og.anim's (presentation only); og.anim still poses the skeleton every tick for everything the simulation reads, and is what is drawn until the model is resident.

rig.description: The humanoid map of the skeleton (og.load.rig); 0 detects the bones from their names, as og.anim.humanoid does.

drive.description: og.motion moves og.Transform to the goals in the tick (walkTo, place, face) with fixed math, and the pose is re-rooted onto it; off, the game moves the Transform and the motion follows it, and only pose goals are taken.

turnSpeed.description: How fast a driven character turns to its heading.

lookahead.description: How much motion the model keeps generated ahead of what is drawn: more absorbs a slow GPU, less follows a changed goal sooner. Presentation only.

PoseGoalDesc.description: A pose of the model's library where the character stands (og.motion.pose).

duration.description: How long the goal is current.

PlaceGoalDesc.description: A pose of the library at a place (og.motion.place): the character's hips over `position`, facing `heading`.

position.description: Where the character stands (y is ignored: the ground is the Transform's).

heading.description: Its facing: 0 looks down +Z, π/2 down +X.

duration.description: How long the goal is current; a driven character moves there in a straight line over it.

FaceGoalDesc.description: Turn to a heading where the character stands (og.motion.face).

heading.description: The facing: 0 looks down +Z, π/2 down +X.

duration.description: How long the goal is current at least; a driven character's turn at turnSpeed may take longer.

WalkGoalDesc.description: Walk or run to a point (og.motion.walkTo); needs og.MotionAgent.drive.

speed.description: How fast: the motion walks below 2.5 m/s and runs above.

pose.description: The pose taken on arrival; empty is `idle`.

arrivalHeading.description: Facing after arrival; omitted keeps the travel heading. The goal ends only after this turn completes.

deceleration.description: Braking near the target; 0 uses 3 m/s². A CharacterController owns ground height and collision when present; otherwise motion keeps the Transform's height.

acceleration.description: How fast the walk gains speed; 0 uses 4 m/s². It starts from the speed the last walk or jump left, so a walk queued after another keeps moving through the first target (braking only to the next walk's speed, less by the corner it turns), and a jump queued after a walk takes off at the speed it arrives with. A large value, such as 1000, starts at full speed in the first tick.

JumpGoalDesc.description: A jump (og.motion.jump); needs og.MotionAgent.drive. The simulation owns its whole arc: after `prepare` the og.motion system takes off in the tick, with an og.CharacterController through the controller's jump (it sets the controller's jumpSpeed for `height` under the controller's gravity and holds `jump` on the takeoff tick, so a ceiling cuts the rise and the landing is wherever the controller reaches ground), without one by the fixed ballistic arc of `height` back to the takeoff height. The goal ends `recover` seconds after the landing tick. The generated jump is drawn in place on that flight, never adding the model's own vertical travel (docs/design.md §2.7).

height.description: The apex over the takeoff height, with gravity og.Physics.gravity (times the controller's gravityScale).

distance.description: How far it travels across the ground while in the air, along `heading`; 0 jumps in place.

heading.description: The way it faces and travels: 0 looks down +Z, π/2 down +X; omitted keeps its facing when the jump starts. It turns there at turnSpeed while preparing.

prepare.description: Seconds of preparation (the crouch) before takeoff.

recover.description: Seconds after the landing tick before the goal ends.

pose.description: The pose held after the jump; empty is `idle`.

LookAtDesc.description: A timed look over locomotion: spine, neck and head share the turn, never the hips or legs. An omitted target releases the look over blend seconds.

target.description: World point to look at; omitted releases the current look.

duration.description: Seconds held after blending in, before blending out.

blend.description: Seconds to enter and leave; 0 is immediate.

maxYaw.description: Maximum yaw from the animated forward.

maxPitch.description: Maximum pitch from the animated forward.

ReactionDesc.description:
An authored humanoid reaction over locomotion. Entry, a held interval, and exit come from a cooked type motion-action asset. Timing and strength belong to the tick; the generated pose is presentation only.
**Action asset.** An .ogt starts with `type motion-action`, `version 1`, then `---`. Its body has `source "anims/brace.glb"`, `clip "brace"`, optional `rig "rigs/meshy.ogt"`, `holdStart 0.5` and `holdEnd 1.5`, each on its own line. Paths are relative to assets/. The hold must lie inside the clip (0 <= holdStart < holdEnd < clip duration), with matching poses at both ends for looping. Use a stationary root, +Z facing the reaction source, entry before the hold, and recovery after it. A 30 Hz clip is recommended; the cook also accepts other sample rates.
**Hood contact.** Optional `hand right` (or left) and `handTarget x y z` attach that wrist to an offset from the head during the hold. Supply the offset in metres along the source head bone's local axes, independent of the GLB's unit scale. Retargeting adjusts it to the target's proportions; IK follows the final head pose after lookAt. The clip owns the stance step and lean: the engine does not synthesize an untrained action. Keep provenance and licensing beside the source asset.

action.description: The motion-action asset path, such as actions/brace.ogt. Empty releases the current reaction.

direction.description: World direction the character reacts toward (toward the wind source for a brace); zero keeps the character's facing.

strength.description: Contribution of the authored reaction; 0 leaves locomotion unchanged.

duration.description: Seconds to hold between the action's holdStart and holdEnd, after its entry; then play its exit.

blend.description: Seconds to blend in and out; 0 is immediate.

MotionStatus.description: An agent's goals, as the game set them: the current goal and how many wait. Deterministic: the same on every GPU, the model's progress never shows here.

goal.description: The current goal (none: the queue is empty and the character holds).

pose.description: The current goal's pose (walkTo's arrival pose), empty for none and face.

target.description: Where the current goal goes (pose and face: where the goal started; jump: its start plus its distance along its heading, on flat ground).

heading.description: The heading the current goal faces (walkTo: towards its target).

elapsed.description: How long the current goal has been current.

airborne.description: The current goal is a jump between its takeoff and its landing tick.

queued.description: Goals waiting after the current one.

completed.description: Goals finished since the agent's first.

looking.description: A look is active, including its entry or release.

reacting.description: A reaction is active, including its entry or release.

MotionPresentationState.description: Presentation progress, dependent on GPU timing, never simulation state.

x-og-variants.loading: Waiting for the model or renderer.
x-og-variants.warming: Weights are resident; this agent has no generated palette yet.
x-og-variants.ready: Generated frames and their palette are ready for the current rendered frame; authored fallback never counts.
x-og-variants.failed: Loading, inference or this agent's retarget failed; reason explains why.

MotionPresentationStatus.description: Visual readiness only, outside snapshots and hashes.

reason.description: Why it is loading, warming or failed; empty when ready.

MotionCapabilities.description: Where the motion model runs and what it knows. Presentation: a frame's answer, not the tick's; never branch the simulation on it.

backend.description: gpu (or cpu with the opt-in) once the weights are resident; none before, or when they failed.

reason.description: Why the backend is none: loading, the reason a load failed, or no GPU adapter (empty otherwise).

modelBytes.description: The size of cooked/motion/model.ogb, once read (0 before).

Destructible.description:
Makes the entity's og.Model, a model cooked with a `fracture` block, break into its chunks. A prop that stands (no og.RigidBody, or a static one) is its chunks from the first tick: each a static og.Collider (the hull of its piece) on an entity with og.Chunk, and the entity's own og.Collider and og.RigidBody are removed, so hits land on the chunks. A prop that moves (a dynamic or kinematic og.RigidBody) collides as itself until its first break, when its chunks take its place, moving as it moved, and it loses its og.Collider, og.RigidBody and og.Velocity. Until the first break the model is drawn whole; from it the model is hidden and each chunk draws its piece of it (with og.Model's tint, variant and shadows). Anchored islands stay static, the rest fall.
Scale it uniformly: a chunk's collider and mass follow og.Transform.scale's mean.

toughness.description: How much damage a square metre of bond takes before it breaks: an impulse of that many newton-seconds through 1 m² (a hit spreads over impactRadius). Glass about 50, wood 300, brick 800, concrete 2000.

strength.description: The stress its bonds hold in tension and shear before they weaken (compression holds thirty times as much, shear more for the compression across it (friction), and a bond breaks outright at twice the stress): low, an overhang falls and a wall shot out at its foot comes down; high, it holds whatever is left. 0 turns the stress solver off.

friction.description: How much more shear a bond holds for the compression across it, per pascal (Mohr–Coulomb, the tangent of the friction angle): a joint pressed by what stands on it holds where an unloaded one slips, so a wall shot out at its foot keeps its loaded piers and drops what hung over the hole, cracking in steps along its courses. 0 is shear at strength alone.

tension.description: The stress its bonds hold pulled apart, as a fraction of strength (shear and compression keep strength's). Masonry and dry stone hold almost none: mortar cracks long before brick does, so brickwork stands by its weight and friction (Heyman's no-tension masonry, the premise of masonry limit analysis), and at about 0.1 no block is left hanging from the course above over air, and a wall shot out at its foot steps back course by course over its piers. At 0.1 or below (with a strength above 0) a block of what stands also needs its weight within the middle third of what bears it from below, the blocks under it (a cracked bed joint bears as well as a sound one) or its foundation: one held only from its side, or by a tie-in into the wall beside it, comes loose whole, and the blocks it bore are judged again. 1 is tension at strength.

density.description: The chunks' density: their mass as bodies and their weight in the stress solver.

impactThreshold.description: A collision's impulse (og.CollisionStarted.impulse) that does no damage: what is above it is the damage of the hit, and, on a prop that stood still, the push the pieces it breaks loose take along the striker's path (shared by falloff, none faster than the striker closed), so a ball through a pane carries its shards on; a moving prop's pieces keep the velocity its hit left it.

impactRadius.description: How far a hit's damage reaches round its point (all of it within a third of this, falling to nothing at it).

anchored.description: Whether its anchors (the chunks on its floor) hold it to the world; false, every island falls.

breakFx.description: A one-shot emitter (og.load.emitter, `looping false`) burst where each island breaks loose, at its broken faces: the material's own, a lit dust puff for stone and brick, splinters and a little dust for wood, shards and glints for glass. 0 none.

hitFx.description: A one-shot emitter burst at each hit that damages it: the material's own, grit and a puff off stone, splinters off wood, glints off glass; sparks only off metal, and a few. 0 none.

debris.description: Fine debris, as visuals only: where a chunk shatters, its pieces smaller than og.Destruction.debrisVolume never become bodies. They fly on the GPU instead, each its own shape and materials, from where and how fast it broke off (the blast's push included), each throwing four to six thick rubble chips of uneven size in the prop's cut-face material, and every joint that breaks sheds three or four small chips of its cut faces and of its mortar (`fracture.mortar`), all tumbling and landing on the colliders that are boxes, spheres and terrains, and this mesh-particle emitter (`render mesh`, best with `blend alpha`, `collision` and `lit true`) bursts its finer grains there too. They never touch the simulation, so the world is the same on every device, and a device without the GPU layer draws none of them (og.destruction.capabilities' visualDebris). They last og.Destruction.debrisLifetime. 0: every piece is a body.

fractured.description: Written: true from its first break (the model hidden, its chunks drawn).

broken.description: Written: its bonds broken so far.

loose.description: Written: its chunks that have broken loose and still exist.

Chunk.description: One chunk of an og.Destructible, written by og.destruction when the prop fractures. A loose chunk is a dynamic body (with og.RigidBody and og.Velocity, or a child collider of its island's body); an anchored one a static collider. Drawn with its part of the destructible's model. Despawn it to clear it away.

chunk.description: Its index in the fracture asset.

level.description: 1 a support chunk, 2 a chunk's child.

body.description: The entity whose og.RigidBody moves it: its own, its island's body, or 0 while anchored.

looseTick.description: The tick it broke loose; 4294967295 while anchored.

Fractured.description: An island of chunks broke loose from a destructible during the tick (or the destructible shattered): read the tick after, for its sound, its camera shake, its score. Sent in the order the islands broke.

body.description: The island's body: the entity with its og.RigidBody.

point.description: Where it broke: the centre of its broken bonds.

cause.description: What broke it: one of the CAUSE_* codes.

maxChunks.description: The most loose chunks alive at once, over every destructible: past it the oldest loose islands (the smallest first among those that broke in the same tick) despawn, each with every chunk it carries.

debrisVolume.description: A loose island smaller than this is debris: it despawns debrisLifetime after it broke loose.

debrisLifetime.description: How long debris lasts (0: until maxChunks takes it).

fxLifetime.description: How long a breakFx or hitFx burst's entity lasts before og.destruction despawns it.

stressIterations.description: The stress solver's iterations when a destructible's support changes (Blast's maxIter). 0, the default, solves until it converges (at most six times its bonds), so a large structure's weight reaches every bond it rests on; a cap is cheaper on a slow device, but an unconverged solve loads distant bonds too little, and what should fall can stand.

stressBudget.description: The stress solver's work in one tick, across every destructible, in bond-iterations (one solver iteration over one bond). A solve that would start past it waits for the next tick, so a tick's worst case is this plus one solve (six iterations a bond) whatever comes down at once; the order is the destructibles' entity order, so a replay waits the same way. The 200-chunk brick wall's largest solve takes about 41000. 0 sets no limit.

point.description: Where it lands, in world space.

radius.description: How far it reaches; it falls linearly to nothing here from innerRadius.

innerRadius.description: Within this the bonds take the whole amount.

amount.description: The damage, as an impulse through a bond (Destructible.toughness says how much a square metre takes).

impulse.description: The momentum the blow carries, along its direction (a hammer, a wrecking ball, a shot): the pieces it breaks loose share it by its falloff and fly on, as a hit's do. Zero, the default, crushes without pushing, and what it breaks out of a standing prop can stay standing on what holds it.

radius.description: How far it reaches.

innerRadius.description: Within this everything takes the whole damage and push.

damage.description: The damage to every destructible's bonds in reach, as og.destruction.damage's amount.

impulse.description: The push outwards on every loose piece in reach, per square metre of the face it shows the blast (the two-thirds power of its volume), at its centre, falling off as the damage does: a blast pushes on surfaces, so a lone brick flies faster than a run of bricks, but not by their count. The pieces it drives apart pull on the bonds between them, so a run of bricks by the charge breaks up rather than flying off whole. Brick by a demolition charge about 2500.

DestructibleInfo.description: What a destructible holds and how much of it stands (og.destruction.info).

bonds.description: The bonds of its support graph.

anchored.description: Its support chunks still held to the world.

health.description: Its bonds' remaining health over their total, 1 intact to 0 rubble.

debris.description: Its fine pieces on the GPU now (og.Destructible.debris): broken off within og.Destruction.debrisLifetime, whether or not this device draws them.

crumbs.description: Its broken joints shedding grit on the GPU now (og.Destructible.debris): a few clay and mortar chips each, broken within og.Destruction.debrisLifetime (at most 48 joints a tick, spread over all that broke), whether or not this device draws them.

DestructibleMaterial.description: A material's og.Destructible fields (og.destruction.material): spread it into the component and add the material's fx, `{ ...og.destruction.material(world, MATERIAL_BRICK), breakFx }`, so a prop is tuned by what it is made of rather than by numbers in the scene. Its fields are og.Destructible's, for a prop of about a metre; override any one after the spread.

DestructionCapabilities.description: What destruction does on this device.

visualDebris.description: Whether og.Destructible.debris pieces and bursts are simulated and drawn on the GPU here (a renderer with compute passes: og.render.capabilities' compute); false draws none of them. The bodies are the same either way: pieces given to `debris` are never bodies, on any device, so a game never depends on it.

maxVisualDebris.description: The most fine pieces the GPU layer holds at once: past it the oldest go first (og.Destruction.debrisLifetime takes them sooner).

visualDebrisContacts.description: What the GPU pieces collide with: `world` (the colliders that are boxes, spheres and terrains); they pass through each other and through the chunks that are bodies.

PixelTerrain.description:
Destructible 2D ground of square cells (Worms, Noita): solid ground, bedrock or empty. Its og.Transform's position is the bottom-left corner of its cell (0, 0), x right and y up (its rotation and scale are not used). The first tick it is seen it is filled: `bedrock` rows at the bottom, then ground up to `ground` of its height; carve2d, fill2d, explode2d and fracture2d change it from then on, in the tick (og.destruction2d runs after the game's systems, before og.physics).
It collides chunk by chunk: each `chunk` × `chunk` block of cells with any solid in it is an entity with a static og.Collider (SHAPE_TRIMESH, an outline in 2D) of its cells' outline, smoothed within `tolerance` cells, so a body rolls along a carved slope rather than bumping down steps. A change rebuilds only the chunks it touched. Solid cells no longer joined (through their four sides) to bedrock or to the bottom row fall: each such island of at least `minPiece` cells becomes an og.PixelPiece, smaller ones vanish.
Drawn as one sprite of its cells, one texel a cell: ground in `color` with a per-cell `grain`, bedrock in `bedrockColor`, empty clear; the image is remade from the cells only on a frame after they changed. Changing width, height or chunk starts it over (filled again); despawning it takes its colliders with it (its pieces stay).

chunk.description: The side of the blocks of cells that collide and rebuild together: smaller rebuilds less per carve and makes more colliders.

ground.description: How much of its height is ground (bedrock included) when it is first filled; 0 starts it empty, to build with fill2d.

bedrock.description: The rows of bedrock at its bottom when it is first filled: never carved, and what the ground must stay joined to (as to the bottom row) to stand.

seed.description: The seed of its grain and of the pieces explode2d and fracture2d cut.

grain.description: How much each ground cell's brightness varies, fixed per cell by the seed (pieces keep the grain of the ground they were).

layer.description: Its sprite's draw order (its pieces' too); higher draws on top.

friction.description: Its colliders' and its pieces' friction.

density.description: Its pieces' density (per square metre in 2D).

layers.description: Its colliders' and pieces' collision layers, as og.Collider.layers.

mask.description: The layers they collide with, as og.Collider.mask.

tolerance.description: How far, in cells, the collision outline may cut across the cells' stair steps.

minPiece.description: An island cut loose with fewer cells vanishes instead of falling as an og.PixelPiece.

maxPieces.description: The most og.PixelPiece entities of this terrain at once: past it the oldest despawn.

solid.description: Written: its solid cells (ground and bedrock).

PixelPiece.description: A piece of an og.PixelTerrain cut loose (an island carve2d cut free, a piece explode2d threw or fracture2d broke off), written by og.destruction2d: a dynamic og.RigidBody whose og.Collider is the convex hull of its cells (SHAPE_CONVEX, a polygon in 2D), drawn as its cells at its og.Transform (the bottom-left corner of its cell (0, 0), turning with the body). Its cells are world state; despawn it to clear it away.

terrain.description: The og.PixelTerrain it was part of.

tick.description: The tick it broke loose.

PixelDetached.description: Cells of an og.PixelTerrain (or of an og.PixelPiece fracture2d broke) broke loose during the tick, read the tick after: one for each piece, in the order they were cut, for its sound, its dust, its score.

piece.description: The og.PixelPiece it became; 0 for an island under minPiece, which vanished.

cause.description: What broke it loose: CAUSE_CARVE, CAUSE_EXPLOSION or CAUSE_FRACTURE.

point.description: Its centre, in world space (its xy).

radius.description: Its radius: every cell whose centre is within it is emptied (bedrock stays).

Fill2dDesc.description: A round patch of ground for og.destruction.fill2d.

point.description: Its centre, in world space (its xy).

radius.description: Its radius: every cell whose centre is within it is made solid.

bedrock.description: Fill with bedrock (never carved) instead of ground.

point.description: Its centre, in world space (its xy).

radius.description: The hole it blows in every og.PixelTerrain in reach.

debris.description: The width of the ring of ground round the hole that it breaks into pieces and throws (0 none): the ground there is cut into Voronoi pieces of about pieceCells cells, each an og.PixelPiece.

pieceCells.description: About how many cells each thrown piece has.

speed.description: How fast it throws the pieces it cuts and the islands it cuts loose outwards, at its centre, falling linearly to nothing at radius plus debris; the og.PixelPiece entities already in reach take the same push on their og.Velocity.

pieces.description: How many Voronoi pieces (fewer when some are under the terrain's minPiece cells).

VfxAsset.description: A loaded composed effect (og.load.vfx): its elements and the emitters, effect materials, meshes, textures and sounds they name.

Vfx.description: Plays a composed effect at the entity's MatrixWorld from startTick (og.vfx.spawn makes one in a call).

seed.description: Its random seed: what `random` values, emitters and sound pitches pick (instances with different seeds differ).

startTick.description: The tick it started: write the tick (`world.tick`) to play it, or to play it again. Its default, never written, waits: an effect spawned ahead of its use plays nothing until a tick is written.

scale.description: Its size: offsets, meshes, trails, beams, lights' reach, decals and flashes scale with it; its emitters are placed and shaped by the scaled transform.

tint.description: Multiplies the colour of everything it draws (linear; above 1 brightens).

despawn.description: Despawn the entity on the tick after a non-looping effect ends.

ran.description: Written by og.vfx: the last tick it ran this effect through (its events, shakes and sounds up to there are sent). Writing startTick again plays it from the start.

VfxEvent.description: A composed effect reached one of its `event` lines (an `impact` line included, named `impact`): the frame a fireball lands, a slash connects, a spell resolves. Read in the tick after, like every event; a replay sends the same.

VfxSpawnDesc.description: Where and how og.vfx.spawn plays an effect.

position.description: Where: in the world, or in the parent's space with a parent.

parent.description: An entity to follow (a sword's tip, a character's chest): the effect's entity becomes its child, so it moves with it and despawns with it.

scale.description: Its size (og.Vfx.scale).

seed.description: Its seed (og.Vfx.seed); 0 takes one from the new entity's id, so each instance differs and a replay repeats it.

loop.description: Whether it starts over at its end.

events.description: Its events' names in time order, `impact` included.

impact.description: Its impact's time, or -1 without one.

elements.description: Its elements' kinds, in file order (emitter, mesh, trail, beam, light, decal, flash, flipbook, shake, sound).
